hadiths.text: Muḥammad b. Yūsuf > Sufyān > al-Aʿmash > Abū Wāʾil > ʿAbdullāh [Machine] A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, will a person be held accountable for what they did in pre-Islamic times?" He replied, "Whoever does good in Islam will not be held accountable for what they did in pre-Islamic times, and whoever does evil in Islam will be held accountable for both the past and present."

A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we were people of ignorance and worshipped idols. We used to kill our children, and I had a daughter. She would respond [to my call] and was pleased when I called her. One day, I called her, and she followed me. I passed by a well belonging to my people, not far away, and I took her hand and dropped her into the well. The last thing I heard from her was her saying, ‘O my father! O my father!’ The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) wept until his tears stopped. A man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “You have grieved the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).” He said to him: “Restrain yourself, for he is asking about that which concerns him.” Then he said to him: “Relate your story to me again.” So he recounted it, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) wept until the tears flowed onto his beard. Then he said to him: “Indeed, Allah has abolished what they used to do in the time of ignorance, so begin your work anew.”

Harun ibn Muawiyah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Sulaiman al-Mudabbir, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, who said: My master told me, "His people sent with him a bowl containing clarified butter and milk to their deities. He forbade me from eating the butter for fear of them. Then a dog came and ate the butter and drank the milk, and then urinated on the idol, which was Usaf and Naila." Harun said: "In the pre-Islamic period, a man, when he traveled, would carry with him four stones: three for his cooking pot and the fourth he would worship and raise a dog, and kill his son."

"We used to, in the time of ignorance, if we found a good stone, we would worship it. And if we did not find a stone, we would gather a mound of sand, then we would bring a pure female camel and make her tread upon it, and we would milk her onto the mound until we filled it. Then we would worship that mound as long as we remained in that place.” Abu Muhammad al-Safi said: “The one with abundant milk.”

Al-Hasan ibn ar-Rabee’ narrated to me, he said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to me from al-A’mash from Abu Salih, who said: Kab said: “We find it written: ‘Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is not harsh, nor rude, nor loud in the marketplaces, nor does he recompense evil with evil, but rather pardons and forgives. And his followers, the Praiseworthy, magnify Allah on every hardship, and praise Him in every circumstance, and they gird their loins and wash over their extremities. Their caller calls out in the expanse of the sky. Their ranks in fighting are equal to their ranks in prayer. They have a buzzing sound at night like the buzzing of bees. His birth was in Mecca, his emigration was to Tayba [Madinah], and his dominion was in Syria.’”

Narrated by Ibn Salam: “Indeed, we find the description of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): ‘Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a herald, and a warner, and a safeguard for the unlettered. You are My slave and My Messenger. I have named him al-Mutawakkil (one who relies on Allah). He is not harsh nor rude, nor loud in the marketplaces, nor does he recompense evil with its like, but rather he pardons and overlooks. And I will not take him back until I straighten the crookedness of the religion by him witnessing that there is no deity except Allah. We will open with him blind eyes and deaf ears and hardened hearts.” ‘Ata’ ibn Yasir said: And Abu Waqid al-Laythi informed me that he heard Ka’b saying the same as Ibn Salam said.

Zayd ibn ‘Auf narrated: Abu ‘Awanah narrated to me from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr from Dhakwan, Abu Salih, from Ka’b: “On the first line: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, My slave and the chosen one, neither coarse nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, nor does he recompense evil with evil, but rather pardons and forgives. His birth was in Mecca, his emigration was to Tayyiba, and his dominion is in Syria. On the second line: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, his community are the Praisers, praising Allah in prosperity and adversity, praising Allah in every circumstance, and exalting Him on every elevation. The shepherds of the sun offer the prayer when its time comes, even if they are on the top of a tower. They draw their waistbands around their middles, and purify the edges of their bodies. And their voices at night in the atmosphere of the sky are like the voices of bees.”

Narrated by Ibn Abbas, that he asked Kab al-Ahbar: "How do you find the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Torah?" Kab al-Ahbar said: "We find it: Muhammad, the son of Abdullah, is born in Mecca, and he migrates to Medina, and his kingdom will be in Syria. He is neither coarse nor loud in the markets, nor does he recompense evil with evil, but rather he pardons and forgives. His community are the Praisers [al-Ḥammadūn], who praise Allah in all ease and adversity, and they magnify Allah on every rise [of fortune]. They wash the edges [of their bodies] and wear belts around their middles. They stand in rows in their prayers as they stand in rows in fighting. The sound of their voices in their mosques is like the buzzing of bees. His caller is heard in the expanse of the sky."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, a Messenger has come to you, neither weak nor indolent, to revive hardened hearts, to open blind eyes, to hear deaf ears, and to straighten the crooked sunnah, until it is said: ‘There is no deity except Allah, alone.’”

Narrated ‘Amir: A man from the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) had a need to be fulfilled from him, so he walked with him until they entered. He said: One of his legs was inside the house and the other outside, as if he were having a private conversation. Then he turned and said: "Do you know who I was speaking to? Indeed, this is an angel whom I have never seen before today. He asked his Lord’s permission to greet me." He said: "Indeed, We have given you the Qur’an in portions, and We have bestowed upon you tranquility, and We have sent down to you the distinguishing judgment."

Narrated ‘Attiya: I heard Rabia Al-Jurashi saying: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was informed, and it was said to him, “Let your eye rest, and let your ear listen, and let your heart comprehend.” He said, “My eyes rested, and my ears listened, and my heart comprehended.” Then it was said to me, “A lord built a house and prepared a feast, and sent a caller. Whoever answered the caller entered the house and ate of the feast, and the lord was pleased with him. And whoever did not answer the caller did not enter the house, nor did he eat of the feast, and the lord was displeased with him.” He said, “Allah is the lord, and Muhammad is the caller, and the house is Islam, and the feast is Paradise.”

The narrator, Hasan ibn Ali, reported: We were told by Abu Usama, from Ja'far ibn Maymun at-Tamimi, from Abu Uthman an-Nahdi, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went out to al-Bat’ha and he was with Ibn Mas’ud. He made him sit and drew a line for him, then said: “Do not move from this place, for men will come to you, so do not speak to them, for they will not speak to you.” Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went where he intended. They kept coming to the line and not crossing it, then they would return to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, until it was late at night. He came to me and rested his cheek upon my thigh. Whenever he slept, he would blow into sleep, a blow. While the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was resting his cheek upon my thigh, asleep, men came to me, appearing like camels, wearing white garments. Allah knows best what beauty they possessed. A group of them sat by his head, and a group of them sat by his feet. They said amongst themselves: “We have never seen a servant given like what this Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has been given. His eyes sleep, but his heart is awake.” They struck a parable for him: “A lord built a palace, then held a feast and invited people to his food and drink, then they departed.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, awoke at that time and said: “Do you know who these are?” I said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “They are the angels.” He said: “And do you know what the parable they struck is?” I said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “The Most Merciful built Paradise and called his servants to it. Whoever answers Him, enters His Paradise, and whoever does not answer Him, He punishes and torments him.”

"Narrated ‘Utbah ibn ‘Abd of the Banu Sulaim, that he narrated to them, and he was among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him, “How was your initial affair, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “My wet nurse was from the Banu Sa’d ibn Bakr. So I and a son of hers set out on two camels. We did not take any provisions with us. I said to my brother, ‘Go and bring us provisions from our mother.’ So my brother went, and I remained with the camels. Then two white birds, like two eagles, approached. One of them said to the other, ‘Is this he?’ The other said, ‘Yes.’ Then they came towards me and seized me, and pressed me against the nape of my back, and split open my belly. Then they extracted my heart and split it. Then they brought out two black clots from it. One of them said to the other, ‘Bring me water from ice.’ So he washed my belly with it. Then he said, ‘Bring me water from frost.’ So he washed my heart with it. Then he said, ‘Bring me tranquility.’ So he placed it in my heart. Then one of them said to the other, ‘Seal him.’ So he sealed him and stamped him with the seal of prophethood. Then one of them said to the other, ‘Place him in one scale and place a thousand from his community in the other scale.’ The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, “Then I look and see the thousand above me, and I fear that some of them will fall upon me.” He said, “If his community were weighed against him, they would outweigh him.” Then they departed and left me. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, “Then I was separated with a severe separation.” Then I went to my mother and told her what I had encountered. She feared that it had mingled with me, so she said, ‘I seek refuge in Allah for you.’ So she prepared a camel for a journey and placed me on the saddle and rode behind me until we reached my mother. She said, ‘I have fulfilled my trust and my pledge.’ And she told her what I had encountered. That did not alarm her, and she said, ‘I saw something come out of me, meaning a light that illuminated the palaces of Syria.’”

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, how did you know that you were a Prophet until you became certain?" He said, "O Abu Dharr, two angels came to me while I was in a part of Batḥā’ of Mecca. One of them fell to the earth, and the other was between the heaven and the earth. One of them said to his companion, ‘Is he he?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ Then he said, ‘Weigh him against a man.’ I was weighed against him, and I outweighed him. Then he said, ‘Weigh him against ten.’ I was weighed against them, and I outweighed them. Then he said, ‘Weigh him against a hundred.’ I was weighed against them, and I outweighed them. Then he said, ‘Weigh him against a thousand.’ I was weighed against them, and I outweighed them, as if I saw them scattering upon me from the lightness of the scale. Then one of them said to his companion, ‘If he were weighed against his ummah, he would outweigh them.’”
Narrated by Abu Salih: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to call out to them, “O people, I am truly a mercy sent down.”

We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey when a Bedouin approached. When he drew near, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Where are you going?" He said, "To my family." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do you desire goodness?" He said, "And what is that?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, alone, without any partners, and that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger." He said, "And who bears witness to what you say?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "This Salama." So, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called her while she was at the riverbank, and she came hurrying, stamping the ground until she stood before him. He testified her three times, and she bore witness three times that it was as he said. Then she returned to her place, and the Bedouin returned to his people. He said, "If they follow me, I will bring them to you, otherwise I will return." So, I was with him.

I went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) on a journey, and he would not relieve himself until he disappeared from sight. We then stopped at a barren piece of land with no tree or landmark. He said, "O Jabir, make some water available in your waterskin, and let us proceed." So, we proceeded until we were out of sight, and there were two trees, four cubits apart. He said, "O Jabir, go to these trees and say to them, 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sends greetings and asks you to join your companion so that I may sit behind you.'" So, they returned to her, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat behind them. Then, they returned to their places, and we rode with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us as if birds were shading us. A woman approached him with her son, and she said, "O Messenger of Allah, this son of mine is taken by Satan every day three times." He took the boy and placed him between himself and the front of the camel. Then he said, "Get lost, enemy of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Get lost, enemy of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," three times. Then he returned him to her. When we completed our journey, we passed that place, and the woman approached us with her son and two rams that she was driving. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, accept my gift." She said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, he has not returned to that since." He said, "Take one of them and return the other to her." Then we traveled, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us as if birds were shading us. Then a camel came braying, and when it was between two saddles, it fell prostrate. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down and said to us, "Whose camel is this?" Some young men from the Ansar said, "It is ours, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "What is the matter with it?" They said, "We have been tethering it for twenty years, and it had a hump, so we wanted to slaughter it and divide it among our boys, but it escaped from us." He said, "Buy it from us." They said, "No, it is yours, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Alright, treat it kindly until its time comes." At that time, the Muslims said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are more deserving of prostrating to you than the beasts." He said, "Nothing should prostrate to anything, even if that were the case, women would be for their husbands."

We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we were directed towards a courtyard in Bani an-Najjar. There was a camel in it that would attack anyone who entered. They mentioned this to the Prophet ﷺ, so he went to it. He called it, and it came, lowering its flank and kneeling before him. He said, "Bring a rein," and he put it on and handed it over to its owner. Then he turned and said, "No one between the heavens and the earth knows that I am the Messenger of Allah except the jinn and mankind who disobey.”

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) with her son, and said: “O Messenger of Allah, my son is afflicted with madness, and he takes possession of himself at our meals, and spoils things for us.” So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) wiped his chest, and then invoked [a blessing], and a gurgling sound came forth, and from his belly came forth something like a black puppy, which ran away.

Muḥammad b. Saʿīd > Yaḥyá b. Abū Bukayr al-ʿAbdī > Ibrāhīm b. Ṭahmān > Simāk > Jābir b. Samurah I recognise the stone in Mecca which used to pay me salutations before my advent as a Prophet and I recognise that even now. (Using translation from Muslim 2277)

"We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) in Mecca. We went out with him in one of its valleys, and we passed between mountains and trees. We did not pass by any tree or mountain but it said, ‘Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.’”

Narrated: A man from Muzayna or Juhaina said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered the Fajr prayer. When he finished, he saw nearly a hundred wolves that had gathered. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Do you concede to them anything of your food and secure what is other than that?" They complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about their need. He said, "Announce their presence." He said, "So, he announced their presence, and they came out, bleating."

Narrated Anas bin Malik (RA) that Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was sitting, grieved, and had become stained with blood due to the actions of the people of Mecca from the tribe of Quraysh. Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you wish that I show you a sign?" He said, "Yes," and he looked at a tree behind him. Gabriel said, "Call for it," so he called for it, and it came and stood before him. Then he said, "Order it to return," so he ordered it to return, and it returned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Sufficient is sufficient for me."

Narrated Abu Huraira, that a man from the tribe of ‘Amir came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah! Teach me something of the Quran.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “Go and call that palm-tree.” He called it, and it came leaping before him. He said, “Tell it to return.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “Return.” So it returned to its place. Then he said, “O tribe of ‘Amir! I have not seen anyone more bewitched today than him!”

Narrated Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) called Bilal, and Bilal sought water, then he came (and said), "By Allah, I found no water." The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Is there anything (like a container)?" So Bilal brought a shahn (a small container), and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) spread his hands in it, and a spring burst forth beneath his hands. Ibn Mas’ud (may Allah be pleased with him) drank from it, and others performed ablution.

Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: We went out on a campaign or journey with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when we were two hundred and thirteen young men. The time for prayer arrived, so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Is there anyone among you who is in a state of purity (i.e., has water to perform ablution)?” A man came running, carrying a small vessel with some water in it. There was no water among the people except for that. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) poured it into a cup, then performed ablution, perfecting the ablution. Then he turned away and left the cup. The people mounted that cup and said: “Rub yourselves, rub yourselves!” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Be gentle” when he heard them saying that. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) placed his hand in the water and the cup and said: “In the name of Allah.” Then he said: “Ensure thorough purification.” By the One who has tested me with my sight, I certainly saw the eyes of the water emerging from between his fingers, and he did not lift his hand until everyone had performed ablution.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi and Sa’id ibn al-Rabee’ said: We were told by Shu’bah, from ‘Amru ibn Murrah and Husein, that they heard Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d saying: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them) say: We were afflicted with thirst and became exhausted, so we came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He placed his hand in a water skin, and it began to bubble forth like springs between his fingers. He said: "Mention the name of Allah." So we drank until it satisfied us and was sufficient for us. In the narration of ‘Amru ibn Murrah: We said to Jabir: How many were you? He said: We were one thousand five hundred, and if we were a hundred thousand, it would have been sufficient.

Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) said: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about thirst, so he called for a container, and water was poured into it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his hand in it, and I began to see springs of water welling forth from between his fingers, and the people began to draw water until all the people had drawn water."

Abdullah (RA) heard a rumbling sound and said, “We, the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), used to consider signs as blessings, and you consider them as a means of frightening. Indeed, while we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and we had no water, he said, ‘Seek out someone who has extra water.’ So, water was brought, and he poured it into a vessel, then placed his hand in it, and the water began to flow out between his fingers. Then he said, ‘Come, come to purity that is blessed,’ and the blessing is from Allah. We drank, and Abdullah said, ‘We used to hear the food praising Allah while it was being eaten.’”

Narrated Abdullah (RA): The earth trembled during the time of Abdullah. I was informed about it, and he said: “Indeed, we, the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), used to see signs as blessings, and you see them as a means of frightening. While we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, the time for prayer approached, and we had only a little water with us. So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for water in a basin and placed his hand in it, and the water began to gush forth between his fingers. Then he said: “Come, perform ablution, and the blessing is from Allah.” So, the people rushed to perform ablution, and I had no concern except what I would put into my stomach because of his saying: “The blessing is from Allah.” I narrated this to Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, and he said: “They were one hundred and fifteen (men).”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to deliver sermons standing on a tree trunk. When the pulpit was built, the trunk moved until it came to him, and he wiped it.

Narrated Ibn Buridah, from his father: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to stand (while delivering the Khutbah) and prolong the standing, which would tire him. So, a trunk of a palm tree was brought and a hole was dug for it and it was set beside him, so that the Prophet (ﷺ) could lean against it while standing. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) delivered the Khutbah and prolonged the standing, he would lean against it. A man who had come to Medina saw him standing beside that trunk and said to those behind him: "If I had known that Muhammad (ﷺ) praised me for anything that would ease his burden, I would have made him a platform on which he could stand, and if he wished, he could sit, and if he wished, he could stand." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said, "Bring him to me." So, they brought him to him, and he was ordered to make three or four such platforms, which are now in the minbar of Medina. The Prophet (ﷺ) found rest in that, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) left the trunk and resorted to those which were made for him, the trunk grieved and groaned as a camel grieves when separated from its young one. Ibn Buridah’s father claimed that the Prophet (ﷺ) heard its groaning and returned to it and placed his hand upon it and said, "Choose whether I should plant you in the place where you were, so that you remain as you were, or if you wish, I should plant you in Paradise, so that you drink from its rivers and springs, and its growth becomes beautiful, and its fruit is eaten by Allah’s friends and its palm trees." He claimed that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying to it, "Yes, I have done so twice." The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about it and said, "It chose that I should plant it in Paradise."

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah Al-Ansari (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to stand up to a trunk (of a tree) before the pulpit was made. When the pulpit was made, that trunk withered, and we heard its groaning. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his hand upon it, and it became silent.

Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) narrated: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to deliver sermons standing on a wooden platform. When a pulpit was constructed and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat upon it, the wooden beam began to sway, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his hand upon it and it became still.”
Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) narrated: "The piece of wood grieved with the grief of a female camel in labor."

Zakarriya ibn ‘Adiyy narrated from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Amr from ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Aqil from At-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka’b from his father, who said: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray towards a tree trunk and deliver sermons to it when the mosque was a mere shade (arish). A man from among his companions said to him: ‘Should we not make a shade for you, so that people can see you and hear your sermon on Fridays?’ He (the Prophet) said: ‘Yes.’ So, three steps were made for him, which are the ones on the pulpit. When the pulpit was made and placed in the place where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had placed it, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came intending to go to the pulpit, he passed over the tree trunk. As soon as he passed it, the trunk shook and split. So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to it and stroked it with his hand until it calmed down. Then he returned to the pulpit. So, whenever he prayed, he would pray towards it. When the mosque was demolished, Ubayy ibn Ka’b took that trunk and it remained with him until it wore out and the earth consumed it, and it became remains.”

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to deliver sermons standing on a tree trunk. A Roman man came to him and said, "I will make a pulpit for you to deliver sermons on." So, he made for him this very pulpit that you see. When the Prophet ﷺ stood on it to deliver a sermon, the tree trunk swayed like a female camel longing for its calf. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended to it and embraced it, and it became calm. He then ordered that it be dug and buried.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, and he said: Al-Sa’q narrated to me, and he said: I heard Hasan say: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) arrived in Medina, he would lean his back against a piece of wood and address the people. They then gathered around him in great numbers. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) wanted to make them hear him, and he said, "Build for me something that I can stand on." They said, "How, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "A platform like the platform of Moses." When they built it for him, Hasan said: By Allah, the piece of wood grieved. Hasan said: Glory be to Allah! Are the hearts of a people who have heard [the message] sought? Abu Muhammad said: He means this.

Hudayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to deliver sermons to a tree trunk before he had a pulpit built. When he had the pulpit built and moved to it, the tree trunk grieved and embraced it, and became still. He (the Prophet) said: "If I had not embraced it, it would have grieved until the Day of Resurrection."

Hudayjah narrated: Al-Hajjaj bin Mihal narrated to me, he said: Hammad bin Salama narrated to me, from Thabit, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), with a similar narration.
Narrated by Sahl bin Sa’d (RA): A piece of wood which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to lean against, grieved, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and placed his hand upon it, and it became calm.

Narrated Anas bin Malik (RA): The Prophet (ﷺ) used to stand on Fridays and lean his back against a propped-up trunk in the mosque and deliver the sermon to the people. A Roman came and said, "Should I not make something for you to sit on, as if you were standing?" So he made a pulpit for him with two steps, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would sit on the third step. When the Prophet (ﷺ) sat on that pulpit, the trunk groaned like an ox until the mosque shook with grief for the Prophet (ﷺ). So the Prophet (ﷺ) descended from the pulpit to it, and embraced it. When the Prophet (ﷺ) embraced it, it became still. Then he said, "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I had not embraced it, it would not have ceased groaning until the Day of Resurrection, out of grief for the Prophet (ﷺ)." So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered it to be buried.
Jabir narrated: I said to Jabir, "Recount to me a Hadith from

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu Talha ordered Umm Sulaim to prepare food for the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) to eat from. Then Abu Talha sent me to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and I went to him. I said, “Abu Talha sent me to you.” He then told the people, “Rise!” and he and the people set out. Abu Talha said, “O Messenger of Allah, did I only prepare this food for you?” He said, “No, go ahead.” So he went ahead, and the people went with him. The food was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) placed his hand over it and said a blessing upon it. Then he said, “Permit ten (people).” He permitted them, and he said, “Eat in the name of Allah.” They ate until they were sated, then they rose. Then he placed his hand as he had done in the first instance and said a blessing upon it. Then he said, “Permit ten (people).” He permitted them, and he said, “Eat in the name of Allah.” They ate until they were sated, then they rose. He did that with eighty men. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), his family, ate, and they left some leftovers.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Aban, who is Al-Attar, narrated to me, he said: Qatadah narrated to me from Shahribin Hawshab from Abu Ubaid (may Allah be pleased with him) that he cooked a pot for the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). The Prophet said to him: "Bring me the arm [of the sheep]." And he liked the arm [of the sheep]. So he brought him the arm, then he said: "Bring me the arm." So he brought him an arm, then he said: "Bring me the arm." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many arms does a sheep have?" He said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you had remained silent, I would have given you an arm for every time you asked."

Muslim b. Ibrāhīm > Abān > al-ʿAṭṭār > Qatādah > Shahr b. Ḥawshab > Abū ʿUbayd > Ṭabakh Lilnnabī ﷺ Qidr [Machine] "He cooked a pot of food for the Prophet ﷺ and the Prophet said to him, 'Serve me a forearm (portion) of it.' He was fond of the forearm, so he served him a forearm. Then he said, 'Serve me the forearm,' so he served him another forearm. Then he said, 'Serve me the forearm,' so I said, 'O Prophet of Allah, how many forearms does a sheep have?' He said, 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you had remained silent, I would have given you forearms as many as you asked for.'"

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allah favored Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, over the prophets and the inhabitants of the heavens. They said: O Ibn Abbas, with what was he favored over the inhabitants of the heavens? He said: Allah said to the inhabitants of the heavens, ‘And whoever says, “I am a god besides Him,” then those We will reward with Hell. Thus do We reward the wrongdoers.’ And Allah said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, ‘Indeed, We have given you a clear victory, That Allah may forgive you what has passed of your sin and what has come after it…’ They said: So, what is his favor over the prophets? He said: Allah said, ‘And We have not sent a messenger except in the language of his people, that he may make clear to them…’ And Allah said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, ‘And We have not sent you except to all mankind, as a messenger…’ So He sent him to the jinn and mankind."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: Some companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) were sitting waiting for him. He came out and when he drew near to them, he heard them discussing. So he listened to their talk. Some of them said, “How astonishing that Allah has taken a friend among His creation! Ibrahim is His friend.” Another said, “What is more astonishing than [Allah spoke to Moses directly]?” Another said, “Jesus is the word of Allah and His spirit.” Another said, “And Allah chose Adam.” Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) came out to them and greeted them, and said, “I have heard your talk and your astonishment. Ibrahim is the friend of Allah, and that is so. Moses is His intimate, and that is so. Jesus is His spirit and His word, and that is so. And Allah chose Adam, and that is so. Know that I am the beloved of Allah, and there is no boasting. I am the bearer of the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting. I am the first intercessor and the first to be interceded for on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting. I am the first to shake the chains of Paradise, and there is no boasting, so Allah will open [them] and let me in with the poor believers, and there is no boasting. I am the most honored of the first and the last with Allah, and there is no boasting.”

Narrated Anas (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the first to depart (for the intercession), and I am their leader when they arrive, and I am their speaker when they listen, and I am their intercessor if they are detained, and I am their bearer of good news when they despair. On that day, the honor and the keys will be in my hand, and I am the most noble of Adam’s descendants before my Lord. A thousand servants will roam around me, appearing as if they are hidden eggs or scattered pearls."

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "I am the leader of the messengers, yet there is no boasting; I am the last of the prophets, yet there is no boasting; and I am the first intercessor and the first to be interceded for, yet there is no boasting."

Narrated Anas bin Malik (RA) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the first one to take hold of the ring of the gate of Paradise and shake it." Anas said: "I could almost see the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moving it.” Sufyan described it to us in this manner, and Abu ‘Abdullah gathered his fingers and moved them. Thabit said to him: “Did you touch the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with your hand?” He said: “Yes.” Thabit said: “Give it to me so that I may kiss it.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I will be the first intercessor in Paradise.”

I will be the first among people whose forehead will split open upon the earth on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting. And I will be given the banner of praise, and there is no boasting. And I am the chief of the people on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting. And I am the first of the people to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting. And I come to the gate of Paradise and grasp its ring, and they say, "Who is this?" And I say, "I am Muhammad." So they open it for me, and I find the Almighty (Allah) facing me, so I prostrate to Him. He says, "Raise your head, O Muhammad, and speak, so that you may be heard, and say, so that it may be accepted from you, and intercede, so that you may intercede." So I raise my head and say, "My community, my community, O Lord." He says, "Go to your community, and whoever you find in whose heart is a speck of a grain of barley’s weight of faith, let him enter Paradise." So I go, and whoever I find in whose heart is a speck of that weight, I let them enter Paradise. Then I find the Almighty facing me, so I prostrate to Him. He says, "Raise your head, O Muhammad, and speak, so that you may be heard, and say, so that it may be accepted from you, and intercede, so that you may intercede." So I raise my head and say, "My community, my community, O Lord." He says, "Go to your community, and whoever you find in whose heart is a speck of a grain of mustard seed’s weight of faith, let him enter Paradise." So I go, and whoever I find in whose heart is a speck of that weight, I let them enter Paradise. And the accounting of the people is completed, and whoever remains from my community is admitted into the Fire with the people of the Fire. The people of the Fire say, "What availed you that you used to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him?" He says, "By My majesty, I will surely redeem them from the Fire." So He sends for them, and they come out of the Fire, having their skins peeled off. Then they are admitted into the River of Life, and they grow in it as a grain grows in the silt of a flood. And it is written between their eyes, "These are the freed slaves of Allah." Then they are taken and enter Paradise. The people of Paradise say to them, "These are the people of Hell." He says, "Rather, these are the freed slaves of the Almighty."

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, Muawiyah narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Maysarah, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Ibn Ghanm, who said: "Gabriel descended upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and split open his abdomen. Then Gabriel said: 'There is a heart within it, with two ears that hear and two eyes that see. Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, the one who will follow [others], the one who will gather [on the Day of Judgment]. Your character is sound, your tongue is truthful, and your soul is tranquil.'" Abu Muhammad said: "Wakī‘ means severe."

Narrated by ‘Amr bin Qais: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Indeed, Allah has decreed a term for me, and has shortened it for me, so we are the last, and we are the foremost on the Day of Resurrection. And I say a statement without boasting: Ibrahim is Allah’s intimate friend, Musa is Allah’s chosen one, and I am Allah’s beloved. And with me is the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah has promised me in my Ummah three things: that they will not be afflicted by a year of famine, nor will an enemy uproot them, nor will they be gathered upon misguidance.”

While we were in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man said: “O Messenger of Allah, have you been brought food from the heavens?” He (ﷺ) said: “Yes, I have been brought food.” He said: “O Prophet of Allah, was there any abundance in it?” He (ﷺ) said: “Yes.” He said: “What was done with it?” He (ﷺ) said: “It was returned to the heavens, and it has been revealed to me that I will not remain among you for long, and then you will remain, until you say: ‘When, when?’ Then you will come to me in groups, each group destroying the other, before the Hour, there will be severe deaths, and after that will be years of earthquakes.”

Narrated by Samura bin Jundub (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “A bowl of thick porridge was brought and placed before the people, and they ate from it until noon. Some people would stand and others would sit. Then a man said to Samura bin Jundub: ‘Was it not extended (i.e., replenished)?’ Samura said: ‘What are you astonished at? It was not extended except from up there,’ and he pointed with his hand towards the sky.

Jabir ibn Samurah (RA) said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) on a moonlit night wearing a red garment. I kept looking at him and the moon, and he appeared to me more beautiful than the moon."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He who perfects his two front teeth, a light is seen emanating from between his teeth when he speaks.”
"I have never seen anyone with more generosity, courage, brilliance, or eloquence than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
I asked Rubayyi’ bint Mu’awwidh ibn ‘Afraa’ to describe the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to me. She said, “O my son, if you had seen him, you would have seen the rising sun.”

Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was of a bright complexion, as if his perspiration were pearls. When he walked, he would sway. I have never touched silk or satin softer than his hand, nor have I ever smelled a fragrance sweeter than his, whether musk or other than musk.

Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I served the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he never said 'ugh' to me, nor did he reproach me for anything I did, saying, 'Why did you do such and such?' or 'Why didn't you do such and such?' He said, 'By Allah, I have never touched silk or satin softer than the hand of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I have never smelled a fragrance or felt a scent sweeter than the scent of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.'"

I was with my father when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stoned Ma’iz ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him. When the stones struck him, I was frightened. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, embraced me, and his armpit perspiration flowed over me like the scent of musk.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Baraa', who said: A man asked him, "Did you see the face of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, like a sword?" He said, "No, like the moon."
Narrated by Yazid ibn Harun: He narrated to me, Sharik narrated to me, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was recognized at night by his pleasant scent."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “No one treads a path or refrains from treading a path, but someone follows him, except that he knows he has trodden it by the fragrance of his scent,” or he said, “by the scent of his sweat.”

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, and Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Laythi narrated to me, from Abu Salama, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would eat gifts and would not accept charity. A woman from the Jews of Khaybar presented to him a cooked sheep, so he took from it, and Bishr ibn al-Bara' took from it. Then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his hand and said: "Indeed, this [sheep] informs me that it is poisoned." Bishr ibn al-Bara' died. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent for the woman and asked her: "What prompted you to do what you did?" She said: "If you are a prophet, nothing will harm you, and if you are a king, I have relieved the people of you." He said, while he was ill: "I have been from the food I ate at Khaybar, so this is the time for the severing of my eyesight."

Hakam ibn Naafi’ reported: We were told by Shu’aib ibn Abi Hamza, from Zuhri, that Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) narrated that a Jewish woman from the people of Khaybar poisoned a sheep and presented it as a gift to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) took a piece of its arm and ate from it, and his companions ate with him. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them, "Lift your hands." The Prophet (ﷺ) then sent for the Jewish woman and said to her, "Did you poison this sheep?" She said, "Yes, and who informed you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "This arm informed me: ‘For the arm’." She said, "Yes." He said, "What was your intention in doing that?" She said, "I said, ‘If he is a prophet, it will not harm him, and if he is not a prophet, we will be rid of him.’" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forgave her and did not punish her. Some of his companions who had eaten from the sheep died, and the Prophet (ﷺ) applied cupping on his shoulder because of those who had eaten from the sheep. Abu Hind, the freed slave of Banu Biyada, cupped him with the horn and the blade, and he was from Banu Thamama, who are a tribe of the Ansar.

Narrated Abu Huraira: When Khaybar was conquered, a sheep containing poison was presented as a gift to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He (ﷺ) said, "Gather for me all the Jews who are here.” They were gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them, "I ask you about something, will you truthfully answer me about it?” They said, “Yes, O Abu al-Qasim.” He (ﷺ) said to them, “Who is your father?” They said, “So-and-so.” He (ﷺ) said, “You have lied; your father is so-and-so.” They said, “You have told the truth and judged rightly.” He (ﷺ) said, “Will you truthfully answer me about anything if I ask you about it?” They said, “Yes.” He (ﷺ) said, “Who are the people of the Fire?” They said, “We will be among them for a while, then you will replace us in it.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “Get out of it, and by Allah, you will never replace us in it.” Then he (ﷺ) said to them, “Will you truthfully answer me about anything if I ask you about it?” They said, “Yes.” He (ﷺ) said, “Did you put poison in this sheep?” They said, “Yes.” He (ﷺ) said, “What made you do that?” They said, “If you were a liar, we would rest from you, and if you were a prophet, it would not harm you.”
Narrated Jabir: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was never asked anything that he said "no" to. Abu Muhammad said: Ibn Uyaynah said: If he did not have it, he would promise.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was modest and would give whatever was asked of him.

I jostled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn, and I had a thick shoe on my foot. I stepped on the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it. He blew on me with a blow of his whip and said, "In the name of Allah, you have pained me." I spent the night blaming myself, saying, "I have pained the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." I spent the night as Allah knows. When morning came, there was a man saying, "Where is so-and-so?" I said, "This is, by Allah, the one who happened from me yesterday." So I left, and I was fearful. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "Indeed, you stepped on my foot with your shoe yesterday and pained me, so I blew on you with a blow of the whip. Here are eighty sheep, take them with it."

Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. Abū Khalaf > ʿAbd al-Raḥman b. Muḥammad > Muḥammad b. Isḥāq > ʿAbdullāh b. Abū Bakr > a man from al-ʿArab [Machine] I stepped on the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Battle of Hunayn, and I had thick-soled sandals on. He took a whip and lightly hit me, saying, "In the name of Allah, you hurt me!" I felt guilty and said to myself, "I hurt the Messenger of Allah ﷺ". I spent that night in distress, knowing that Allah knew what had happened. The next morning, a man asked, "Where is so and so?" I said, "I swear by Allah, yesterday I did something to him." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "You stepped on my foot with your sandal yesterday and caused me pain. I hit you back lightly with the whip. Here are eighty sheep, take them as compensation."

"The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would frequently engage in remembrance of Allah, be sparse in idle talk, prolong the prayer, shorten the sermon, and would not feel ashamed or reluctant to walk with a widow or a poor person to fulfill their needs."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ayyub, from Ikrimah, who said: Al-’Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “I wanted to know how long the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would remain among us.” So he said: “O Messenger of Allah, I see that they are troubling you and the dust from them is troubling you. Why don’t you build a canopy and speak to them from it?” He (the Prophet) said: “I will remain among them as long as they tread on my heels and dispute with me about my garment until Allah gives me relief from them.” He said: “So I knew that his stay among us would be brief.”

Sulaymān b. Ḥarb > Ḥammād b. Zayd > Ayyūb > ʿIkrimah [Machine] Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, asked: "O Messenger of Allah, do you know how long you will stay among us?" The Prophet ﷺ replied, "I see that they have harmed you, and their disturbance has caused you discomfort. If you were to take a tent to speak to them from, would it be better?" The Prophet responded, "I will continue to stay in their midst, enduring their abuse and disputes over my cloak until Allah relieves me from them." Abbas said, "I understood from this that his stay among us would not be for long."

Zakarriya ibn ‘Adiyy narrated to me, he said: Hatim ibn Isma’il narrated to me, from ‘Unays ibn Abi Yahya, from his father, from Abu Sa’id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came out to us while he was suffering from the illness in which he died, and we were in the mosque. He had a cloth wrapped around his head, and he leaned towards the pulpit until he reached it. He then stood upon it and we followed him. He said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I see the Hawd (fountain) from my position here.” Then he said: “Indeed, a servant has been presented with the world and its adornments, and he chose the Hereafter.” He said: No one understood it except Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), so his eyes overflowed, and he wept. Then he said: “Rather, we redeem you with our parents, our mothers, ourselves, and our wealth, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: Then he descended from it and he did not stand upon it until the Hour.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings upon him, said to me, "Indeed, I have been commanded to seek forgiveness for the people of Baqi’, so come with me.” So I went with him in the middle of the night. When he stood before them, he said, “Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the graves, may it lighten what you have become in, from what the people have become in. The trials and tribulations have come like a dark night, its end following its beginning: the latter is worse than the former.” Then he turned to me and said, “O Abu Muwaihbah, indeed, I have been given the keys to the treasures of the world and perpetuity therein, then Paradise. I was given a choice between that and meeting my Lord.” I said, “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, take the keys to the treasures of the world and perpetuity therein, then Paradise.” He said, “No, by Allah, O Abu Muwaihbah, I have chosen to meet my Lord.” Then he sought forgiveness for the people of Baqi’, and then he turned away. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings upon him, was afflicted with the illness in which he died.

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: When the verse (When Allah’s help comes and the conquest [of Makkah]) was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) called Fatima and said, "My soul has been announced to me." She wept, and he said, "Do not weep, for you will be the first of my family to join me." She then laughed. One of the Prophet’s wives saw her weeping and then laughing and said, "O Fatima, we saw you weeping, then laughing. What happened?" She said, "The Messenger of Allah told me that his soul had been announced to him, so I wept. Then he said to me, ‘Do not weep, for you will be the first of my family to join me,’ so I laughed.” The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Allah’s help and the conquest have come, and the people of Yemen have come. They are the most tender of hearts, and faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni.”

Aisha (RA) narrated: The Prophet (ﷺ) returned to me one day from a funeral from Baqi’, and I was suffering from a headache and saying, “Woe to my head!” He said, “Rather, I (am saying it), O Aisha, woe to my head!” He said, “What harm would it be to you if you died before me, so I would wash you, shroud you, pray over you, and bury you?” I said, “I think that if I did that, you would return to my home and marry one of your wives.” Aisha (RA) added, “Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled, and then he was afflicted with the illness in which he died.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) during his illness said, "Pour over me seven pitchers of water from seven different wells until I emerge to the people and give them a farewell address." So, we placed him in a basin belonging to Hafsa, and we poured water over him, either pouring or sprinkling, the uncertainty being from Muhammad ibn Ishaq. He then felt relief, and he went out and ascended the pulpit. He praised Allah and glorified Him, and sought forgiveness for the martyrs of Uhud, and supplicated for them. Then he said, "As for what follows, the Ansar are my refuge to which I have taken shelter, so honor their noble ones, and pardon their wrongdoers except in a matter that warrants punishment. Indeed, a servant of Allah has been given a choice between this world and what is with Allah, and he chose what is with Allah.” Abu Bakr wept, thinking that he was referring to himself. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Remain silent, O Abu Bakr. Block all the gates and streets leading to the mosque except the gate of Abu Bakr, for I do not know of anyone who is better with me in companionship than Abu Bakr.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was summoned for prayer while he was ill, and he said, "Order Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer." Then he lost consciousness. When he recovered, he said, "Did I order Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer?" I said, "Indeed, Abu Bakr is a gentle man, so if you had ordered Umar, he would have done so." He said, "You are like the companions of Yusuf; order Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer, for there may be a speaker who desires [something] but Allah and the believers reject it."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Ikrimah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away on a Monday, and the remainder of that day and night, and the following day, were spent in suspension until he was buried on Wednesday night. They said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has not died, but his spirit has been taken up as the spirit of Moses was taken up.’ Then Umar stood up and said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has not died, but his spirit has been taken up as the spirit of Moses was taken up. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, will not die until he cuts off the hands and tongues of people.’ Umar continued speaking until his cheeks became red from what he promised and said. Then Al-Abbas stood up and said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has indeed died. He was a human being, and he would experience hardship like any human being.’ O people, bury your companion, for he is more honored before Allah than to die twice – to die the death of one of you and then to die a second death. Is he more honored before Allah than that? O people, bury your companion. If it is as you say, then it is not difficult for Allah to search for him beneath the dust. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, by Allah, did not die until he left a clear and well-defined path, legalizing what is permissible and prohibiting what is forbidden, marrying and divorcing, fighting and making peace. No shepherd ever tended his flock, following its owner over the mountain peaks, striking at the wild goats with his staff and watering its troughs with his hand, was more diligent than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He was among you, O people, so bury your companion. Umm Ayman began to weep, and they said to her, ‘O Umm Ayman, are you weeping for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?’ She said, ‘By Allah, I am not weeping for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, because I do not know that he has gone to something better for him than this world, but I am weeping because the news from the heavens has ceased.’ Hammad said: ‘A tear choked Ayyub when he reached here.’”

Narrated by Yahya ibn ‘Umar: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When any one of you is afflicted by a calamity, let him mention his calamity because of me, for it is among the greatest of calamities."

Narrated by Abu Nu'aim, from Fitr, from Ata': He said that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When any one of you is afflicted by a calamity, let him mention his calamity with [mentioning] me, for it is among the greatest of calamities."
I have never heard Ibn Umar mention the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, without weeping.

Fatima (RA) said, "O Anas! How did your souls become content to throw dust upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)? " And she said, "O my father! From his Lord comes what is closest. O my father! The Garden of Paradise is his abode. O my father! To Gabriel we announce his passing. O my father! He answered his Lord’s call.” Hammad said: When Thabit narrated, he wept. And Thabit said: When Anas narrated, he wept.

I witnessed him on the day he entered Medina, and I have never seen a day more radiant or beautiful than the day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon us. And I witnessed him on the day of his death, and I have never seen a day more dreadful or gloomy than the day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, died.

Abdullah ibn Salam said to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), "O Messenger of Allah, indeed we find you on the Day of Resurrection standing before your Lord, and you are crimson, and your two flanks are shamed before your Lord by what your community has innovated after you."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: When this Surah was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), [referring to Surah An-Nasr: "When comes the Help of Allah, and the Victory, and you see the people enter the religion of Allah in troops," (110:1-2)], the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "They will surely go out of it in troops, just as they entered it in troops."

al-Qāsim b. Kathīr > ʿAbd al-Raḥman b. Shurayḥ > Abū al-Aswad al-Qurashī > Abū Qurrah a freed slave of Abū Jahl > Abū Hurayrah [Machine] From the Prophet ﷺ that when this Surah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ{When the victory of Allah and the conquest comes, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes}[Al-Nasr 2], the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "They will enter it in groups just as they entered it in groups."

Abu al-Jawza’ (Aus ibn Abdillah) narrated: "The people of Medina experienced severe drought, so they complained to Aisha. She said: 'Look at the grave of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and make vessels from it to the sky, so that there is no roof between it and the sky.' They did so, and we were rained upon until grass grew and camels fattened until their humps split. That year was named ‘the year of splitting.’”

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated from Saeed ibn Abdul-Aziz, who said: "During the days of the heat, the adhan was not called out three times in the Prophet’s Mosque (peace be upon him), nor was the iqama announced. Saeed ibn al-Musayyib did not leave the mosque, and he did not know the time of prayer except by a murmuring sound he would hear from the Prophet’s grave.” Then he mentioned its meaning.

K`ab entered upon Aisha, and they mentioned the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. K`ab said: “Every morning, seventy thousand angels descend to surround the grave of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, striking their wings, and they send blessings upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. When evening comes, they ascend, and a like number descends, and they do the same. And when the earth splits open for him, seventy thousand angels will emerge, escorting him.”

Abu 'Asim narrated to me, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, who said: Khalid ibn Ma'dan narrated to me, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr, from 'Irbad ibn Sariyah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offered the Fajr (dawn) prayer for us, then delivered a profound sermon that brought tears to the eyes and caused hearts to tremble. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah! It seems like a farewell sermon." So he gave us advice, and said: "I advise you to fear Allah, and to listen and obey, even if the ruler is an Ethiopian slave. Whoever lives after me will surely see much disagreement. So adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided Caliphs. Hold firmly to it. And avoid innovations, for every innovation is a misguidance." Abu 'Asim said once: "And avoid innovations in matters, for every innovation is a deviation."

Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from Zuhri, who said: Those of our scholars who have passed away used to say: "Clinging to the Sunnah is salvation, and knowledge is withdrawn swiftly. The vitality of knowledge is the stability of religion and the world, and with the disappearance of knowledge, all of that disappears."

It has reached me that the first departure of religious commitment is the abandonment of the Sunnah. Religious commitment departs bit by bit, with each Sunnah abandoned, just as a rope frays strand by strand.

Narrated to us Abu al-Mughira, who said: Sufyan narrated to us from Hasan, who said: "Whenever a people introduce a novelty into their religion, Allah takes away from their sunna an equivalent to it, and He does not return it to them until the Day of Resurrection."
Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Ayyub narrated to me, from Abu Qilaba, who said: "Whenever a man introduces something new (in religion), he declares the sword permissible."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, who said: "Indeed, the people of whims and desires are people of misguidance, and I do not see their end but in the Fire. So, test them, for none of them adopts a statement or a saying but the matter reaches the sword. And indeed, hypocrisy was of various kinds. Then he recited: ‘And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give thanks, and we will be of the righteous. [Surah At-Tawba 9:75]’ And: ‘And among them are those who reproach you for the charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased, but if they are not given from them, they are displeased. [Surah At-Tawba 9:58]’ And: ‘And among them are those who hurt the Prophet and say, “He is but a deafened one.” Say, “An ear of goodness for you. [Surah At-Tawba 9:61]” So their words differed, and they gathered upon doubt and disbelief. And these people, their words differed and they gathered upon the sword. And I do not see their end but in the Fire.” Hammad said: Then Ayyub said, at the end of this narration or at the beginning: “By Allah, he was one of the knowledgeable and discerning scholars,” meaning Abu Qilaba.

'Amru ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Ata', from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud and Hudhaifa, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they were sitting when a man came and asked them about something. Ibn Mas'ud said to Hudhaifa: "For what reason do you think they ask me about this?" He said: "They know it, but then they abandon it." Then Ibn Mas'ud turned to him and said: "If you have asked us about anything from the Book of Allah, the Exalted, that we know, we will tell you about it, or about any Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that we know. But we have no capacity for what you have innovated."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Musawwidi narrated to me, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, who said: "I witnessed every sermon that Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) delivered in Kufa. One day, he was asked about a man who divorces his wife eight times and similar matters. He said: 'It is as he said,' then he said: 'Indeed, Allah revealed His Book and clarified His explanation. So whoever comes to the matter from its proper face, it has been clarified to him. And whoever contradicts, by Allah, we cannot accept your contradiction.'"

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysara told me: I heard al-Nazzal ibn Sabra say: "I witnessed 'Abd Allah, and a man and a woman came to him seeking a ruling regarding prohibition [from marriage]. He said: 'Indeed, Allah has made it clear. So whoever approaches the matter from its face [i.e., directly and without deviation], then it has been clarified for him. And whoever contradicts [this], by Allah, we cannot accept your contradiction.'"
"He would not express an opinion except for something he had heard."
Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me, that 'Aththam, the father of 'Ali ibn 'Aththam, and Al-A'mash narrated to me, that he said: "I never heard Ibrahim express an opinion based on his own reasoning."
Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Qatada, who said: "I have not expressed an opinion based on my own reasoning for thirty years." Abu Hilal said: "For forty years."

Malik related to me, and Hakim related to me, from Abu Khaithama, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay‘, who said: Ata’ was asked about something, and he said, “I do not know.” It was said to him, “Why don’t you give your opinion about it?” He said, “I am ashamed before Allah that my opinion should be taken as a judgment on earth.”

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, Hatim, who is the son of Isma'il, narrated to me, from 'Isa, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: A man came to him asking about something, and he said, "Ibn Mas'ud used to say so and so about it." The man said, "Tell me your opinion." He said, "Do you not marvel at this? I informed him about what Ibn Mas'ud said, and he asks me for my opinion. My religion is more precious to me than that. By Allah, I prefer to recite a poem than to tell you my opinion."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, and Hammam narrated to me, he being the son of Isma'il, from 'Isa, from Ash-Sha'bi, who said: "Beware of analogical reasoning (qiyas). By Him whose soul is in my hand, if you were to follow analogical reasoning, you would certainly permit what is forbidden and prohibit what is lawful. Rather, whatever reaches you from those who memorized the teachings of the Companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), act upon it."

Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to me from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Alqamah, who said: A man came to Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) and said, "I divorced my wife yesterday with eight revocations." He said, "With a single word?" He said, "With a single word." He said, "Do they intend to declare your wife divorced?" He said, "Yes." Then another man came and said, "He divorced his wife one hundred times." He said, "With a single word?" He said, "With a single word." He said, "Do they intend to declare your wife divorced?" He said, "Yes." Then Abdullah said, "Whoever divorces as Allah has commanded, Allah has declared the divorce. And whoever confuses himself, We entrust him with his confusion. By Allah, you do not confuse yourselves, and We will bear it. It is as you say."
"It is better for a man to live in ignorance after knowing his right due to Allah than to utter what he does not know."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, who said: I heard al-Qasim being asked, and he said: "By Allah, we do not know everything you ask about, and if we did, we would not conceal it from you, nor would it be permissible for us to conceal it from you."

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Ibn 'Awn who said: Al-Qasim was asked about something he had named, and he said: "I do not feel the need for consultation, and I am not of those who deliberate in anything."

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Yahya, who said: I said to Qasim: "What is more difficult for me than being asked about something you do not have knowledge of, especially since your father was a leading scholar?" He said: "What is more difficult, in the sight of Allah and in the view of one who understands from Allah, is that I give a legal opinion without knowledge, or narrate from an untrustworthy source."

"Whenever a matter would befall them for which there was no precedent from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, they would gather and deliberate, and the truth would be in what they saw."

Narrated by Wahb bin Amr Al-Jumahi, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not hasten the calamity before it comes. For if you do not hasten it before it comes, the Muslims will not break apart even if it descends amongst them, and there will be one among them who speaks, and he will be guided and directed. But if you hasten it, you will disagree amongst yourselves, and you will take [different paths], gesturing with his hands before him, to his right, and to his left.”

Narrated by Abu Salama: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was asked about a matter that did not occur in the Book or the Sunnah. He said: "Let the devout worshippers among the believers look into it."

Qasim said: "Indeed, you ask about matters we did not ask about, and you inquire about things we did not inquire about, and you ask about things I do not know what they are. If we had known them, it would not be permissible for us to conceal them from you."
"Indeed, there will come people who argue with you using ambiguities of the Quran, so confront them with the Sunnah, for the people of the Sunnah are more knowledgeable about the Book of Allah."

"The affair of the Children of Israel remained moderate, free from fault, until the Muwalladun arose among them – the offspring of captives, the sons of women whom the Children of Israel had taken captive from other nations. Then they began to say, 'Let us rule by opinion,' and that led them astray."

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, that Hammad ibn Yazid al-Minkari narrated to me, that my father narrated, that a man came to Ibn Umar one day and asked him about something he did not know what it was. Ibn Umar said to him, "Do not ask about that which has not occurred, for I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab curse one who asks about that which has not occurred."

Hakim ibn Naafi’ reported: Shu’aib reported to us from Zuhri who said: It reached us that Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, if asked about a matter, “Was this?” If they said, “Yes, it was,” he would relate what he knew and what he saw concerning it. And if they said, “No, it was not,” he would say, “Leave it until it comes to be.”

Imaam Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Hishaam al-Mazumi narrated to me, saying: Wuhayb narrated to me, saying: Dawood narrated to me, from ‘Aamir, who said: ‘Ammaar ibn Yaasir, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked a question. He said, "Was this [matter] after [a certain event]?" They said, "No." He said, "Leave us until it occurs. When it does, we will bear it with you."
'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said from the pulpit: "By Allah, I forbid anyone from asking about that which has not occurred, for Allah has already clarified what will be."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shaiba, he said: Ibn Fudail narrated to me from Ata, from Saeed, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I have never seen a people better than the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. They did not ask him about anything except thirteen matters until he was taken [by death], and all of them were mentioned in the Quran, such as: # ‘Ask them about the sacred month’ (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 217) # and # ‘And they ask you about menstruation’ (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 222) #. He said: They did not ask except about that which benefited them.”

"I asked those of the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, whom I found more than those who preceded me. I have not seen a people with easier conduct nor less strictness than them."

Al-Abbas ibn Sufyan narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Hubab, who narrated to me, that: I heard ‘Ubadah ibn Nusayr al-Kindi. He was asked about a woman who died with a group of people and she had no guardian. He said: “I found people who did not intensify [restrictions] as you do, nor did they ask questions like yours.”

Al-`Abbas ibn Sufyan narrated to me, and Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to me, and Raja’ ibn Abi Salama narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Hazim narrated to me from Hisham ibn Muslim al-Qurashi, who said: I was with Ibn Muhayriz at Marj al-Dibaj, and I saw him in seclusion. I asked him a question, and he said to me: "What do you do with questions?" I said: "If there were no questions, knowledge would vanish." He said: "Do not say that knowledge vanishes, for it does not vanish as long as the Quran is recited. But if you said: 'Understanding vanishes,' that would be correct."

Narrated by 'Umar (RA): "O people, indeed we do not know. It is possible that we order you to do things that are not permissible for you, and it is possible that we forbid you from things that are lawful for you. The last verses to be revealed from the Qur'an were the verses concerning riba (interest), and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) did not clarify them for us until he died. So, abandon what causes you doubt to what does not cause you doubt."

Salim ibn Junadah narrated to me, that Ibn Idris narrated to me from his uncle, who said: "I left the presence of Ibrahim, and Hammad met me. He burdened me with eight questions, and I asked him, and he answered four and left four."
Qabisa reported: Sufyan narrated to me from Abd al-Malik ibn Abjar from Zubayd who said: "I never asked Ibrahim about anything but I recognized aversion in his face."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me, from Umar ibn Abi Zaidah, who said: "I have not seen anyone more frequently saying, 'I have no knowledge of that,' than the people when asked about something, [saying so] regarding al-Sha'bi."

Abu 'Aasim narrated to me from Ibn 'Awn, who said: I heard him mention, saying: Al-Sha'bi, whenever something came to him, would be cautious. And Ibrahim would say, and say, and say. Abu 'Aasim said: "In this matter, Ibn 'Awn considered Al-Sha'bi to be in a better state than Ibrahim."

Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated: Ahmad ibn Bashir narrated to me: Shu'bah narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Iyas, who said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, "Why don't you speak about divorce?" He said, "There is nothing about it that I have not inquired about, but I dislike declaring permissible what is forbidden, or forbidding what is permissible."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me, from Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, who said: I heard Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla saying: "I witnessed in this mosque two hundred and twenty from the Ansar, and none of them would relate a hadith except that he wished his brother would suffice him with it, and none of them would be asked for a legal opinion except that he wished his brother would suffice him with it."

Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Saffar narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to me, from Dawud, who said: I asked al-Sha'bi, "How did you people proceed when you were asked [a question]?" He said: "You have fallen upon the knowledgeable one. Whenever a man was asked [a question], he would say to his companion, 'Inform them,' and it would continue until it returned to the first [person]."
"The scholar enters into that which is between Allah and His servants, so let him seek a means of escape [from trial]."

Muhammad ibn Qudamah narrated to me, Abu Usama narrated to me, from Mis’ar, who said: Ma’n ibn ‘Abd ar-Rahman brought a letter to me and swore to me by Allah that it was his father’s handwriting. In it was written: “Abdullah said: ‘By the One who is not worshipped but Him, I have not seen anyone harsher towards those who feign piety than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And I have not seen anyone harsher towards them than Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. And I see ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, as the most fearful to them or for them.’”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Uthman ibn Hadhir al-Azdi, who said: I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and I said to him: Advise me. He said: Yes, "Hold fast to the remembrance of Allah and steadfastness, follow [the established way] and do not innovate."
Narrated by Ibn Sirin: "They considered that he was upon the right path as long as he was upon the trace (of the Prophet)."
"As long as one adheres to the way (of the Prophet), he is upon the path."

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Learn knowledge before it is taken away, and its being taken away is when its people vanish. Beware of boastfulness, delving too deeply, and innovations; and adhere to the traditional teachings."

Ibn Mas’ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Adhere to knowledge before it is taken away, and its taking away is the departure of its people. Adhere to knowledge, for one of you may not know when he will be needed or when his knowledge will be needed. You will find people claiming they call you to the Book of Allah, yet they have cast it behind their backs. So adhere to knowledge, and avoid innovation, avoid boastfulness, avoid delving deeply, and adhere to the traditional knowledge.”

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, Yazid ibn Hazim narrated to me, from Sulaiman ibn Yasar, that a man named Sabigh came to Medina and began to inquire about the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an. Umar (RA) sent for him and prepared palm fiber ropes. He said, "Who are you?" He said, "I am Abdullah Sabigh." Umar took a rope from those ropes and struck him, saying, "I am Abdullah Umar." He kept striking him until his head bled. He said, "O Commander of the Believers, that is enough; what I used to feel in my head has gone."

Narrated Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: “He has revealed to you (O Muhammad) the Book with verses that are decisive [muhkamat] – they are the mother of the Book – and others allegorical [mutashabihat].” [Surah Al-Imran 3:7] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If you see those who follow what is ambiguous of it, then beware of them.”
