Abdullah b. Muhammad narrated to us, that Hafs narrated to us, from Al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, that he said: Abdullah was asked about something, and he said: "Indeed, I hate to permit you something that Allah has forbidden you, or to forbid you something that Allah has permitted you."
"It is more beloved to me to return it to its owner even if it is in its filth, than to undertake for him what I do not know."

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Layth narrated to me, saying: Ibn ‘Ajlan narrated to me from Naafi’, the freedman of Abdullah, that Sabigh al-’Iraqi used to inquire about certain matters of the Quran in various regions among the Muslims until he came to Egypt. Then ‘Amr ibn al-‘Aas, may Allah be pleased with him, sent him to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. When the messenger brought the book to him, and he read it, ‘Umar said: "Where is the man?" He was told: "In the baggage." ‘Umar said: "Be careful lest he has gone and you incur a painful punishment from me because of him." So, he brought him to him. ‘Umar said: "You ask about novelties." Then ‘Umar sent for bundles of palm leaves and struck him with them until he left his back bare. Then he left him until he healed. Then he returned to him, and left him until he healed. Then he summoned him to treat him again. Sabigh said: "If you intend to kill me, then kill me in a beautiful manner. And if you intend to treat me, then by Allah, I have been cured." So, ‘Umar permitted him to return to his land, and wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, may Allah be pleased with him, instructing him not to allow anyone from the Muslims to sit with him. This caused the man great distress, so Abu Musa wrote to ‘Umar: "His repentance has become good." So, ‘Umar wrote: "Permit the people to sit with him."

Abu al-Mundhir was asked by a man about something, and he said, "O my son, was this the matter about which you inquired?" He said, "No." He said, "Then do not, postpone me until it occurs, so that we may take care of ourselves until we inform you."

I was walking with Ubayy ibn Kab (may Allah be pleased with him) when a young man said, “O my uncle, what do you say about such and such a thing?” He replied, “O my nephew, was this already?” The young man said, “No.” He said, “Then let us be lenient until it comes to be.”
Ibrahim would not answer anything except with a response to the very question that was posed to him.
He (Muhammad ibn Sirin) would not give a legal opinion regarding anything concerning sexual relations where there was a difference of opinion.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, Al-Salt ibn Rashid narrated, saying: I asked Tawus about a matter, and he said to me, "Was it like this?" I said, "Yes." He said, "By Allah, I swear!" I said, "By Allah, I swear!" Then he said: "Our companions narrated to us from Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: 'O people, do not hasten the trials before their arrival, lest you be taken here and there. If you do not hasten the trials before their arrival, the Muslims will always have among them one who, when asked, is guided, and when he speaks, is successful.'"

I asked Ibn Abbas about a man who was overtaken by two Ramadans. He said, “Was he or was he not?” I said, “He was not.” He said, “Leave his affliction until it descends.” So, we presented a man to him, and he said, “He was.” He said, “He should feed thirty poor people for them, each day a poor person.”

I was sitting in Mecca one day with Ibn Umar and another day with Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Whenever he was asked a question, Ibn Umar would say, "I have no knowledge [of it] beyond what others give rulings upon."
Narrated by Abdullah: "Learn, for none of you knows when they will be called upon [to answer]."
The most daring among you in giving legal opinions (fatwa) is the most daring among you in the Fire.

One who introduces an opinion that is not in the Book of Allah and is not sanctioned by a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, does not know what he will be accounted for when he meets Allah.
"Whoever is given a legal opinion (fatwa) without proper verification, then his sin is upon the one who gave it to him."
One who gives a legal opinion without sufficient knowledge, then the sin of that opinion is upon him.

Muhammad ibn Salit narrated to me, saying: Zuhayr narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Burqan, who narrated to me from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when a disputant came to him, would look in the Book of Allah. If he found therein a judgment between them, he would judge accordingly. And if he did not find it in the Book, but knew from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, a practice (sunnah) in that matter, he would judge accordingly. If he was perplexed, he would go out and ask the Muslims, saying: “Such and such came to me, do you know that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, judged in that with a judgment?” Sometimes a group would gather to him, all of them remembering a judgment from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in that matter. Then Abu Bakr would say: “Praise be to Allah who has placed among us those who preserve the teachings of our Prophet.” If he was perplexed to find a sunnah from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, he would gather the leaders of the people and their best, and consult them. And when their opinions converged on a matter, he would judge accordingly.

Ibrahim ibn Musa and Amr ibn Zurara narrated from Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad, from Abu Suheil, who said: My wife was obligated to perform an 'itkaf of three days in the Sacred Mosque. I asked Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and Ibn Shihab was with him. I said to him, "She is obligated to fast." Ibn Shihab said, "There is no 'itkaf except with fasting." Then Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to him, "Is this from the Prophet (peace be upon him)?" He said, "No." He said, "Is it from Abu Bakr?" He said, "No." He said, "Is it from Umar?" He said, "No." He said, "Is it from Uthman?" He said, "No." Umar said, "I do not see her obligated to fast." So I went out and found Tawus and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, and I asked them. Tawus said: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I do not see her obligated to fast unless she makes it upon herself." Ata' said, "That is my opinion."

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated: Abu ‘Akil narrated to me: Saeed al-Jurairi narrated to me from Abu Nadra, who said: When Abu Salama came to Basra, I went to him along with Hasan. He said to Hasan: "Are you Hasan? No one’s meeting in Basra was dearer to me than yours. That was because I had been informed that you give legal opinions based on your own reasoning. So do not give legal opinions based on your own reasoning unless there is a Sunna from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, or a revealed text."

"’Ikrama ibn al-Fadl narrated to me, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubaab narrated to me, from Yazid ibn ‘Uqba, who narrated to me, from Jaabir ibn Zayd, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar met him during the circumambulation (Tawaf) and said to him: “O father of the tangled hair, you are indeed among the jurists of Basra, so do not issue a legal opinion except based on a reciting Quran or a established Sunnah. For if you act other than that, you will perish and cause others to perish.”

"We have come upon a time when we neither judge nor are we there [in that state]. And Allah has decreed that we reach what you see. So whoever is presented with a judgment after today, let him judge according to what is in Allah’s Book. If he finds something not in Allah’s Book, let him judge according to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged. If he finds something not in Allah’s Book and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not judge, let him judge according to what the righteous have judged. And let him not say, ‘I fear,’ or ‘I see [it this way]’. For the forbidden is clear, and the lawful is clear, and between them are matters that are doubtful. So leave that which causes you doubt to that which does not cause you doubt."

"Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, that Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Ubaidullah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) would, when asked about a matter, if it was found in the Qur’an, he would relate it. And if it was not in the Qur’an but was from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), he would relate it. And if it was not, then he would relate it from Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them). And if it was not, then he would give his opinion regarding it."

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated from ‘Ali ibn Musahir from Abu Ishaq from Al-Sha’bi from Shurayh: That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to him: “If something comes to you that is in the Book of Allah, then judge by it and do not let people distract you from it. If something comes to you that is not in the Book of Allah, then look to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and judge by it. If something comes to you that is not in the Book of Allah and there is no Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) in it, then look to what the people have agreed upon and take that. If something comes to you that is not in the Book of Allah, and there is no Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) in it, and no one has spoken about it before you, then choose whichever of the two you wish: if you wish to strive with your opinion and then proceed, then proceed, and if you wish to delay, then delay, and I do not see anything but good for you in delaying.”

Narrated by Yahya bin Hammad, from Shu'bah, from Muhammad bin 'Ubaidullah ath-Thaqafi, from Al-Harith bin 'Amr bin brother of Al-Mughirah bin Shu'bah, from some people of Hims, companions of Mu'adh (RA), that Mu'adh (RA) said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he sent me to Yemen, said to me, 'How will you judge if a matter is brought before you that is not found in the Book?' I said: 'I will judge according to the Book of Allah.' He said: 'And if you do not find it in the Book of Allah?' I said: 'Then according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).’ He said: 'And if you do not find it in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?’ I said: 'Then I will strive with my opinion and spare no effort.' He struck my chest and said: 'Praise be to Allah, Who has guided the envoy of His envoy to that which pleases His Messenger.'"

“Narrated by Hurayth bin Zuraq: I think that ‘Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud) said, “Indeed, a time has come upon us when we are not asked [about matters], and we are not present [to answer]. And Allah has decreed that I reach the state you see [now]. So, when you are asked about something, look in the Book of Allah. If you do not find it in the Book of Allah, then look in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah. If you do not find it in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, then take what the Muslims have come to agree upon. If it is not in what the Muslims have come to agree upon, then exert your opinion, and do not say, ‘I fear and I dread.’ For the lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear, and between them are matters that are doubtful. So, leave what causes you doubt to what does not cause you doubt.”

Narrated Abdullah: "O people, you will innovate (new things) and things will be innovated for you. So, when you see an innovation, adhere to the original way." Hafs said: I used to transmit from Habib, from Abu Abdur-Rahman, then doubt entered me concerning it.
Umar said to Ibn Mas'ud: "Was I not informed, or am I being informed, that you issue legal opinions without being an official?" Appoint an overseer for its pastures for one who tends to its herds.
"Indeed, the one who gives legal opinions on everything people ask about is insane."

Hudayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Only three types of people give legal opinions to people: a leader or ruler, and a man who knows the abrogating verses of the Quran from the abrogated." They said: "O Hudayfah, and who is that?" He said: "‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, or a foolish pretender."

Hudhaifa (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “People are only given legal opinions by one of three: a man who knows the abrogating verses of the Quran from the abrogated, or a ruler who finds no alternative, or a foolish man who pretends to know.” They said: “And who is the first?” He said: “‘Umar ibn al-Khattab.” He said: “And a ruler who finds no alternative.” He said: “Or a foolish man who pretends to know.” Then Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: “I am not one of these two, and I hope I am not the third.”

"One of you who possesses knowledge, let him speak with it, and whoever does not possess knowledge, let him say, 'Allah knows,' for the scholar, when asked about what he does not know, says, 'Allah knows.' And Allah has said to His Messenger: 'Say, "I ask of you no reward for it, and I am not of those who speculate."' [Surah Sad, verse 86]"

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Abu Raja, from Abu Muheilab, that Abu Musa (RA) said in his sermon: "Whoever possesses knowledge, let him teach it to the people, and let him avoid saying that which he has no knowledge of, lest he fall out of the religion and become one of those who feign knowledge."
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “It cools my heart when I am asked about something I do not know, to say: ‘Allah knows best.’”
"It cools the liver to say, when one does not know, 'Allah knows best.'"

Narrated ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said: "If you are asked about something you do not know, then flee (from answering)." They said: "How can we flee, O Commander of the Believers?" He said: "You say: 'Allah knows best.'"

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Say, ‘How cool is it upon the liver,’ three times.” They said, “And what is that, O Commander of the Believers?” He said, “That a man is questioned about what he does not know, and he says, ‘Allah knows best.’”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: A man asked him a question, and he said, “I have no knowledge of it.” When the man turned away, Ibn ‘Umar said, “Ibn ‘Umar spoke well. He was asked about something he did not know, so he said, ‘I have no knowledge of it.’”
Yahiya ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Abu ‘Awana narrated to me from Mughira from Al-Sha’bi, who said: "I do not know half of the knowledge."

Abdullah ibn Maslama narrated to us on the authority of Abdullah al-Umari, from Naafi’, that a man came to Ibn Umar asking him about something. He (Ibn Umar) said, “I have no knowledge.” Then, after the man had left, he turned and said, “Excellent was what Ibn Umar said! He was asked about something he did not know, so he said, ‘I have no knowledge.’” Meaning, Ibn Umar himself.

Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Jarir narrated to me from Mughira, who said: "‘Amir, when asked about something, would say, ‘I do not know.’ If he were challenged, he would say: ‘If you wish, I would swear by Allah that I possessed knowledge of it, if I did.’”

Harun ibn Muawiyah narrated to me from Hafs, from Ash’ath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "I do not mind whether I am asked about what I know or what I do not know, for if I am asked about what I know, I say what I know, and if I am asked about what I do not know, I say: I do not know."
Harun narrated to me from Hafs, from Al-A'mash, who said: "I never heard Ibrahim say 'halal' or 'haram.' Rather, he would say, 'They disliked it, and they favored it.'"

Yala narrated to me, and al-A'mash narrated to me from Shaqiq, who said: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: "How will you be when trials befall you wherein the elderly become senile and the young grow bold, and the people take them as a tradition? Then, when it is altered, they say, 'The Sunnah has been altered.'" They said: "When will that be, O Abu Abdur-Rahman?" He said: "When your reciters become numerous and your scholars become few, and your rulers become numerous and your trustworthy ones become few, and the world is sought through actions meant for the Hereafter."

Abdullah (RA) said: "How will you be when a trial (fitna) befalls you wherein the elderly become feeble and the young grow bold? When something is left from it, they say, 'The Sunnah has been abandoned.'" They said, "When will that be?" He said, "When your scholars disappear, and ignorance increases, and reciters (of the Quran) become numerous, and jurists (fuqaha) become few, and rulers become abundant, and trustworthy ones become scarce, and the world is sought through actions meant for the Hereafter, and instruction is given for something other than religion."
I was informed that it was said: "Woe to those who acquire knowledge other than for the sake of worship, and those who permit what is forbidden through flimsy excuses."

"Do not pass a year upon you but it is worse than the one before it. I do not mean a year more fertile than another, nor a ruler better than another, but rather your scholars, your best people, and your jurists disappear, and you will not find a replacement for them, and there will come a people who judge matters based on their own opinions."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khallaf narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to me, saying: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind from Ibn Sirin, who said: "The first to measure [things], and the sun and moon were not worshipped except through measurement."

Narrated on the authority of Hasan that he recited this verse: "I was created from fire, and he was created from clay." (Surah Al-A’raf, verse 12) He said: “Iblis was defiant, and he was the first to be defiant.”
"I fear, or I dread, that I will measure [things], and my foot will slip."
"By Allah, if you adhere to measurements [literal calculations] alone, you will certainly forbid what is lawful and permit what is unlawful."

Al-Hasan ibn Bishr narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from Isma'il, from 'Amir, that he said: "Nothing displeased me more than seeing someone ask, 'Did you see?' and 'Did you see?' and he did not reason or make comparisons."
Sadqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me from al-Zubriqan who said: Abu Wail forbade me from sitting with the people of 'Ara'it.

Sadqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to me, and Ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, from Ismail, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "If these people had been upon the covenant of the Prophet, peace be upon him, the entire Quran would have been revealed [to them], asking you, asking you."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, and Muhammad, who is Ibn Talha, narrated to me, from Maymun Abu Hamza, who said: Ibrahim said to me, "O Abu Hamza, by Allah, I have spoken, and if I had found a way out, I would not have spoken. And indeed, a time when I am the jurist of the people of Kufa will be a time of adversity."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Beware of equivocation (or prevarication) in speech."

Hajjaj of Basra narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudali narrated to me from al-Sha'bi, who said: "I witnessed Sharh, and a man came to him from Murad and said: O Abu Umayya, what is the diyya (blood money) for the fingers? He said: Ten, ten. He said: Glory be to Allah, are these (two fingers) worse than these? He gathered the little finger and the thumb together. Sharh said: Glory be to Allah, is your ear worse than your hand? For the ear is covered by hair, a head covering, and a turban, which is half the diyya, and in the hand is half the diyya. Woe to you, the sunna preceded your qiyas (analogical reasoning), so follow and do not innovate. You will never be misguided as long as you adhere to the sunna. Abu Bakr said: Then al-Sha'bi said to me: O Hudali, if the most upright among you were killed and this boy was in his cradle, would their diyya be equal? I said: Yes. He said: So where is the qiyas?"

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated: Saeed narrated to us from Rabiah ibn Yazid, who said: Mu’adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Qur'an will be opened to the people until a woman, a child, and a man read it. Then a man will say: ‘I have recited the Qur'an, but I have not been followed.’ By Allah, I will certainly act upon it among them, perhaps I will be followed.’ So he acts upon it among them, but he is not followed. Then he says: ‘I have recited the Qur'an, but I have not been followed, and I have acted upon it among them, but I have not been followed.’ By Allah, I will certainly establish a mosque in my house, perhaps I will be followed.’ So he establishes a mosque in his house, but he is not followed. Then he says: ‘I have recited the Qur'an, but I have not been followed, and I have acted upon it among them, but I have not been followed, and I have established a mosque in my house, but I have not been followed.’ By Allah, I will certainly come to them with a narration that they do not find in the Book of Allah and they have not heard from the Messenger of Allah, perhaps I will be followed.’ Mu’adh said: ‘So beware of what comes to them with it, for what comes to them with it is misguidance.’”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me: Malik, who is ibn Mughul, said: Ash-Sha'bi said to me: "Whatever these people relate to you from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, accept it. And whatever they say based on their own opinion, cast it into the husk."

Al-Abbas ibn Sufyan narrated to me from Zayd ibn Hubab, who narrated to me from Raja’ ibn Abi Salama, who said: I heard ‘Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah saying: "I am content with the people of my time that they do not ask me and I do not ask them. Rather, one of them says, ‘Do you see? Do you see?’”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, drew a line for us one day, and said, "This is the way of Allah." Then he drew lines to his right and to his left, and said, "These are paths, and on every path is Satan calling to it." Then he recited: "And indeed, this is my straight path, so follow it, and do not follow the ways [that lead you] astray from His path, that you may not go astray." [Surah Al-An'am, verse 153]

Narrated from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, he said: Warqa’ narrated to us from Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid concerning: #And do not follow the ways [of those who reject faith] - (Surah Al-An’am, verse 153) #, he said: "Innovations and ambiguities."

We used to sit at the door of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud (RA) before Fajr prayer. When he would come out, we would walk with him to the mosque. Then Abu Musa al-Ash’ari (RA) came and said, “Has Abu Abdur-Rahman (Abdullah ibn Mas’ud) come out yet?” We said, “No,” so he sat with us until he came out. When he came out, we all went to him, and Abu Musa said to him, “O Abu Abdur-Rahman, I saw something in the mosque that I disliked, and praise be to Allah, I have not seen anything but good.” He said, “What was it?” He said, “I saw people sitting in groups, waiting for the prayer, with a man in each group. They had pebbles in their hands, and one would say, ‘Say Allahu Akbar one hundred times,’ and they would say it one hundred times. Then he would say, ‘Say La ilaha illallah one hundred times,’ and they would say it one hundred times. And he would say, ‘Say Subhanallah one hundred times,’ and they would say it one hundred times.” He said, “What did you say to them?” He said, “I did not say anything to them, waiting for your opinion or your command.” He said, “Should you not have ordered them to count their sins, and guaranteed them that nothing would be deducted from their good deeds?” Then he left, and we left with him until he came to one of those groups. He stopped before them and said, “What is this that I see you doing?” They said, “O Abu Abdur-Rahman, we are counting with these pebbles the Takbir, the Tahleel, and the Tasbeeh.” He said, “Then count your sins, and I guarantee that nothing will be deducted from your good deeds. Woe to you, O community of Muhammad! How quickly you are perishing! These are the companions of your Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), abundant and present. These are his clothes, not worn out, and his utensils, not broken. By the One in whose hand is my soul, you are on a path that is more guided than the path of Muhammad, or you are openers of the door of misguidance.” They said, “By Allah, O Abu Abdur-Rahman, we intended nothing but good.” He said, “How many are those who intend good but do not attain it? Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) told us about people who recite the Qur’an, but it does not pass their throats. By Allah, I do not know, but perhaps most of them are among you.” Then he turned away from them. Amr ibn Salama said, “We saw most of those groups fighting against us on the Day of Nahrwan with the Kharijites.”
Narrated by Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him): He said, "Follow (the Sunnah), and do not innovate, for you have been granted sufficiency."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon to us, praised Allah, and spoke highly of Him. Then he said: “The best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad ﷺ, and the worst of matters are newly invented ones, and every innovation is a misguidance.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas’ud (RA): He would say when Thursday evening came, the night of Jumu’ah, “Indeed, the truest speech is the speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The wretched one is he who is wretched in his mother’s womb, and the worst of narrations is the narration of falsehood. The worst of affairs are newly invented matters, and everything that is to come is near.”
Muhammad ibn 'Uyaynah told me from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Layth, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said, "No man takes up an innovation and then turns to the Sunnah."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "I only fear for my community the misleading scholars."

Narrated Hayya bint Abi Hiyya: A man came to us in the afternoon, and I said to him, "O Abdullah, from where have you come?” He said, “I came with a companion of mine seeking amusement. My companion went off to seek amusement, and I entered to seek shade and drink something. I got up to a sour lemon (or a sour grape), and I gave him to drink from it, and he drank, and I drank.” She said, “Then I recognized him and said, ‘O Abdullah, who are you?’ He said, ‘I am Abu Bakr.’ I said, ‘Are you Abu Bakr, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), about whom I have heard?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ She said, “Then I remembered our campaign against the Banu Khuza’a and our fighting against each other in the pre-Islamic period. Then Allah brought about brotherhood and extended tents, and Ibn ‘Awn interlocked his fingers, and Mu’adh described him to us, and Ahmad interlocked his fingers, and I said, ‘O Abdullah, how long will you see the affairs of the people like this?’ He said, ‘As long as the Imams are not upright.’ I said, ‘What are the Imams?’ He said, ‘Do you not see how the leader is in the open space and they follow him and obey him? They are not upright as long as that is the case.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the thing I fear most for you is misleading leaders."

Abu Nu'man narrated: Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Bayan ibn Bishr from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, visited a woman from the tribe of ‘Ahmas whose name was Zaynab. He saw that she was not speaking, so he said: "What is the reason she does not speak?" They said: "She intended to perform a silent pilgrimage (Hajj)." He said to her: "Speak, for this is not permissible; this is from the practices of pre-Islamic ignorance." So she spoke and said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am a migrant (Muhajir)." She said: "From which of the migrants?" He said: "From Quraysh." She said: "From which of Quraysh are you?" He said: "You are asking a lot of questions. I am Abu Bakr." She said: "How long will we remain on this righteous matter that Allah brought after the age of ignorance?" He said: "Your remaining on it is as long as your leaders are upright." She said: "And who are the leaders?" He said: "Did your people not have leaders and nobles who would command them and they would obey them?" She said: "Yes." He said: "They are like those among the people."

Narrated ‘A’idhah: I saw Ibn Mas’ud advising men and women, saying: “Whoever of you – whether a woman or a man – attains the first practice (of Islam), then you are upon the natural disposition (fitrah).” Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud) said: “The first practice is the way (or path).”

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me, he said: ‘Ali, who is the son of Musahir, narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Sha’bi, from Ziyad ibn Hudair, who said: ‘Umar said to me, “Do you know what destroys Islam?” I said, “No.” He said: “The lapse of a scholar, the argument of a hypocrite with the Book, and the ruling of misleading leaders.”
Do not sit with those who engage in arguments, for they delve into the verses of Allah.

By the One who is free from all partners, your tradition is between the extremist and the overly harsh, so persevere upon it, may Allah have mercy on you. Indeed, the people of the Sunnah were the fewest of people in the past, and they are the fewest of people who remain: those who did not go along with the people of boastfulness in their boastfulness, nor with the people of innovation in their innovations, and they patiently adhered to their tradition until they met their Lord. So may it be that you are like that, if Allah wills.
Moderation in adherence to the Sunnah is better than diligent innovation.

I have witnessed people such that if one of them did not surpass a single fingertip [in piety], I would not surpass him, for it is sufficient disgrace for a people that their actions are contradicted.

Narrated Ya’li: He said, “Allah and His Messenger should be obeyed, and those in authority among you. [Surah An-Nisa, 59]” He (the Prophet) said: “Those possessing knowledge and understanding, and obedience to the Messenger, are following the Book and the Sunnah.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Adham narrated to me: I asked Ibn Shubrumah about something, and I had a difficult question. I said to him: May Allah have mercy on you, look into it. He said: "If the path becomes clear to me, and I find the trace, I will not delay."

Ibn Mas’ud said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: "Learn knowledge and teach it to the people, learn the rulings [of Islamic law] and teach them to the people, learn the Qur’an and teach it to the people. For I am a Messenger whose time has been decreed, and knowledge will diminish, and trials will appear until two people disagree over a ruling and find no one to resolve their dispute."

Yaqoob ibn Ibrahim narrated to us on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Abi Khalifa, who said: I heard Ziyad ibn Mihraq mention, from Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Mu’adh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa to Yemen. He said: "Support each other and cooperate, and give good news and do not deter (people)." So they went to Yemen, and Mu’adh addressed the people and encouraged them to embrace Islam, and ordered them to study the Quran. He said: "If you do that, then ask me, and I will tell you about the people of Paradise from the people of Hell.” They stayed as long as Allah willed them to stay, then they said to Mu’adh: “You ordered us, if we study and recite, to ask you, and you would tell us about the people of Paradise from the people of Hell.” Mu’adh said to them: “When a person is mentioned with good, then he is from the people of Paradise, and when he is mentioned with evil, then he is from the people of Hell.”

Narrated Abu Huraira (RA) that he said, "Someone asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, who among the people is the most noble?' He (the Prophet) said: 'The most pious.' They said: 'Not what we are asking you.' He (the Prophet) said: 'Then Joseph, son of Jacob, a prophet of Allah, son of a prophet of Allah, son of a friend of Allah.' They said: 'Not what we are asking you.' He (the Prophet) said: 'Are you asking about the origins of the Arabs? The best of them in the pre-Islamic period are the best of them in Islam, if they understand (the religion).'"

Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: "Whoever Allah intends good for, He grants him understanding in the religion."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever Allah intends good for, He grants him understanding in the religion."
He (the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever Allah intends good for, He grants him understanding in the religion."

Narrated by Abu Huraira: He witnessed the Khutbah (sermon) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of ‘Arafah in the Farewell Hajj: “O people! By Allah, I do not know if I will ever meet you again at this place after this day. May Allah have mercy on whoever hears my words today and understands them, for there are those who carry knowledge but have no understanding, and there are those who carry knowledge to one who is more knowledgeable than him. And know that your wealth and blood are forbidden to you, just as this day, this month, and this city are sacred. And know that hearts do not harbor ill-will towards three things: sincerity in work for Allah, advising those in authority, and adhering to the community of Muslims, for their support surrounds them.”

Narrated by his father: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at al-Khiif in Mina and said: “May Allah bless a servant who hears my words, understands them, and then conveys them to one who did not hear them. There are bearers of knowledge who have no knowledge themselves, and bearers of knowledge to those who are more knowledgeable than they. Three things the heart of a believer does not harbor resentment towards: sincerity in the work for Allah, obedience to those in authority, and adhering to the community. Their invocation is made for them [by those who follow them].”

Zayd ibn Thabit left the presence of Marwan ibn al-Hakam midway through the day. I said, “He does not leave the presence of Marwan at this hour except after he has asked him about something.” So I went to him and asked, and he said, “Yes, he asked me about a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: ‘May Allah bless a man who hears a hadith from us and preserves it, then conveys it to one who is more capable of preserving it than he is. For there are carriers of knowledge who are not scholars, and there are carriers of knowledge who convey it to one more discerning than they are. Whoever’s heart does not hold firm to three qualities, then Paradise does not enter him.’” I said, “What are they?” He said, “Sincerity in work for Allah, advice to those in authority, and adherence to the community. For their call surrounds them from behind. Whoever makes the Hereafter his intention, Allah will make wealth in his heart, reunite his affairs, and the world will come to him submissive. And whoever makes the world his intention, Allah will scatter his affairs and make poverty before his eyes, and he will not obtain from the world except what is decreed for him.” I asked him about the middle prayer, and he said, “It is the Zuhr prayer.”

Narrated Abu ad-Darda’: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon to us and said: “May Allah brighten the face of a man who hears something from me and conveys it as he heard it. Often, a conveyer understands better than the listener. Three things will not make the heart of a Muslim feel resentment: sincerity in work for Allah, giving sincere advice to every Muslim, and adhering to the Muslim community, for their supplication encompasses them from behind.”
One who deliberately fabricates against me, let him take his seat in the Fire.
One who deliberately fabricates against me, let him take his seat in the Fire.
One who deliberately fabricates a story about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.
One who deliberately fabricates against me, let him take his seat in the Fire.

Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If I did not fear error, I would relate to you things I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, or things the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said. That is because I heard him, peace and blessings be upon him, say: 'Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.'"
One who deliberately tells a lie against me, let him take his seat in the Fire.

Narrated Abu Qatada (RA): I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying on the pulpit: “O people, beware of excessive talk about me. Whoever speaks about me, let him say only the truth or sincerity. And whoever says about me what I have not said, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever deliberately fabricates a lie against me, let him take his seat in the Fire."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Indeed, Allah does not take away knowledge by seizing it from the people, but rather He takes away knowledge with the passing away of the scholars. So, when He does not leave any scholar, the people choose ignorant leaders, and they are asked questions about which they give verdicts without knowledge, and thus they go astray and lead others astray.”

Narrated Abu Umama, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Acquire knowledge before it disappears." They said: "How does knowledge disappear, O Messenger of Allah, while the Book of Allah is among us?" He became angry and said: "May your mothers be bereaved! Did not the Torah and the Gospel disappear from the Children of Israel, and they availed them nothing? Indeed, the disappearance of knowledge is when its carriers disappear. Indeed, the disappearance of knowledge is when its carriers disappear."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to me, saying: Hilal, who is the son of Khabbab, said: I asked Saeed ibn Jubair, and I said to him: O Abu Abdullah, what is the sign of the destruction of the people? He said: "When their scholars die."

"People will continue to be well as long as the earlier ones teach the later ones, or the later ones learn from the earlier ones. But if the earlier ones die before teaching or the later ones learn, then people will perish."
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Do you know what the disappearance of knowledge is?" They said, "No." He said: "The disappearance of the scholars."

Hudayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Do you know how knowledge diminishes?” I said: “Like dust being shaken off a garment, and like a dirham becoming hardened.” He said: “No, and that is from Allah. The diminishing of knowledge is the passing away of scholars.”

Abu ad-Darda’ reported that he said: “Why do I see your scholars disappearing and your ignorant ones not learning? So learn before knowledge vanishes, for the vanishing of knowledge is the disappearance of scholars.”
Narrated Abu ad-Darda’: “The people are of two categories: a knower and a learner, and there is no good in anyone beyond that.”
The one who teaches good and the one who learns it are equal in reward, and after them, there is no good for anyone.
"Set out as a scholar, or a student, or a listener, and do not be the fourth, lest you perish."

Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “People will continue to be in goodness as long as the earlier generations teach the later ones. But if the earlier generations die before the later ones learn from them, then people will perish.”
'Umar said: "Seek knowledge before you are given authority."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, Sufyan ibn Rustam narrated to me, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Maisara, from Tamim ad-Dari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The people lengthened in building during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. So Umar said: ‘O tribe of Arabs, the earth, the earth! There is no Islam except with a community, and no community except with an Imamate, and no Imamate except with obedience. Whoever a people elevate due to their understanding, he is a source of life for them, and whoever a people elevate without understanding, he is a source of ruin for them.’”

Allah the Exalted said: “I do not accept every word of the wise man, but I accept his concern and desire. If his concern and desire are in obedience to Me, then I make his silence praise of Me and reverence. And if it is not.”

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated that Allah said: "I will disseminate knowledge in the latter days until a man and a woman, a slave and a free person, a young one and an old one acquire it; and when I do that for them, I will take them to account for My right upon them."

One who seeks something of this knowledge and intends thereby what is with Allah, he may attain it if Allah wills, and one who seeks it for the sake of the world, then by Allah, that is his portion of it.

Ibn Mas’ud said: “Do not seek knowledge for three reasons: to contend with the ignorant, to argue with scholars, and to turn people’s faces towards yourselves. Rather, seek it for what is with Allah, for that will endure and remain, and what is other than that will perish.”

"With this chain of narration, he said: "Be springs of knowledge, lamps of guidance, inhabitants of homes, lamps of the night, renewers of hearts, adornments of garments, known among the people of the heavens, and concealed from the people of the earth."
"None seeks this knowledge intending thereby only the world, but Allah will forbid him from the scent of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection."
The man said to al-Sha'bi: "Advise me, O scholar." He said: "The scholar is one who fears Allah."

Learn knowledge, so you may be known for it, and act upon it, so you may be among its people. Indeed, a time will come after this one in which nineteen out of every twenty will be ignorant of what is right, and none will survive it except every heedless one. These are the leaders of guidance and the lamps of knowledge; they are not those who spread rumors, nor those who scatter falsehood.
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Act as you wish after you have knowledge, for Allah, the Exalted, will not reward you for knowledge until you act upon it."

Sa'd came to Ibn Munabbih and asked him about Hasan, and asked him, "What is his intellect like?" He informed him, then said, "Indeed, we relate or find in the books that: 'God, may He be glorified and exalted, does not grant a servant knowledge and he acts upon it as a means of guidance, but He takes away his intellect until He reclaims it.'"
"Among the people who have the worst position with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is a scholar who does not benefit from his knowledge."

Abu ad-Darda’ said, "Whoever increases in knowledge, increases in grief." He reported and said, "I fear for myself not that they will say to me, 'What did you know?', but I fear that they will say to me, 'What did you do?'"

I have heard Ibn Jurayj relate, from someone who reported to him, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "An hour of studying knowledge during the night is better than spending the entire night awake."

Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I divide the night into three parts: a third for sleep, a third for prayer, and a third for remembering the sayings of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
One who seeks knowledge intending thereby to seek the countenance of Allah, the Exalted, Allah will grant him sufficiency from it.

I asked al-Sha'bi about a hadith, and he narrated it to me. Then I said, "Indeed, it is raised to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him." He said, "No, those below the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, are more beloved to us. If there is an addition or a deficiency in it, then it is upon those below the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him."

Narrated Ishaq bin Iyas: Hammad bin Zayd narrated to me from Abu Hashim from Ibrahim who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade Muhāqalah and Muzābanah.” It was said to him, “Do you not recall any other Hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besides this one?” He said, “Yes, but I say: Abdullah said: Alqamah said, ‘What is dearest to me.’”

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me from Al-Awza’i, from Ismail ibn ‘Ubaidullah, who said: Abu ad-Darda’ would, when relating a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), say: "This or something similar to it, or resembling it, or its form."
Abu ad-Darda’ (may Allah be pleased with him) would, when relating a narration, say: "O Allah, except in this manner, or resembling it."

I used to never miss Thursday evenings without visiting Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and I never heard him attribute anything to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, until one evening when he said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said…” Then his eyes welled up and his jugular veins swelled, and I saw his tunic unbuttoned, and he said something similar, or nearly so, or something like that.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Ash'ath narrated to me, from Al-Sha'bi and Ibn Sirin, that Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, would, when he narrated from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, his face would redden, and he would say: "Like this or something similar to this, like this or something similar to this."

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Tawbah al-'Anbari narrated to me, saying: Al-Sha'bi said to me: "Do you know the man who says, 'The Messenger of Allah said,' 'The Messenger of Allah said'?" I sat with Ibn Umar for two years, or a year and a half, and I never heard him relate anything from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, except this narration.
I was with Ibn Umar for a year, and I did not hear him mention a single narration from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.
'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) would relate to us in the month two or three hadiths.
Anas ibn Malik passed by us, and we said, "Recite to us some of that which you heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." He said, "And I purify myself."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ibn ‘Awn from Muhammad, who said: Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). And whenever he narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), he would say: "Or as the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said."

Narrated Anas: He narrated a Hadith from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he said, "Or as the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa’id, who said: Sa’ib ibn Yazid told me: “I set out with Sa’d [ibn Abi Waqqas] may Allah be pleased with him, to Mecca. I did not hear him relate a single narration from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) until we returned to Medina.”

Umar (RA) accompanied the Ansar when they set out from Medina and said, "Do you know why I accompanied you?" They said, "Because of the right of the Ansar." He said, "Indeed, you are going to a people whose tongues tremble with the Quran like the trembling of date palms. So, do not deter them from the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and I am your partner in this." He said, "So, I did not relate anything, although I had heard as much as my companions had heard.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Ash’ath ibn Sawwar narrated to me, from Al-Sha’bi, from Qurazah ibn Ka’b, who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) sent a group of the Ansar to Al-Kufa. He sent me with them. He kept walking with us until we reached Sirar. Sirar is a watering place on the road to Medina. He began to shake the dust off his feet, and then said: “You will come to Kufa, and you will come to a people who recite the Quran with a buzz. They will come to you and say: ‘The companions of Muhammad have arrived! The companions of Muhammad have arrived!’ They will come to you and ask you about hadith. So know that the most complete ablution is three [washes], and two suffice. Then he said: ‘You will come to Kufa, and you will come to a people who recite the Quran with a buzz. They will say: ‘The companions of Muhammad have arrived! The companions of Muhammad have arrived!’ They will come to you and ask you about hadith. So reduce the narration from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and I am a partner with you in it.” Qurazah said: “I used to sit among the people, and they would mention hadith from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and I was among the best of them in memorizing it. But when I remembered Umar’s command (may Allah be pleased with him), I would fall silent.” Abu Muhammad said: “Its meaning to me is that hadith refers to the events of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), not the sunnah and rulings.”
Narrated Abdullah (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and then he trembled, and then he said something to that effect or even more than that.

Bishr ibn al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, who said: I accompanied Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) to Medina, and I did not hear him relate any narration from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), except that he said: I was with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when a juniper was brought to him, and he said: "Indeed, among the trees there is a tree like a Muslim man.” I wanted to say: ‘It is the date palm,’ but I looked and found myself the youngest of the people, so I remained silent. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I wished you had said it, and I would have said so.
Salih the Dyer said: I have never heard Jabir ibn Zayd say that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "Out of reverence and fear of speaking falsely about me."

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) came to Ka'b asking about him, and Ka'b was among a group of people. Ka'b said, "What do you want from him?" He said, "Indeed, I do not know anyone among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who is more attentive to his narrations than I am." Ka'b said, "Indeed, you will not find a seeker of anything but that he will be satisfied with it one day, except for a seeker of knowledge or a seeker of the world.” He said, "Are you Ka'b?" He said, "Yes." He said, "I have come to you for something like this."

It was narrated to me by Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, who said: Malik narrated to me, that Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to me, that Shibl narrated to me, from Amr ibn Dinār, from Tawus, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who among the people is most knowledgeable?" He said: "He who gathers the knowledge of the people to his own knowledge, and every seeker of knowledge is thirsty for knowledge."

Narrated ‘Abid ibn ‘Amr: I was sitting in a gathering with some elderly people who were engaged in conversation. A young man in a corner of the gathering said, “O people, devote yourselves to the remembrance of Allah, may Allah bless you.” The people looked at each other, wondering what they had seen. Then one of them said, “Who ordered you to say this?” The young man replied, “No one ordered me.” They said, “If you repeat this, we will do something to you.”
Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What an excellent assembly is one in which wisdom is disseminated and mercy is hoped for."

We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he looked towards the sky, then said: “This is the time when knowledge is stolen from people, so they will not be able to obtain anything from it.” Then Ziyad ibn Labid al-Ansari said: “O Messenger of Allah, how can it be stolen from us when we have recited the Quran?” He said: “By Allah, we will recite it and teach it to our women and children.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May your mother be orphaned, O Ziyad! I considered you among the scholars of Medina. This Torah and Gospel are with the Jews and Christians, so what benefit do they derive from them?” Jubair said: “I met Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and I said to him, ‘Do you not hear what your brother Abu Dardaa says?’ So I informed him of what he had said. He said: ‘Abu Dardaa has spoken the truth. If you wish, I will tell you about the first knowledge to be taken away from people: reverence (khushu’) – it will soon come about that you enter a mosque of congregation and not see a single reverent person in it.”

Yaqoob ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Al-Walid ibn Jamil Al-Kitani narrated to me, saying: Makhool said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The superiority of the scholar over the worshiper is like my superiority over the lowest among you." Then he recited the verse: "Only those who fear Allah among His servants are the scholars." [Surah Fatir, 35:28]. Then he said: "Indeed, Allah and His angels, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and the whales in the sea, send blessings upon those who teach people good."
"A man will not be a scholar until he does not envy those above him in knowledge, nor despise those below him, and does not seek a price for his knowledge."

Said Saeed bin Sulaiman, from Abu Usama, from Mis’ar, that he heard ‘Abd al-A’la at-Taymi say: "Whoever is granted knowledge that does not make him weep, then it is fitting that he not have been granted knowledge that benefits him, for Allah the Exalted described the scholars, and then recited: 'Indeed, those who have been given knowledge [from their Lord] know that you are speaking the truth...' to the end of the verse [17:107-109] in Surah Isra'."
Do not be a scholar until you possess three qualities: do not act arrogantly towards those above you, do not despise those below you, and do not sell your knowledge for worldly gain.

Do not be a scholar until you are a student, and do not be considered a scholar with knowledge until you act upon it. It is sufficient for you as a sin to remain an arguer, and it is sufficient for you as a sin to remain one who practices contention. And it is sufficient for you to be a liar if you constantly speak about things other than Allah.

I said to Hasan one day regarding something he said, "O Abu Saeed, the scholars do not say it like this." He said, "Woe to you! Have you ever considered yourself a scholar? Indeed, the scholar is one who is detached from the world and eager for the Hereafter, who possesses insight into the matter of his religion, and who perseveres in the worship of his Lord."
He said, "He was asked, 'Who is the most discerning of the people of Medina?' He replied, 'The most God-fearing of them to his Lord.'"
The learned one is only he who fears Allah, the Exalted.

"The true scholar is he who does not despair the people of Allah’s mercy, nor does he make permissible for them Allah’s disobedience, nor does he feel secure from Allah’s punishment, and who does not leave the Quran as a neglected thing for something else. Indeed, there is no good in worship devoid of knowledge, nor knowledge devoid of understanding, nor recitation devoid of reflection."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The true scholar is one who does not despair the people of Allah’s mercy, nor assure them against Allah’s punishment, nor permit them to commit sins against Allah. Indeed, there is no good in worship devoid of knowledge, nor in knowledge devoid of understanding, nor in reading devoid of contemplation."

"I found the description of a people who learn for other than acting upon [what they learn], and acquire religious knowledge for other than worship, and seek this world with the deeds of the Hereafter, and they wear the skins of sheep, but their hearts are more bitter than wormwood. By [Allah], I have sworn that I will grant them a trial in which the most patient will be perplexed."

Narrated by Harim ibn Hayyan: He said, "Beware of the corrupt scholar. It reached Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), so he wrote to him and feared it. He asked, 'What is a corrupt scholar?' Harim wrote to him: 'O Commander of the Believers, by Allah, I did not intend anything but good. It is someone who is an Imam (leader) who speaks with knowledge but acts with corruption, thus confusing people and leading them astray."
"One who desires that his religion be honored, let him not enter the presence of a ruler, nor be alone with women, and let him not argue with people of whims and desires."

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Ismail ibn Ibrahim from Yunus who said: Maymun ibn Mihran wrote to me: "Beware of argumentation and disputation regarding religious matters. Do not argue with a scholar, nor with an ignorant person. As for the scholar, he will withhold his knowledge from you and will not care about what you do. And as for the ignorant person, he will harden your heart and will not obey you."
Sulayman (peace be upon him) said to his son: "Avoid argumentation, for its benefit is little, and it incites animosity among brothers."

He narrated to me, Yahya ibn Hassan, that Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to me, from Ismail ibn Abi Hakim, who said: I heard Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz say: "Whoever makes his religion a target for arguments, will travel much."

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Saeed ibn Abdul-Aziz told me that Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz wrote to the people of Medina: "Indeed, whoever practices devotion without knowledge, his corruption outweighs his reform. And whoever considers his speech as part of his actions, his speech will be little except for that which concerns him. And whoever makes his religion a target for arguments, his shifting will be frequent."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Ja’far ibn Burqan, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: A man asked him about something pertaining to desire, so he said to him: "Adhere to the religion of the Arab Bedouin and the boy learning to write. Abandon everything else besides that." Abu Muhammad said: He was excessively shifting, meaning: he shifts from one opinion to another.
Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "If you see a people innovating something without the consensus of the generality [of Muslims], then they are establishing misguidance."

Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Awza’i, who said: "Iblis said to his allies: From what do you come to the children of Adam? They replied: From everything. He said: Do you come to them from the side of seeking forgiveness? They said: No! That is something linked to Tawhid (monotheism). He said: I will surely sow among them something that they will not seek forgiveness from Allah for. He then sowed among them desires."
Mujahid said, "I do not know which of two blessings is greater upon me: that He guided me to Islam, or that He spared me from these desires."

"Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'If a man were to fast for all of his life and stand in prayer for all of his life, and then be killed between the pillar and the station [of circumambulation in the Ka'bah], Allah would resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection with those who believe they were upon guidance.'"

Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If a man were to place his head upon the Black Stone, fast the days, and stand [in prayer] the nights, Allah would resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection with his desire."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Be among the people like the bee among birds: there is nothing of the birds but they weaken it, and if the birds knew what was in its belly of blessing, they would not do that to it. Mix with people with your tongues and bodies, and distance yourselves from them with your actions and hearts. Indeed, a person has what he has earned, and he will be on the Day of Resurrection with those he loves."
Al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to me from Al-Awza'i, from Zuhri, who said: "Sound judgment is an excellent minister for knowledge."

It is sufficient for a person to be knowledgeable that he fears Allah, and it is sufficient for a person to be ignorant that he is pleased with his own knowledge. Masruq said: A person is deserving to have gatherings where he secludes himself, so that he remembers his sins and seeks forgiveness from Allah the Exalted.
"If we relate to you a hadith conveying its meaning, that is sufficient for you."

'Aasim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us from Hisham from Ibn Sirin: "That whenever he narrated, he did not anticipate nor delay. And Hasan, whenever he narrated, would anticipate and delay."
Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, and Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: "Hasan used to relate the Hadith from a single original source, but the wording would vary."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “The example of a hypocrite is like a sheep between two flocks.” Then Ibn ‘Umar said: “No, he said so and so.” And Ibn ‘Umar would, when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ), not add to it, nor diminish from it, nor exceed it, nor curtail it.

Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me, that Ibn Ulayyah narrated to me, from Ibn ‘Awn, that: Al-Sha’bi, An-Nakha’i, and Al-Hasan would relate a narration sometimes in this manner, and sometimes in that manner. I mentioned this to Muhammad ibn Sirin, and he said: “Indeed, if they had related it as they heard it, it would have been better for them.”
"I would hear a Hadith with a flaw in it, and I would err in following it, due to what I heard."

Mujahid saw Tawus in a dream, as if he were in the Ka'bah praying, veiled. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was at the door of the Ka'bah, and he said to him, "O Abdullah, uncover your veil and display your recitation." He said, "So it seemed as if he interpreted it for him as knowledge," and thereafter he expanded in the narration (of Hadith).
The world is cursed, and everything in it is cursed, except for one who learns good or teaches it.
Narrated by Khalid ibn Ma'dan: "People are either knowledgeable, or learners, or between the two; and those beyond that are savages in whom there is no good."

Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Hakam, who said: Muhammad ibn Rafi’ narrated to us from Hisham from Hasan who said: They used to say, "The death of a scholar is a void in Islam which nothing can fill as long as the night and day alternate."
"A gathering where knowledge is debated is more beloved to me than performing a prayer, for perhaps one of them may hear a word and benefit from it for a year, or whatever remains of his life."

Yaqoob ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, and Waqi’ narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: “I do not know of any work superior to seeking knowledge and preserving it for one whom Allah intends to do good.” And he said: Hasan ibn Salih said: “Verily, people need this knowledge in their religion, just as they need food and drink in their worldly lives.”

Abu ad-Darda’ reported: “Learn knowledge before it is taken away, for the taking away of knowledge is the taking away of scholars, and the scholar and the one who seeks knowledge are equal in reward.”
But be devout scholars in accordance with what you teach of the Book [Quran], [Surah Al-Imran, verse 79]. He [the Prophet] said: "It is incumbent upon every reader of the Quran to be a scholar."
Harun ibn Muawiyah narrated to me from Hafs, from Ash’ath ibn Sawwar, from Hasan: Reciting Surah Al-Ma’idah, verse 63, he said, "The wise are the scholars."
Narrated by Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from ‘Ata’ ibn as-Sa’ib, from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said, quoting [Quran 3:79], “Be devout scholars,” he said, “Scholars who are jurists.”
"ʿUbaydullah ibn Saʿīd narrated to me: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah say: 'Intention for knowledge includes preservation, action, listening, attentive silence, and dissemination.'"

He (the narrator) said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, Abu Abdallah, told me, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, who said: "The most ignorant of people is he who abandons what he knows, and the most knowledgeable of people is he who acts upon what he knows, and the best of people are those who are most humble before Allah."

"He said: There are two insatiable desires: a desire for knowledge from which one is never satiated, and a desire for the world from which one is never satiated. So, whoever makes the Hereafter his concern, his striving, and his preoccupation, Allah will suffice him in his affairs and make richness in his heart. And whoever makes the world his concern, his striving, and his preoccupation, Allah will expose his deficiency, and make poverty before his eyes, so he will not be but a poor man in the morning and a poor man in the evening."

"‘Ja’far ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, and Abu ‘Umais narrated to me, from ‘Awn, who said: ‘Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “There are two who are never satisfied: the possessor of knowledge and the possessor of the world. And they are not equal. As for the possessor of knowledge, his satisfaction with the Most Merciful increases, and as for the possessor of the world, he persists in transgression.” Then Abdullah recited: ‘Nay! Indeed, man transgresses [and exceeds bounds] because he sees himself free from need.’ [Al-’Alaq 6-7] He said: And the other [verse] says: ‘Only those who fear Allah among His servants are the scholars.’ [Fatir 28]”

It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Humayd, who said: He narrated to us Ibrahim ibn Mukhtar, who said: He narrated to us from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that regarding the verse: "Only those who have knowledge fear Allah among His servants," (Surah Fatir, 28), he said: "Whoever fears Allah, then he is knowledgeable."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to me, from Layth, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There are two types of people who are never satisfied: a seeker of knowledge and a seeker of the world."

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, Yazid ibn Rabia’h al-San’ani narrated to me, Rabia’h ibn Yazid narrated, saying: I heard Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever seeks knowledge and attains it, he gains two folds of reward. And if he does not attain it, he gains one fold of reward."

It reached me that Prophet David (peace be upon him) used to say in his supplication: "Glory to You, O Allah! You are my Lord, Exalted above your Throne, and You have placed Your fear upon those in the heavens and the earth. So, the closest of Your creation to You in position is the one with the greatest fear of You. And what knowledge is there for one who does not fear You? And what wisdom is there for one who does not obey Your command?"
"Be either a scholar, or a student; for there is no good in anything other than these two."

Narrated Abu Umama, “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘There will be trials (fitan). A man will pass through them as a believer in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening, except for one whom Allah revives with knowledge.’”

"Set out each day as either a scholar or a student, and do not set out in between these two states, for that which lies between them is ignorance. Indeed, the angels spread their wings for the person who sets out seeking knowledge out of contentment with what he does."

Abu al-Mughira reported: We were told by al-Awza'i, from Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about two men among the Children of Israel: one of them was a scholar who performed the obligatory prayer, then sat and taught the people good, and the other fasted the days and stood the nights. Which of them was better? The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The superiority of this scholar who performs the obligatory prayer, then sits and teaches the people good, over the worshiper who fasts the days and stands the nights, is like my superiority over the least of you."

I entered the mosque and found Aswad ibn Surai reciting [the Quran], and Humaid ibn Abdur-Rahman discussing knowledge in a corner of the mosque. I hesitated as to which of them I should sit with, and then I dozed off. A man came to me and said, "You hesitated as to which of them you should sit with? If you wish, I will show you the place of Gabriel, peace be upon him, with Humaid ibn Abdur-Rahman."

I was sitting with Abu ad-Darda’ in the mosque of Damascus when a man came to him and said, “O Abu ad-Darda’, I have come to you from Medina, the city of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seeking a hadith that reached me from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” Abu ad-Darda’ asked, “Did you come seeking trade?” He said, “No.” Abu ad-Darda’ asked, “Did anyone else bring you?” He said, “No.” Abu ad-Darda’ said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever seeks a path to knowledge, Allah will make a path to Paradise easy for him. And the angels spread their wings in contentment for the seeker of knowledge. And the seeker of knowledge is forgiven by those in the heavens and on the earth, even the whales in the sea. And the superiority of the scholar over the worshiper is like the superiority of the moon over the rest of the stars. Indeed, the scholars are the heirs of the prophets. Indeed, the prophets did not bequeath a dinar or a dirham, but they bequeathed knowledge. So whoever takes it, he has taken a share, or an abundant share.”
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that: "The teacher of good has forgiveness sought for him by everything, even the fish in the sea."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no person who treads a path in search of knowledge, but Allah makes a path to Paradise easy for him, and whoever’s deeds are slow, his lineage will not hasten him.”
"No person sets out on a quest for knowledge but that Allah makes for him a path to Paradise easy thereby, and whoever’s deeds are slow, his lineage does not hasten him."

Indeed, We have made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there not a reminder? [Surah Al-Qamar, 17]. He [the Prophet] said: “Is there one seeking good, so that he may be assisted?” And Marwan narrated from Damrah who said: “One seeking knowledge.”

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, and he said: Ya'qub, who is Al-Qummi, narrated to me from Amir ibn Ibrahim, who said: Abu ad-Darda’ would, when he saw seekers of knowledge, say: "Welcome, seekers of knowledge!" And he would say: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entrusted you (with this pursuit)."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Yazid: Abdullah ibn Amr narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by two gatherings in his mosque and said: “Both of them are upon good, and one of them is better than its companion. These [one group] supplicate Allah and yearn towards Him, and if He wills, He gives to them, and if He wills, He withholds from them. And these [the other group] learn jurisprudence and knowledge, and teach the ignorant. They are better, and I was sent as a teacher.” He then sat with them.
"Tell me, O my son, verily knowledge is superior to action."
"There is no gift better than a word of wisdom, which you present to your brother."

"Narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Imran, who said: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan narrated to me, from Zuhri, who said: The superiority of the scholar over the diligent (striving) person is one hundred degrees, and the distance between the two degrees is five hundred years, like the galloping of a swift, barded horse."
"Allah raises those among you who believe and those who possess knowledge degrees." He [the Prophet] said, "Allah raises those who have been given knowledge above those who believe, by degrees."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever is visited by death while seeking knowledge to revive Islam thereby, there is a single degree of distinction between him and the prophets in Paradise."

Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, he said: Mihran narrated to me, he said: Abu Sinan narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "‘Umar took away two-thirds of knowledge," so I mentioned this to Ibrahim, and he said: “‘Umar took away nine-tenths of knowledge.”

Narrated ‘Abbas (RA): “Whenever a group of people gather in a house of Allah, discussing His Book and studying it amongst themselves, the angels spread their wings over them, and they are enveloped by the mercy of Allah, as long as they do not engage in talk other than that. Whoever seeks a path to knowledge, Allah makes his path to Paradise easy. And whoever is delayed by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him.”

I was once visiting Sufyan ibn ‘Asal al-Muradi, and I intended to ask him about wiping over the khuffs (leather socks). He asked, "What brings you?" I said, "Seeking knowledge." He said, "Shall I give you good news?" I said, "Yes." He said, "I have raised this matter to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he said: ‘Indeed, the angels spread their wings for the seeker of knowledge out of contentment with what he seeks.’”

"ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿImrān narrated to me, saying: Yahyā ibn Yamān narrated to me, saying: I heard Sufyān forty years ago say: “Seeking knowledge (Hadith) has never been better than it is today.” They said to Sufyān: “They seek it without intention?” He said: “Their seeking it is an intention.”
We sought this knowledge with no great intention, and then Allah subsequently granted us the intention therein.
Some people sought knowledge, but not for the sake of Allah or what is with Him. Consequently, knowledge did not truly benefit them until they sought it for the sake of Allah and what is with Him.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, who said: Abu Muslim al-Khawlani said: "Scholars are of three types: a man who lives in his knowledge and the people live with him in it; a man who lives in his knowledge but no one lives with him in it; and a man in whose knowledge the people live, but it is a burden upon him."

Moses, peace be upon him, said: "O my Lord, who are Your most just servants?" He said: "He who judges for others as he judges for himself." Moses, peace be upon him, said: "O my Lord, who are Your wealthiest servants?" He said: "Those who are most content with what I have allotted them." Moses, peace be upon him, said: "O my Lord, who are Your most fearful servants?" He said: "Those who know Me best."

Narrated by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Sufyan, who said: "It was said that scholars were of three types: a scholar of Allah, who fears Allah, but is not a scholar of Allah’s affair; and a scholar of Allah, a scholar of Allah’s affair, who fears Allah – that is the complete scholar; and a scholar of Allah’s affair, but not a scholar of Allah, who does not fear Allah – that is the wicked scholar."
"The knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge in the heart, which is beneficial knowledge, and knowledge on the tongue, which is Allah’s argument against the children of Adam."
Learn, learn, and when you have learned, act.

"Whoever seeks knowledge for four [reasons], he will enter the Fire: to show off to scholars, to argue with the ignorant, to turn people's faces towards himself, or to obtain worldly gain from rulers."

"I was told by Sa'd ibn 'Amir, from Hisham, the bearer of the Dastawai, who said: I read in a book that reached me, purportedly from the words of Jesus, peace be upon him: "You work for the world, while you are sustained in it without work, and you do not work for the Hereafter, while you are not sustained in it except through work. Woe to you, bad scholars! You take the reward and neglect the work. Soon, the Lord of work will demand his work, and you will soon emerge from this vast world into the darkness and narrowness of the grave. Allah forbids you from sins, just as He commands you to prayer and fasting. How can one of the people of knowledge be displeased with his provision and despise his status, when he knows that it is from Allah’s knowledge and power? How can one of the people of knowledge accuse Allah in what He has decreed for him, so he is not content with anything that befalls him? How can one of the people of knowledge let his world be more favored with him than his Hereafter, while he is in the world the most desirous? How can one of the people of knowledge whose ultimate destination is the Hereafter be inclined towards his world, and what harms him is more appealing to him – or he said: more beloved to him than what benefits him? How can one of the people of knowledge seek knowledge to speak it, and not seek it to act upon it?"

Learn knowledge and benefit from it, and do not learn it only to adorn yourself with it, for it is likely that if your life prolongs, one who possesses knowledge will adorn himself with his knowledge, just as one with finery adorns himself with his garment.

A man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) about evil, so he said, “Do not ask me about evil, and ask me about good.” He repeated this three times, then said, “Indeed, the worst of evils are the wicked scholars, and indeed, the best of goods are the virtuous scholars.”

Sha'bi said: "One who seeks this knowledge must possess two qualities: intelligence and piety. If he is pious but lacks intelligence, he says: ‘This is something that only the intelligent can attain,’ and does not seek it. And if he is intelligent but lacks piety, he says: ‘This is something that only the pious can attain,’ and does not seek it. Sha'bi then said: ‘I have become apprehensive that today, someone who lacks both intelligence and piety would seek it.’"
Abu 'Aasim narrated: Sufyan said to me: "A man would not seek knowledge until he had devoted himself to worship for forty years beforehand."
One who seeks knowledge to argue with the ignorant, to show off to scholars, or to direct people's faces towards himself, is in the Fire of Hell.

Narrated from Makhool that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever seeks knowledge to boast to scholars or to argue with the ignorant or to seek the approval of people, Allah will admit him to Hell."
"Indeed, a man's narration is preserved only to the extent of his intention."
Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I often think that a man forgets knowledge he once possessed because of a sin he committed."
