Al-Hakam ibn Naafi’ reported: Shu’aib ibn Abi Hamza reported from Ibn Abi Husain from Shahribin Hawshab who said: It reached me that Luqman al-Hakim used to say to his son: “O my son, do not seek knowledge to boast to scholars with it, or to argue with the ignorant, or to show off in assemblies. And do not abandon knowledge out of disdain for it and a desire for ignorance. O my son, choose your company carefully. And when you see a people remembering Allah, sit with them, for if you are a scholar, your knowledge will benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will teach you. And perhaps Allah will overlook them with His mercy and include you with them. And when you see a people who do not remember Allah, do not sit with them, for if you are a scholar, your knowledge will not benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will increase your ignorance. And perhaps Allah will overlook them with punishment and include you with them.”

Do not relate falsehood to the learned, for they will despise you, and do not relate wisdom to the foolish, for they will deny it. Do not withhold knowledge from its people, lest you incur sin, nor place it with those who do not deserve it, lest you be rendered ignorant. Indeed, you have a right concerning your knowledge, just as you have a right concerning your wealth.

"Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, used to say: 'Do not withhold knowledge from its people, lest you incur sin, and do not publicize it among those who are not its people, lest it be misunderstood. And be a gracious healer, placing medicine where you know it will benefit.'"
Do not feed your food to one who does not desire it.

"Tell me, my son, do not seek knowledge to show off with it to scholars, or to argue with the ignorant, or to display it in gatherings. And do not abandon knowledge out of disdain for it and a desire for ignorance. If you see a people remembering Allah, then sit with them. If you are a scholar, your knowledge will benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will teach you. Perhaps Allah will glance upon them with His mercy and include you with them. And if you see a people who do not remember Allah, then do not sit with them. If you are a scholar, your knowledge will not benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will increase you in error or foolishness. Perhaps Allah will glance upon them with His displeasure and include you with them."

Narrated ‘Ali (RA): “O bearers of knowledge, act upon it, for the true scholar is one who acts upon what he knows, and whose knowledge corresponds with his actions. There will be people who carry knowledge but it does not go beyond their collarbones, their actions contradicting their knowledge, and their secrets contradicting their outward appearances. They will sit in circles and boast to one another, to the extent that a man may become angry with his companion for sitting with someone else and leaving him. Their deeds will not ascend to Allah, the Exalted, in those assemblies.”
It is sufficient for a person to be knowledgeable that he fears Allah, and it is sufficient for a person to be ignorant that he is pleased with his own knowledge.
"If the least learned person among this community possessed knowledge that another nation adopted, that nation would be rightly guided."

Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, a man may acquire a portion of knowledge and act upon it, and that is better for him than the world and all that is in it, were he to possess it and devote it to the Hereafter." Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, when a man seeks knowledge, it is not long before it is manifested in his vision, his reverence, his tongue, his hand, his prayer, and his asceticism." Muhammad said: "Consider from whom you take this hadith, for it is your religion."
"No servant increases in knowledge and thereby increases his desire in this world, except that Allah increases his distance from Him."

No servant increases in knowledge of Allah except that the people draw nearer to Allah’s mercy through him. And he said in another narration: “No servant increases in knowledge except that he becomes more righteous, and Allah does not place a better necklace upon a servant than tranquility.”

Qasim ibn Kathir narrated: I heard Abdur-Rahman ibn Shuraih recounting, from Amira, that he heard him say: A man said to his son, "Go, seek knowledge." So he went and was absent for a period. Then he came to him and related some accounts. His father said to him, "O my son, go, seek knowledge." He was also absent for a time, then he came with bundles containing books, and recited them to him. His father said to him, "This is black writing on white paper." He said, "Go, seek knowledge." He went and was absent for a period, then he came and said to his father, "Ask me about whatever occurred to you." His father said to him, "Suppose you passed by a man praising you and another criticizing you?" He said, "I would not blame the one criticizing me, nor praise the one praising me." He said, "Suppose you passed by a gold coin?" Abu Shuraih said, "I do not know if it was of gold or silver." He said, "Then I would not stir it up nor approach it." He said, "Go, for you have known."

"The Hakim ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, and Bakiyyah narrated to me, from As-Sakan ibn ‘Umayr, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih saying: “O my son, adhere to wisdom, for all goodness lies within it. It elevates the young over the old, the slave over the free man, and increases the noble’s dignity, and seats the poor among the assemblies of kings.”
"And what would we be were it not for the words of the scholars?"

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me from Hammad ibn Zayd from Ayyub, who said: Abu Qilaba said: "Do not sit with people of whims and desires, nor argue with them, for I fear that they may immerse you in their misguidance, or confuse you with what you used to know."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, that Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ayyub, who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr saw me sitting with Talq ibn Habib, and he said to me: “Did I not see you sitting with Talq ibn Habib? Do not sit with him.”

Abu 'Asim narrated to me, he said: Hiywah ibn Shuraih narrated to me, he said: Abu Sakhr narrated to me, from Naafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man came to him and said: "So-and-so sends you his greetings." He (Ibn Umar) said: "It has reached me that he has innovated (in religion). If he has indeed innovated, then do not return his greetings."
Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not consider backbiting against an innovator as permissible.
Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, Jarir narrated to me, from Ibn Shubrumah, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "It was named 'longing' (al-hawa) because it makes its companion incline (yahwi) towards it."
Muslim ibn Yasar said, "Beware of argumentation, for it is a moment of ignorance for the scholar, and through it Satan seeks his lapse."

Two men from among those who followed their desires came to Ibn Sirin and said, "O Abu Bakr, shall we relate a report to you?" He said, "No." They said, "Shall we recite a verse from the Book of Allah to you?" He said, "No, either you leave me, or I will leave you." They departed, and some of the people said, "O Abu Bakr, what prevented you from allowing them to recite a verse from the Book of Allah?" He said, "I feared that they would recite a verse from the Book of Allah to me and distort it, and that would become established in my heart."

Sa'id narrated to us from Salam ibn Abi Mutee' that a man from the people of whims said to Ayyub: "O Abu Bakr, I ask you about a word?" He [Ayyub] turned away while gesturing with his finger, not even half a word. And Sa'id gestured to us with his little finger of the right hand.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me from Hammad ibn Zayd from Kulthum ibn Jabir that a man asked Saeed ibn Jubair about something, and he did not answer him. It was said to him about this, and he said, "Azishan."

Narrated to me Ahmad ibn Abdullah, who said: Fudayl narrated to me, from Layth, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: "Do not sit with those who engage in arguments, for they are those who delve into the verses of Allah."
"Do not sit with the people of whims and desires, nor argue with them, and do not listen to them."
Narrated by Ahmad: Ahmad said, “Tell us,” Sharik narrated to me from Umayya from Al-Sha’bi, who said, “They were called the people of desire because they will desire [or suffer] in the Fire.”

Bishr ibn al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Ibn Maysara, who said: "I have not seen anyone among the people, whether noble or humble, equal in the eyes of anyone other than Tawus, and he swears by him."

Bishr ibn al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Zuhri, who said: "We used to dislike writing knowledge until the ruler compelled us to do so. Thus, we disliked preventing anyone from doing it."

Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to me, Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, Ibn 'Awn said: We spoke to Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a man who was relating something to him. He said: "If he were a man from among the Zanj, he would be with me, and Abdullah ibn Muhammad would be the same in this regard."

Yahyá ibn Hasan narrated to me, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Salt ibn Ráshid, that Salm ibn Qutaybah asked Táwus about a matter, and he did not answer him. Then it was said to him, "This is Salm ibn Qutaybah." He said, "That is lighter for him upon me."
Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Baqiyyah who said: Habib ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: "I feared no one from the people as much as I feared Khalid ibn Ma'dan."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me from Mughira, who said, "We used to fear Ibrahim out of reverence, as we feared a ruler."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated a hadith one day, and I stood up to him and questioned him about it. He said to me, "Do you question me every hour [about something] so that you milk [a camel] and drink [the milk]?"
Abu Abd al-Rahman disliked the narration of hadith on the road.

We were with Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and he narrated a hadith. A man said to him, “Who narrated this to you, or from whom did you hear this?” So he became angry and withheld his narration from us until he stood up.
Abu Salama said: "Had I treated Ibn Abbas with kindness, I would have gained much knowledge from him."
Hakim ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: "Baqiyyah narrated to me from Ummu Abdillah, daughter of Khalid, who said: 'I have not seen anyone who honors knowledge more than my father.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Awza'i, from Sulaiman ibn Musa, who said: I said to Tawus: “Indeed, so-and-so narrated to me such and such.” He said: “If your companion is eloquent, then take [knowledge] from him.”
Sa'd ibn Ibrahim said: "Let none relate from the Messenger of Allah except those who are trustworthy."

Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, Jarir narrated to me, from ‘Asim, from Ibn Sirin, who said, "They used not to inquire about the chains of narration (isnad). Then they began to inquire afterward to know who was a follower of the Sunnah from whom they would take knowledge, and from whom was not a follower of the Sunnah, they would not take knowledge." Abu Muhammad said: I do not think he heard it from ‘Asim.
Muhammad ibn Sirin said, "Do not tell me about the sayings of two men, for they do not care from whom they receive their narrations." Abu Muhammad Abdullah said: I do not think he heard it.
Ibrahim said: "If you narrate to me, narrate to me from Abu Zur'ah, for he narrated a hadith to me, and I questioned him about it after a year, and he did not miss a single letter of it."
"Tell us 'Affan, narrated to us Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, who said: 'Indeed, this knowledge is religion, so let a man look to whom he takes his religion from.'"
Narrated Ibrahim: "Whenever they came to a person to learn from him, they would look at his prayer, his conduct, and his appearance."

"Amru ibn Zurara narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to me, Mughira narrated to me, from Ibrahim, who said: 'Whenever they would come to a man to take knowledge from him, they would look at his prayer, his conduct, and his appearance, and then they would take knowledge from him.' Abu Ma'mar Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from Ruh, from Hisham, from Hasan, a similar narration to the narration of Ibrahim."

We would visit a man to learn from him, and we would observe his prayer. If he performed it well, we would sit with him and say, “He performs it better than others.” And if he performed it poorly, we would leave him and say, “He performs it worse than others.”
Abu 'Aasim narrated: I do not know whether I heard it from him or from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad: "Indeed, this knowledge is religion, so look from whom you take your religion."

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Saeed ibn Abdul Aziz narrated to me from Sulaiman ibn Musa, who said: I said to Tawus: "Indeed, so-and-so has informed me of such and such." He said: "If your companion is eloquent, then learn from him."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Hujayr, from Tawus, who said: Bashir ibn Ka'b came to Ibn Abbas and began relating to him. Ibn Abbas said, "Recite the first story to me again." Bashir said to him, "Do you know my entire narration and reject this [particular part], or do you know this [particular part] and reject my entire narration?" Ibn Abbas said, "Indeed, we used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, when no one lied about him. But when people began riding difficult and extravagant camels, we abandoned narrating from him."
"We used to memorize the Hadith, and the Hadith was memorized from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, until you began to ride swift camels and mules."
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr: He said, "It is nearing that jinn will appear, whom Solomon (peace be upon him) had bound, and they will interpret religious matters for people."
"Observe from whom you take this narration, for it is your religion."
"One should guard against interpreting the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as one guards against interpreting the Quran."
Narrated 'Abdullah ibn Abbas: "Do you not fear that you will be punished or that the earth will swallow you up for saying: 'The Messenger of Allah said,' and 'So-and-so said'?"

Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote: “There is no independent opinion for anyone regarding the Book of Allah. Rather, the opinion of the scholars is only concerning that which the Book of Allah has not explicitly mentioned, and upon which no established practice (sunnah) from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has come. And there is no independent opinion for anyone regarding a practice established by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

Narrated by Musa bin Khalid, from Mu’tamir bin Sulaiman, from ‘Ubaidullah bin ‘Umar, that ‘Umar bin ‘Abd al-‘Aziz delivered a sermon and said: “O people, Allah did not send any prophet after your Prophet, and He did not reveal any book after this Book which He revealed [the Quran], so whatever Allah has permitted on the tongue of His Prophet is permissible until the Day of Resurrection, and whatever Allah has forbidden on the tongue of His Prophet is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection. Know that I am not a judge, but an executor; nor am I an innovator, but a follower; nor am I better than you except that I carry a heavier burden. Know that none of Allah’s creation is to be obeyed in disobedience to Allah. Have I made it clear?”

'Ubaidullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me, he said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to me from Hisham ibn Hujayr, who said: Tawus used to pray two rak'ahs after the 'Asr prayer. Then Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "Leave them." He said: "They were only forbidden to be taken as a ladder." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Indeed, it has been forbidden to pray after 'Asr, so I do not know whether I will be punished for it or rewarded, for Allah says: 'And it was not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should oppose their decision.' And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then he has certainly gone astray in a clear going astray.' [Quran 33:36]" Sufyan said: "Taken as a ladder, meaning to pray after 'Asr until night."

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala narrated to me, that Ibn Numair narrated to me, from Mujahid, from 'Amir, from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) with a copy of the Torah. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is a copy of the Torah." He remained silent, and 'Umar began to read, and the face of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) began to change. Then Abu Bakr (may Allah have mercy upon him) said: "May your camels be orphaned! What do you see in the face of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)?" 'Umar looked at the face of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the anger of Allah and from the anger of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). We are pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a Prophet." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if Moses appeared to you and you followed him and abandoned me, you would go astray from the straight path. And if he were alive and attained my prophethood, he would follow me."

Qabisa reported: Sufyan narrated to me from Abu Rabah, an elderly man from the family of Umar, who said: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib saw a man praying two rak’ahs after the Asr prayer, pronouncing the takbir. He said to him: “O Abu Muhammad, will Allah punish me for praying?” He replied: “No, but Allah will punish you for acting contrary to the Sunnah.”

While a man was strutting along in two fine garments, the earth swallowed him up, and he continued to churn within it until the Day of Resurrection. Then a young man, wearing a fine garment of his own, said to him, "O Abu Hurairah, did that young man who was swallowed up walk in this manner?" Then he struck his hand, and stumbled so much that he nearly broke himself. So Abu Hurairah said to his nostrils and his mouth, "Indeed, We have sufficed you against the deriders.” [Quran 15:95]

I saw a young man throwing pebbles in the mosque. An elderly man said to him, "Do not throw pebbles, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbid it." The young man forgot and thought the elderly man did not notice him, so he threw a pebble again. The elderly man said to him, "I tell you that I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbid throwing pebbles, and yet you do it? By Allah, I will not attend your funeral, visit you when you are sick, or speak to you ever again." I told a companion of mine, named Muhajir, "Go to Khirash and ask him about this." So he went to him and asked him about it, and he related the story to him.

Narrated Abdullah ibn Mughaffal (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade throwing with stones. He said: "It does not hunt game, nor injure an enemy, but it breaks a tooth and gouges out an eye." A man, who was related to Sa’id, raised a handful of earth between them and said, "Is this it? What is this?" Sa’id said: "Do you not see that I am narrating to you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you treat it lightly? I will never speak to you again."

Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, may Allah be pleased with him, saw a man among his companions throwing pebbles. He said, "Do not throw pebbles, for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade it or disliked it." And he said, "Indeed, you will not wound an enemy with it, nor hunt game with it, but it may gouge out an eye and break a tooth." Then he saw him doing it again, so he said to him, "Did I not tell you that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade it? Yet I see you doing it. By Allah, I will never speak to you again."

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Saeed ibn Bashir narrated to me from Qatadah, who said: Ibn Sirin narrated a Hadith to a man from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). A man said: "So-and-so said such-and-such." Ibn Sirin said: "Do I narrate to you from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and you say: 'So-and-so said such-and-such'? I will never speak to you again."

Narrated by Ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If your wife asks your permission to go to the mosque, do not prevent her.” A man from the people said, “Then by Allah, I would prevent her.” Ibn Umar turned towards him and cursed him in a way I had never seen him curse anyone before, and then said: “I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and you say, ‘Then by Allah, I would prevent her’!”

Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, he said: Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated to me from Ma’ruf from Abu al-Mukharik, who said: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade selling two dirhams for one dirham. A man said: “I do not see any harm in this, hand to hand.” ‘Ubadah said: “I say: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, and you say: I do not see any harm in it? By Allah, no roof will ever shelter me and you.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Do not visit women at night.” Then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) returned, and two men slipped to their wives’ homes, and they both found another man with their wives.

Abu al-Mughirah narrated: "Tell us," he said, "that al-Awza'i narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmala al-Aslami, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to, when he returned from a journey, descend at the halting place (al-mu'arras), and then he said: 'Do not visit women at night.' Two men of those who heard his saying went out and visited their wives, and each of them found a man with his wife."

Abu al-Mughirah narrated to me, he said: al-Awza'i narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmala narrated to me, he said: A man came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib to bid him farewell before setting off for Hajj or 'Umrah. Sa'id said to him: "Do not leave until you pray." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one leaves the mosque after the call to prayer except a hypocrite, unless one is compelled by a need and intends to return to the mosque." The man said: "My companions are in al-Harra." Sa'id said: "Then leave." He left, and Sa'id longed to remember him until he was informed that he had fallen from his mount and broken his thigh.
"Do not weary the people [with lengthy sermons or stories]."
"Indeed, hearts experience animation and inclination, and they also experience turning away and rejection. So, relate to people only that which they accept."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to me, saying: I heard Hasan say: It was said, "Speak to the people only as long as they turn their faces towards you; and if they turn away, know that they have needs."

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not write anything from me other than the Quran. And whoever writes anything other than the Quran, let him erase it."
Abu Sa’id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: They asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) for permission to write from him, but he did not permit them.

"Bishr ibn al-Hakam narrated to me from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Ibn Shubrumah, from Al-Sha'bi, that he used to say: 'O Shabaak, should I respond to you, meaning: to the Hadith? I never desired that a Hadith be disputed with me.'"

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalifa reported: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi saying: I heard Malik ibn Anas saying: Al-Zuhri brought a hadith, and I met him on the road. I took hold of his reins and said: O Abu Bakr, repeat to me the hadith you narrated to us. He said: "Do you request that I repeat the hadith?" I said: "And were you not accustomed to repeat the hadith?" He said: "No." I said: "And do you not write it down?" He said: "No."

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me from Al-Awza'i, who said: "Qatadah disliked writing. If he heard the sound of writing, he would object to it and seek it out with his hand." Abu al-Mughirah narrated to me, saying: "Al-Awza'i disliked it."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Mansur, that Ibrahim disliked the book, meaning: knowledge.

Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to me, Azhar narrated to me, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "If I were to choose a book, I would choose the letters of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to me from Ibn 'Awn, who said: "I saw Hammad writing with Ibrahim, and Ibrahim said to him: 'Did I not forbid you?' He said: 'It is only brief notes.'"
Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to me, from Shu'bah, from Al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, who said: 'Abidah said to me, "Do not permanently record anything against me."
Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Hisham who said: "I did not write down anything from Muhammad except profound hadiths. Once I memorized them, I erased them."
Marwan ibn Muhammad said: I heard Saeed ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz say: "I have never written down a hadith."
I have never written anything.
I asked ‘Abidah for a piece of skin to write on, and he said, “O Ibrahim, do not immortalize anything from me.”
Ibrahim disliked that hadith be written in notebooks, saying, "It is made to resemble the Musahafs." Yahya said: And I found in my book, from Ziyad the scribe, from Abu Ma'shar, "Write as you wish."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf and 'Ubaydullah narrated to me on the authority of Sufyan, from Nu'man ibn Qays, that 'Abidah summoned his books and erased them at the time of his death, and said: "I fear that people will inherit them and not place them in their proper positions."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak and Zakariyya ibn ‘Adiyy narrated to me on the authority of ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, that he disliked that knowledge be written in notebooks.
"This knowledge has always been rare, sought out by men, until it fell into writings. Then it was carried [transmitted] by them, or others who were not its people entered into it."

Yusuf ibn Musa reported: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, and he said: Shu'bah told us from Yunus that: Hasan used to write and have things written for him, while Ibn Sirin neither wrote nor had things written for him.

Yazid narrated to us, saying: Al-’Awam narrated to us from Ibrahim At-Taymi, who said: It reached Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that there was a book with some people that they admired, and it persisted with them until they brought it to him. So he erased it, and then said: "Indeed, those of the People of the Book before you perished because they turned to the books of their scholars and abandoned the Book of their Lord."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, who said: I said to 'Abidah, "Should I write down what I hear from you?" He said, "No." I said, "Then if I find a book, should I read it?" He said, "No."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Al-Jariri narrated to me from Abu Nadra, who said: I said to Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: "Should we not write [these sayings] down, for we do not remember?" He said: "No, we will not write you [down], nor will we make it Quran. But preserve from us as we have preserved from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me from Al-Awza'i, who said: I heard Abu Kathir saying: I heard Abu Hurairah saying: "Abu Hurairah neither writes nor is written to."

"Asad ibn Musa narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abu Musa, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Burdah: That he used to write down the narrations of his father, and Abu Musa saw it and erased it."
Al-Walid ibn Shu'ja narrated to me, saying: Quraish ibn Anas narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Awn said to me: "I have never written down a Hadith."

Ibn Sirin, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "By Allah, I never wrote down a narration." Ibn ‘Awn said, “Ibn Sirin told me, from Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, that Marwan ibn al-Hakam, while he was governor of Medina, wanted me to write something for him. I did not do so. He then drew a curtain between his sitting area and the rest of his house. His companions would enter and converse in that area. Then Marwan turned to his companions and said, ‘I do not think we have anything but betrayal [of Ibn Sirin].’ Then he turned to me and said, ‘And what makes you say that?’ I said, ‘I do not think we have anything but betrayal of you.’ He said, ‘And what makes you say that?’ He said, ‘We ordered a man to sit behind this curtain and write down what these people are given rulings on and what they say.’”

'Affan narrated to me, saying: "Yahyá ibn Sa'íd al-Qattán narrated to me, saying: "Sufyán narrated to me from Mánsur, who said: I said to Ibrahim: 'Indeed, Salim has more complete narrations than you.' He said: 'Indeed, Salim used to write.'"

Al-Walid ibn Hisham narrated to me, saying: Al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Himchi narrated to me from ‘Amru ibn Qays, who said: “I came to Yazid ibn Mu’awiya in Huwarin with my father when Mu’awiya died, may Allah be pleased with him, to console him and congratulate him on the caliphate. Then I saw a man in the mosque saying: ‘Verily, among the signs of the Hour is that the wicked are elevated and the righteous are degraded. Verily, among the signs of the Hour is that speech becomes prevalent and actions are concealed. Verily, among the signs of the Hour is that the Matnatu is recited, and no one is found to change it.’ It was asked him: ‘What is the Matnatu?’ He said: ‘Any writing that is written other than the Quran.’ So fear Allah and the Quran, for by it you are guided, by it you will be rewarded, and from it you will be questioned.” I did not know who that man was, so I narrated this hadith afterward in Hims. Then a man from among the people said to me: ‘Don’t you know him?’ I said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘That is Abdullah ibn ‘Amru, may Allah be pleased with them.’”

Abu Qura’s al-Kindi brought a letter from Syria, and he carried it and handed it to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him. He looked at it, then called for a basin, then called for water, and tested it in the water. He said: “Those who preceded you perished because they followed the scriptures and abandoned their scripture.” Husein said: Then Murra al-Hamdani said: “Indeed, if it were from the Qur’an or the Sunnah, it would not be erased, but it was from the scriptures of the People of the Book.”

Narrated by Yahya ibn Ja’dah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was brought a shoulder blade with a writing on it. He said, “It is sufficient for a people to be misguided that they turn away from that which their Prophet has come with to that which a prophet other than their prophet has brought, or a book other than their book.” Then Allah revealed: “Is it not enough for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Verily, therein is a mercy and a reminder for a believing people.” [Surah Al-Ankabut (29:51)]

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Shu’bah narrated to me from Al-Ash’ath, from his father, who was among the companions of Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud), that he said: I saw a man with a scroll containing: “SubhanAllah,” “Alhamdulillah,” “La ilaha illallah,” and “Allahumma Akbar.” I said to him, "Let me copy it." He seemed reluctant to give it to me. Then he promised to give it to me, so I went to Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud) and there it was before him. He said: "Indeed, what is in this book is an innovation, a trial, and misguidance. Those before you were destroyed because of this and things similar to it. They wrote it down, their tongues concealed it, and their hearts absorbed it. I command every person who knows the location of a book [containing such things] to reveal it. And I swear by Allah.” Shu’bah said: “Did he swear by Allah?” He said: “I think he swore.” He said: “I think he swore: If it were mentioned to him in the monastery of the Hindus – meaning a place far from Kufa – he would come to it, even if he had to walk.”
Narrated Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari: "The Children of Israel wrote a book and followed it, abandoning the Torah."
"Indeed, there are people who hear my words and then depart and write them down, yet I do not permit anyone to write except the Book of Allah."
"I have never written anything black on white, nor have I repeated a narration from anyone."

"None of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, narrated more traditions from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, than I did, except for Abdullah ibn Amr, for he used to write, and I did not."

Musaddad narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to me, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn al-Ahnas, who said: The Walid ibn ‘Abdullah narrated to me, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said: “I used to write down everything I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), intending to preserve it. Then the Quraysh forbade me, saying: ‘You write down everything you hear from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)? Is the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) not a human being who speaks in anger and satisfaction?’ So I stopped writing. Then I mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and he gestured with his finger to his mouth and said: ‘Write, by the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing comes out of it but the truth.’”

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, Layth narrated to me, Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Qays, who said: A reporter informed me, from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intend to relate from your sayings, and I wanted to assist with the writing in my hand along with my heart, if you see that permissible?" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If you say it, narrate my hadith, then assist with your hand along with your heart."

While we were sitting around the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, writing, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked: “Which of the two cities will be conquered first, Constantinople or Rome?” He said, “No, but Heraclius’ city will be conquered first.”

Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, Abu Ma'mar, narrated to me from Abu Dhamra, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Dinār, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, saying: "Write to me with whatever has reached you of narrations from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and with the narrations of 'Amra, for I have feared the disappearance of knowledge and its vanishing."

Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote to the people of Medina: "Look into the narrations of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and write them down, for I fear the disappearance of knowledge and its people."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Malih, who said: "They criticize us regarding the scripture, yet Allah the Exalted said: 'Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book.'" (Surah Taha, verse 52)
One said, "That which is not written down is not considered knowledge."
Narrated by Anas (RA): He used to say to his sons, "O my sons! Restrain this knowledge."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to me from Mahdi ibn Maymun from Salim al-’Alawi, who said: "I saw Aban writing on a board in the presence of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him)."
Abu Amama al-Bahili (RA) was asked about a book on knowledge. He said, "There is nothing wrong with that."

I was writing down what I heard from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him. When I intended to leave him, I brought his writings to him, and I recited them to him. I said to him, "Is this what you heard?" He said, "Yes."
I used to hear from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, the Hadith at night, and I would write it on the side of my travel bag.

"What encourages me in life are two things: the Sadiqah and the Wahṭ. As for the Sadiqah, it is a scroll I wrote from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And as for the Wahṭ, it is land that ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, may Allah be pleased with him, gave in charity, and he used to stand (pray) upon it."
"Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Record knowledge in writing.'"
"Record this knowledge in writing."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Abdul Wahid narrated to me, saying: Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to me, saying: I heard Saeed ibn Jubayr saying: "I used to travel with Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, on the road to Mecca at night. He would relate to me hadiths, and I would write them down on a piece of parchment in my bag until morning, when I would write them down again."
I was writing on a scroll for Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and also writing in my sandals.
I was sitting with Ibn Abbas and would write on a paper until it was full, then I would turn my sandals over and write on their soles.
Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, saying: Fudayl narrated to me from ‘Ubayd al-Mukattib, who said: "I saw them writing down interpretations in the presence of Mujahid."

Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, and Waqi' narrated to me, that my father narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Hanash, who said: "I saw them writing at the home of Al-Bara' using reeds on the palms of their hands."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, from Ibn Idris, from Harun ibn 'Antarah, from his father, that Ibn Abbas related a Hadith to me. I said, "Shall I write it down from you?" He said, "He permitted me, and he barely did so."
Rajā’ b. Haywah reported: Hisham b. ‘Abd al-Malik wrote to his governor to ask me about a hadith. Rajā’ said: “I would have forgotten it had it not been for a written record I possessed.”
Al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Shu'aib narrated to me, Hisham ibn al-Ghazal said: "‘Atā’ ibn Abi Rabah was asked questions, and what he answered was written down before him."

Al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to me, and Muhammad ibn Shu'aib ibn Shabur narrated to me, and Al-Walid ibn Sulaiman ibn Abi as-Sa'ib narrated to me, from Sulaiman ibn Musa, that he saw Naafi', the freed slave of Ibn Umar, dictating his knowledge, and it was being written before him.
Al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to me, and Mubark ibn Sa'id said: "Sufyan would write down the Hadith at night in the courtyard, and when morning came, he would copy it and then erase it."

I said to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, "Someone from the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, has narrated to me," and Umar recognized him. I said, "He narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, modesty, chastity, and restraint of the tongue are from faith, and they increase in the Hereafter and decrease from the world. And what increases in the Hereafter is greater. And indeed, extravagance, harshness, and miserliness are from hypocrisy, and they increase in the world and decrease in the Hereafter. And what decreases in the Hereafter is greater.'"

Husayn ibn Mansur narrated, "We were told by Abu Usama, who narrated to me, Sulayman ibn Mughira said: Abu Qilaba said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz came out for the Dhuhr prayer with a paper, and he came out for the Asr prayer with it. I said to him, "O Commander of the Believers, what is this writing?" He said, "This is a hadith that 'Awn ibn Abd Allah narrated to me, and I was impressed by it, so I wrote it down." And indeed, it contained this hadith.

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Mas'ud narrated to me from Yunus ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwa from Surhabeel ibn Abi Sa'd, who said: Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) called for his sons and the sons of his brother. He said: "O my sons and the sons of my brother, you are a small people, and you will soon become the greater ones. So, acquire knowledge. Whoever among you is unable to recite it, let him write it down and place it in his home."

Narrated Jabir bin ‘Abdullah (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever initiates a good practice and others follow it, he will have the reward of it along with those who follow him, without their reward being diminished. And whoever initiates a bad practice and others follow it, he will bear the sin of it along with those who follow him, without their sin being diminished.”

"Whoever calls [others] to guidance, he will receive a reward equal to the reward of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever calls [others] to misguidance, he will bear the burden of the sin of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their sins."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, delivered a sermon to us. He urged the people to give charity, but they delayed, until anger appeared on his face. Then a man from the Ansar came with a single date, and the people began to give generously until joy was seen on his face. He then said: "Whoever initiates a good practice, he will receive its reward and the reward of those who act upon it, without diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever initiates a bad practice, he will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it, without diminishing anything from their burdens."
"I am the one who will have the greatest reward on the Day of Resurrection, for I have My reward and the reward equivalent to that of everyone who follows me."

Malik related to me, from Abdullah as-Salam, from Layth, from Bishr, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever calls someone to something, even if he calls one man to another, he will be held accountable for it on the Day of Resurrection, bound by its consequence. Then he recited: 'And stop them, for they will be questioned.'" (Surah As-Saaffaat, 37:24)

"‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Four things a person is given after his death: a third of his wealth, if he had been obedient to Allah in it before that; a righteous child who supplicates for him after his death; a good practice which he initiated and people act upon after his death; and intercession, if they intercede for a person, they will be interceded for.”
Abu Hurairah (RA) reported: “We exerted ourselves to make Ibrahim (AS) sit on a cushion, but he refused.”
He [Ibrahim] would dislike leaning against a date palm trunk.
Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Abu ‘Awanah narrated to me from Mughirah, who said: "Ibrahim (peace be upon him) would not initiate a conversation unless he was asked."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Sa’id: Yunus ibn Bukair narrated to me, and he said: Al-A’mash narrated to me from Khaithama who said: Al-Harith ibn Qais al-Ju’fi was among the companions of Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud), and they were impressed by him. So a man or two would sit with him and he would relate to them. But when they became numerous, he would stand up and leave them.
It was said to him when Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) died, "If you had stayed and taught the people the Sunnah?" He said, "Do you want my successors to be trampled upon?"

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala’ narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to me, he said: I heard Harun ibn ‘Antarah from Sulaym ibn Hanbalah, who said: We came to Ubayy ibn Ka’b to converse with him. When he rose, we rose. We were walking behind him, when ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) overtook us and struck him with a jewel-encrusted staff. He defended himself with his arms and said: “O Commander of the Believers, what should we do?” He said: “Do you not see? A trial for the followed and humiliation for the follower.”
Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Jarir narrated to me, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "They disliked that their heels be trodden upon."

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Bistam ibn Muslim who said: Muhammad ibn Sirin, whenever a man walked with him, he would stand up and say, "Do you have a need?" If he had a need, he would fulfill it. And if the man returned to walk with him, he would stand up and say, "Do you have a need?"
"Beware that your heels are trampled upon."

Malik narrated: Makhlad ibn Malik narrated to me, that Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to me, that Shu'bah narrated to me, from Al-Haytham, from 'Asim ibn Damrah, that he saw people following Sa'id ibn Jubayr. He said: It seems he said to them, "Indeed, this action of yours or this manner of walking of yours is a humiliation for the follower and a trial for the followed."

I asked Muhammad about building a structure I intended to build in the valley. He indicated to me, saying: "If you intend to lay the foundation, give me notice so that I may come with you." So I came to him, and while we were walking, a man came and walked with us. He stood up and said, "Do you have a need?" He replied, "No." He said, "Then, no, go away." Then he turned to me and said, "You too, go away." So I left until I deviated from the path.
Abu Hurairah (RA) reported: "Whenever the people came to Rabi', he would say, 'I seek refuge in Allah from your evil,' meaning his companions."

We were with Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions were gathered around him, and he was silent. They said to him, "Why don't you tell your companions [something]?" He said, "I fear that I will say to them what I do not act upon."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Salih, who said: I heard Al-Sha'bi say: "I wished that I were saved from my work, sufficient for me and not burdensome to others."

Narrated by Ibn Mas’ud (may Allah be pleased with him): People were treading on his heels as he was walking. He said: “Do not tread on my heels. By Allah, if you knew what I shut my door against, none of you would follow me.”
"There will be a trial for the one followed, and humiliation for the follower."
They walked behind Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said, "Let your footwear striking the ground be minimal, for it corrupts the hearts of men."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Hazim, who said: I heard Hasan say: "The striking of the feet (of horses) around men is something the foolish do not remain long at."
Narrated: Tawus said: "Whenever a man or two sat with him, he would stand and move aside."

Narrated Abu Barzah Al-Aslami: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about his life as to how he spent it, about his knowledge as to what he did with it, about his wealth from where he acquired it and in what he spent it, and about his body as to how he used it.”

"Allah will not leave the servants on the Day of Resurrection – the day when people arise before the Lord of the worlds – until He questions them about four things: about how they spent their lives, about how they used their bodies, about what they earned and in what they spent it, and about what they acted upon of that which they knew."

Narrated by Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA): "The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about four things: about his life and how he spent it, about his body and how he used it, about his wealth from where he acquired it and what he spent it on, and about his knowledge and what he did with it."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Layth, who said: Tawus said to me: "Whatever you learn, learn it for yourself, for the trustworthiness has vanished from the people."
Al-Hasan said: "I found people and ascetics; when an ascetic practices devotion, he is not recognized by his speech, but by his actions. That is beneficial knowledge."

Narrated Abu Al-Mughira: He told me that Hammad narrated to me from Hasan from Abu Kabsha who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: "Convey my message even if it is just a single verse, and narrate about the Children of Israel without any hesitation. Whoever deliberately fabricates a lie against me, let him take his seat in the Fire."

Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated to me, and Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, and Al-Awam ibn Hawshab, Abu Aisa al-Shaybani, narrated to me, and Qasim ibn Auf al-Shaybani narrated to me, from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered us to not allow them to overcome us in three matters: enjoining good, forbidding evil, and teaching the people the Sunnah.

Sulaym ibn ‘Amir said: Abu Umama would, when we sat with him, bring forth a great matter in discourse, and he would say, "Listen and understand, and convey to us what you hear." Sulaym said: "Like one who bears witness to what he knows."

Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: I went to Abu Dharr while he was sitting by the middle Jamrah, and people had gathered around him seeking legal opinions. A man came to him and stood before him, then said: “Were you not forbidden from giving legal opinions?” Abu Dharr raised his head to him and said: “Are you a watchman over me? If you were to place a heavy stone on the back of my neck, and then you suspected that I would carry out a word I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) before you authorized me, I would carry it out.”

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Hammad, who is Ibn al-‘Awwam, narrated to me from ‘Auf, from Abu al-Aliya, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, about something. He said: "O Abu al-Aliya, do you want to be a jurist?" I said: "No, but I fear you will depart and we will remain." He said: "Abu al-Aliya spoke the truth."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: 'Abbad narrated to me, from Husayn, from Ibrahim, who said: "‘Abidah would visit Abdullah ibn Mas’ud every Thursday and ask him about matters that had escaped him. Thus, the majority of what was preserved from Abdullah was that which ‘Abidah asked him about."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Ghassan, who is the son of Mudara, narrated to me from Sa’id ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Ikrimah saying: "What is the matter with you that you do not ask me? Have you become bankrupt?"
Knowledge is repositories, and questioning unlocks them.

Ibrahim narrated to me from Jarir who said: Ibrahim said: "If his face is softened (with humility), then his knowledge is softened."

Waki' narrated to me from his father, from Ash-Sha'bi, who said: "If his face is softened (with humility), then his knowledge is softened."

And from Damrah, from Hafs ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If his face is softened (with humility), then his knowledge is softened."
Mujahid said, "One who feels shame and arrogance does not learn."

Narrated by Anas ibn ‘Iyad, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwa, from his father, that he used to gather his sons and say, “O my sons, learn, for if you are a small group, perhaps you will become a larger one. And how unsightly it is for an elderly person to be asked a question when he has no knowledge.”

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) would place me on his feet, and teach me the Quran and the Sunnah.
One who hastens to assume leadership harms more than he benefits of knowledge, and one who does not seek leadership diligently seeks and seeks until he attains it.
"Knowledge which is not acted upon is like treasure from which nothing is spent."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The example of knowledge which is not put to use is like that of a treasure which is not spent in the way of Allah.”

It reached me that Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to Abu ad-Darda’ (may Allah be pleased with him): “Indeed, knowledge is like springs, which people cover over, so this one stirs it up and that one. Then Allah benefits others through it. And indeed, wisdom that is not spoken is like a body without a soul. And indeed, knowledge that is not brought forth is like a treasure from which nothing is spent. And the example of a scholar is like a man who carries a lamp in a dark path, by which those who pass by are illuminated, and everyone calls blessings upon him.”
"A man is followed after his death by three things: a charity that continues after him, the prayer of his son for him, and knowledge which he disseminated and by which people act after him."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "When a person dies, his actions are cut off except for three: righteous charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him."
Abu Musa (RA) narrated: "When I came to Basra, Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) sent me to you to teach you the Book of your Lord and your Sunnah, and to purify your ways."
Whoever seeks knowledge, it is an expiation for that which has passed.

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, who said: "I resided in Medina for three days without needing anything, except that I had already fulfilled it. However, a man whom they were anticipating used to relate a hadith. So, I stayed until he arrived, and then I questioned him."
I would often ride to Egypt from various lands, solely for a single narration, to hear it.
"We used to hear the narrations in Basra from the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, but we did not be satisfied until we rode to Medina and heard them from their mouths."

Narrated by Abu Dawood: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Tell the possessor of knowledge to take a staff of iron, and shoes of iron, and seek knowledge until his staff breaks and his shoes are worn out."

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: “I sought knowledge and did not find it more abundant among the Ansar. So I would visit a man and ask him about it, and they would tell me he was asleep. I would then rest my head on my garment and lie down until he came out at noon. He would then say, ‘When did you come to be here, O cousin of the Messenger of Allah?’ I would say, ‘For a long time.’ He would say, ‘You have done badly. Why didn’t you let me know?’ I would say, ‘I wanted you to come out to me after you had fulfilled your need.’”

"Ibrahim ibn Salama informed me that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The majority of the Messenger of Allah’s (peace and blessings be upon him) hadith was found amongst this group of the Ansar. By Allah, I would come to a man amongst them and they would say, ‘He is sleeping.’ If I wished, I would let him remain until he awoke so that I could obtain his hadith from him."
Abu Salama said: "Had I treated Ibn Abbas with kindness, I would have gained much knowledge from him."
I used to visit the door of Urwa, and sit at the door, and if I had wanted to enter, I could have entered, but I refrained out of reverence for him.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me on the authority of Ya’la ibn Hakim on the authority of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas (RA) who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, I said to a man from the Ansar: ‘O so-and-so, let us go and ask the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), for they are numerous today.’ He said: ‘How astonishing you are, O Ibn Abbas! Do you think people need you when there are among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) those whom you see?’ So I abandoned that, and I devoted myself to seeking knowledge. If a hadith reached me from a man, I would go to him, and he would be speaking. I would lean my garment against his door, and the wind would blow dust on my face. He would then come out and see me and say: ‘O nephew of the Messenger of Allah! What brings you?’ Would you not have sent for me to come to you? I would say: ‘No, I am more deserving to come to you.’ Then I would ask him about the hadith. The man remained until he saw me surrounded by people. He said: ‘This young man was more sensible than I was.’”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Al-Jariri narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Buridah, that a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) traveled to Fadala ibn Ubaid (may Allah be pleased with him), who was in Egypt. He came to him while he was feeding his camel. The man said, "Welcome!" He (Fadala) replied, "Indeed, I did not come to visit you, but I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and you also, and I hoped you might have some knowledge of it." He (Fadala) said, "So and so."

Narrated Muhammad bin Sa’id: Muhammad said, “Abdus Salam bin Harb narrated to me from Abd al-‘Ala from Hasan that he entered the market and bargained with a man over a garment. He said, “I will give it to you for so and so, and by Allah, if it were not you, I would not give it to him.” The man said, “You have done it.” After that, he was never seen buying or selling in the market until he met Allah.
He (Ibrahim) used to not buy from one he knew.

Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-Salam narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Muzani, from 'Ubaid ibn al-Hasan, who said: “Mus'ab ibn Zubair divided wealth among the reciters of the people of Kufa when the month of Ramadan entered. He sent to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'qil two thousand dirhams, saying to him: "Utilize this in your month." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'qil returned it and said: "We do not recite the Quran for this."

Narrated by Anas ibn ‘Iyad: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) asked Abdullah ibn Salam, “Who are the people of knowledge?” He said, “Those who act upon what they know.” Umar then asked, “What removes knowledge from the hearts of men?” He replied, “Greed.”
"Nothing blends more beautifully with anything than forbearance with knowledge."
"The beauty of knowledge is the forbearance of its people."
"Knowledge cannot be contained in a scabbard of patience."
Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, Jarir narrated to me, from Ibn Shubrumah, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "The beauty of knowledge is the forbearance of its people."
"Indeed, wisdom dwells in the tranquil and settled heart."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: I heard Sufyan say: 'Obaydu'llah said: "You have consumed knowledge and extinguished its light. Had Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) lived to see you and me, he would have inflicted pain upon us."
Learn knowledge, and when you acquire it, suppress it and do not mix it with laughter or play, lest hearts become frivolous.
One who laughs a laugh that is a thorough laugh from knowledge.

Narrated by 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): He asked Ka'b, "Who are the people of knowledge?" He said, "Those who act upon what they know." 'Umar said, "What removes knowledge from the hearts of scholars?" He said, "Greed."

I was visiting ‘Amru ibn an-Nu‘man when a messenger from Mus‘ab ibn az-Zubayr arrived bearing two thousand dirhams, saying, “The Amir sends you greetings and says, ‘We have not left a noble reciter but have sent him a kindness from us.’ Utilize these [dirhams] to support your expenses for this month.” He replied, “Convey greetings to the Amir and say to him, ‘Indeed, we have not recited the Qur’an seeking the world or its dirhams.’”

Asad ibn Musa narrated to me, Muawiya narrated to me, Hasan ibn Jabir narrated to me, from Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’di Karib Al-Kindi (may Allah be pleased with him): That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade certain things on the day of Khaybar: the donkey and others. Then he said: “It will come about that a man, reclining on his sofa, will be informed about my teachings and will say: ‘Between us and you is the Book of Allah. Whatever we find in it as lawful, we make lawful, and whatever we find in it as forbidden, we forbid.’ Do they not know that whatever the Messenger of Allah forbade is like what Allah forbade?"
Muhammad ibn Uyaynah narrated to me from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Katir, who said: "The Sunnah judges over the Quran, and the Quran does not judge over the Sunnah."

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me from Al-Awza’i, from Hassan, who said: "The Angel Gabriel would descend upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with the Sunnah just as he would descend upon him with the Quran."

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated from Al-Awza'i, from Makhul, who said: "The Sunnah are of two types: a Sunnah adhering to which is obligatory and abandoning it is disbelief, and a Sunnah adhering to which is a virtue and abandoning it is not burdensome."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated: "One day, I related a Hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ). A man said: 'Is there anything in the Book of Allah that contradicts this?' Sa'id replied: 'I do not think I should relate to you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while you question it in relation to the Book of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was more knowledgeable about the Book of Allah than you.'"

Narrated by Ibn Mas’ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "When you are reported a Hadith from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), consider it with that which is most likely to be true, that which is most guided, and that which is most righteous."

"When you are informed of something from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, consider the one who transmitted it – which one of them is most guided, most righteous, and most prepared [with knowledge]."

Narrated Abu Huraira (RA): Whenever he narrated a Hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would say: “He (the Messenger of Allah) ﷺ said: Whoever deliberately tells a lie against me, let him take his seat in the Fire.” Ibn Abbas, when he narrated, would say: “If you hear me narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and you do not find it in the Book of Allah, or it is not considered good (authentic), then know that I have lied against him.”
Narrated ‘Ikrimah: “Indeed, the most ascetic of people in this world are the people of knowledge.”
Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Recite (or remind each other) the Hadith (narrations of the Prophet), for the Hadith reminds (or stirs up) the Hadith (i.e., knowledge)."
Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: “Recite the Hadith, for the Hadith reminds one of the Hadith.”
Abu Sa’id al-Khudri (RA) said, "Recite the Hadith, for the Hadith reminds one of the Hadith."
Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me, from ‘Amr, who said: Tawus said to me, "Go, take us to sit with the people."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Qummi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Abi Mughira narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Discuss this hadith amongst yourselves, lest it slip away from you, for it is not like the Quran, which is collected and preserved. And if you do not discuss this hadith, it will slip away from you. And let none of you say, 'I narrated yesterday, so I will not narrate today,' rather, narrate yesterday, and narrate today, and narrate tomorrow."

Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Relate the hadith and remind yourselves of it, for if you do not remember it, it will vanish. And let no one say about a hadith he has heard, 'I have narrated it once,' for whoever heard it will increase in knowledge with it, and one who did not hear it will hear it."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Abu Awana narrated to me from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: "Discuss (the Hadith) amongst yourselves, for the revitalization of the Hadith is through discussing it."
Recount the Hadith amongst yourselves, for its remembrance is life.
Muhammad ibn Qudamah narrated to me from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Ziyad ibn Sa’d, who said: "Ibn Shihab used to relate (narrate) to the Bedouins."

Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to me, from Al-A'mash, who said: "Ismail ibn Raja' would gather the boys of the writing school and narrate to them, being cautious about that."
Narrated by Ibrahim: "Relate your story to those who desire it and to those who do not desire it, for it will become with you as if it were a recitation from an Imam."

Abu Ma'mar and Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me on the authority of 'Abd al-Salam, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of 'Ata, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas (May Allah be pleased with him), who said: "When you hear a hadith from us, deliberate upon it amongst yourselves."
Abu Ma'mar narrated: Yunus said: "We used to visit Hasan, and when we left his presence, we would discuss amongst ourselves."
"When any of you wishes to relate a Hadith, let him repeat it three times."

Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to me, from Yazid, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: "Reviving a Hadith is to remember it." Then Abdullah ibn Shaddad said to him: "May Allah have mercy on you, how many a Hadith have you revived in your breast that was once dead?"

Abdullah ibn Sa’id narrated: Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to me from his father, who said: “Al-Harith ibn Yazid al-‘Ukli, Ibn Shubrumah, Al-Qaaqa’ ibn Yazid, and Mughirah, whenever they prayed the last night prayer (Isha), they would sit for learning (religious knowledge), and nothing separated them except the Adhan (call) for Fajr (dawn).”
Malik related to me, saying: I heard Sharik mention, from Layth, from Ata, Tawus, and Mujahid, that they said from two of them: "There is no harm in conversing about jurisprudence."
Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: Abdul-Salam narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "There is nothing wrong with discussion in jurisprudence."
Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The studying of knowledge for an hour during the night is better than spending the entire night awake."

Abu Ma'mar and Muhammad ibn 'Isa reported from Hisham, that Hajjaj reported from Ata', who said: "We used to visit Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), and when we left his presence, we would discuss it, and Abu Zubayr was the one among us who best remembered his hadith."

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated: I heard al-Layth ibn Sa'd saying: "Ibn Shihab (Az-Zuhri) discussed a hadith one night after the 'Isha' prayer while sitting in a state of ritual purity. He remained in that gathering until morning." Marwan said: "He kept discussing the hadith."
"Whenever I met with 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, it was as if I was plunging into a sea."
Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Jarir narrated to me, from Uthman ibn Abdullah, who said: "Al-Harith al-'Ukli and his companions would gather at night and discuss jurisprudence."
Abdullah (RA) said, "Discuss this hadith, for its life lies in its discussion."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, he said: Al-Mas'udi narrated to me from 'Awn, who said: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said to his companions when they came to him: "Do you visit one another?" They said: "We are not left to do that." He said: "Then do you exchange gifts?" They said: "Yes, O Abu Abdur-Rahman! A man among us may lose his brother, so he walks in search of him to the farthest reaches of Kufa until he finds him." He said: "Indeed, you will remain in goodness as long as you do that."
Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, he said: Al-Walid narrated to me, from al-Awza'i, from Zuhri, who said: "The affliction of knowledge is forgetfulness, and abandoning review."
Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The affliction of knowledge is forgetfulness."
"Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Indeed, everything has a detriment, and the detriment of knowledge is forgetfulness."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The affliction of knowledge is forgetfulness, and its loss is to relate it to those who are not its people."
Al-Hasan said: "The bane of knowledge is forgetfulness."
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Discuss this hadith amongst yourselves and visit each other regarding it, for if you do not, it will be lost."
Bisr ibn al-Hakam narrated: I heard Sufyan say: Zuhri said: "I used to think that I had attained some knowledge, then I sat with ‘Ubaidullah, and it was as if I was in a valley of valleys."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Hammad ibn Salama from Humaid, who said: It was said to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him: "If you could unite the people on something?" He said: "I would not like that they did not differ." He then wrote to the regions and to the lands, instructing each community to rule according to what their scholars had agreed upon.

Yazid narrated from Al-Mas’udi, from ‘Awn ibn ‘Abdullah, who said: “I do not like that the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not differ. For if they gathered upon something and a man abandoned it, he abandoned the Sunnah. And if they differed, and a man took the statement of one of them, he took the Sunnah.”
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Hasan narrated to me, from Layth, from Tawus, who said: "Sometimes Ibn Abbas would have an opinion, then abandon it."

Uthman ibn 'Affan said to me, "‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said to me, ‘I have seen an opinion in old age.’ He said, ‘If you see fit to follow it, then follow it.’ Uthman said, ‘If we follow your opinion, then it is sound guidance, and if we follow the opinion of the elder before you, then he was indeed one of great insight.’ He said, ‘And Abu Bakr used to consider him as a father.’”
Ibrahim ibn al-Munzir al-Hizami narrated to me, Marwan ibn Muawiyah narrated to me, ‘Asim al-Ahwal narrated, saying: “I presented legal rulings to al-Sha’bi, and he approved them for me.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundir narrated to me, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told me: I said to Amr ibn Dinār: Did you hear Jabir ibn Abdullah say that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a man who passed through the mosque carrying arrows: "Hold onto the bowstring of your bow"? He said: Yes.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundir narrated to me, he said: I said to Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim: Did you hear your father relate from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, "used to kiss her while fasting?" He said: Yes.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to me, he said: Muskin ibn Bukayr narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah said: Mansur wrote to me with a Hadith, so I met him and said to him: "Shall I narrate it from you?" He said: "Isn't it the case that when you write to me, you have narrated to me?" I asked Ayyub as-Sakhtiyani, and he said: The same.

Zakarriya ibn 'Adi narrated to me, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me from Ma'mar, from Zuhri, who said: "I presented a book to him and said, 'Shall I relate it from you?' He said, 'And who tells it to you other than me?'"
"The presentation of a book and the narration of a hadith are equal."
"The presentation of the book and the narration of a hadith are equal."

Ibrahim ibn al-Munzir narrated to me, he said: Dawud ibn ‘Ata’ narrated to me, he said: Zayd ibn Aslam considered the outward appearance of a written text and a narration (Hadith) to be equal, and Ibn Abi Zayd also held that view.
"He (Malik) would see the apparent and the hidden as equal."

Qabisa narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to me from Al-A'mash, who said: Ibrahim used to stand up from his left side. I informed him about Sumay' al-Zayyat, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) "raised him up from his right side," and he grasped him.

Umar questioned the people, "Did any of you hear anything from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the fetus?" Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba stood up and said, "He decreed it as a slave or a female slave." Umar then questioned the people again, and the one to whom it was decreed stood up and said, "The Prophet (ﷺ) decreed it for me as a slave or a female slave." Umar questioned the people again, and the one against whom the decree was made stood up and said, "The Prophet (ﷺ) decreed against me a slave or a female slave." I said, "Do you decree against me in something that has not eaten, drunk, babbled, or spoken? That you expose it, and it is the most rightful of what is exposed?" The Prophet (ﷺ) seemed to be about to say something to me, and he said, "Is he eloquent?" Umar said, "If it had not reached me of the Prophet’s (ﷺ) decree, I would have made it a diyya between two diyyas."
Sa'id ibn 'Amir reported: Salam mentioned to me, from Ayyub, who said, "If you wish to know the fault of your teacher, sit with others."

We were discussing the death of a woman in Mecca. I said, "Her waiting period is from the day the news reaches her, due to the statement of Hasan, Qatada, and our companions." Then Talq bin Habib al-'Anzi met me and said, "You are generous, and you are from a people whose eyes are quick to perceive. I do not trust you regarding this." He said, "You have said a statement here contrary to the statement of the people of the city, and I do not trust you." I said, "Is there a difference regarding this?" He said, "Yes, her waiting period is from the day of her death." I then met Sa'id bin Jubair and asked him, and he said, "Her waiting period is from the day of her death." I asked Mujahid, and he said, "Her waiting period is from the day of her death." I asked 'Ata' bin Abi Rabah, and he said, "From the day of her death." I asked Abu Qilaba, and he said, "From the day of her death." I asked Muhammad bin Sirin, and he said, "From the day of her death." He said, "And Naafi' informed me that Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them) said, 'From the day of her death.'" I heard Ikrimah saying, "From the day of her death." He said, "And Jabir bin Zayd said, 'From the day of her death.'" He said, "And Ibn Abbas used to say, 'From the day of her death.'" Hammad said, "And I heard Layth narrate from Al-Hakam that Abdullah bin Mas'ud said, 'From the day of her death.'" He said, "And Ali said, 'From the day the news reaches her.'" Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman said, "I say, 'From the day of her death.'"

Narrated by Al-Hakim bin Mas’ud: We came to Umar (regarding the Musharaka) and he did not share (the profit). Then we came to him the following year and he did share (the profit). We said to him, and he said: “That was according to what we had decided, and this is according to what we had decided.”

Yaqoob ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Rawh narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj al-Aswad narrated to me, saying: Ibn Munabbih said: "In the past, the people of knowledge were stingy with their knowledge towards the people of the world, so the people of the world desired their knowledge, and they would give them their worldly possessions. But the people of knowledge today have given their knowledge to the people of the world, so the people of the world have become indifferent to their knowledge, and they have become stingy with their worldly possessions towards them."
Muḥammad b. Yūsuf > Sufyān > Ṭāriq > Ḥakīm b. Jābir [Machine] Abdullah said, "Indeed, everything has a harm, and the harm of knowledge is forgetfulness."

"O possessor of knowledge, act upon your knowledge, and give generously from your wealth. Restrain your words unless they contain a beneficial narration that will benefit you before your Lord. O possessor of knowledge, that which you have learned but not acted upon invalidates your argument and excuse before your Lord when you meet Him. O possessor of knowledge, that which you are commanded to do by obedience to Allah will occupy you from that which you are forbidden from by disobedience to Allah. O possessor of knowledge, do not be strong in the work of others, and weak in your own work. O possessor of knowledge, let what is for others not distract you from what is for you. O possessor of knowledge, sit with the scholars, mingle with them, and listen to them, and abandon disputing with them. O possessor of knowledge, honor the scholars for their knowledge, and humble the ignorant for their ignorance, and do not estrange yourself from them, but bring them close and teach them. O possessor of knowledge, do not relate a narration in a gathering until you understand it, and do not respond to a person in his words until you know what he has said to you. O possessor of knowledge, do not be deceived by Allah, nor be deceived by people, for deception regarding Allah is abandoning His command, and deception regarding people is following their desires. Beware from Allah of that which He has warned you against from Himself, and beware from people of their tribulation. O possessor of knowledge, the light of the day is not perfected except by the sun, likewise wisdom is not perfected except by obedience to Allah. O possessor of knowledge, a plant does not thrive except with water and soil, likewise faith does not thrive except with knowledge and action. O possessor of knowledge, every traveler is provisioned, and he will find when he needs his provision what he provisioned, and likewise every worker will find when he needs his work in the Hereafter what he did in the world. O possessor of knowledge, if Allah intends to encourage you to worship Him, know that He only intends to make clear to you your honor upon Him, so do not turn to others, lest you return from His honor to His ignominy. O possessor of knowledge, it is lighter for you to move stones and iron than to relate a narration to one who does not understand it. And the one who relates a narration to one who does not understand it is like one who calls the deceased and sets a table for the people of the graves."
ʿAffān > Ḥammād b. Salamah > Abū Ḥamzah al-Tammār > al-Ḥasan [Machine] Al-Hasan said, "The ruin of knowledge is forgetfulness.

“Anas ibn Malik (RA) said: ‘After we were discouraged from initiating greetings to the Prophet (peace be upon him), we would be pleased when a bedouin or an intelligent Arab would come forward and ask the Prophet (peace be upon him) a question while we were in his presence. So, while we were like that, an Arab came and prostrated himself between the hands of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: ‘O Muhammad!
