Your messenger came to us and claimed that you claim that Allah has sent you.’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘He told the truth.’ He said: ‘By the One who raised the heavens and spread out the earth and established the mountains, has Allah sent you?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then your messenger claimed that you claim that there are five prayers upon us in the day and night?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘He told the truth.’ He said: ‘By the One who sent you, has Allah commanded you with this?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then your messenger claimed that you claim that there is fasting for a month in the year upon us?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘He told the truth.’ He said: ‘By the One who sent you, has Allah commanded you with this?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then your messenger claimed that you claim that there is Zakat upon us from our wealth?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘He told the truth.’ He said: ‘By the One who sent you, has Allah commanded you with this?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then your messenger claimed that you claim that there is Hajj to the House for whoever can afford the way to it?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘He told the truth.’ He said: ‘By the One who sent you, has Allah commanded you with this?’ The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘By the One who sent you with the truth, I will not leave anything of them, nor will I exceed them.’ Then the Arab stood up, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘If the Arab has told the truth, he has entered Paradise.’”

A man from Banu Sa'd bin Bakr came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "As-salamu alaykum, O nephew of the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib." The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "And upon you." He said, "I am a man from your uncles, from Banu Sa'd bin Bakr, and I am an envoy and representative of my people to you. I ask you a question, and I will intensify my questioning, and I invoke you, and I will intensify my invocation of you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Take your ease, O brother of Banu Sa'd." He said, "Who created you and those who came before you, and who is the creator of those who will come after you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah." He said, "I invoke you by that, did He send you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." He said, "Who created the seven heavens and the seven earths, and provided sustenance between them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah." He said, "I invoke you by that, did He send you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." He said, "Indeed, we have found in your Book, and your messengers have commanded us to pray five prayers during the day and night at their appointed times. I invoke you by that, did He command you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." He said, "Indeed, we have found in your Book, and your messengers have commanded us to take from the edges of our wealth and return it to our poor. I invoke you by that, did He command you with that?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes." Then he said, "As for the fifth, I will not ask you about it, nor do I have any reservation about it." Then he said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will act upon it, and whoever obeys me from my people will also act upon it." Then he returned, and the Prophet (ﷺ) laughed until his back teeth were exposed. Then he said, "By the One whose soul is in My Hand, if he speaks the truth, he will surely enter Paradise."

Banū Sa'd ibn Bakr sent Ḍimām ibn Tha'labah to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he came to him, tethering his camel to the door of the mosque. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his companions, and Ḍimām was a handsome man with thick hair and two forelocks. He stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "Which of you is Ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I am Ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib." He said, "Muhammad?" He said, "Yes." He said, "O Ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, I ask you a question and will be insistent in it, so do not find aversion in your heart." He said, "I do not find aversion in my heart." He said, "Ask about whatever appears to you." He said, "I invoke you by Allah, your God and the God of those who were before you, and the God of those who will be after you, has Allah sent you to us as a messenger?" He said, "Yes, by Allah." He said, "I invoke you by Allah, your God and the God of those who were before you, and the God of those who will be after you, has Allah commanded you to worship Him alone, associating nothing with Him?" He said, "Yes, by Allah." He said, "I invoke you by Allah, your God and the God of those who were before you, and the God of those who will be after you, has

"Cleanliness is a part of faith, and praise be to Allah fills the scales, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, fill the space between the heavens and the earth, and prayer is light, and charity is a proof [of your faith], and ablution is a radiance, and the Qur’an is an argument [for you] or against you, and all people rise in the morning – either selling themselves [into slavery], then setting them free, or destroying them [with their actions]."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, tied them in my hand, or he said: tied them in his hand and his hand in mine, saying: “SubhanAllah fills half of the scale, and Alhamdulilah fills the scale, and Allahu Akbar fills between the heavens and the earth, and the ablution is half of the faith, and fasting is half of patience.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Be upright, and you will not count [your deeds]. And know that the best of your deeds is prayer.” And another said: “Indeed, among your best of deeds is prayer.” “And none will maintain purification [i.e., ablution] except a believer.”
“Straighten yourselves [in religious matters], be moderate, and the best of your deeds is the prayer. And none will maintain the ablution except a believer.”

Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, used to perform all the prayers with a single ablution, and Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to perform ablution for every prayer, and he recited the verse: "O you who believe! When you rise up for prayer, wash your faces and your hands..." (Surah Al-Ma’idah, verse 6).

I asked [Abdullah ibn Umar], “Do you see that Ibn Umar performs ablution for every prayer, whether in a state of purity or otherwise? What is the reason for that?” He said, “Asma’ bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab informed me that Abdullah ibn Hanbalah ibn Abi Amir told her that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, ‘I was commanded to perform ablution for every prayer, whether in a state of purity or otherwise. But when that became difficult for [the people], I was commanded to use the siwak for every prayer.’ And Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) considered that he had the strength to do so, so he did not omit performing ablution for every prayer.

Narrated by Ibn Buridah from his father: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer until the day of the conquest of Makkah. On that day, he performed the prayers with a single ablution, wiping over his Khuffs.” Umar (RA) said to him, “I saw you doing something you had not done before?” He (the Prophet) said, “I intentionally did it, O Umar.” Abu Muhammad said: “The action of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicates that the meaning of Allah’s statement, ‘When you rise for prayer, wash your faces…’ (Surah Al-Ma’idah, 5:6), is for every one who is in a state of impurity, not for the purified. And from this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), ‘There is no ablution except from impurity.’ And Allah knows best.”

Yalaa ibn ‘Ubayd narrated to me, Muhammad ibn ‘Amr narrated to me, from Abu Salama, from Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: “I was with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during one of his journeys, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would go far away when he needed to relieve himself.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me from Ibn Sirin, from 'Amr ibn Wahb, from Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would move away when he relieved himself." Abu Muhammad said: "That is the etiquette."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever uses kohl (eye-liner), let him use an odd number. Whoever does that, he has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm. Whoever uses a styptic (to stop bleeding), let him use an odd number. Whoever does that, he has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm. Whoever eats, let him interspace (between bites). If he interspaces, he has done well, and if he does not, let him spit it out. If something sticks to his tongue, let him swallow it. Whoever goes to the place of defecation, let him cover himself. If he does not find anything but a sand dune, let him turn his back to it, for the devils play with the seats of the sons of Adam. Whoever does that, he has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm."
He (Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him) would seek refuge for his needs in a target or a palm grove.

Narrated by Sahl bin Hunayf (RA): The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me, "You are My messenger to the people of Makkah. Say to them: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sends you greetings and orders you that when you come out, you should not face the Qibla (direction of prayer) nor turn your backs towards it."

Narrated Abu Nu’aim, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to me from Zuhri, from ‘Atta bin Zubayr, from Abu Ayyub, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When you go to the place of defecation, do not face the Qibla with your behind or urine, and do not turn your back towards it.” Abu Ayyub said: “Then we migrated to Syria and found lavatories built facing the Qibla, so we would turn aside and seek forgiveness from Allah.” Abu Muhammad said: “This Hadith is more authentic than the Hadith of ‘Abd al-Karim, and ‘Abd al-Karim is almost abandoned.”
Narrated Anas (RA): The Prophet (ﷺ) used to lower his garment until it reached the ground. Abu Muhammad said: It is an etiquette, and it is more reliable than the Hadith of Mughira.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “I saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) on the roof of our house, and then I saw him sitting on two bricks, facing towards the House of Jerusalem.”

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, and Hammad narrated to me from Abu Wail, from Hudhaifa (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to a place where people were urinating and he urinated while standing." Abu Muhammad said: "I do not know of any dislike in it."
Narrated Anas bin Malik (RA): Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would enter the lavatory, he would say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from evil and from those who do evil.”
Narrated ‘Aisha: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said: “When anyone of you goes to the place of defecation, he should go with three stones to cleanse himself with them, and they suffice for him.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Three things contain no filth." He meant: purification (Istihabah).

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to him, "You are my messenger to the people of Makkah, so say: ‘The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) sends you greetings and orders you not to use bones or date stones for purification.’" Abu ‘Aasim said once: and forbids you or orders you.
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Let none of you touch his private parts with his right hand, nor wipe himself with it.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am only like a father to you, teaching you. So, do not face (the Qibla) and do not turn your backs to it. And when you bathe, do not use your right hand.” And he used to order us to use three stones, and forbade us from excrement and the worn-out bones. Zakariyya said: meaning the worn-out bones.

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would go to relieve himself, I and a young boy would accompany him with a bucket and a stick."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abu Mu'adh, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, when he exited the lavatory, a servant would bring a dipper of water with which he would perform istinja (ritual cleansing). Abu Muhammad said: Abu Mu'adh’s name is Ata' ibn Muneeb, the father of Abi Maymuna.
My aunt, who was married to Hudhaifa (may Allah be pleased with him), informed me that Hudhaifa used to perform istinja (ritual cleansing after urination or defecation) with water.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Bring me water." Then he went to the privy. I brought him water, and he performed ablution, then wiped his hand over the earth, and then washed his hands.

Malik related to me, from Isra'il, from Yusuf ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) informed him that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would say, "Your forgiveness," when he exited the lavatory.
Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I have increased upon you (in regard to) the siwak."
Narrated Anas bin Malik (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “I have encouraged you greatly regarding the siwak.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Were it not that it would be burdensome for my community, I would have ordered them to use the siwak with every prayer." Abu Muhammad said: "Meaning, the siwak."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The siwak is a purifier for the mouth, and pleasing to the Lord."
Abu Wail reported from Hudhaifa (RA) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to brush his teeth with a siwak when he stood up for the night prayer (Tahajjud).
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Allah does not accept a prayer without purification, nor a charity from illicit gain.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The key to prayer is purification, its prohibition is the takbir, and its termination is the taslim."

Narrated by Safwan ibn Mu’awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would perform ablution with a mudd and bathe with a sa’ during the days of heat.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Jabir narrated to me, he said: I heard Anas (RA) saying: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to perform ablution with the makkah and bathe with five makkahs."

Zayriyyah ibn ‘Adiyy narrated to me, he said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Amr narrated to me, from ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Aqil, from Rubayyi’ bint Mu’awwidh ibn ‘Afraa – may Allah be pleased with them both – who said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would come to our home, and I would bring a small earthenware vessel for him, which held a mudd or a little less than a mudd, or a quarter of a mudd, and I would pour water into it, and he would perform ablution three times.”
"There is no purification (ablution) for one who does not mention the name of Allah upon it."

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Nu'man ibn Salim narrated to me, saying: I heard Ibn Amr ibn Aus recounting, from his grandfather, Aus ibn Abi Aus, that he saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, perform ablution and he sniffed (his nose) three times. I said to him, "What was the reason for sniffing three times?" He said, "He washed his hands three times."

Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) performed ablution; he rinsed his mouth, sniffed his nose, washed his face three times, his hands three times, wiped his head, and washed his feet three times. Then he said, “I have seen the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) perform ablution as I have performed it.” Then he said, “Whoever performs ablution like my ablution and then prays two rak’ahs without engaging in idle talk in them, his past sins will be forgiven.”

"He (Abdullah ibn Zayd) called for a vessel of water and poured it over his hands, washing them three times. Then he washed his face three times, and his hands up to the elbows twice, twice. Then he said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) perform ablution." Yahya reported: Yahya narrated to me, telling me that 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salama narrated to me from 'Amr ibn Yahya from his father from 'Abdullah ibn Zayd from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) something similar to this.

Abu 'Aasim narrated: Sufyan ath-Thawri narrated to me: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me from 'Ata' ibn Yasir, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Shall I not tell you about the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)? He performed ablution once, or he said: once."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, on the authority of ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darwardi, who narrated to me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasir, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) performed ablution once, and he combined the rinsing (of the mouth) and the sniffing (of the nose).”

"Verily, should I guide you to that which erases sins and increases in good deeds? " They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Perfecting the ablution upon the disliked things, frequently stepping to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, who (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "We were commanded to perform ablution completely."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Zaidah narrated to me, he said: Khalid ibn ‘Alqamah al-Hamdani narrated to me, he said: ‘Abd al-Khair said: ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) entered the courtyard after the Fajr prayer, and sat in the courtyard. Then he said to a servant of his: “Bring me purification.” So the servant brought him a vessel with water and a cup. ‘Abd al-Khair said: “And we were sitting watching him.” Then he put his right hand in his mouth, filled his mouth, rinsed, and sneezed, and scattered with his left hand. He did this three times. Then he said: “Whoever wishes to see the purification of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), then this is his purification.” Abu Naim narrated to me, he said: Hasan ibn ‘Uqbah al-Muradi narrated to me, he said: ‘Abd al-Khair narrated to me on his chain of narration, similar to this.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "If one sneezes, he should say 'Praise be to Allah,' and if one passes urine, he should say 'Ease and well-being.'"

Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to me, he said: Israel narrated to me from Amir ibn Shaqiq, from Shaqiq ibn Salama, who said: I saw Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) perform ablution. He cleansed his beard and said: "Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) perform ablution."
Narrated: 'Auf ibn Malik from Waid of the Banu al-Muntafiq, who said, "When you perform ablution, ensure you wash it completely and clean between your fingers."
Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Woe to the heels from the Fire! Ensure you rinse thoroughly in ablution.”

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would pass by us while people were performing ablution, and he would say: "Ensure you rinse thoroughly." Abu al-Qasim (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Woe to the heels from the Fire." Abu Muhammad said: "This narration is more appealing to me than the narration of Abdullah ibn Amr."

Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to me, that Isra'il narrated to me, from Amir ibn Shaqiq, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, who said: I saw Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) perform ablution, and he wiped over his head and ears, both their outer and inner surfaces, then he said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) do as I did, or similar to what I did.”

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to me, he said: Ibn Lahi’a narrated to me, he said: Habban ibn Wa’id narrated to me from his father, from Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn ‘Asim al-Mazini, who said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performing ablution with a jugfah (a small skin water-carrier). He rinsed his mouth and sniffed his nose, then washed his face three times, then washed his hands three times, then wiped his head, and washed his feet until he cleansed them. Then he wiped his head with water other than the water that remained in his hands.” Abu Muhammad said: He intends by this to explain the wiping of the first (time).

Abu al-Mughira reported: "We were told by al-Awza'i, from Yahya, from Abu Salama, from Ja'far ibn 'Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) wiping over the khuffs and the head covering." It was said to Abu Muhammad: "Do you act upon this?" He said: "Indeed, by Allah!"
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed ablution, and he washed his private parts.

I asked my aunt Maymunah about the way the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed ghusl (ritual bath) for janaabah (major ritual impurity). She said: “An vessel would be brought to him, and he would pour it with his right hand over his left hand, and then wash his private parts and whatever had been affected. Then he would perform ablution (wudu) as for prayer. Then he would wash his head and the rest of his body. Then he would turn around and wash his feet. Then a towel would be brought and placed between his hands, and he would shake his fingers without touching it.”

I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during a night journey, and he said, "Do you have water?" I said, "Yes." So he dismounted from his camel and walked until he disappeared from my sight in the darkness of the night. Then he returned, and I poured water from the waterskin over him. He washed his hands and face. He was wearing a woolen cloak, and he could not draw his arms out of it until he pulled them out from the bottom of the cloak. Then he washed his arms and wiped over his head. I intended to remove his sandals, but he said, "Leave them, for I have admitted them clean," and he wiped over them.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) designated three days and their nights for the traveler, and one day and its night for the resident – meaning the wiping over the khuffs.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd al-Khair, who said: I saw Ali performing ablution, wiping over his sandals, and he widened [the wiping area]. Then he said: "If I had not seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, doing as you see me doing, I would have thought that the inner sides of the feet were more deserving of wiping than their outer sides." Abu Muhammad said: This hadith is abrogated by the statement of Allah, the Exalted: "And wash your faces and your hands to the elbows and your feet up to the ankles." [Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 6].

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir Al-Ghifaari: I went out with Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) in the campaign of Tabuk. Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) sat with his companions one day and said, “Whoever performs ablution when the sun rises, does it perfectly, and then prays two Rak’ahs, he is absolved of all sins as if he was born just now.” ‘Uqba said, “I said, ‘Praise be to Allah Who has granted me the opportunity to hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).’” ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab (RA) who was sitting opposite to me, said, “Are you amazed by this?” I said, “Yes.” ‘Umar said, “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said something more amazing than this before this.” I said, “What was that?” He said, “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ‘Whoever performs ablution perfectly, then raises his gaze towards the sky and says: ‘I testify that there is no god but Allah alone, without any partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger,’ eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he will enter through whichever he pleases.’”

Abu Ayyub reported: We went on an expedition to Salasil and returned to Mu'awiya. Abu Ayyub said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever performs ablution as commanded and prays as commanded, his past sins are forgiven.' Is it so, O 'Uqba?" He said, "Yes."

"When the Muslim or believing slave washes his face, all sins that his eyes have looked at come out with the water or the last drop of the water. And when he washes his hands, all sins that his hands have committed come out with the water or the last drop of the water, until he emerges free from sins."

Yahyá ibn Hasan narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from ‘Alí ibn Zayd, from Abú ‘Uthmán, who said: I was with Salmán (may Allah be pleased with him) under a tree, and he took a dry branch from it and shook it until its leaves fell off. He said: Do you not ask me why I do this? I said to him: Why did you do it? He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did this to me. Then he said: "Indeed, when a Muslim performs ablution and perfects it, and prays the five [daily] prayers, his sins fall off as these leaves fall off." Then he recited: "And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of night." [Quran 11:114] … to the saying: "That is a reminder for those who remember." [Quran 11:114]
Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, and one of us would suffice with the ablution as long as he did not experience impurity.

"Narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If one of you feels a movement in his body during prayer and is unsure whether he has passed wind or not, he should not turn away until he hears a sound or smells an odor.'"

Narrated ‘Attiya bin Qais Al-Kal’i: That Mu’awiya bin Abi Sufyan said, “The eyes are the wakefulness of the sentinel; when the eyes sleep, the sentinel becomes negligent.” It was said to Abu Muhammad Abdullah: Do you say this? He said: No, if one sleeps standing and is not in a state of purification (ablution).

I used to experience a significant discharge of pre-seminal fluid (madhy). Consequently, I would perform frequent ablutions (ghusl) due to it. I mentioned this to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and asked him about it. He said, "It suffices you from that, the ablution (wudu)." I said, "Then what about what affects my garment from it?" He said, "Take a handful of water and pour it over where you see it has affected it."

Abu al-Mughira reported: Sufyan narrated to me from al-Awza'i, from Zuhri, who narrated to me from Ibn Hazm, from Urwa, from Busra bint Safwan (may Allah be pleased with them), that she heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saying: "A man performs ablution after sexual contact."

Narrated By Bisrah bint Safwan (RA) that she heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying: "If anyone touches his private parts, he should perform ablution." Abu Muhammad said: This is more reliable concerning touching the private parts, and he said: The ablution is more established.

Narrated by Zaid bin Thabit (RA): I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Wudu (ablution) is from that which fire has touched." It was said to Abu Muhammad (Malik): Do you act upon this? He said: No.

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: Layth narrated to me, and he said: ‘Uqail narrated to me from Ibn Shihab, and he said: Ja’far bin ‘Amr bin Umayya narrated to me, that his father, ‘Amr bin Umayya, (May Allah be pleased with him) informed him, that he saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) skinning a sheep, and he was called for prayer, so he threw the knife he was using, and then he stood up and prayed without performing ablution.

Some men from the tribe of Mudlij came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we are sailors, and we hunt on the sea. We may stay out for one, two, three, or four nights. We carry fresh water for drinking, and if we perform ablution with it, we fear for ourselves. If we prefer ourselves and perform ablution from the sea, we feel something from it, and we fear that it may not be pure. ” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Perform ablution from it, for its water is pure and its dead creatures are lawful.”

A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “We ride the sea, and we have little water with us. If we bathe with it, we become thirsty. Can we perform ablution with seawater?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Its water is purifying, and its dead creature is permissible.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Let none of you urinate into stagnant water, and then bathe in it."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Zubair, from 'Ubaidullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, being asked about water that is found in the desert and what befalls it from animals and wild beasts. He said: "When water reaches two qullahs, nothing makes it impure."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about water and what impurities it might contain from animals and wild beasts. He ﷺ said: "If the water is two qullahs, it does not carry impurity."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi and Abu Zayd, Sa’id ibn al-Rabee’, narrated to us: “We were told by Shu’bah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to visit me while I was sick and senseless. He performed ablution and poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained my senses.”

A woman among the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) stood up and performed ghusl (ritual bath) in a small basin from janabah (major ritual impurity). The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) then rose to bathe in the same basin. She said, "I have already performed ghusl in it before you." The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "There is no janabah on water."

Kabshah bint Ka'b ibn Malik, who was married to the son of Abu Qatadah, narrated: Abu Qatadah entered upon her and she poured water for ablution. A cat came and drank from it. Abu Qatadah inclined the vessel towards it so that it drank. Kabshah said: He saw me looking (at him), and he said: "Are you astonished, O daughter of my brother?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'They are not impure, rather they are among those who go around you and the female ones who go around you.'"
Narrated by Abdullah bin Mughaffal that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If a dog licks a vessel, wash it seven times, and the eighth time, rub it with earth."
Maymunah (RA) narrated: A mouse fell into a vessel of clarified butter and died. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Throw it and that which is around it and eat it."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by two graves, and he said: “Indeed, they are being punished in their graves, and their punishment is not for a major sin. One of them used to spread gossip, and the other used to not deflect from urine, or from the urine.” Then he took a fresh palm leaf and broke it, and planted a piece of it at the head of each grave. Then he said: “Perhaps it will be alleviated for them until they become dry.”

Jarir narrated: "A bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and when he stood up, he urinated in a corner of the mosque. The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) protested loudly, but the Prophet (ﷺ) stopped them, then he called for a bucket of water and poured it over his urine."

Umm Qais bint Mihsan reported: "I brought my son to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was not yet able to eat food. I sat him in his lap, and he urinated on him. He then called for water and poured it over him, without washing him."

Yahiya ibn Hassan narrated to me, he said: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amara, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim At-Taymi, from a wet nurse of Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn ‘Auf, that she asked Um Salamah, and she said: “I lengthen the hem of my garment and walk in a dirty place?” Um Salamah said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is purified by what comes after it.’” It was said to Abu Muhammad: “Do you act upon this?” He said: “No, I do not know.”

We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he dismounted, then called for purification water and performed ablution. The call to prayer was then announced, and he led the people in prayer. When he finished his prayer, he saw a man secluded who had not prayed with the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "What prevented you, O so-and-so, from praying with the people?" He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was in a state of major ritual impurity and had no water." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Use the dust; it is sufficient for you."

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: Two men set out on a journey and the time for prayer approached them, but they had no water. So they performed Tayammum (ablution with dust) and prayed. Then they found water afterward within the time (of the prayer). One of them repeated the prayer with ablution, but the other did not. Then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned this to him. He said to the one who did not repeat (the prayer): “You have followed the Sunnah, and your prayer is sufficient for you.” And he said to the one who performed ablution and repeated (the prayer): “You have two rewards.”
Narrated ‘Ammar bin Yasir (RA) that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say while performing Tayammum: “One strike to the face and the hands.” Abdullah (RA) said: Its chain is authentic.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated: "She borrowed a necklace from Asma (may Allah be pleased with her), and it was lost. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) sent some of his companions to look for it. They were overtaken by the time of prayer, so they prayed without performing ablution. When they came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), they complained to him about that, and the verse on Tayammum was revealed.” Then Usayd ibn Hudhayr said: “May Allah reward you with good, and by Allah, no matter what happens to you, Allah provides you with a way out of it, and He bestows blessings upon the Muslims through it.”

Maymunah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: “I prepared water for the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He poured it over his hands and began to wash his private parts with it. When he finished, he wiped it [the water] on the ground or a wall, and Sulaiman was unsure about this. Then he rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and forearms, and poured water over his head and body. When he finished, he moved aside, and washed his feet. I gave him a garment [to dry himself], but he refused and began to shake [the water] off with his hand. Maymunah said: “So I covered him until he finished bathing.” Sulaiman said: “Salim mentioned that this was a ghusl for a major ritual impurity (janabah).”

"Narrated Aisha (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would start by washing his hands, then perform ablution like for prayer, then he would put his hand into the water and run it through the roots of his hair until he felt that the skin had been cleansed. Then he would scoop with his hand three times and pour it over his head, and then he would bathe."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to perform ghusl from a single vessel due to janaabah."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to bathe from a single vessel, which was a large basin."

Narrated ‘Ali (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Whoever leaves even the space of a hair’s breadth of Janabah (impurity) unwashed, it will be afflicted with such and such a punishment from the Fire.” ‘Ali (RA) said: “Because of this, I began to wash my head, and he (the Prophet) used to cut his hair.”

Abu Mughira narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: It reached me that Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: I heard Ibn Abbas reporting: A man was wounded in the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him). Then he experienced a nocturnal emission. He was ordered to perform ghusl (ritual bath), and he died. This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he said: "They killed him, may Allah kill them! Did they not know that asking was the cure?" Ata' said: It reached me that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about this afterward, and he said: "If he had washed his body and left his head as it was, where the wound was."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Thabit, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to go around his wives in a single day.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once went around all his wives in a single night.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once rode me behind him, and he confided in me a piece of knowledge that I would not relate to anyone of the people. And the Prophet ﷺ preferred to conduct his affairs in seclusion, whether it was a target or a date palm grove.

Umar (RA) asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), “Does Janabah (sexual impurity) befall me at night?” So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to wash his private parts and perform ablution, then to sleep.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: I asked Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) how the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would act when he intended to sleep while being in a state of ritual impurity (junub). She said: “He would perform the ablution (wudu) as he performs it for prayer, then he would sleep.”
Narrated ‘Abdu Allah ibn Sa’d, who was acceptable among the people of Madinah, from Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Water comes from water."

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, Layth narrated to me, ‘Uqail narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl ibn Sa’d As-Sa’idi, may Allah be pleased with him, who had witnessed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and heard from him while he was fifteen years old when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away. He said: Ubayy ibn Ka’b, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that the legal opinion (fatwa) they were given regarding the statement, "Water comes from water," was a concession that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, permitted in the early days of Islam, then later he ordered washing (ghusl). Abdullah said: Another person said: Zuhri narrated to me that some of those who were content with Sahl ibn Sa’d informed him.

Ubayy (may Allah be pleased with him) reported: “The legal opinion (fatwa) they were given was, ‘Water is from water,’ which was a concession permitted by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the early days of Islam or time, and then he bathed afterwards.”
Narrated Abu Huraira (RA) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If a man sits between her four parts and then exerts himself, then the obligatory bath (ghusl) becomes due."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me from Ata' al-Khurasani, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib saying: My aunt, Khawla bint Hakim as-Sulamiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, "Does a woman experience nocturnal emission?" He ordered her to perform ghusl.

Narrated ‘Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that Um Sulaim, the mother of the children of Abu Talha (RA), came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: “O Messenger of Allah, Allah does not feel shy of the truth. What about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees, should she perform ghusl (ritual bath)?” He (ﷺ) said: “Yes.” ‘Aisha said: “I said: ‘How can a woman see that?’” So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to her and said: “May your right hand be covered with dust! From where does such a thing come?”

Narrated Anas: Umm Sulaym entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while Umm Salama was with him. Umm Sulaym said, "Does a woman see in her dream what a man sees?" Umm Salama said, "May your hands wither, Umm Sulaym! You have disgraced the women." The Prophet ﷺ said, defending Umm Sulaym, "Rather, may your hands wither! You are the one who has disgraced them. The best of you are those who inquire about what concerns them. If a woman sees water, let her perform ghusl. " Umm Salama said, "Do women have water?" He ﷺ said, "Yes. How else would they resemble their children? Women are like the branches of men."

Narrated Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said concerning a man who awakens and finds a wetness, but does not recall a dream: “Let him perform ghusl (ritual bath), and if he sees a dream and does not see wetness, then there is no ghusl upon him.”
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When anyone of you wakes up from sleep, let him not dip his hand into the water for ablution until he washes it three times."

We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when he went to relieve himself. Then he returned, and food was brought. Someone said, “Should you not perform ablution?” He said, “Do I perform ablution before praying?”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: Um Habibah, the daughter of Jahsh, experienced bleeding while she was with Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf for seven years. She complained about this to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “This is not a menstrual period; it is merely a discharge. When the menstrual period comes, cease prayer, and when it departs, perform ghusl and then pray.” Aisha said: “So she would perform ghusl for every prayer, then pray. She would sit on a cushion belonging to her sister, Zainab bint Jahsh, to the extent that the color of the blood would appear on the water.”
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would engage in marital relations while fasting."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to practice intercourse while fasting.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: Sulaiman narrated to me from Thabit ibn Ubaid, from al-Qasim, from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to her, "Hand me the container of dates." She said: "Indeed, I am menstruating." He said: "Indeed, it is not in your hand."

Fatima bint al-Mundhir reported from her grandmother Asma bint Abu Bakr, who said: I heard a woman asking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) how she should deal with her garment when she became clean from her menstrual period. He (ﷺ) said: "If you see blood in it, rub it, then wring it, then rinse it in the rest of your garment, and then pray in it."

A woman from the Ansar asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about menstruation. He said: “Take your water and sidr (lote tree) leaves, then perform ablution and purify yourself, then pour it over your head until it reaches the hair of your head, then take a piece of cloth that is held (firmly).” She said: “How should I do that, O Messenger of Allah?” He remained silent. She said: “How should I do that, O Messenger of Allah?” He remained silent. Then Aisha, the mother of the believers, may Allah be pleased with her, said: “Take a piece of cloth that is held firmly and follow the traces of the blood with it.” And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was listening, and he did not reproach her.

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, he said: Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated to me from his father, from 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: Fatima bint Abi Hubaysh came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who suffers from excessive bleeding and does not become pure." She asked, "Should I abandon prayer?" He (the Prophet) said: "No. It is merely a vein. When the menstrual flow comes, abandon prayer, and when it stops, wash it off and pray."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) reported: The daughter of Jahsh experienced a flow (menstruation) during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered her to perform ablution for every prayer. She would enter a vessel filled with water and immerse herself in it, then exit it, and the blood would still be prevalent upon it, and she would then pray.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "She was only Fulana." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) had ordered her to perform ablution for every prayer. When that became difficult for her, he ordered her to combine Dhuhr and Asr with one ablution, and Maghrib and Isha with one ablution, and to perform ablution for Fajr.” Abu Muhammad said: "The people say she was Sahla bint Suhayl.” Yazid ibn Harun said: "Sahla bint Suhayl."

Hashim ibn Qasim narrated to us on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: I asked ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Qasim about the woman suffering from excessive flow (istihada), and he informed me, from his father, from ‘Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), that a woman suffered from excessive flow in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and she was ordered. I said to ‘Abd al-Rahman: Did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) order her? He said: I do not relate to you anything about the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He said: “She was ordered to postpone the Dhuhr (noon) prayer and hasten the ‘Asr (afternoon) prayer, and to perform ghusl (full ablution) for them. And to postpone the Maghrib (sunset) prayer and hasten the ‘Isha’ (night) prayer, and to perform ghusl (full ablution) for them, and to perform ghusl (full ablution) for the Fajr (dawn) prayer.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: Um Habibah, the daughter of Jahsh, suffered from a condition resembling menstruation for seven years while she was with Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. She complained about this to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to her: “You are not experiencing menstruation; it is merely a vein. When the menstrual flow comes, cease prayer, and when it stops, perform ghusl and pray.” Aisha said: “She would perform ghusl for every prayer, then pray. She would sit on a cushion belonging to her sister, Zainab bint Jahsh, to the extent that the color of the blood would appear above the water.”

Fatima bint Abi Hubaysh said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who suffers from excessive bleeding, should I leave off the prayer?” He said: “No, it is merely a vein, and it is not menstruation. When menstruation comes, leave off the prayer, and when it ceases, wash away the blood and perform ablution and pray.” His son, Hisham, said: “My father used to say: She performs ghusl like the first [menstruation], then whatever comes after that. Thus, she is purified and prays.”

A man informed me, on the authority of Um Salama, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that a woman who suffered bleeding during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) asked Um Salama to inquire for her from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). He (peace and blessings be upon him) said to her, "Let her observe the number of nights and days she used to experience it before it ceased, and its proportion of the month. She should abstain from prayer during that period. Once that period has passed, and the time of prayer arrives, she should perform ghusl, and wear a clean garment, then pray."
Um Habibah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: “O Messenger of Allah, I was overcome by bleeding.” He said: “Wash yourself and pray.”

Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: Um Habibah, the daughter of Jahsh, came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), for she had been experiencing bleeding for seven years. She complained to him about it and asked him for a ruling regarding it. He said to her: “This is not menstruation; it is merely a vein. So, perform ablution and pray.” Aisha said: Um Habibah would perform ablution for every prayer and pray. She would sit on a cushion, and the redness of the blood would appear above the water, and then she would pray.

Aisha narrated: Umm Habiba, daughter of Jahsh, experienced excessive bleeding during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered her to perform ablution for every prayer. She would immerse herself in a vessel filled with water, then come out of it, and the bleeding would still be dominant, so she would pray. Ahmad ibn Khalid narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Zuhri, from al-Qasim: "She was Badia daughter of Ghilan al-Thaqafiyya." And Ahmad ibn Khalid narrated: Muhammad narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Abdurrahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Aisha, who said: "She was Sahla daughter of Suhail ibn Amr, who experienced excessive bleeding, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered her to perform ablution at every prayer." When this became difficult for her, he ordered her to combine the Dhuhr (noon) and Asr (afternoon) prayers in one ablution, and the Maghrib (evening) and Isha (night) prayers in one ablution, and to perform a separate ablution for Fajr (dawn). Ahmad ibn Khalid narrated: Muhammad narrated to me, from Sa’d ibn Ibrahim: "The difference among them arose because they were all three (the women) with Abdurrahman ibn Awf (RA), and some said: 'She is Umm Habiba,' and some said: 'She is Badia,' and some said: 'She is Sahla daughter of Suhail.'"

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to me that Al-Qaaqa’ bin Hakeem informed him that he asked Saeed about the woman who suffers from excessive bleeding. Saeed said to him, “O my nephew, there is none more knowledgeable about this than I am.” He said: “When the menstrual flow begins, she should leave the prayer, and when it ceases, she should perform ghusl and pray.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: Concerning a woman who suffers from excessive bleeding, “She should abstain from prayer during the days of her bleeding, then perform ghusl, then use a cloth to stop the flow and a sponge to cleanse herself, and then pray.” A man said, “Even if it continues to flow?” He (Ibn ‘Abbas) said, “Even if it flows like this container.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from ‘Ammar ibn Abi ‘Ammar, who said: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) was the most severe in his statement concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding (istihada), then he later eased the ruling. A woman came to him and said: “Should I enter the Ka’abah while menstruating?” He said: “Yes, even if you bleed profusely. Enter, then inquire about the regulations, then enter.”

Aisha (RA) narrated: I asked her about the woman experiencing excessive bleeding. She said: "She should wait for her usual days, the days in which she used to miss prayers before this, and when it becomes her day of purity, the day she used to become pure, she should perform ghusl (ritual bath), then perform ablution (wudu) for every prayer and pray."

Aisha (RA) narrated: I asked her about the woman experiencing excessive bleeding. She said: "She should wait for her usual days, the days in which she used to miss prayers before this, and when it becomes her day of purity, the day she used to become pure, she should perform ghusl (ritual bath), then perform ablution (wudu) for every prayer and pray."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding: "She should wait for the days during which she used to miss prayers, and when her days of purity arrive, the days on which she used to become pure, she should perform ghusl and then perform ablution for every prayer."

Narrated ‘Adi bin Thabit from his father, from his grandfather, (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The woman experiencing menstrual bleeding should abstain from prayer during her menstrual days each month. And when it ceases, she should perform ghusl, pray, fast, and perform ablution for every prayer."

Narrated Muhammad bin Isa: Muhammad said, "Tell me, Abu Hurairah, about the woman who suffers from istihaada (bleeding outside of menstruation) and knows her menstrual days. If she is divorced, and the bleeding prolongs, what should she do?" He said, "She should observe ‘iddah (waiting period) for the duration of three menstrual cycles. And regarding prayer, when the time for her menstrual period arrives each month, she should refrain from prayer."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, he said: Ma’tamar narrated to me from his father, who said: I said to Qatadah: "A woman whose menstrual period was known, and it increased by five days, or four days, or three days? " He said: "She prays." I said: "Two days?" He said: "That is from her menstrual period." And I asked Ibn Sirin, and he said: "Women are more knowledgeable about that."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Mutamir narrated to me from his father, from Hasan, concerning a woman who sees blood during her period of purity. He said: "I believe she should perform ghusl and pray."

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: It was asked of Ibn Abbas concerning a woman who experiences excessive bleeding (istihadha). He said, "She should wait for the period she used to menstruate for, and she should abstain from prayer. Then she should perform ghusl and pray. And when it is the time she used to menstruate, she should abstain from prayer, then perform ghusl. Indeed, this is from Satan, who intends to make one of them disbelieve.”

He (Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali) said concerning the woman experiencing istihaada (menstrual-like bleeding): "She should abstain from prayer during the days of her bleeding, then perform ghusl (full ritual bath) and use a cloth as a pad, and perform ablution (wudu) for every prayer."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The woman experiencing menstrual flow (mustaha) sits for the number of days prescribed for her, then performs a single ritual bath (ghusl), and performs ablution (wudu) for each prayer."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to me, saying: Khalid narrated to me from Anas ibn Sirin, who said: A woman from the family of Anas experienced menstrual flow. They ordered me to inquire about it, so I asked Ibn Abbas. He said: "As for the seeing of the black sea-like blood, she should not pray. But if she sees purity, even for an hour of the day, she should perform ghusl and pray."

Abu Nu'man narrated: Yazid ibn Zura'i narrated to me, saying: Khalid narrated to me from Anas ibn Sirin, who said: A foster mother of Anas ibn Malik experienced menstrual flow. They ordered me to seek a ruling from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. So I asked him, and he said: "If she sees the dark, flowing blood, she should not pray. And if she sees purity, then she should perform ghusl and pray."

Hajjaj ibn Naysir narrated to me, he said: Qura narrated to me, from Adh-Dhahhak: That a woman asked him, saying, "Indeed, I am a woman who suffers from excessive bleeding." He said, "If you see bright red blood, then abstain from intercourse for the number of days you menstruate."

Narrated from Muhammad bin Yusuf, he said: Sufyan narrated to me from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "The woman who suffers from istihadah (menstrual bleeding outside the normal period) sits for as many days as she usually menstruates, then performs a single ablution for Zuhr and Asr, postpones Maghrib, hastens Isha, and that is during the time of Isha, and performs a single ablution for Fajr. She does not fast, her husband does not approach her, and she does not touch the Mus'haf (Quran)."

Al-Hasan ibn ar-Rabee’ narrated to me, he said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to me from ‘Abd al-‘Azeez ibn Rufeiq from ‘Ataa’ who said: Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) used to say concerning the woman experiencing excessive flow: “She performs a single washing for Dhuhr and ‘Asr, and a single washing for Maghrib and ‘Isha’.” And he used to say: “She delays Dhuhr and hastens ‘Asr, and delays Maghrib and hastens ‘Isha’.”

Narrated ‘Ubaidullah ibn Musa, from ‘Utman ibn Al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning a woman who suffers from excessive flow: “When her menstrual blood ceases, and she has a discharge, if when it is evening she performs a complete ablution, then she should take a garment and wrap herself in it, then she should pray Zuhr and ‘Asr together, then she should do like that, then she should pray Maghrib and ‘Isha together, then she should do like that, then she should pray Fajr.”

They (‘Attā’, Sa‘īd, and ‘Ikrimah) said concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding: "She performs ghusl each day for the Fajr and ‘Asr prayers, and prays them. She performs ghusl for the Maghrib and ‘Ishā’ prayers and prays them. And she performs ghusl for the Fajr prayer."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Shaddad: "The woman who suffers from excessive bleeding (istihada) performs ghusl, then combines the Dhuhr and Asr prayers. If she sees anything (bleeding), she performs ghusl again and combines the Maghrib and Isha prayers."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Samiyya, who said: I asked Saeed ibn Musayyib about the woman experiencing excessive flow (mustaha), and he said: "She sits for the number of days she normally menstruates, and performs ghusl from noon until noon, and she uses a cloth to stop the flow, and her husband may visit her, and she fasts." I said: "About whom is this?" He then took a pebble and threw it.

Abu al-Mughira reported: Sufyan narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to me from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said, "She would bathe from noon until noon, and perform ablution for every prayer. If the blood overcame her, she would cleanse herself thoroughly." And Hasan used to say the same.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, that Yahya narrated, that Sumayya, the servant of Abu Bakr ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, informed him, that al-Qaaqa’ ibn Hakim and Zayd ibn Aslam sent him to Saeed ibn Musayyib to ask him how the woman experiencing istihaada (menstruallike bleeding outside of menstruation) should perform ablution. Saeed said: "She should perform ghusl from Zuhr (midday prayer) until a time similar to it the following day for the Zuhr prayer. If the bleeding overcomes her, she should cleanse herself and perform ablution for each prayer and pray."

"Mus’ab bin Khalid narrated from Mu’tamir, from his father, from Hasan, concerning a woman experiencing excessive bleeding: “She performs ghusl from the prayer of Dhuhr until the prayer of Dhuhr the following day.”

The menstruating woman abstains from prayer during her menstrual days of the month, then performs a ritual bath from noon until noon, and performs ablution for every prayer. She fasts and prays, and her husband may approach her.
Narrated by Aisha (RA): Concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding, "She should perform ghusl once each day."

Marwan narrated to me, from Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Naafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to say concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding: "She performs ghusl from noon until noon." Marwan said: And this is the statement of Awza'i.
Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "The woman experiencing istihaada (menstruallike bleeding outside of menstruation) performs ghusl (full ritual bath) every day at the time of the Fajr (dawn) prayer."
Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding: "He (the Prophet) saw no harm in her husband visiting her."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Salim al-Aftas, who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr was asked: "Is the woman experiencing istihadha (excessive bleeding) to be accompanied (in marital relations)?" He said: "Prayer is of greater importance than companionship."
Narrated by Muhammad bin Yusuf: Sufyan narrated to me from Samiyyar from Saeed bin Musayyib, who said, "Her husband will come to her."
Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, concerning a woman experiencing excessive bleeding, that he said: "Her husband may visit her."

Abu 'Aasim narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding: "Her husband may visit her, even if the blood flows onto the mat."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, he said: Hammad narrated to me from Humaid, who said: It was said to Bakr ibn Abdullah, "Indeed, al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf says, 'Indeed, a woman experiencing excessive bleeding (mustada) should not be approached by her husband.'" Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani said, "Prayer is of greater sanctity; her husband should approach her."
"Her husband will come to her."

‘Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Khalid ibn ‘Abdullah, from ‘Ata’ ibn as-Sa’ib, from ‘Ata’, who said concerning the woman experiencing istihaada (abnormal vaginal bleeding): “Her husband may have relations with her, she should omit prayer during her days of bleeding, and when prayer becomes permissible for her, then let him have relations with her.”
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The woman who suffers from istihadah (menstrual bleeding outside the normal period) may be joined by her husband."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to me, from Qatada, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and Hasan, and Ata', that they said concerning the woman experiencing excessive bleeding: "She performs ghusl, prays, fasts Ramadan, and her husband may approach her."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Hafs, from Hasan, who said: "He (Hasan) used to say: A woman experiencing istihadah (abnormal vaginal bleeding) should not be approached by her husband." Abu Nu'man said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan said to me, "I do not know anyone who has reported this from Hasan."

ʿAffan narrated to me, saying: “Wahb narrated to me from Khalid who said: ‘Muhammad (peace be upon him) disliked that a man should have intercourse with his wife while she was experiencing istihaada.’”
Narrated from Ibrahim: "The woman experiencing excessive bleeding (istihada) does not have conjugal relations with her husband, nor does she fast, nor does she touch the Mus'haf (the Quran)."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The woman experiencing menstrual flow (mustaha) should not be approached by her husband."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Ja'far ibn al-Harith, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "It was said, 'The woman experiencing istihadah [abnormal vaginal bleeding] should not be approached in intimacy, nor should she fast, nor touch the Mus'haf [Quran]. She was only permitted to pray.' Yazid said: 'Her husband may approach her in intimacy, and it is permissible for her what is permissible for the pure [woman].'"

Narrated Muhammad ibn ‘Isa: Muhammad said to me, “Tell me,” he said, “About a woman who is in menses.” He said, “A woman abstains from prayer during her menses for seven days. If she becomes clean, that is sufficient. If not, she abstains until ten days have passed. If she becomes clean, that is sufficient. If not, she performs ghusl and prays, being a mustahaadah.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Rabi’, from Hasan, who said: "Menstruation lasts for ten days, and anything beyond that is considered istihadah (prolonged bleeding)." And ‘Ata’ said: "Menstruation lasts for fifteen days."
Narrated by Anas bin Malik: "The menstrual period is ten days or so, and if it exceeds that, she is considered a mustaha."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Ali ibn Thabit, from Muhammad ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Menstruation extends to thirteen days, and anything beyond that is considered Istihada (bleeding outside of menstruation)."
Anas ibn Malik (RA) said: "A woman's menstrual period is ten days, then she is a mustaha."

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Ali ibn Thabit, from Muhammad ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Menstruation lasts up to thirteen days, and whatever is beyond that is considered Istihada (bleeding outside of menstruation)."

Narrated by Hassan: "If a woman sees blood, she abstains from prayer, counts the days of her menstrual period, whether one day or two days, and after that, she is considered a menstruating woman (mustaha)."
Anas (RA) said: "The woman experiencing menstrual flow (mustahada) waits three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten (days)."
Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Ibn Jurayj from 'Ata' who said, "It has reached us that the woman experiencing excessive bleeding (mustaha) waits upon her menstrual cloth for a day."
Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Anything exceeding ten [days of menstruation] is considered Istihada."
ʿAtā’ said: "The furthest extent of menstruation is fifteen [days]."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan said: It reached me from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "The minimum of menstruation is three days." Abdullah ad-Darimi was asked: Do you act upon this? He said: "Yes, if it is her habit." I also asked him about this, and he said: "The minimum of menstruation is one day and night, and the maximum is fifteen."
Abu Muhammad, that is Abu Sa'd al-Saghani, narrated to us from Sufyan, from Rabi', from Hasan, who said: "The minimum duration of menstruation is three [days]."
Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, Makhlad ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ma’qil ibn ‘Ubaidullah, from ‘Ata’, who said: “The earliest onset of menstruation is one day.”

Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi narrated to me, he said: We were told by Wahb, he said: We were told by Yunus, from Hasan, who said: "If a woman sees blood before her menstrual period by one or two days, it is considered part of her menstrual period."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, that Hammad narrated to me, from Qatadah and Kays ibn Sa’d, from ‘Ata’, that they said concerning a virgin woman who experiences bleeding after intercourse, they said: “She abstains from prayer as a woman among other women does.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan said: "When a woman first menstruates, she should sit with women experiencing menstruation for a period." It was asked of Abdullah about this, and he said: "It is the most likely of things."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Layth, from Ata, concerning a major bleeding (referring to postpartum bleeding), he said: "We do not consider it to be menstruation."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, that Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, that Ibn Jurayj narrated to me from Ata, concerning a woman who was without menstruation for thirty years, then she saw blood. So, an order was given regarding the affair of the woman experiencing istihaada.

Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yusuf, he said: Sufyan narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, concerning a major bleeding: He said, "It is like the condition of a woman experiencing istihaada, she acts as the woman experiencing istihaada does."

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Hajjaj, from Ata, and Al-Hakam bin ‘Utaybah, concerning the woman who has ceased menstruation: "When she sees the blood, she performs ablution and prays without performing ghusl." It was asked of Abdullah concerning a major ritual bath, and he said: "She performs ablution and prays, and if she is divorced, she observes the waiting period in months."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan said: "Purity consists of fifteen [things]."

Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "If a woman menstruates in a month, or forty nights, three times, then if righteous women witnesses testify that she has seen what prohibits her from prayer from the impurity of women, which is the known menstruation, then her term is complete." Abu Muhammad said: I heard Yazid ibn Harun say: "I prefer purity after fifteen [days]."

Yala narrated to me, saying: Ismail narrated to me, from Amir, who said: A woman came to Ali disputing with her husband, who had divorced her. She said: "I have had three menstrual periods this month." Ali said to Shurayh: "Judge between them." Shurayh said: "O Commander of the Believers, and are you here too?" Ali said: "Judge between them." Shurayh said: "O Commander of the Believers, and are you here too?" Ali said: "Judge between them." Shurayh said: "If a trustworthy person from her household, whose religion and integrity are acceptable, testifies that she has had three menstrual periods, purifies at each course, and prays, then it is permissible for her. Otherwise, it is not." Ali said: "Qalon said it, and Qalon means 'excellent' in the Roman tongue."

'Amru ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Khalid ibn Abdullah from Khalid al-Hazza'i from Ikrimah: "[And they are not permitted to conceal what Allah has created for them in their wombs] (Surah al-Baqarah, verse 228)." He said, "Menstruation." It was said to Abu Muhammad, "Do you say this?" He replied, "No." And Abdullah was asked about the narration of Shu'aib: "Do you say this?" He replied, "No," and said, "How can there be three menstruations in a month?"
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) forbade women from looking at the moon at night during menstruation, saying: "It may be yellow or murky."
"‘Amrah used to instruct women not to bathe until the cotton discharge became white."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan said: "Darkness and yellowness during the days of menstruation are considered menstruation. And every color seen after the days of menstruation, whether blood, darkness, or yellowness, she is considered a menstruating woman (mustaha)." It was asked of Abdullah: Do you follow the statement of Sufyan? He said: Yes.

Yalaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from his wife Fatima daughter of Muhammad, who was in the care of ‘Amra, that a woman from the Quraysh sent to ‘Amra a piece of cotton cloth, the color of yellow, asking her: "Do you think that if a woman sees only this (yellow color) from her menstrual flow, she has become pure?" ‘Amra replied: "No, until she sees pure white."

Asma’ reported: “We used to sit in her lap (that of the Prophet’s wife Aisha). If one of us had a menstrual period, then became clean (ceased menstruation), she would bathe and pray. Then a slight yellowish discharge would appear, and she would order us to abstain from prayer until we saw only pure white.”
'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to me from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: "Darkness, yellowness, and blood during menstruation are considered as menstruation."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "If a woman sees the blood, she should abstain from prayer until she sees the purity white as wool, then she should perform ghusl and pray."
Al-Hasan would not consider yellowness or muddiness, nor anything like the washing of meat, as anything significant.
Narrated 'Umm 'Atiyyah: "We used to consider yellowness and darkness (in menstruation) as nothing."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Hammam narrated to me from his father, from Hasan, concerning a woman who sees blood during her days of purity. He said: "I think she should perform ghusl and pray." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not consider blackness or yellowness to be of consequence."

Narrated Muhammad ibn Yusuf: I was told by Israel, from ‘Abd al-A‘la, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiya, concerning a woman who sees yellow after purification, he said: "Let her wash it and perform ablution and pray."

Abu Nu'aim and Hajjaj narrated to me on the authority of Hammad bin Salama, from Yunus and Humaid, from Hasan, who said: "There is nothing left in the state of ritual purity (after bathing) except purity itself." Abdullah (ibn Salama) said: "The yellow and the muddiness (remaining after bathing) is the state of ritual purity."
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If a woman sees the white discharge (triya) after menstruation, on the first or second day, then she should purify herself and pray."
Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Qays, from Ata’, who said: "There is nothing left in the waiting period after the bath but purity."
Umm 'Atiyyah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that she said: "We did not consider menstrual spotting or yellowish discharge after bathing as anything."

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Yunus, from Hasan, who said: "When a menstruating woman sees bright blood after washing (from menstruation) by one or two days, she abstains from prayer for one day, and thereafter she is considered a mustahaadah (one experiencing prolonged bleeding)."

Narrated ‘Ali (RA): “When a woman purifies herself from menstruation, and then sees after purification something that doubts her, then it is only a splash of Satan in the womb. If she sees something like mucus, or a drop of blood, or the washing of flesh, then she performs ablution for prayer, and then prays. If it is a thick, unmistakable blood, then she should leave prayer.” Abu Muhammad said: I heard Yazid ibn Harun say: “If a woman’s menses are seven days, and she sees whiteness as purification, then she marries, and then sees blood between her and ten (days), then the marriage is permissible and sound. If she sees purification less than seven (days), then she marries, and then sees blood, then it is not permissible, and it is menstruation.” And ‘Abdullah was asked about this, and he said: “Yes, I say it.”

Yahya related to me from Yazid ibn Harun, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning a woman whose menstrual period is six or seven days, then she sees a dark hue or yellowness, or she sees a drop or two of blood, that it is invalid and nothing harms her.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to me from Abd al-Karim, who said: "I asked Ata' about a woman who bathes from menstruation and sees yellowness, so he said: 'She performs ablution and rinses.'"

Yalaa narrated: Abdullah al-Malik narrated to me from Ata’ about a woman experiencing excessive bleeding, who said: "She should abstain from prayer during her bleeding period for one or two days, then perform ghusl (ritual bath). If she sees moisture (wetness) at the time of the first (prayer), she should perform ablution and pray. If she sees blood, she should delay the Dhuhr (noon) prayer and hasten the Asr (afternoon) prayer, then pray them with one ghusl. If the sun sets, she should look; if she sees moisture, she should perform ablution and pray. If she sees blood, she should delay the Maghrib (sunset) prayer and hasten the Isha (night) prayer, then pray them with one ghusl. If the dawn appears, she should look; if she sees moisture, she should perform ablution and pray. If she sees blood, she should perform ghusl and pray the Fajr (dawn) prayer each day and night three times.” Abu Muhammad said: “The term ‘aqraa’ (wetness) with me refers to menstruation.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) observed 'itikaaf (seclusion in the mosque), and some of his wives observed it with him while she was experiencing istihada (menstruation-like bleeding) and saw the blood. Sometimes, she would place a cloth beneath her due to the blood. And she claimed that Aisha saw the discharge of a bird, and she said, "It seems this is something that Fulana used to experience."

Abu Nu'man narrated: Abdul Wahid narrated to me from al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Ata' about a woman who becomes clean from menstruation, then sees yellowness, and he said: "She should perform ablution."

Abu Muhammad said: I recited to me from Zayd ibn Yahya, from Malik, who is Ibn Anas, that I asked him about a woman whose menstruation was seven days, and her menstrual period increased. He said: "She may observe purification for three days."
Narrated by Hasan: "If a woman becomes clean (from menstruation) at the time of a prayer, but does not perform ghusl (ritual bath) while she is able to do so, she fulfills that prayer."
Narrated by Hasan: "If a woman prays two rak'ahs, then menstruates, she does not make up [the missed prayer] when she becomes pure."

Narrated Muhammad ibn 'Isa: Muhammad ibn Hamid, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, said: I have narrated to me from Abu Mu'awiya, who narrated to me from al-Hajjaj, from 'Ata' concerning a woman who purifies herself at noon and delays her washing until the time of 'Asr enters, they said: "She makes up the Dhuhr (noon prayer)."

Narrated Muhammad ibn Isa: Muhammad said, "Tell us, Ishaq said, 'I narrated to me from Yunus, from Hasan, and Mughira, from Amir and Ubaida, from Ibrahim, concerning a woman who neglects prayer until menstruation overtakes her. They said, 'She should repeat those prayers.'"

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulaiman, and Yunus, from Hasan, concerning a woman upon whom the time for prayer approached, but she delayed until she menstruated. They (Hasan) said: "She should pray that prayer once she has performed ghusl (ritual bath)."

Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Zahrani narrated to me, Abu Shihab narrated to me, from Hisham, from Hasan and Qatadah, that they said: "If a woman neglects prayer until she menstruates, then she must make up for it once she is purified."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Hasan narrated to me, from Mughira, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "If it is delayed, then it arrives, then its time is fulfilled."
