"When a woman menstruates during the time of prayer, she is not obligated to make up [the missed] prayers."

"Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to us, from Hajjaj and Qays, from Ata, who said: 'If a woman becomes clean before sunset, she prays the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, and if she becomes clean before Fajr, she prays the Maghrib and Isha prayers.' Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Saeed ibn Musayyib, a similar statement. Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Misqam, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, a similar statement."

Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Isa, he said: Hisham narrated to me, he said: Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, concerning a menstruating woman: "She prays the prayer that she purifies from menstruation in its time."
They (‘Ata’, Tawus, and Mujahid) said: "If a menstruating woman becomes clean before Fajr, she prays Maghrib and ‘Isha’. And if she becomes clean before sunset, she prays Zuhr and ‘Asr."

Narrated Muhammad ibn Yusuf: Muhammad said, "Tell us, Hakim, about a woman experiencing menstrual flow." He said, "If she sees purity late in the day, she prays the Dhuhr and Asr prayers. And if she sees purity late at night, she prays the Maghrib and Isha prayers." Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated from Sufyan, from Layth, from Tawus, a similar statement.
Abu Zayd, Sa'id ibn al-Rabee', narrated to me, that Shu'bah narrated to me from Mughirah, who said: Ibrahim used to say: "If a woman becomes clean at the time of 'Asr, she prays Zuhr and 'Asr."
Abu Zayd narrated: Shu'bah said: I asked Hammad, who said: "If a woman becomes clean during the time of a prayer, she should pray."
Narrated Anas (RA): "If a woman becomes clean (from menstruation) at the time of a prayer, she should pray that prayer and not pray anything else."

Abu Muhammad said: I recited from Zayd ibn Yahya, from Malik, who said: I asked him about a woman who purifies herself after the afternoon prayer. He said: "Pray the noon and afternoon prayers." I said: What if her purification is close to sunset? He said: "Pray the afternoon prayer and do not pray the noon prayer. And if she did not purify herself until the sun has set, then nothing is incumbent upon her." It was asked of Abdullah whether he acts upon this. He said: No.

A woman wrote to him [i.e., Ibn Abbas], saying, "I have been experiencing bleeding for so long." It reached her that Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "She should perform ghusl at every prayer." Ibn Abbas said, "We do not find anything other than what Ali said."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, that Al-Awza’i narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Abi Katir, who said: He told me, Abu Salama, or Ikrimah, said: Zainab used to seclude herself with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) while she was menstruating. So he ordered her to “bathe after every prayer.”
"Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, used to say: 'The woman experiencing menstrual flow (mustaha) performs ghusl before each prayer.'"

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Al-Awza'i told me that he heard Ata' ibn Abi Rabah say: "One performs a single washing between every two prayers, and one performs a single washing for Fajr." Al-Awza'i said: And Zuhri and Makhul would say: "One performs a washing at every prayer."

Umm Habibah related: "Umm Habibah, the daughter of Jahsh, used to experience excessive bleeding, and she asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about it. He ordered her to perform ghusl (full ritual bath) before each prayer."

A woman wrote to Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both: “I experience excessive bleeding and do not become pure.” I remind you of Allah, but you do not give me a ruling. I inquired about this, and they said: “Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: ‘Perform ghusl for every prayer.’” So I read [the question] and wrote the response with my own hand: I find nothing for her except what Ali said. It was said: “The land of Kufa is cold.” He said: “If Allah had willed, He would have tested it with something more severe than that.”

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Qays, from Mujahid, who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him: “Its land is cold.” He said: “Postpone the Dhuhr prayer and hasten the Asr prayer, and perform a ghusl. Postpone the Maghrib prayer and hasten the Isha prayer, and perform a ghusl. And perform a ghusl for Fajr.”

Zaynab bint Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the daughter of Jahsh was married to Abdurrahman ibn Auf, and she suffered from excessive bleeding. Consequently, she would leave her place of rest while the blood was still flowing, and she would pray.

Wahb ibn Sa’id of Damascus narrated to me, from Shu’aib ibn Ishaq, who said: We were told by al-Awza’i, who said: I heard Zuhri and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir saying: "A washing (ghusl) is dedicated for each prayer." Al-Awza’i said: And it reached me from Makhhul, something similar to that.

I have been narrated to me by Wahb ibn Sa'id, from Shu'aib, who said: "Malik narrated to me, that 'Ata' informed me, that Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: 'For every two prayers, there is a purification (ghusl), and the purification for the Fajr prayer is separate.'"

Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Hammad narrated to me from Hammad al-Kufi, that a woman asked Ibrahim, and she said: "Indeed, I experience excessive bleeding." He said: "Use water and rinse with it, for it cuts off the bleeding from you."

Uffan ibn Muslim narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Dinār narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, concerning the divorced woman whose waiting period was stipulated: "She observes a year. If she menstruates, then she observes another three months after the completion of the year. If she menstruates, then her waiting period has ended; otherwise, it has lapsed."

Abdullah ibn Maslama reported: Malik was asked about the waiting period of a woman who has been divorced, so Malik related, from Ibn Shihab, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyib, who said, "Her waiting period is a year." Abu Muhammad said: This is the statement of Malik.

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, Amr ibn Dinār narrated, saying: Jabir ibn Zayd was asked about a young woman who is divorced and her menstruation ceases without old age. He said: "Does she menstruate without menstruation?!" And Tāwūs said: "Three months."

Narrated by Az-Zuhri: "When a man divorces his wife and she experiences a period or two periods, and her period ceases if that is due to old age, she observes an 'iddah of three months. And if she is a young woman and experiences doubt (about pregnancy), she observes an 'iddah of one year after the doubt."

Khalifa ibn Khayyat narrated to me, saying: "Gundar narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to me from Qatada, from Ikrimah, who said: 'The woman who suffers from istihada (abnormal vaginal bleeding) and the woman for whom menstruation does not come regularly, who menstruates once in a month and twice in another, their 'iddah (waiting period after divorce or widowhood) is three months.'"
Khalifa ibn Khayyat narrated to me, Abu Dawud narrated to me, from Hisham, from Hammad, who said: "Observe 'Iddah (waiting period) with the reciters (of the Quran)."

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated: Malik narrated to me from Ibn Shihab from Saeed ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "The waiting period for a woman experiencing istihadah (menstrual-like bleeding outside of the normal menstrual cycle) is a year."

Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, from Yunus, from Hasan, who said: "The woman experiencing istihaada (menstruallike bleeding outside the normal menstrual period) observes 'iddah (waiting period) according to the days of her menstruation."

Khalifa narrated to me, saying: "About the women who are 'al-aqira'." Abu Muhammad said: "The people of Hijaz say, 'Al-aqira' are the pure ones.' The people of Iraq say, 'It is menstruation.' Abdullah said: 'And I say, 'It is menstruation.'"

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, who said, "The woman experiencing istihaada (menstruallike bleeding outside the normal menstrual period) observes 'iddah (waiting period after divorce or widowhood) according to the days of her menstrual cycles."

I asked Zuhri about a woman who was young and menstruating, and her husband divorced her. Then menstruation ceased from her at the time of the divorce, and she did not see any blood. How long should she observe ‘iddah (waiting period)? He said, "Three months." I said, and I asked Zuhri about a man who divorced his wife and she had two menstrual periods, then her menstruation ceased. How long should he wait? He said, "Her ‘iddah is a year.” I said, and I asked Zuhri about a woman who was menstruating when her husband divorced her, she stays for three months, then she has a menstrual period, then menstruation is delayed from her. Then she stays for seven months and eight days, then she has another menstrual period, sometimes she hastens to it, and sometimes it is delayed. How should she observe ‘iddah? He said, "If her menstruation differs from her usual periods, her ‘iddah is a year.” I said, "And how if he divorced her while she was menstruating once every year, how long should she observe ‘iddah?” He said, "If her usual periods are known, that is her usual period, then we believe she should observe ‘iddah according to her usual periods.”

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, he said: Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Wahid narrated to me, from al-Awza’i, who said: I asked Zuhri about a man who buys a female slave who has not reached puberty nor is pregnant, how long should he wait before consummating the marriage? He said: "Three months." Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said: "Forty-five days."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Hisham al-Dustawa'i, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he used to say concerning the woman experiencing istihaada (menstrual-like bleeding not due to menstruation): "She performs ghusl (full ritual bath) at every prayer and prays." Hammad said: "If a woman experiencing istihaada was unaware [of the ruling] and neglected prayer for months, she makes up those prayers. They said to him: How does she make them up? He said: She makes them up in a single day if she is able." It was said to Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): Do you say it like this? He said: By Allah, yes.
I asked Zuhri about a pregnant woman who sees blood, and he said, "She should leave the prayer."

ʿUbaydullah ibn Musa narrated from ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad, who said: I asked Mujahid about a woman who saw blood while I suspected she was pregnant. He said: "That is a discharge from the womb. Allah knows what every female carries and what discharges and increases in the wombs [Quran 13:8]. So, she does not discharge due to anything she sees similar to it in the pregnancy."

Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me from ‘Asim al-Ahwal, from Ikrimah, concerning this verse: "Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs withhold or increase, and everything is [under His] measure." [Surah Ar-Ra’d, 13:8] He said: "That is the menstrual flow during pregnancy. She does not experience a menstrual period while pregnant, but if she does, it increases her purity within her pregnancy."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "It is a matter upon which we do not differ among us that a pregnant woman, if she sees blood, does not pray until she is purified."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to me, saying: 'Aasim narrated to me, from Ikrimah: Reciting, "And the wombs do not discharge [their burden] except in accordance with a specified term," [Surah Ar-Ra'd, 8], he said: "It is the menstrual flow during pregnancy." Reciting, "And they increase [in growth],” [Surah Ar-Ra'd, 8], he said: "For every day she menstruates during her pregnancy, a day is added to her purification, until she completes nine months in a state of purity."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Abu Bishr from Mujahid, concerning the verse: "And the wombs do not discharge [their burdens] except in their appointed term," (Surah Ar-Ra'd, 13:8). He said: "If a woman menstruates while pregnant, that is a deficiency in the child. But if she exceeds nine months, it completes what was deficient in her child."

Mujajjaj narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me from Humaid, from Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, who said: "My wife menstruates while she is pregnant." Abu Muhammad said: I heard Sulaiman ibn Harb say: "My wife menstruates while she is pregnant."

"’Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "When a pregnant woman sees blood, she should abstain from prayer, for it is menstruation." Al-Harith narrated to us, that Malik told us, that it reached him from ‘Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), the like of that."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to me from Layth, from Ash-Sha'bi, concerning a pregnant woman who sees blood, "If the blood is a splash, she performs ghusl and prays. And if it is a trickle, she performs wudu' and prays." Abu al-Mughira narrated to me from al-Awza'i, with a similar narration.

Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated: "If a woman finds her husband in a state of janabah (sexual impurity), she should not pray with him in her salaah (prayer) until he performs ghusl (ritual bath). But if it is only for a day or two, she should not abandon the salaah."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said concerning a pregnant woman who sees blood, "It does not prevent her from prayer."
Aisha reported that when a pregnant woman sees blood, she should perform ghusl and pray. Yazid said, "She does not perform ghusl." Abdullah said, "I say according to the statement of Yazid."

Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Yazid ibn Zuraik narrated to me, from Yunus, from Hasan, concerning a woman who sees blood during pregnancy: "Her situation is like that of a woman experiencing istihaada, except that she does not omit prayer."

Narrated by Muhammad ibn Isa: He said, "Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Mughira from Ibrahim concerning a woman who sees blood while pregnant, he said: 'She should wash it off, perform ablution, and pray.'"
Narrated ‘Ata and Al-Hakam: "When a pregnant woman sees blood, she performs ablution and prays."
Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated: "When a woman who is menstruating sees blood, she should perform ablution and pray."
He said: "It is like the condition of a woman suffering from istihada."
"There is no menstrual bleeding for a pregnant woman."
Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Hisham from Hasan concerning a woman who sees blood during pregnancy: "She is like a woman experiencing istihaada."
Narrated by Abu al-Walid: Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Mughira from Ibrahim: "If a pregnant woman sees blood, she should not abandon the prayer."

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Hajjaj, from Ata and Hakim ibn Utaiba, that they said concerning pregnant women: "The woman who is menstruating, if she sees the blood, she performs ablution and prays, and they do not perform ghusl."
Hajjaj narrated from Hammad, from Mtar, from Ata’, who said, "They bathe and then pray."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: “A pregnant woman does not experience menstruation; so, if she sees any blood, she should perform ghusl and pray.”

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to me, Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated to me, from Hasan ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, concerning a woman who sees blood while in labor, he said: "It is menstruation; she should leave the prayer."

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, he said: Yunus narrated to me from Hasan concerning a pregnant woman: "When the pangs of labor strike her, and she sees blood on the child, she should abstain from prayer." Abdullah said: "She should pray as long as she has not delivered."
Abu Sufyan narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatada, concerning the postpartum woman: "She is like a woman purifying herself from among other women."

Narrated Muhammad ibn ‘Isa: Muhammad said, “I was told by Yunus from Hasan concerning a woman in childbed, ‘She abstains from prayer for forty days. If she sees purity, then that is sufficient. If she does not see purity, she abstains from prayer for five or six days. If she purifies, then that is sufficient. Otherwise, she abstains from prayer between that and fifty days. If she purifies, then that is sufficient. Otherwise, she is a mustahaadah.’”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Yunus ibn ‘Ubaid, from Hasan, from ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As, that he would not approach a woman in childbed for forty days. Hasan said: "The period of a woman in childbed is from forty-five to fifty days, and if it exceeds that, she is considered to be experiencing post-partum bleeding."

Ja'far ibn 'Awn reported: Ismail ibn Muslim reported to me from Hasan from 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, who said, "The waiting period for a woman who has given birth is forty days; if she is purified, then [the waiting period is over], and if not, she should not exceed that time until she prays."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Ash'ath, from Ata', who said: "If a woman has a customary period, then she observes it; otherwise, she observes forty nights."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata’, who said: "Postnatal bleeding (nifas) is menstruation (hayd)."
Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The woman who has given birth waits forty days or close to that."

Um Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "During the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), a woman giving birth would sit observing ‘iddah (waiting period) for forty days, or forty nights, and one of us would apply kohl to her face due to the puffiness (caused by childbirth)."

Narrated ‘Auf bin ‘Amr: A woman of ‘Auf bin ‘Amr menstruated, and she came to him after twenty nights had passed. She entered his blanket, and he said, "Who is this?" She said, "I am so-and-so; I have become clean (purified)." He kicked her with his foot and said, "Do not deceive me about my religion until forty nights have passed."
Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "A woman in postpartum confinement sits for approximately forty days."
Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The woman in postpartum observes a waiting period of approximately forty days."

Al-Hasan said concerning a woman who sees blood after childbirth, "She observes a period of forty nights, then she prays." And Sha'bi said, "Two months, then she is like a woman experiencing istihaada (menstrual-like bleeding)."

Marwan narrated to me on the authority of Muhammad bin Shu'aib, who narrated from Ibrahim bin Sulaiman al-Aftas, who said: I heard Al-Ala' bin al-Harith from Makhul, who said: "A woman awaiting purification after childbirth waits thirty days for a boy and forty days for a girl." Marwan said: This is the statement of Saeed bin 'Abd al-'Aziz. Awza'i said: They are equal.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Raqashi narrated to me, he said: Wehib narrated to me, he said: Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, who said: "If a woman sees blood with the onset of labor for one or two days, it is considered from her post-partum bleeding (nifaas)."

Narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn Mubarak narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, about a pregnant woman who sees blood and is undergoing divorce. He said, "She should act as the menstruating woman does."

Narrated Muhammad ibn Yusuf: Muhammad said, "Tell me," and he narrated from Sufyan, from Mughira, from Ibrahim about a woman who experiences istihaada (bleeding between periods), then menstruates. He said, "She performs ghusl (a full ritual bath)." Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Muhammad said, "Tell me," and he narrated from Sufyan, from Hisham, from Hasan, a similar statement.
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Musayyib, from Ata’, who said: "The menstrual period is a major matter."
Abu Hurairah reported: "Someone asked Ibrahim about a man who had intercourse with his wife and she began to menstruate. He said, 'It is preferred that she perform ghusl.'"

Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Hammad narrated to me from Hajjaj, from Ata and Al-Nakha'i, that they said: "Bathe yourself from Janabah." Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Hammad narrated to me from Amir Al-A'hwal, from Hasan, similar to that.
Al-Mula narrated to me, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, from Al-Ala' ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Hammad was asked about it, and he said: Ibrahim said: "Perform a ritual bath."
He said: "He would bathe."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to me, saying: I heard Hakim ibn ‘Utaybah say: "They liked that a menstruating woman should perform ablution like for prayer, then she should glorify and exalt Allah during the time of prayer."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Sulaiman al-Taymi, who said: I said to Abu Qilaba, "Does a menstruating woman perform ablution at the time of every prayer and remember Allah?" He said, "I have not found any basis for this."

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir Al-Juhani (RA): “He (the Prophet) used to order a menstruating woman, when the time of prayer came, to perform ablution, sit in the courtyard of the mosque, remember Allah, and glorify Him.”

Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Malik narrated to me from Ata’ about a menstruating woman: “Does she recite [the Quran]?” He said: “Not except a portion of an ayah, but she performs ablution at the time of every prayer, then she faces the qibla, and she glorifies [Allah], and she exalts [Him], and she supplicates to Allah.”
Narrated by Makhool: "The menstruating woman is ordered to perform ablution at the times of prayer, to face the qibla, and to remember Allah."

Narrated Muhammad ibn Yusuf: Sufyan narrated to me from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "When a menstruating woman and a person in a state of ritual impurity hear the call to prayer (adhan), the person in ritual impurity should perform ghusl and pray, and the menstruating woman should not make up the missed prayer, for she does not pray."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Mughira, from Ibrahim concerning a woman in ritual impurity (hayd) hearing the prostration, he said: "Do not judge (it as permissible)."
Ibrahim said: "There is nothing upon it."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "We used to menstruate during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he would not order any of us to abandon the prayer."

A woman asked Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her): "Does any of us observe the prayers during her menstrual period?" She said: "Are you a pagan? Women used to menstruate during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and were not ordered to make up [missed] prayers." Abu Nu'man said: "It seems Hammad divided the narration of Ayub, and then brought this [alternative narration]."
Amr ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Ata’ ibn As-Sa’ib, from Amir, who said: "When a menstruating woman hears the prostration, she should not prostrate."

"‘Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Khalid ibn ‘Abdullah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’i, from Abu Qilaba, who said: ‘The menstruating woman should not prostrate [in prayer] when she hears the prostration.’”
Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Khalid, from Hasan ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim, that he disliked that a menstruating woman should prostrate when she hears the prostration.

Yalaa narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Awn, from Abu Ghaleb ‘Ajlan, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) about women who have just given birth and menstruating women: Do they pray if they purify themselves? He said: “Indeed. The wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did so. If they were doing that, we would order our women to do so as well.”

A woman came to Aisha and asked, "Should I make up the prayers I missed during my menstrual period once I become pure?" Aisha replied, "Are you from the people of Hura?" [meaning, are you adhering to a misguided opinion?] "We used to be with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and if one of us menstruated and became pure, he would not order us to make up [the missed prayers]."

Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Sharif narrated to me, from Kathir, the father of Ismail, who said: I said to Fatima, meaning the daughter of Ali: "Do you pray during your menstrual period?" She replied: "No."

A woman asked Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her): Does a menstruating woman offer prayers? She (Aisha) replied: “Are you a pagan? The wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) menstruated, and he ordered them to make up [missed] prayers.” Abdullah said: Its meaning is that they do not make them up.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "A menstruating woman and a person in a state of ritual impurity (janaba) mention Allah and pronounce His Names."

It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Yusuf: He said: Sufyan said: It reached me from Ibrahim and Sa’id ibn Jubayr that they said: "The person who is in a state of ritual impurity (janaba) and the menstruating woman should not recite a complete verse. They may recite a letter (of the Quran)."

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Bazzaz narrated to me, he said: Shareek narrated to me, from Firas, from Amir: "The one in a state of ritual impurity (junub) and the menstruating woman do not recite the Quran."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Hakim narrated to me, from Ibrahim, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) disliked or forbade a person in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) from reciting [the Quran]. Shu'bah said: "I found in the book [the text] and the menstruating woman [were also included]."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Hisham al-Dustawa'i, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "Four [categories of people] do not recite the Quran: one who recites while relieving himself, one who recites in the bathhouse, the one in a state of ritual impurity (janabah), and the menstruating woman, except for verses permissible for them, such as those pertaining to ritual impurity and menstruation."
Those experiencing menstrual bleeding and ritual impurity recite the opening verses of [a chapter of the Quran] but do not complete the final verses thereof.
Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Hammad bin Salama narrated to me, from ‘Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Aliya, concerning a menstruating woman, who said: "Do not recite the Quran."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) used to recite the names of Asma (may Allah be pleased with her) while she was being veiled.
Muslim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me, he said: Qatadah said: "The person in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) remembers the name of Allah, the Exalted."

Sahlu ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to me from Siyar from Abu Wail, who said: It was said, "The one in a state of ritual impurity (janaba) does not recite [the Quran], nor does the menstruating woman, and it is not recited in the bathhouse. And there are two situations in which a servant does not mention Allah, namely when relieving himself and during sexual intercourse, except that a man, when he goes to his wife, should begin by mentioning Allah."
Yalaa narrated to me, saying: Abdullah al-Malik narrated to me from Ata’ about a menstruating woman: “Does she recite [the Quran]?” He said: “Not except a portion of a verse.”

Narrated Abu Huraira (RA) that he said: "Four things are not forbidden to a person in a state of ritual impurity (janaba) or a menstruating woman: SubhanAllah (Glory be to Allah), Alhamdulillahi (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illallah (There is no deity but Allah), and Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest)."

Abu Muhammad Abdullah was asked: "Is it permissible for a person in a state of ritual impurity to recite verses (of the Quran)?" He replied: "I do not like it."
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: He was asked about a menstruating woman hearing the prostration. He said, “She should not prostrate, for it is a prayer.”

Yaḥyá b. Ḥassān > Muḥammad b. al-Fuḍayl > al-Ḥasan b. al-Ḥakam > al-Ḥakam [Machine] About Ibrahim regarding women when they see blood while giving birth? He said, "It is menstruation and they should leave prayer."
"There is nothing more important than that prayer."
Attah narrated: "Nothing is more deserving of being prevented from doing than the obligatory prayer."
Narrated by Hasan: "Do not prostrate."

Abu al-Hasan al-Asadi narrated: Ahmad narrated to me, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from Yunus, from Zuhri, concerning a woman who sees her menstrual period and hears the prostration [being performed]. He said: "Do not prostrate until she performs ghusl."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA): The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the women: “Give charity, for you are the majority of the people of the Fire.” A woman, who was not from the elite women, said, “Why is that? Or because of what? Or for what reason?” He (ﷺ) said: “You outdo men in cursing and you reject your husbands.” Abdullah (RA) said: “There is nothing that lacks religious understanding and intellect that is more overpowering to men of authority in their affairs than women.” A man said to Abdullah (RA): “What is the deficiency in her intellect?” He said: “Her testimony is equal to the testimony of two men.” It was asked: “What is the deficiency in her religion?” He said: “She remains for so and so many days and nights without performing a single prayer to Allah.”
"When a woman is cleansed from menstruation, she should follow her garment that is next to her skin, and wash what has been affected by impurity, then pray in it."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "It would happen that one of us would have a garment, in which she would experience menstruation and in which she would perform ghusl. Then she would see a spot of her menstrual blood in it, so she would lick it off."
Narrated by Umm Salama: "One of you may be bled by a drop of blood. So, if that happens to one of you, let her wipe it off with her saliva."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "If a woman washes away blood and it does not go away, then let her change it with yellow safflower or saffron."
A woman asked Aishah, "Blood stains my garment, and I wash it but it does not go away, so should I cut it off?" Aishah replied, "The water is purifying."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), known as Abu al-Qasim, would share a single garment with me while I was menstruating and experiencing flow. If anything of mine touched him, he would wash what touched him and not extend that to anything else, and he would pray in it, then return. And if anything of mine touched him, he would do the same – wash the place it touched and not extend that to anything else, and he would pray in it.

Narrated Yazid ibn Harun, from Hisham al-Dustawa'i, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning what a woman wears of clothing while in menstruation: "If blood stains it, she washes it; otherwise, she is not obliged to wash it. And if she sweats in it, it suffices her to rinse it."

'Obaydullah ibn Musa narrated to me from 'Utman, from Mujahid, who said: "A menstruating woman prays in the clothes in which she menstruates, unless something of it affects her with blood, in which case she washes the place of the blood."
I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the blood of menstruation that stains the garment, and he said: "Scrub it, then sprinkle it with water."
The menstruating woman is not required to wash her garment unless there is blood upon it.

Narrated Asma bint Abu Bakr: I heard a woman asking the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about her garment when she became clean from menstruation, how should she deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: "If you see blood in it, rub it, then wring it out with water, then rinse the rest of it, and then pray in it."

Umm Qais bint Mihsan (RA) said: I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about the blood of menstruation found on clothing, and he said: "Wash it with water and sidr (lote tree leaves), and scrape it with a bone."

Narrated by Karima, who said: I heard Aisha, and a woman asked her about a garment that was stained with the blood of her menstruation. Aisha said: "Let her wash it with water." The woman said: "But we wash it and the stain remains?" Aisha said: "Indeed, water is purifying."
Aisha would see the traces of menstruation in her garment, and she would scrape it off with a stone, or a twig, or a horn, and then sprinkle water upon it.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me from Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi from Abd Allah ibn 'Utman ibn Khuzaim, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about a person who is in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) and sweats in his garment, then wipes it with the garment. He said: "There is nothing wrong with that."
Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, "He did not see any harm in the sweat of a person who performs ghusl (ritual bath) being on the garment."
Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from ash-Sha'bi that he considered it permissible.

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Humayd, from Hasan, who said: "Not all of the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to find two garments. He (the Prophet) said: 'If you bathe, are you not then clothed? So it is like that.'"

‘Amr ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, saying: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa’id, from Qasim ibn Muhammad, that ‘Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) was asked about a man who has intercourse with a woman, then puts on clothing in which he sweats. She did not see any harm in that.

Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, saying: “Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ‘Ata’, who said: ‘There is no harm if a person who is in a state of ritual impurity (junub) or a menstruating woman sweats while wearing clothing in which they pray.”

'Amru ibn 'Awn narrated to me, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to me from Abu Hamza, from Ibrahim concerning a man in a state of ritual impurity sweating in his garment, he said: "It does not harm him, and he should not pour water over him."
Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Hisham from Hammad from Ibrahim concerning a woman in ritual impurity (hayd) who sweats in her garments, "It is sufficient for her to rinse them with water."

Abdullah ibn Maslama narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, from Naafi’, from Ibn Umar, that he would perspire in his garment while being in a state of ritual impurity (junub), and then he would pray in it.

He, Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "He [the Prophet, peace be upon him] did not see any harm in the sweat of a menstruating woman or a person in a state of ritual impurity (janabah)."

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me from Zayd ibn Aslam who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, "What is permissible for me regarding my wife while she is menstruating?" He said, "Let her tighten her garment and then do as you wish [with the rest of her]."

Khalid narrated to me, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Naf'i', that Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Umar sent to Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) to ask her: Does a man consummate with his wife while she is menstruating? She said: "Let her tighten her garment around her lower part, and then let him consummate with her."

Narrated by Muhammad bin Isa: He said, "I narrated to me from Ibn Abi Zaidah, from Al-Ala' bin Al-Musayyib, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: 'The menstruating woman is visited by her husband in her marital bed and between her thighs, and if he discharges, she washes what affected her, and he performs ablution.'"

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: I asked Abd al-Karim about a menstruating woman, and he said: Ibrahim said: "Indeed, Ummi Imran knew that I would prick her side, meaning while she was menstruating."
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, and Malik ibn Mughul said: A man asked about the allowance for a menstruating woman. He (the Prophet) said: “He sees no harm in anything less than the blood.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whenever I would menstruate, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would command me to wear a cloth wrap, and he would consummate his marriage with me."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Al-Awza'i narrated to me, saying: Maimun ibn Mihran narrated to me, saying: 'Aisha was asked, "What is permissible for a man with his wife during her menstrual period?" She said: "Anything above the izar (garment)."

I said to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, "What is permissible for a man from his wife when she is menstruating?" She said, "Everything except intercourse." I said, "And what is forbidden for him from her when they are in ihram?" She said, "Everything except her speech."
"A man once asked me, 'What is the most virtuous of actions?' I replied, 'Avoiding the traces of blood.'"
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Ismail, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "When bloodshed ceases…"
Zakarriya ibn 'Adiyy narrated to me, he said: Sharik narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "There is no harm if a menstruating woman is touched between her thighs and on her navel."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Hasan ibn Salih narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "It turns and retreats, except for the defecation and menstruation."

Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) under a single blanket, and I felt what women feel (during menstruation). So I got up, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'What is wrong with you? Are you menstruating?' I said: 'I felt what women feel.' He said: 'That is what Allah has ordained for the daughters of Adam.' She said: 'So I got up and rectified myself, then I returned, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'Enter the blanket.' So I entered."

Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) said: While I was lying with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) in the Khumila, I had a menstrual period. So, I slipped away and took my menstrual clothes. He said, "Are you menstruating?" I said, "Yes." He called me, and I lay down with him in the Khumila. She (Umm Salama) and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to bathe from the same vessel due to janaba (ritual bath after sexual intercourse), and he used to kiss her while fasting.
Maymunah (RA) said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would consummate his marriage with his wives above the garment while they were menstruating."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would order one of us, when she was menstruating, to tighten her garment, and then he would approach her."

The Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I used to wear a wrap while in ritual impurity, then enter with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the same blanket."

'Amru ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Khalid ibn 'Abdullah, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: Ibn Jubayr was asked: "What is permissible for a man with his wife during her menstrual period?" He said: "Anything above the izar (waist cloth)."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Ibn ‘Aun narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from ‘Abidah, who was asked about a woman in her menstrual period. He said: "The bed is one, but the coverings are diverse. If they do not find [a separate covering], he should return a part of his covering to her."
Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sirin from Shurayh, who said to him: “That which is above the navel is private.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would wrap himself in me even when I was menstruating, and a garment separated me from him."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Thabit, from Anas (RA) that the Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would not eat with her, nor drink with her, and would drive her out of the house, and she would not be with them in the houses. So, the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about that, and Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed: “And they ask you about menstruation. Say, ‘It is a ritual impurity.’” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:222). So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them to eat with them, and to drink with them, and to let them be with them in the houses, and to do everything except intercourse. The Jews said: “What does this man want, but to contradict us in everything?” Then, ‘Abbad ibn Bishr and Usayd ibn Hudhayr (RA) came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him about that, and said: “O Messenger of Allah, should we marry them during menstruation?” The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned red with anger, so much so that we thought he was angry at them. So, they stood up and left. Then, a present of milk was sent after them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for them and brought them back and gave them milk to drink. So, we knew that he had not been angry at them.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Abu Hilal said, to me, Shayba ibn Hisham ar-Rasibi said: I asked Salim ibn Abdullah about a man who lies with his wife while she is menstruating in the same bedsheet. He said: "As for us, the family of Umar, we boycott them if they are menstruating."
Narrated by Ibn Umar: "There is nothing wrong with a woman's excess water (from ablution) or her rinsing, as long as she is not in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) or menstruating."
He said: "He places it in position, meaning upon the vulva."

Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), related: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) would consummate his marriage with his wives while they were menstruating, if they were wearing a garment that covered half of their thighs or knees, holding them back with it."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I would comb the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) while in a state of menstruation."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I would comb the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) while in a state of menstruation."
Khalid narrated to me, saying: Malik narrated to me from Naafi’, who said: "The maidservants of Ibn Umar would wash his feet while menstruating, and they would give him the cloth (to wipe himself)."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I would be brought a vessel and I would apply my mouth to it and drink while in menstruation, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would apply his mouth to the place where I had applied mine and drink. I would also be brought a wineskin and I would sip from it, and he would apply his mouth to the place where I had sipped and sip. Then he would order me and I would put on a covering while in menstruation, and he would consummate the marriage with me."

Narrated from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, he said: Sufyan narrated to me from Mughira from Ibrahim, who said: It was said, "A menstruating woman does not have the menstrual flow in her hand; she washes her hands, kneads dough, and prepares drinks."

Abu Zayd narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: He used to say, "Indeed, a menstruating woman's menstrual flow is not in her hand." And he used to say: "A menstruating woman is beloved to her husband."

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me from Hammad who said: I asked Ibrahim about shaking hands with a Jew, a Christian, a Zoroastrian, and a menstruating woman. He did not see any requirement for ablution in it.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was in the mosque, and he said to a young girl, "Bring me the khumra (a garment)." She said, "He intended to spread it out and pray upon it." She then said, "Indeed, she is menstruating." He said, "Indeed, her menstruation is not in her hand."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would bring his head out to me from the mosque, and I would wash it," meaning while he was in seclusion (itikaf).
Al-Mulla ibn Asad narrated to me, he said: Abu Awana narrated to me, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "He [Ibrahim] did not see any harm in a menstruating woman washing a sick person."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I used to wash the head of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) while in menstrual impurity."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I used to wash the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) while I was menstruating, and he was observing seclusion (in the mosque)."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: I heard Mughirah say: Abu Dhiyān sent to Ibrahim asking him whether a menstruant woman could perform ablution for a sick person? He said: "Yes, and she can support him (in prayer)." I said: No. Then I said to Mughirah: Did you hear this from Ibrahim? He said: No. Abdullah said: And she can support him – meaning in prayer.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to her, "Hand me the container of dye." She said, "I am menstruating." He said, "It is not in your hand."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Kathir ibn Shanzir from al-Hasan: that he was asked about a menstruating woman who drank from water, whether ablution could be performed with it? He laughed and said: Yes.
I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about the eating of food belonging to a menstruating woman, and he said, "Eat it."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: He used to order his maidservant to hand him the water pitcher from the mosque. She would say, “I am menstruating.” He would say, “Your menstruation is not in your hand,” and she would hand it to him.

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated: Hisham ibn Humeid narrated to me: Al-Ala’ ibn al-Harith narrated to me from Hāram ibn Hakim, from his uncle, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the matter of a menstruating woman’s husband sharing food with her. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Indeed, one of my family was menstruating, and we shared a meal together, if Allah wills.”
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "She would not see any harm in a menstruating woman touching khumur."

Muhammad ibn Isa reported: Hushaym narrated to me, and Mughira narrated, from Ibrahim and Yunus, from Hasan and ‘Abd al-Malik, from ‘Ata, that Muhammad said, and Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Qattan narrated to me, from ‘Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning a menstruating woman: “When she is cleansed of the blood, her husband should not approach her until she performs ghusl.” ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to me, from ‘Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, a similar report.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan was asked: "Can a man have intercourse with his wife if the bleeding has stopped from her before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)?" He said: "No." It was said: "What if she leaves the bath for two days or some days?" He said: "She is considered pure."

Narrated from Mujahid, interpreting the verse, "And do not approach them until they purify themselves” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 222), he said: “Until the bleeding stops. And when they have purified themselves,” interpreting the verse, “So when they have purified themselves,” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 222) he said: “When they bathe.”
Narrated ‘Mujahid: (Regarding the verse: “And they ask you about menstruation.”) When the bleeding stops, then they should purify themselves (perform ghusl).

"’Ubaidullah narrated to me, that ‘Utman ibn al-Aswad said: I asked Mujahid about a woman who sees her menstrual period: Is it permissible for her husband to have relations with her before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: "No, until prayer becomes permissible for her."
I asked Ata, and Maimun ibn Mihran, and Hammad narrated to me from Ibrahim, and they said: "It should not be approached until she performs ghusl."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Hisham, from Hasan, concerning a man who has intercourse with his wife before she has bathed after seeing purity, he said: "She is in a state of ritual impurity until she bathes, and there is an expiation upon him, and he is permitted to have relations with her until she bathes."
Al-Mulla ibn Asad narrated to me, Abd al-Wahid narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, who said, "Her husband does not approach her."
"By Allah, I do not lie with my wife on the day she becomes clean (after menstruation) until a day has passed."

Ya'la ibn 'Ubaid narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Malik narrated to me from 'Ata' concerning a woman who sees her purity: Does her husband approach her before she performs ghusl? He [‘Ata’] said: "No, until she performs ghusl."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to me, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaim, from 'Ata' concerning a woman whose menstruation ceases, he said: "If she experiences desire, she should wash her private parts and then proceed."

Farwa ibn Abi al-Maghra’ reported: I heard Sharik, and a man asked him a question, saying: "A woman’s menstruation ceases; may her husband approach her before she performs ghusl?" He said: ‘Abd al-Malik reported from ‘Ata’ that he permitted this due to lust.” Abu Muhammad said: “I fear that this may be an error, and I fear that it is from a narration of Layth, which I do not know from the narration of ‘Abd al-Malik.” Abu Muhammad said: “By ‘lust’ is meant that which one desires.”
Muhammad ibn Isa reported: Hushaym claimed to us from Abu Hurra, Wasil ibn Abd ar-Rahman, from Hasan, who said, "I saw women of the women of Medina praying in khilāb."
Aisha was asked about a woman wiping over her hair dye, and she said, "It is more beloved to me that my hand be cut with knives than that."

Narrated by Abu Sa’id, that a woman asked Aisha, "Does a woman pray while wearing kohl?" Aisha said, "Ask him, and against his will." Abu Muhammad said: Abu Sa’id is the son of Abu al-‘Anabs, and the name of Abu al-‘Anabs is Sa’id ibn Kathir ibn ‘Ubaid.

"The women among us used to dye their hair at night, and when morning came, they would uncover it, perform ablution, and pray. Then they would dye it again after the prayer. When noon approached, they would uncover it, perform ablution, and pray. They had the best dye, and it did not prevent them from praying."
Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Nafi’, that the women of Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to dye their hair while menstruating.

"The women among us, when they prayed the night prayer (Isha), would dye their hair. Then, when morning came, they would let it loose and perform ablution and pray. And when they prayed the noon prayer (Zuhr), they would dye their hair. Then, when they intended to pray the afternoon prayer (Asr), they would let it loose, beautify their dye, and not delay the prayer."

Narrated: Muhammad ibn Isa, he said: Hushaim narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim. And Ismail ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Amir, concerning a man who visits his wife while she is menstruating, they said: "It is a sin for him, he seeks forgiveness from Allah and repents to Him, and does not return [to that action]." Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Zaidah narrated to us, from Al-Muthanna, from Ata’, similar to this.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, "A sin came to him for which there is no expiation."
It was narrated that his father was asked about a man who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating. He said: "He should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Allah."
"Seek forgiveness for Allah, and you have nothing upon you," meaning: if he has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating.
I was sitting and hearing a man being questioned about visiting his wife while she was menstruating. He said, "May Allah forgive him."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, that a man came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and said, "I saw in a dream as if I was vomiting blood." He said, "Does your wife menstruate?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Fear Allah, and do not repeat [such dreams]."
Narrated Muhammad ibn Yusuf: He said, "Tell me about the man who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating," and he said, "Let him seek forgiveness from Allah."

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: I heard Hasan say, concerning one who breaks a fast during Ramadan, "It is as if he has freed a slave, or slaughtered a sacrificial animal, or given twenty sa’s of food to forty poor people." And concerning one who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, it is the same.

Narrated by Abu al-Walid, he said: Shaykh narrated to me, from Khusayf, from Misqam, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said concerning the man who visits his wife while she is menstruating, "He should give in charity half a dinar."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying, "Shareeb narrated to me from al-Hakam, from Abd al-Hamid, from Misqam, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning the man who visits his wife while she is menstruating. Al-Hakam was unsure, but he said: 'He should give charity of one dinar, or half a dinar.'"

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: Concerning the man who visits his wife while she is menstruating, (the Prophet said) “He should give in charity a dinar or half a dinar.” Shu’bah said, “As for my narration, it is authentic (marfu’), but so-and-so and so-and-so said it is not authentic (not marfu’). Some of the people said, ‘Tell us your narration and abandon what so-and-so and so-and-so said.’ He (Shu’bah) said, “By Allah, I do not like that I should live in this world as long as Noah lived, and I narrated this or remained silent about it.” Abu Muhammad said: Abd al-Hamid was the son of Zayd, the son of Abd al-Rahman, the son of Zayd, the son of al-Khuttab, and he was the governor appointed by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz to Kufa.
He (the Prophet) said: "If one visits her while she is in a state of bleeding, then a dinar (is sufficient), and if one visits her after the bleeding has ceased, then half a dinar (is sufficient)."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said concerning the man who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating: "He should give in charity half a dinar."

Narrated ‘Abd Al-Hamid bin Zayd bin Al-Khattab (RA): “‘Umar bin Al-Khattab (RA) had a wife who disliked intimacy. Whenever he intended to approach her, she would claim to be menstruating. He would then have intercourse with her, and if she was truthful, he would visit the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (peace be upon him) would order him to give in charity two-fifths of a dinar.”

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If a man visits his wife while she is menstruating, and the discharge is a bright red color, then let him give charity of one dinar, and if it is a yellowish color, then let him give charity of half a dinar."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to me from Al-A’mash, from Al-Hakam, from Misqam, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was asked about a man who visits his wife while she is menstruating. He (Ibn Abbas) said, "He should give in charity a dinar or half a dinar." Ibrahim said, "He should seek forgiveness from Allah."
Narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that if a man has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, then he should give in charity a dinar.

Yala ibn 'Ubaid narrated to me, that 'Abd al-Malik narrated to me, from 'Ata, concerning a man who had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating, he said: "Let him give charity of one dinar."
He narrated to us, 'Ubaidullah ibn Musa, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Misqam, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "He gives a dinar or half a dinar."

Narrated by Wahb bin Sa'id, from Shu'aib bin Ishaq, from Al-Awza'i, concerning a man who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, or she has seen the purity (end of menstruation) but has not performed ghusl (ritual bath), he said: "Let him seek forgiveness from Allah and give in charity two-fifths of a dinar."

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Muhsir from ‘Abd al-Malik from ‘Ata’ who said: "If a man has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, he should give in charity half a dinar." A man from the people said to him: "But Hasan says: ‘He should manumit a slave.” He (Ata’) said: "I do not forbid you from drawing near to Allah as much as you are able."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Musa, from Ibn Abi Layla, from ‘Ata, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning that which occurs with a woman while she is menstruating, he said: "He should give charity of one dinar."

I asked Hafsa, the daughter of ‘Abd ar-Rahman, who is the son of Abu Bakr, “I wish to ask you about something, and I feel shy to ask you about it.” She said, “Ask, O my brother’s son, about whatever has occurred to you.” I said, “I ask you about the women’s entry [into their husbands] from behind.” She said, “My mother, Umm Salama, informed me that the Ansar did not practice [this], and the Muhajirun did. A man from the Muhajirun married a woman from the Ansar, and he practiced [it] with her, but the Ansar woman refused. So she came to Umm Salama and mentioned that to her. When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived, the Ansar woman felt shy and left. Then Umm Salama mentioned that to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Call her for me.” She was called for him, and he said to her, “Your wives are fields for you, so go to your fields as you will. [Quran 2:223] One way.” And the “one way” is the single path.

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Aban ibn Salih, from Mujahid, who said: "I recited the Quran to Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) three times. I would stop at every verse and ask him about its revelation and its context. I said to Ibn Abbas: 'What is the meaning of Allah’s statement: "And when they purify themselves, then come to them from where Allah has commanded you" [Surah Al-Baqarah (2):222]?' He said: 'From where Allah has commanded you to leave them.'"

Narrated from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, he said: Sufyan narrated to me, from 'Utman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning [the verse: "And fulfill their obligations to them in a fair manner, but if you intend to divorce them, then give them their due allowance according to the prescribed manner until they complete their term; and if you return them, then they have no right to withhold anything of what you gave them, except for what they have earned thereafter. And fear Allah and know that Allah sees what you do." (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:222)], he said: "They were commanded to come from where they were forbidden."

Narrated Abu Razīn: He said, "Approach them from the way Allah has commanded you," (referring to the verse: "And when you resolve to marry women, give them their dowry with a good heart...") Then he said, "From the path of purity."
Narrated Mujahid, interpreting the verse: "And do you leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives?" (Surah Ash-Shu'ara, 166), he said: "By Allah, it is the foreplay."

Narrated ‘Ikrimah: We were sitting with ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan when he said, “Your wives are fields for you, so cultivate your fields as you will.” Then he recited, “And your wives are lawful for you as fields.” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 223) He said, “It is only the vagina.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Ali al-Rifa'i narrated to me, saying: I heard Hasan say: The Jews did not cease to intensify their pressure on the Muslims. They would say: "O companions of Muhammad, by Allah, it is not permissible for you to approach your wives except in one way." He (Hasan) said: Then Allah revealed: "Your wives are fields for you, so go to your fields as you will." (Surah Al-Baqarah, 223) Then Allah released the believers and their need.

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him: About the verse, “And when you approach them from above or from below, there is no sin on you,” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:223), it was said, “Wait until he has intercourse.”

Khalifa ibn Khayyat narrated to me, saying: “The people of pre-Islamic times used to do something similar to what the Zoroastrians did with women during their menstrual period. This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and the verse [And they ask you about menstruation. Say, ‘It is a ritual impurity, so keep away from women during menstruation…’ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:222)] was revealed. Consequently, their situation only worsened.”

Khalifa narrated to me, Mu'ammal narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the statement: "Say, it is an affliction" (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:222), he said: "It is the blood."
He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Salit, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, saying: "Say, it is an aversion," (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 222), he said: "It is filth."

Narrated: Khalil ibn Khayyat said, "Tell us, Al-Mu'tamir said, 'I heard Layth narrate, from 'Isa ibn Qays, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who recited: 'Your wives are fields for you, so go to your fields as you will.' (Surah Al-Baqarah, 223) He said, 'If you wish, practice 'azl (coitus interruptus), and if you wish, do not practice it.'"
Khalifa narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me from 'Auf from Hasan who said: "As you wish," meaning: entering it through the vagina.

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah Al-Ansari (RA): The Jews said to the Muslims, "A child is born crooked if a man has intercourse with his wife from behind." So Allah revealed: "Your wives are fields [ḥurṣun] for you, so go to your fields as you will." [Quran 2:223]

Narrated ‘Amru bin ‘Aun, from Khalid bin Abdullah, from Khalid Al-Hazra’i, from ‘Ikrimah: [Mentioning the verse: "And approach them from where and how you will," (Al-Baqarah 2:223)], he (the Prophet) said: "Their families come to them in whatever manner they wish, standing, sitting, in front of them, and from behind them."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Sa’id al-Ashja’: He said, “I narrated to me Ibn Idris, from his father, from Yazid ibn al-Walid, from Ibrahim. [Ibrahim said,] ‘Give them from where Allah has commanded you [in Surat al-Baqarah, verse 222]’ – he said, ‘[It is] in the private parts.’”

Mujahid said: "Whoever approaches his wife through her backside, it is like it being from a man. Then he recited: ‘And they ask you about menstruation. Say, it is a purification, so keep away from women during their menstruation and do not approach them until they are clean. And when they have cleansed themselves, then come to them as Allah has commanded you.’ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:222) – [referring to] keeping away from them during menstruation: the vulva. Then he recited: ‘Your wives are fields for you, so go to your fields as you will.’ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:223) – standing, sitting, facing, and turning away in the vulva."
"Whoever goes to a menstruating woman, or a woman in her backside, or a diviner and believes in what he says, then he has rejected what Allah has revealed to Muhammad."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah Ash-Shaqri, from Abu Al-Qaqaa' Al-Jarmi, who said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abu Abdur-Rahman, may I approach my wife whenever I wish?" He said: "Yes." He said: "From where I wish?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And how I wish?" He said: "Yes." Then a man said to him: "O Abu Abdur-Rahman, surely this man intends evil." He said: "No, the wombs of women are inviolable for you." It was asked Abdullah: "Do you say this?" He said: "Yes."
Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, from Dawood, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he disliked a man visiting his wife through her back passage, and he considered it a severe defect.

Indeed, you come with a shameful act that none before you from among the people of the world has come with. [Quran, Surat Al-Ankabut, 28] He [‘Amr ibn Dinār] said: “No male has mentioned [intimately] to another male until the people of Lot did so.”
One who approaches a woman from behind, Allah the Exalted will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.

"Narrated by 'Ali ibn Talq: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If anyone of you commits an act of impurity during prayer, let him turn away and perform ablution, then pray." And the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not approach women from behind, for Allah does not feel shame from the truth." It was asked Abdullah: Did 'Ali ibn Talq have companionship (Sahaba)? He said: Yes."

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Layth narrated to me, saying: Harith ibn Ya’qub narrated to me, from Saeed ibn Yasar, Abu al-Hubab, who said: I said to Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "What is your opinion regarding slave girls when one sweetens them?" He said: "And what is sweetening?" I mentioned the anus, and he said: "Would anyone among the Muslims do such a thing?"

Narrated by ‘Ubaidullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Husayn al-Ansari: A man from my people, one of my trusted companions, told me that Harim ibn ‘Abdullah said, “We were discussing the matter of women in a gathering of the people of Banu Waqif and what was done with them. Then Khuzaymah ibn Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him) said, ‘I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: “O people, indeed Allah does not feel shame about the truth. Do not approach women in their backsides.”’”

Narrated Mujahid: They used to avoid women during menstruation and would approach them from behind, and they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, so Allah revealed: “And they ask you about menstruation. Say, ‘It is a ritual impurity, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are clean.’ And when they have cleansed themselves, then come to them as Allah has ordained for you. And announce to them what Allah has taught you, and reckon Allah’s favor upon you and your instruction. Perhaps they will be mindful.” (Al-Baqarah 2:222) “In the vulva, and do not transgress it.”

Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to me, Yunus ibn Bukair narrated to me, Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Aban ibn Salih narrated to me, from Tawus, and Sa’id, and Mujahid, and Ata’ that they used to disapprove of women coming [to the mosque] through their backsides, and they would say: “It is disbelief.”
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Al-Awza'i narrated to me from Ata and from Zuhri, that they said: "The purification from janaabah (sexual impurity) and menstruation is one (ritual)."
Hudayfa (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “To his wife, ‘intermingle water in your hair before a small fire intermingles with it.’”

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, he said: Zaidah narrated to me, from Sadaqah ibn Sa’id al-Hanafi, who narrated to me, that Juma’ ibn ‘Umayr, one of the tribe of Taym ibn Thalaabah, said: “I entered with my mother and my aunt to ‘Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), and one of them asked her: ‘How do you perform ablution?’ She said: ‘The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would perform his purification for prayer, and he would pour water over his head three times, and we pour it over our heads five times because of the braids.’”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) was asked about a woman who bathes and washes her hair. She said, "How fortunate she is, even if she spends a dirham on it! It is sufficient for her to pour water over her head three times."
He (the Prophet) said: "She would comb it through with her fingers."

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: Concerning the menstruating woman and the one in a state of ritual impurity, "they pour water, and they do not comb their hair." Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated: He told us, Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Abu Zubair, from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning the menstruating woman and the one in a state of ritual impurity: "they pour water, and they do not comb their hair." Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated: He told us, Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Ata', a similar report.
Ibrahim said: "If its roots and ends are moistened, it will not break."
The wives of Ibn Umar and his mothers (stepmothers) would, when they performed ghusl (ritual bath), not remove their menstrual cloth or the cloth used after sexual intercourse.
"She (Um Salama) said: 'They should not remove their cerements (due to menstruation) or from ritual impurity.'"

Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said, “I tie my hair very tightly.” He said: “Give me three handfuls [of hair], and then pinch [my fingers] after each handful.”

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, that Zaidah narrated to me, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, from Hudhaifa, that he said to his wife: "Pluck out the hair (pubic hair), for there is no fire that touches it, even if a little remains upon it." Mansur said: "He meant (the state of) Janabah (sexual impurity)."
Hudayfa said to his wife: "Remove the hair with water; no fire touches it, however little remains of it."
Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When a woman performs ghusl for janaabah, she should not uproot her hair, but should pour water over its roots and moisten it."

Yahya related to me from Malik from Ata’ about a woman who experiences janaba (ritual impurity) and her head is braided; does she unravel it? He (Malik) said: “No, but she pours water over her head, pouring, until it saturates the roots of the hair.”

Aisha, the mother of the believers, may Allah be pleased with her, said to me: “Doesn’t one of you, when she purifies herself from menstruation, use something of costus, if she finds it? If she doesn’t find it, then something of asafoetida? If she doesn’t find it, then something of black seeds? If she doesn’t find it, then something of salt.”
"When a woman cleanses herself from menstruation, she should seek out any trace of blood with perfume."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: “His wives and mothers of his children used to bathe from menstruation and from janaabah (sexual impurity), and they did not cut their hair, but they would lavishly wet it.”
Al-Mulla ibn Asad narrated to me, he said: Abu Awana narrated to me from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "There is no harm for a menstruating woman to take something from the mosque."
Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Ja'far ibn al-Harith, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "A menstruating woman may handle objects within the mosque, but she should not enter it."
Muslim narrated from Hisham, from Qatadah, who said: "The person who is in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) may enter the mosque, but he does not place himself (i.e., pray) therein."
Yahya related to me from Malik from Ata’ about a menstruating woman: “Does she take anything from the mosque?” He said: “Yes, except the Mus'haf (the written Quran).”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me, he said: Qatadah narrated to me from Abu Mijliz, from Ibn Abbas, who said regarding the verse: "And [those] who are under travel from the state of ritual impurity," [Surah An-Nisa, 43], he said: "It is the traveler."

Narrated Anas (RA): Regarding the verse, "But those who purify themselves among the believers… [Quran 4:43],” he (the Prophet) said: “The one in a state of ritual impurity may pass through the mosque but should not sit therein.”

Abu 'Ubaidah said: "The one in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) passes through the mosque and does not sit in it." Then he recited this verse: "And do not be intimate with anyone in a state of ritual impurity until he has purified himself." (Surah An-Nisa, 43)
Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, Sharik narrated to me, from Simak, from Ikrimah, and Salim, from Saeed, that they said: "He passes by and does not reside therein."
Narrated Jabir (RA): "We used to walk in the mosque while being in a state of ritual impurity (janabah), and we did not see any harm in that."

Yahya related to me from Ya'li bin 'Ubaid, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', concerning a woman in her menstrual period who has an amulet or writing around her neck. He said: "If it is made of leather, then she should remove it. But if it is a crafted stick of silver, then there is nothing wrong with it, if she wishes to keep it, and if she wishes, she may remove it." It was said to 'Abdullah: "Do you say this?" He said: "Yes."

Narrated by Matar: I asked Hasan and Ata’ about a woman who is traveling with her husband and menstruates, then becomes clean, but finds no water. They said, "She performs tayammum and prays." I said to them, "May her husband have intercourse with her?" They said, "Yes, prayer is more important than that."

Sa'id ibn al-Mughira narrated: I narrated from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, concerning a woman who purifies herself but finds no water. He said: "Her husband may touch her if she performs tayammum." It was asked of Abdullah: Do you say this? He said: Yes, by Allah!
Yazid narrated to me, he said: Sharik narrated to me, from Layth, from Tawus, concerning the purification of a female slave if she does not menstruate, he said: "Forty-five [days]."
Yazid narrated to me, Sharik narrated to me, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’i, from Abu Qilaba, who said: "Three months."

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Wahid, from al-Awza’i, who said: I asked Zuhri about a man who buys a female slave who has not reached puberty nor is pregnant, how long should he wait before consummating the marriage? He said: "Three months." And Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said: "Forty-five days."

Hisham ibn Jamil narrated to me from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Bishr, from Ikrimah, who said: "By a month." It was asked of Abdullah: "Which of these do you say?" He said: "Three months are more secure, and a month suffices."

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The example of the obligatory prayers is like a river flowing by the door of one of you, which he bathes in five times a day."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tell me, what would you say if a river flowed past the door of one of you and he bathed in it every day five times, what would remain of his dirt?" They said: "Nothing of his dirt would remain." He (ﷺ) said: "Likewise, the five (obligatory) prayers abolish all sins." Abdullah said: The Hadith of Abu Huraira is more authentic with me.

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us on the authority of Shu’bah, who narrated from Sa’d ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, during the time of al-Hajjaj, and he used to delay the prayers from their appointed times. Jabir said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pray the Zuhr prayer when the sun had declined, the Asr prayer while it was still bright or fading, the Maghrib prayer when the sun had set, and the ‘Isha’ prayer, sometimes he would hasten it and sometimes delay it. If the people gathered, he would hasten it, and if they delayed, he would delay it. And he would sometimes pray the Fajr prayer in the darkness.

Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, that ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz delayed the prayer one day. ‘Urwa ibn al-Zubayr entered upon him and informed him that al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba had delayed the prayer one day. ‘Urwa informed him that Abu Mas’ud al-Ansari entered upon him and said: “What is this, O Mughira? Did you not know that Gabriel descended upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and prayed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed? Then he prayed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed? Then he prayed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed? Then he prayed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed? Then he prayed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed, and then he said: ‘You have been commanded with this.’” He said: “Know what you are reporting, O ‘Urwa. Are you saying that Gabriel fixed the time of prayer for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?” He said: “Bashir ibn Abi Mas’ud also narrates from his father in this way.”
‘Urwa reported: And Aisha informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray the afternoon prayer while the sun was in her chamber before it appeared.

Narrated by Muhammad ibn Humayd: He said, “Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) arrived in Medina, people gathered for prayer until the appointed times without any call. So the Prophet (peace be upon him) considered making a horn like that of the Jews who call to their prayers with it. Then he disliked it. Then he ordered a bell to be made so that it could be struck for the Muslims for the prayer. While they were doing that, Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih, the brother of Harith ibn al-Khazraj, had a dream. He came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, a man on two green garments passed by me last night, carrying a bell in his hand.
