I said to him, ‘Are you following this bell?’ He said, ‘What would you do with it?’ I said, ‘We would call to prayer with it.’ He said, ‘Would you not prefer I show you something better than that?’ I said, ‘What is it?’ He said, ‘You say: Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, Ashhadu an Muhammadan Rasulullah, Ashhadu an Muhammadan Rasulullah, Hayya ‘ala as-salat, Hayya ‘ala as-salat, Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Hayya ‘ala al-falah, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah.’ Then he repeated it briefly and said, ‘The prayer has begun, the prayer has begun, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah.’ When the Prophet (peace be upon him) was informed about it, he said, ‘It is a true vision, if Allah wills. So, stand with Bilal and let him recite it, for he has a louder voice than you.’ When Bilal gave the call to prayer, Umar ibn al-Khattab heard it while he was in his house, so he came out to the Prophet
Narrated from Bilal: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Bilal announces the prayer at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum announces it."

Narrated by Aisha: The Prophet (peace be upon him) had two Muadhdhins: Bilal and Ibn Umm Maktum. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Bilal announces the Adhan at night, so eat and drink until you hear the Adhan of Ibn Umm Maktum.” Al-Qasim said: There was nothing between them except that this one would descend and this one would ascend.

Uthman ibn Umar ibn Faris narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Hafs ibn Umar ibn Saad, the muezzin, that "Saad used to give the call to prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him." Hafs said: My family told me that Bilaal came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, to announce the Fajr prayer, and they said: "He is asleep." So Bilaal called out at the top of his voice: "The prayer is better than sleep." Thus, it was incorporated into the call to prayer for Fajr. Abu Muhammad said: It is said: Saad was Al-Qaraz.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) said: "During the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), the adhan was called in pairs, and the iqama was called once. However, when he said, 'The prayer is established,' he would say it twice. And when we heard the iqama, one of us would perform ablution and proceed [to the prayer]."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi and 'Affan narrated to me: Shu'bah narrated to me from Khalid al-Hadhdha'i from Abu Qilaba from Anas, who said: "Bilal was ordered to perform the Adhan and to utter the Iqama in a single tone."
Bilal was ordered to perform the Adhan and to utter the Iqama, except for the words, "Hayya 'ala as-Salat" and "Hayya 'ala al-Falah."

Narrated by Abu Mahdhura: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered some twenty men to give the Adhan, and he was pleased with the voice of Abu Mahdhura, so he taught him the Adhan: “Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to the prayer, come to the prayer, Come to success, Come to success. Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and the Iqama, two times two times.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi and Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to me: Hammam narrated to us, he said: Amr al-Ahwal narrated to us, and Hajjaj said in his narration: Amr ibn Abd al-Wahid narrated to me: Makhul narrated to me, that Ibn Muhriz narrated to him, that Abu Mahzura narrated to him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He taught me the Adhan in nineteen words, and the Iqama in seventeen words."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, that Sufyan narrated, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he saw Bilal giving the Adhan. He said, "So I began to follow his mouth here and there with the Adhan."
Bilal stationed the goat, then gave the adhan, and placed his two fingers in his ears, and I saw him turning them in his ears.
Two supplications are never (or rarely) rejected: supplication at the time of the call to prayer, and supplication during combat when soldiers clash.
Narrated by Abu Sa’id: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When you hear the call to prayer, say what the muadhdhin says."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Hisham al-Dustawa’i, from Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from Isa ibn Talha, who said: We entered upon Mu’awiya, and the herald called out, “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.” Mu’awiya said, “Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.” He said: “I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah.” Mu’awiya said: “And I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah.” He said: “I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” Mu’awiya said: “And I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

Yahya related to me, and some of our companions informed me, that when he said, "Hayya 'ala as-salat (Come for the prayer)," he would say, "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (There is no power and no strength except in Allah)," and then Mu'awiya said, "Thus I heard your Prophet saying this."

Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that Mu'awiya heard the muezzin say: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar," and Mu'awiya said: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar." Then the muezzin said: "Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah, Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah." And Mu'awiya said: "Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah, Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah." Then the muezzin said: "Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullahi, Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullahi," and Mu'awiya said: "Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullahi, Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullahi." Then the muezzin said: "Hayya 'ala as-salat, Hayya 'ala as-salat," and Mu'awiya said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." Then the muezzin said: "Hayya 'ala al-falah, Hayya 'ala al-falah," and Mu'awiya said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." Then the muezzin said: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illallah," and Mu'awiya said: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illallah." Then he said: "Thus, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did."

Narrated Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When the call to prayer is announced, Satan flees away with a sound like a jolt, so that he does not hear the Adhan. And when the Adhan is concluded, he returns. And when the covering (of the mosque) is done, he flees. And when the covering is concluded, he turns back to tempt between man and his soul, saying, 'Remember such and such,' things he had not remembered before." Abu Muhammad said: "The covering means: the Iqama is announced.

Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, saw a man exiting the mosque after the muadhdhin had announced the call to prayer. He said, "As for this man, he has disobeyed Abu al-Qasim, peace and blessings be upon him."

Al-Hakam narrated to me from Shu'aib, from Zuhri, who informed me that Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) went out when the sun began to decline, and he offered the Zuhr prayer with them.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the heat intensifies, cool yourselves with the prayer, for the intensity of the heat is from the heat of Hell."
Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the 'Asr prayer, then the shepherd would go to the grazing grounds, and he would find them and the sun was still high.
Narrated: Salama bin Al-Akwa’ said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray the Maghrib prayer at the hour when the sun sets, when its curtain (the edge) disappears.”
"My community will continue to prosper as long as they do not await the mingling of the stars (at sunset)."

I swear, I knew the time for this prayer – meaning the Isha prayer – better than anyone. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pray it when the moon had set for the third (time). Yahya said: He dictated it to us from his book from Bashir ibn Thabit.

Hajjaj ibn Mihal and Amr ibn Aasim reported: Hammad ibn Salama told us, he said: ‘Asim ibn Bahdala told us on the authority of Abu Salih, from Abu Huraira, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer one night until it was almost a third of the night or close to it. Then he came and people were asleep, some were reclining, and some were in groups. He became angry and said: ‘If a man called out to the people to a race or two, they would respond to him, and yet they neglect this prayer. I would consider ordering a man to lead the people in prayer, and then I would lie in wait for the people of these houses who neglect this prayer, and I would set their houses ablaze with fire.’”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) delayed the Isha’ prayer until Umar ibn al-Khattab called out to him, “The women and children have fallen asleep.” So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) arose and said, “Indeed, none of the people of the earth prays this prayer except you.” And on that day, none prayed except the people of Medina.

Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed ‘Itikaaf (seclusion in the mosque) one night until nearly the whole night had passed, and the people of the mosque had fallen asleep. Then he left (his place of seclusion) and performed (the prayer), and said: “Indeed, this is its time, but I feared burdening my community.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the prayer one night, and it was said, “O Messenger of Allah, the prayer!” The women and children had slept, so he went out while wiping the water from his side, and he said, “This is the time, were it not to cause hardship to my community.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "The wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray Fajr (dawn) prayer with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and then they would return, wrapped in their cloaks, before they could be recognized."
"Hasten to the Fajr (dawn) prayer, for it is the greatest in reward."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Illuminate yourselves with the Fajr prayer, for it is the greatest in reward." Or, "Brighten yourselves."
Whoever catches a single rak'ah of a prayer, he has fulfilled it.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever catches the Fajr prayer before sunrise, he has attained it, and whoever catches the Asr prayer before sunset, he has attained it."

Narrated by Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "If you see a man frequenting the mosque, testify to his faith, for Allah says: 'Indeed, [those who] maintain the mosques of Allah are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and stand in prayer...' [Surah At-Taubah 9:18]"

Narrated ‘Uthman: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever prays the Isha’ prayer in congregation, it is as if he has prayed half the night, and whoever prays the Fajr prayer in congregation, it is as if he has prayed the whole night."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah narrated to me, he said: Al-Walid ibn ‘Ayyar narrated to me, he said: I heard Abu ‘Amr al-Shaybani saying: The companion of this house informed me – and he gestured with his hand towards the house of Abdullah – that he asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): “Which deed is best or most beloved to Allah?” He (the Prophet) said: “Observing the prayers at their appointed times.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Abdullah, who is Ibn An-Nu'man Al-Anṣārī, narrated to me, saying: Sa'd Ibn Ishaq Ibn Ka'b Ibn 'Ujah Al-Anṣārī narrated to me from his father, from Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us while we were seven in the mosque - three of us were from our Arab brethren and four were from our mawali (clients/freedmen), or four of us were from our Arab brethren and three were from our mawali. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then came out to us from one of his chambers and sat with us, and said: "What brings you to sit here?" We said: "Waiting for the prayer." He then tapped with his finger on the earth for a moment. Then he raised his head to us and said: "Do you know what your Lord says?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Indeed, He says: 'Whoever prays the prayer for its appointed time and establishes its limits, then he has a covenant with Me by which I will admit him to Paradise. And whoever does not pray the prayer for its appointed time and does not establish its limits, then he has no covenant with Me; if I will, I will admit him to Hell, and if I will, I will admit him to Paradise.'"

Narrated by Abu adh-Dhar, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to him: “How will you be when you remain among a people who delay the prayer from its time?” Abu adh-Dhar said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Pray the prayer at its time and then leave. If the prayer is established and you are in the mosque, pray with them.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Abu Imran al-Jawni narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn As-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "O Abu Dharr, what will you do if you encounter rulers who delay the prayer from its time?" I said: "What do you command me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Pray the prayer at its time, and make your prayer with them a voluntary (Naflah) prayer."

Narrated by Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps and misses it, he should pray it when he remembers it. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says, 'And establish prayer for My remembrance.'" (Surah Taha, verse 14)
Narrated from my father, he (the Prophet) said: "Indeed, he who misses the prayer of 'Asr, it is as if his family and his wealth have been abandoned."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever misses the prayer of 'Asr, it is as if he has lost his family and his offspring." 
Abu Muhammad said: Or his wealth.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Trench: “May Allah fill their graves and their homes with fire, just as they prevented us from the middle prayer until the sun had set.”

Narrated Jabir: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is nothing between a slave and disbelief or polytheism except abandoning the prayer." Abu Muhammad said: "The slave, if he abandons it without an excuse or reason, must be considered a disbeliever, and he should not be described as a disbeliever."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: While the people were praying Fajr in Quba, a man came and said, “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been ordered to face the Ka’bah (in prayer), so face it.” The faces of the people were towards Sham (Syria), so they turned their faces towards the Ka’bah.

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Musa, from Isra’il, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about those who died while praying towards the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)?" So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "And Allah would not waste the faith of the people." [Surah Al-Baqarah (2):143]

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would begin the prayer with Takbir, begin the recitation with 'All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds' (Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 2), and conclude it with Taslim."
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used not to stand up for the prayer unless he raised his hands to the extent of his forearms.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, when he began the prayer, say Takbir, then say: ‘I have turned my face towards Him Who created the heavens and the earth, as a follower of the right way, and I am not of those who associate partners with Allah. Verily, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are all for Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. And I have been commanded with this, and I am the first of the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King; there is no god but You. You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and confessed my sin, so forgive me all my sins. There is none who can forgive sins except You. And guide me to the best of conduct; there is none who can guide to the best of it except You. And turn away from me its evil; there is none who can turn away its evil except You. Here I respond to Your call, and accept Your bounty; all goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not towards You. I am with You and towards You. Blessed are You and Exalted. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.'"

Narrated by Abu Sa’id: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to, when he stood up for the night prayer, say Takbir, and then say: “Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabarakasmuka, wa ta’ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghairuk. I seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the accursed Satan: from his hissing, his blowing, and his puffing.” Then he would begin his prayer. Ja’far said: Matar interpreted it as follows: his hissing is death, his blowing is poetry, and his puffing is arrogance.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me, he said: Qatadah narrated to me, from Anas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, used to begin their recitation with, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." (Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 2).

Abu Muhammad said: With this do we say, and I do not see the pronouncement of, "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." (Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 1) aloud.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd al-Jabbār ibn Wāil, from his father, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “placing his right hand upon his left, near the wrist.”
One who does not recite the Mother of the Book, his prayer is invalid.

Umaran ibn al-Husain disputed it, so they wrote to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he wrote to them that Samura had spoken truthfully. Abu Muhammad said: Qatadah used to say: "Three silences," and in the narrated hadith there are two silences: one when he enters the prayer and one when he finishes the recitation.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pause between the Takbir and the recitation [of Al-Fatiha] a pause which I thought he said, "a moment." I said to him, "By my father and mother, O Messenger of Allah! What do you say in that pause between the Takbir and the recitation?" He said: "I say: ‘O Allah, keep me far away from my sins as You have kept the East from the West. O Allah, cleanse me from my sins as You cleanse a white garment from dirt. O Allah, wash away my sins with snow and cold water.'"

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the reciter, neither of the disapproved nor astray, recites in Surat Al-Fatiha the verse: ‘You (Alone) are the Master of the Day of Judgment,’ and the one behind him says, ‘Amin,’ and that coincides with the inhabitants of the heavens, then his past sins are forgiven him."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When the Imam says, 'Those who have not incurred the wrath and who are not astray,' (i.e., Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 7), then you say, 'Amen.' For the angels say, 'Amen,' and the Imam says, 'Amen.' So whoever's 'Amen' coincides with the 'Amen' of the angels, his past sins are forgiven."

Narrated by Wail ibn Hujr: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) would, when reciting, '#And not the misguided,' (Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 7), say, "Amen," and raise his voice with it.

Narrated Abu Hurairah: They (Abu Bakr and Abu Salama) prayed behind Abu Hurairah. When he stood up for the bowing, he said, "Allahu Akbar," and when he raised his head, he said, "Samia Allahu liman hamidah. Rabbana wa lakal hamd." Then he prostrated and said, "Allahu Akbar," and when he raised his head, he said, "Allahu Akbar," and when he stood up from the two rak'ahs, he said, "Allahu Akbar." Then he said, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I am the closest of you in resemblance to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and this was his prayer until he passed away."
Narrated by Abdullah: I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) reciting Takbir in every raising and placing (of the hands during prayer), in standing, and in sitting.

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Malik narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would, when he entered prayer, say Takbir and raise his hands to the level of his shoulders. And when he bowed, he would say Takbir and raise his hands. And when he raised his head from bowing, he would do like that. And he would not raise his hands between the prostrations or in prostration.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Nasr ibn 'Aasim, from Malik ibn al-Hawirth, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to, when he would say "Allahu Akbar," raise his hands until they were level with his ears, and when he intended to bow, and when he raised his head from the bowing.

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: Abu al-Bukhteri narrated to me from Abd al-Rahman al-Yahsubi, from Wail al-Hadrami, that he prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would say Takbir when lowering [the voice] and when raising [it], and he would raise his hands at the Takbir, and he would greet on his right and on his left. He (Wail) said: I said: Until his face becomes clear? He (the Prophet) said: Yes.

Yarhiyah narrated from Yahya bin Hasan, who said: Wehib bin Khalid narrated to me, who said: Ayyub narrated to me from Abu Qilaba, from Malik bin al-Hawarith, who said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a group of my people, young men. We stayed with him for twenty nights. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was gentle and kind. When he saw our longing for our families, he said: "Return to your families and be among them. Instruct them and teach them, and pray as you see me praying. And when the time for prayer comes, let one of you call the adhan for you, and let the oldest among you lead the prayer."
Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “If three (people) gather, let one of them lead (in prayer), and the most knowledgeable of the Quran among them should be the Imam.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah narrated to me, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Sa’id ibn Jubayr relating, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: I was with my aunt Maymunah. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came after the ‘Isha’ prayer and prayed four rak’ahs. Then he stood up and said, "Has the sleepless one slept?" or a word similar to it. So he stood up and prayed. I suddenly came and stood on his left side, whereupon he took my hand and placed me on his right.

Narrated Anas: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) rode a horse and fell down from it, and his right side was injured. He offered a prayer from among the prayers while sitting, and we prayed along with him sitting. When he finished, he said: “The Imam is appointed so that people may follow him. So, do not disagree with him. If he offers prayer standing, you should offer it standing; if he bows, you should bow; if he raises his head, you should raise it; and when he says, ‘Sami’ Allahu liman hamidah (Allah listens to those who praise Him),’ you should say, ‘Rabbana wa lakal hamd (Our Lord, all praise is due to You),’ and if he offers prayer sitting, you should offer it sitting, all of you.”

I entered upon Aishah and said to her, "Do not relate to me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him?" She replied, "Yes, indeed. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, became severely ill, and he said, 'Have the people prayed?'" We said, "No, O Messenger of Allah, they are waiting for you." He said, "Prepare for me a basin of water." She said, "So we did, and he performed ablution. Then he intended to stand up, but he fainted, then he regained consciousness and said, 'Have the people prayed?'" We said, "No, O Messenger of Allah, they are waiting for you." He said, "Prepare for me a basin of water." So we did, and then he intended to stand up, but he fainted, then he regained consciousness and said, 'Have the people prayed?'" We said, "No, O Messenger of Allah, they are waiting for you." She said, "And the people were assembled in the mosque, waiting for the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, for the Isha’ prayer.” She said, "So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, sent for Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer." She said, "The Messenger came to him and said, 'The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, commands you to lead the people in prayer.'" Abu Bakr said, and he was a gentle man, "O Umar, you lead the people." Umar said to him, "You are more deserving of that." She said, "So Abu Bakr led them in prayer those days." She said, "Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, felt a lightening of his condition and went out between two men, one of whom was Abbas, for the Dhuhr prayer, and Abu Bakr was leading the people in prayer. When Abu Bakr saw him, he went to move back, but the Prophet, peace be upon him, gestured to him not to move back, and said to them, 'Seat me beside him.'" So they seated him beside Abu Bakr. She said, "So Abu Bakr was praying while the Prophet, peace be upon him, was seated, and the people were praying with the prayer of Abu Bakr, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, was seated.” Abdullah ibn Abbas said: I entered upon Abdullah ibn Abbas and said to him, "Should I present to you what Aishah narrated to me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him?" He said, "Recite it." So I recited her narration to him, and he did not object to anything in it except that he said, "Did she mention the name of the man who was with Abbas?" I said, "No." He said, "It was Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Abu Ma'mar Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting on the pulpit, he said Takbir, and the people said Takbir behind him. Then he stood for prayer while on the pulpit, and then he raised his head and descended backward, and prostrated in the base of the pulpit, then he returned until he finished the last part of his prayer."

Abu Muhammad said: "In this is a concession for the Imam to be higher than his companions, and the value of this action in prayer is also like that."

Narrated Abu Mas’ud Al-Ansari: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said, “By Allah, I delay the Fajr prayer because of the lengthy sermon of so-and-so.” I have never seen the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) angrier in a sermon than on that day.

He (the Prophet) said, “O people, among you are those who drive people away [from the prayer]. So whoever leads (the prayer) for the people, let him be brief, for among them are the old, the young, and those who have a need.”
Narrated Anas: I heard someone saying that the Prophet (ﷺ) offered the most complete prayer among the people.
Narrated by Abdullah bin Abu Qatada from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the call to prayer is made, do not stand up until you see me."
Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Qatada, from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the prayer is announced, do not rise until you see me."
Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Level your rows, for leveling the rows is part of the perfection of the prayer."
Narrated by Al-Baraa’ bin ‘Aazib: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Level your rows, and do not let your hearts differ."
He (the Prophet) also said: "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the first row (of worshippers) or the foremost rows."
Urbad ibn Sariyah reported: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to ask forgiveness for the first row (of soldiers) three times, and for the second row once.”

Abu Mas’ud al-Ansari (RA) said: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pass his hands over our shoulders in prayer and say: ‘Do not disagree, lest your hearts diverge. May those among you who have sound dreams and understanding lead, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.’” Abu Mas’ud (RA) said: “So you are more disagreeing today.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Indeed, those among you who possess sound judgment and foresight will rule over you, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. And avoid discord, for it will cause division in your hearts. And beware of the clamor of the marketplaces.”

Narrated by Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The best row of men is the first, and the worst is the last. And the best row of women is the last, and the worst is the first."

Narrated ‘Ubayy ibn Kab: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Fajr prayer, then faced us and said: “Is so-and-so present?” We said, “No.” He said, “Is so-and-so present?” We said, “No.” This was said about a group of the hypocrites who did not attend the prayer. He ﷺ said: “Indeed, these two prayers – Fajr and Isha – are the most burdensome for the hypocrites. If they knew what was in them, they would come to them even crawling.”

Abu Muhammad, Abdullah ibn Abi Basir, said: My father narrated to me from Ubayy about the Prophet ﷺ, and I heard it from Ubayy.

Abu Ghasan narrated: He said, Zuhayr narrated to me from Abu Ishaq from Abdullah ibn Abi Basir from his father from Ubayy ibn Kab from the Prophet ﷺ, with a similar wording.

Sa’id ibn Amir narrated: Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Arubah narrated to me from Khalid ibn Maymun from Abu Ishaq from Abdullah ibn Abi Basir from his father from Ubayy ibn Kab from the Prophet ﷺ, with a similar wording.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no prayer more burdensome to the hypocrites than the Isha (night) prayer and the Fajr (dawn) prayer, and if they knew what was in them, they would come to them even if crawling.”

Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was seriously considering commanding my young men to gather firewood, then ordering a man to lead the people in prayer, and then going off against some people who neglect this prayer, and burning their homes down. If there were a fat, juicy vein [of fat] or two, they would witness [the prayer]. And if they knew what was in them, they would come to them even crawling."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, that he spent a night in Dhujn, which was a cold night, and he ordered a caller to announce: “Prayer in the tents.” Then he informed that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, “if he was on a journey on a cold night or in rain, order a caller to announce: ‘Prayer in the tents.’”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, saying: I said to Saeed ibn Musayyib: A man prays in his house, then he finds the Imam praying, should he pray with him? He said: Yes. I said: Which of the two should he reckon (as his prayer)? He said: The one he prayed with the Imam. Abu Hurairah narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A man's prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than his prayer alone."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The prayer of a man in congregation is twenty-seven degrees better than his prayer alone."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If your wife asks your permission to go to the mosque, do not prevent her."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not prevent the female slaves of Allah from the mosques of Allah, and let them go out modestly." Saeed bin ‘Aamir said: The modesty mentioned is that of those who do not use perfume.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "When the evening meal is set and the time for prayer arrives, begin with the evening meal."
Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the time for dinner arrives and the prayer is announced, begin with the dinner."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When you come for the prayer, do not come rushing, but come walking calmly and with tranquility. Whatever (of the prayer) you catch, pray it, and whatever you miss, complete it."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Qatada from his father: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When you come to prayer, observe tranquility. Pray what you recognize, and complete what you are preceded in."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Hammad narrated to me from Abu Uthman, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: There was a man in Medina who, among those who prayed towards the Qibla, did not live further from the mosque than he did. He used to pray the prayers with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). It was said to him: "If you bought a donkey to ride in the darkness and the heat?" He said: "By Allah, I would not like my home to be attached to the mosque." The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was informed about this, and he asked him about it. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, so that my footsteps and my return to my family, and my coming and going may be recorded." Or he said something similar. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "May Allah grant you all of that, and give you what you hoped for in entirety." Or he said something similar.

Ziyad ibn Abi Jad took my hand and presented me to a man from the tribe of Asad named Wabisa ibn M’abad. He said, “This man and the man he is referring to claim to have seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, praying, and a man praying behind him without connecting to the rows.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered him to repeat the prayer.

Musaddad narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from ‘Ubaid ibn Abi Ja’d, from Ziyad ibn Abi Ja’d, from Wabisa ibn M’abad, that a man prayed behind the rows alone. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered him to repeat [the prayer]. Abu Muhammad said: I say this is correct.

Narrated Anas: My grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) to a meal she had prepared. He ate, and then said, "Rise, so that I may pray with you." Anas said, "I stood up to a mat we had which had become black from prolonged use. I sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) stood upon it, and I and an orphan stood behind him, and an elderly woman stood behind us. He then prayed two rak'ahs for us, and then he left."

Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Abu Awana narrated to me from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from Al-Walid, my father, Abu Bishr, from Abu As-Siddiq An-Najji, from Abu Sa’id, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the first two rak’ahs of Zuhr, the equivalent of thirty verses, and in the last two rak’ahs, the equivalent of half of that, and in ‘Asr, the equivalent of the last two rak’ahs of Zuhr, and in the last two rak’ahs, the equivalent of half of that.”

‘Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me from Mansur, from Al-Walid, Abu Bishr, from Abu As-Siddiq, from Abu Sa’id, with a similar narration, and he added: “The equivalent of reciting ‘Tasmida’ (Qur'an chapter beginning with “Tasmida” - Surah Al-Mulk).”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samura, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to recite [Surah] “The Sky and the Tarik” and [Surah] “The Sky with the Constellations” in the Dhuhr and ‘Asr prayers.

Abu al-Mughira reported: “Abu Az-Zubair narrated to me that Abdullah ibn Abi Qatada reported from his father that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to recite al-Fatiha and two verses with it in the first two rak'ahs of the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, and he would sometimes make us hear the verse, and he would prolong [the recitation] in the first rak'ah.”

Abu ‘Aasim narrated from Abu Az-Zubair, from Yahya, with a similar chain of narration.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Yahya ibn Abi Katir narrated to me, Abdullah ibn Abi Qatada narrated to me, that his father narrated to him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to recite in the first two rak'ahs of the Dhuhr (noon) prayer, the Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha) and two verses, and in the last two rak'ahs, the Mother of the Book. He used to make us hear the verse, and he used to prolong in the first rak'ah more than he prolonged in the second. And so was the prayer of 'Asr (afternoon), and so was the prayer of Fajr (dawn).
Narrated 'Umm al-Fazl: That she heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting in the Maghrib prayer, "And the sent forth messengers."

Narrated by Muhammad ibn Yusuf: He said, "Ibrahim (Ismail) told me that Ibn Uyaynah narrated to me from Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubair ibn Mut'am, from his father, that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) reciting 'By the Mount (Tur) [At-Tur]’ in the Maghrib (evening) prayer."

Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to me from Shu'bah from Amr ibn Dinār from Jabir ibn Abdullah that Mu'adh used to pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and then he would come to his people and lead them in prayer. One night, he prayed the 'Ishā' prayer and recited Surah al-Baqarah. A man from the Ansar prayed along with him, then left. It reached Mu'adh that this man was taking offense at him, so he complained about this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Mu'adh: "Distracter, distracter, distracter," or "Sower of discord, sower of discord, sower of discord." Then he ordered him to recite two verses from the middle of the Mu'awwidhat (Surahs al-Falaq and an-Nas).

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah, who said: I heard my uncle saying: "I prayed behind the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I heard him reciting, 'And the palms, rising up straight,' in one of the rak'ahs of Fajr." Shu'bah said: I asked him about it once more, and he said: I heard him reciting [the verse] "By the Fig and the Olive."

Qutbah ibn Malik said: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) reciting in the Fajr prayer, in the first rak'ah: "And the palms, their stalks rising up, bearing clusters of dates ripe and fresh.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, he said: Mas’udi narrated to me, from Al-Walid ibn Sarie, from ‘Amru ibn Hurayth, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting in the Fajr prayer, “When the sun is rolled up,” [Surah Al-Takwir, 81:1] and when he reached the verse, “And the night when it grows late,” [Surah Al-Takwir, 81:17], I began to say to myself: ‘What is the night when it grows late?’ Abu Nu’aim narrated to me, he said: Mis’ar narrated to me, from Al-Walid, from ‘Amru ibn Hurayth, with a similar narration.

Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to me, that 'Awf narrated to me, from Sayyar ibn Salama, that he said: I entered with my father to Abu Barza al-Aslami, who was on a high platform made of reeds. My father asked him about the prayer times of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and he said: "He used to pray the afternoon prayer, which you people call Dhuhr, when the sun declined. And he used to pray the evening prayer (Asr), then one of us would go to his family in the farthest part of the city while the sun was still bright. He said: I forgot what he mentioned about the Maghrib (sunset) prayer, and he used to prefer to delay the Isha prayer, which you people call 'Atma (darkness). And he would leave the Fajr prayer while a man knew his companion, and he used to recite between sixty and one hundred [verses] in it."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) entered the mosque and people had raised their gazes during prayer. He said: "You must lower your gazes, or they will not return to you."

Narrated Anas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "What is the matter with people who raise their gazes to the sky during prayer?" He intensified his warning about it to the extent that he said: "They must stop doing that, or Allah will snatch away their eyesight."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, he said: Isr’ail narrated to me, he said: Abu Ya’fur al-‘Abdi narrated to me, he said: Mus’ab ibn Sa’d said: The children of ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, when they prostrated, would place their hands between their thighs. I prayed beside Sa’d, and I did so, and he struck my hand. When he turned, he said: “O my son, strike your hands upon your knees.” Then I did it again another day, and I prayed beside him, and he struck my hand. When he turned, he said: “We used to do this, and we were commanded to strike our hands upon our knees.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated from Isr’ail from Abu Ishaq from Mus’ab, with a similar chain of narration.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, on the authority of Hammaam, who narrated from Ata’ ibn as-Sa’ib, from Salim al-Barraad, who said: I had with me a man who was more trustworthy to me than myself. He said: Abu Mas’ud al-Ansari said to us: “Shall I lead you in the prayer as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray?” So he began by saying Takbir, then he stood for Qiyam (reciting), then he bowed down, placing his hands on his knees, and spreading his fingers until everything was settled.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Miqri: Tell us, Musa ibn Ayyub narrated to me, and my uncle, Iyasu ibn ‘Amir, said: I heard ‘Uqba ibn Amir saying: When the verse, "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Exalted," (Surah Al-Waqi’ah, 74:2) was revealed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to us: "Recite it in your bowing (ruku’)." Then, when the verse, "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," (Surah Al-A’la, 87:1) was revealed, he said: "Recite it in your prostration."

Hudayfa (may Allah be pleased with him) said that he prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) one night, and he used to say in his bowing, "Subhan Rabbiyal-'Adheem," and in his prostration, "Subhan Rabbiyal-A'la." Whenever he reached an Ayah of Mercy, he would pause at it and supplicate. And whenever he reached an Ayah of Punishment, he would seek refuge in Allah from it.

Muhammad ibn Maslama, Abu Usayd, Abu Humayd, and Sahl ibn Sa’d gathered and discussed the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. Abu Humayd said, “I am the most knowledgeable among you regarding the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, stood up, pronounced the takbir, and raised his hands. Then he raised his hands again when pronouncing the takbir for rukū‘. He then bowed down and placed his hands upon his knees as if grasping them, and he interlocked his fingers and moved them away from his sides. He did not turn his head, nor did he incline it.

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from his father, that he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) would, when he began the prayer, raise his hands to the level of his shoulders. And when he bowed, he would do like that. And when he raised his head from bowing, he would do like that. And he would say: 'He (Allah) heard [the words of] those who praised Him. O Allah, our Lord, and to You is the praise.' And he would not do that in prostration."

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to me, that Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), a similar narration.

Except that he said: "Our Lord, and to You is the praise."
Narrated Anas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "And when the Imam says, 'Allah hears those who praise Him,' you should say, 'Our Lord, and to You is the praise.'"

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The Imam is appointed only to be followed. So, when he says 'Allahu Akbar,' say 'Allahu Akbar.' When he bows, bow. When he prostrates, prostrate. And when he says, 'Sami Allahu liman hamidah,' say, 'Allahumma Rabanna lakal hamd.' If he prays standing, pray standing, and if he prays sitting, pray sitting, all of you."

Narrated Abu Musa: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon to us and taught us our prayer and showed us our Sunnah. He said: "I think he said: When the prayer is announced, let one of you lead (the prayer). When he says Takbir, say Takbir. And when he says, 'Not the ones who incurred wrath, nor the ones who are astray' (Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 7), say 'Amin,' so that Allah may respond to you. And when he says Takbir and bows down, say Takbir and bow down, for the Imam bows down before you and raises (his head) before you. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'It is like that, in accordance with that.' And when he says, 'Allah hears those who praise Him,' say, 'O Allah, our Lord, all praise is due to You,' or he said, 'Our Lord, all praise is due to You,' for Allah said on the tongue of His Prophet: 'Allah hears those who praise Him.'"

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Saeed ibn Abdul Aziz narrated to me from Attiya ibn Qais from Qaza'a from Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to, when he raised his head from bowing (in prayer), say: 'Our Lord, praise is for You, filling the heavens and the earth, and filling whatever You will of anything thereafter. O Possessor of praise and majesty! This is the truest statement a servant can say. And all of us are Your servants. O Allah, there is no withholder of what You give, nor a giver of what You withhold, and striving does not benefit anyone before You.'"

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, when he raised his head from rukūʿ, say: ‘Allah has listened to the one who praised Him. Our Lord, and to You is all praise, filling the heavens and the earth, and filling all that is between them, and filling whatever You will after that.’"

It was said to Abdullah: "Do you act upon it?" He said: "No." And it was said to him: "Do you say this in the obligatory prayer?" He said: "Perhaps." And he said: "All of it is good."

"I sometimes strain (to perform the acts of worship), so do not precede me in prostration or bowing. Whenever I outpace you in bowing, you catch up with me when I rise, and whenever I outpace you in prostration, you catch up with me when I rise."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Does none of you fear or does none of you refrain from raising his head before the Imam has raised his?" Lest Allah makes his head the head of a donkey or his image the image of a donkey.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Zaidah narrated to me, he said: Al-Mukhtar bin Fulful narrated to me, from Anas bin Malik, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) encouraged them to hasten in prayer, and forbade them from preceding him in prostration and bowing when he was leading them, and from departing before his departure from the prayer. And he said: "Indeed, I see you before me and behind me."

Abu Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from 'Amr ibn Dinār, who said: I heard Tawus narrating, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones, and he was commanded not to let hair or clothing hang down." Shu'bah said: He narrated to me once more, saying: "I was commanded to prostrate, and not to let hair or clothing hang down."

Muslim ibn Ibrahim and Yahya ibn Hassan narrated: We were told by Wuhayb: He said: Ibn Tawus narrated to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who said: "I was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones: the forehead, and Wuhayb said: and he indicated with his hand to his nose, and the two hands, and the two knees, and the tips of the two feet, and not to uncover the clothing or the hair."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to me, from ‘Asim ibn Kulayb, from his father, from Wail ibn Hujr, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he prostrated, he would place his knees before his hands, and when he rose, he would raise his hands before his knees.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When any one of you prays, let him not bow down as a camel bows down, but let him place his hands on his knees before bowing."

It was said to Abdullah: What do you say? He said: All of it is good.

And he said: The people of Kufa prefer the first (part).
"Moderate in bowing and prostration, and let none of you stretch his arms out as a dog stretches his."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the striking of a wild animal’s flank, the pecking of a crow, and a man from habitually residing in a place as a camel does.

Hudhaifa reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say between the two prostrations: "My Lord, forgive me." It was said to Abdullah: Do you say this? He said: Sometimes I say it, and sometimes I remain silent.

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ unveiled the curtain while the people were standing in rows behind Abu Bakr, and said: “O people, there remain of the signs of prophethood only the good dreams which a Muslim sees or are seen for him. Indeed, I have been forbidden from reciting during a prostration or a bowing. As for the bowing, magnify your Lord, and as for the prostration, strive in supplication, for you may be answered.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I was forbidden from reciting while in prostration or while bowing. As for the bowing, magnify Allah within it, and as for the prostration, strive diligently in supplication, for you may be answered.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “No prayer is valid in which a man does not straighten his back in the bowing and prostration.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Qatada from his father: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The worst of thieves is the one who steals his prayer." They said: O Messenger of Allah, and how does one steal his prayer? He said: "By not perfecting its bowing and prostration."

While we were sitting around the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, or the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was sitting around us, a man entered and stood facing the qibla and prayed. When he finished, he came and greeted the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and the people, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said, “And upon you, go back and pray, for you have not prayed.”

The man returned and prayed, and we watched his prayer, not knowing what was wrong with it. When he finished, he came and greeted the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and the people, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, said to him, “And upon you, go back and pray, for you have not prayed.”

Hammam said: I do not know whether he ordered him to do that twice or three times.

The man said: I am confused, so I do not know what you found fault with in my prayer.

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: “Your prayer is not complete for anyone of you until he performs ablution as Allah has commanded him, washing his face and hands up to the elbows, wiping his head, and his feet up to the ankles, then he says Takbir and praises Allah, then he recites from the Qur’an what Allah has permitted him in it, then he says Takbir and bows down, placing his hands on his knees until his joints settle and relax, and says, ‘Samia Allahu liman hamidah,’ then he stands straight until he straightens his back, taking every bone in its place, then he says Takbir and prostrates, placing his forehead on the ground until his joints settle and relax, then he says Takbir, then he sits straight on his seat and straightens his back. He described the prayer in this way for four rak’ahs until he finished, ‘Your prayer is not complete for anyone of you until he does that.’”

Maymunah bint al-Harith (RA) said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, when he prostrated, raise himself so high that those behind him could see the whiteness of his armpits."

Maymunah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would stretch his legs out during prostration so much that if a donkey were to pass by, it could pass beneath him."

Maimuna, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) prostrated, he would bow his hands until the whiteness of his armpits was visible from behind him, and when he sat, he would settle himself comfortably on his left thigh."

Narrated Al-Baraa': The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to make his bowing, and raising his head from bowing, and his prostration, and between the two prostrations, nearly equal (in duration).

I observed the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, during prayer, and I found him standing, bowing, straightening up after the bow, prostrating, sitting between the prostrations, prostrating again, and sitting between the greeting and departure, all nearly equal (in duration).

Narrated ‘Abdullah bin Salih: Abdullah bin Saleh narrated to me from Layth bin Sa’d, who narrated from ‘Uqail, from Ibn Shihab, who narrated to me ‘Abbad bin Ziyad, from ‘Urwa bin Al-Mughira and Hamza bin Al-Mughira, that they heard Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba narrating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba came with him, and they found the people having already stood for the Fajr (dawn) prayer and ‘Abd Al-Rahman bin ‘Auf was leading them in the prayer. So ‘Abd Al-Rahman led them in one Rak’ah (unit of prayer) of the Fajr prayer before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and stood in a row behind ‘Abd Al-Rahman in the second Rak’ah. When ‘Abd Al-Rahman said, “As-salamu alaykum,” the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and then offered the prayer. The people were frightened by that and increased their glorification (Tasbih). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his prayer, he said to the people, “You have done right, or you have done well.”

We proceeded to the people and they were standing for prayer, and Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Auf was leading them in prayer, and he had already begun the bowing. When he sensed the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), he began to fall back, and he gestured to him with his hand. So he led them in prayer, and when he concluded [the prayer] and said, “Peace be upon you,” the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) stood up, and I stood up with him, and we performed the prostration that we had missed. Abu Muhammad said: I say regarding making up [missed prayers] according to the statement of the people of Kufa: that one should make what he missed of the prayer a qada [makeup prayer].

Anas (RA) said: “We used to pray with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) during intense heat, and if anyone of us was unable to rest his forehead on the ground, he would spread his garment and pray upon it.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me, from Ibn ‘Ajlan, from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said: “I saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) supplicating in this manner,” and Ibn ‘Uyaynah gestured with his finger, and Abu al-Walid gestured with his index finger.

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would, when sitting in the final posture of the prayer, place his left hand upon his left knee, and his right hand upon his right knee, and raise his index finger.

We used to say when praying behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), “Peace be upon Allah before His servants, peace be upon Gabriel, peace be upon Michael, peace be upon Israfil, peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so.” Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) faced us and said, “Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is As-Salam. So, when you sit in prayer, say, ‘The greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the pure words. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. For when you say it, it reaches every righteous servant in the heavens and on earth. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Then say whatever you wish.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Hasan ibn Huraq, that the narrator, Qasim ibn Muqaymah, said: Alqamah took my hand and narrated to me, that Abdullah took his hand, and that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, took Abdullah’s hand and taught him the Tashahhud in the prayer: "All greetings are for Allah, and all prayers, and all good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.” Zuhayr said: I think he said: “I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.” He also hesitated in these two phrases: “If you do this or complete [the prayer], you have completed your prayer. If you wish to stand, then stand, and if you wish to sit, then sit.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me, he said: Al-Hakam narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla saying: Ka'b ibn 'Ujra met me and said: Should I not present you with a gift? The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, came out to us, and we said: We know how to greet you, but how should we send blessings upon you? He said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Magnificent. And bless Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Magnificent."

Narrated Abu Mas’ud Al-Ansari: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us and sat with us in the gathering of Saad bin ‘Ubadah. Bashir bin Saad, who was the father of An-Nu’man bin Bashir, said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, Allah has ordered us to send blessings upon you. How should we do that?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent until we wished he had not been asked. Then he said: “Say: ‘O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim, and bestow your grace upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You bestowed your grace upon the family of Ibrahim, among the worlds. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Magnificent, and the greeting is as you know.’”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When anyone of you finishes the tashahhud, let him seek refuge with Allah from four things: the torment of Hell, the torment of the grave, the trial of life and death, and the evil of the Dajjal."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to greet (people) from his right side until the whiteness of his cheek was seen, then he would greet from his left side until the whiteness of his cheek was seen.

Musaddad narrated to me, he said: Yahya narrated to me, from Shu’bah, from Al-Hakam and Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma’mar, who said: “I prayed behind a man in Mecca, and he said the farewell prayer with two Salam.” I mentioned that to Abdullah, and he said: “How did that happen?” Al-Hakam said: “The Prophet (ﷺ) used to do that.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would not sit after the prayer until he said: “O Allah, You are As-Salam [the Source of Peace], and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Owner of Majesty and Honor.”

Abu Mughira narrated: Tell us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ash-Sha'bi, from Abu Asma' Ar-Rabawi, from Thawban, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to, when he wanted to conclude his prayer, seek forgiveness three times, and then he would say: 'Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minka as-salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram.'"

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, that Sufyan narrated, from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Warrad, the scribe of al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah, who said: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah dictated to me in a letter to Mu’awiyah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say after every obligatory prayer: “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, alone, without any partners. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things, powerful. O Allah, there is no preventer of what You give, and no giver of what You withhold, and striving does not benefit anyone before You.”

Abdullah (RA) said: Let none of you give Satan a share of his prayer; that he thinks he has a right to turn away except from his right side. Indeed, I have often seen the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) turn away on his left side.
Narrated Anas: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turning away from his right side.
Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) turned to his right during prayer.

Abu Dharr said: “O Messenger of Allah, the people of affluence have taken away the rewards. They pray as we pray, and they fast as we fast, and they have surplus wealth with which they give charity, while we have nothing to give.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Should I not teach you words, if you say them, you will overtake those who have gone ahead of you, and none will follow you except one who acts as you act?” He said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Recite, after every prayer, thirty-three times SubhanAllah (Glory be to Allah), and thirty-three times Alhamdulilah (All praise is due to Allah), and thirty-three times Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest), and conclude with ‘La ilaha illallah, Wahdahu la sharika lah, Lahu al-mulk, wa Lahu al-hamd, wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in Qadir.’”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: “We were commanded to say SubhanAllah thirty-three times, and to praise Him thirty-three times, and to say Takbir thirty-four times after every prayer.” Then a man from the Ansar was brought (or shown) in a dream, and it was said to him: “Did Allah’s Messenger order you to say SubhanAllah thirty-three times, and to praise Him thirty-three times, and to say Takbir thirty-four times after every prayer?” He said: “Yes.” He was then told: “Make it twenty-five, twenty-five, and include with it the declaration of Allahu Akbar.” The Prophet ﷺ was informed about this, and he said: “Do it.”

Narrated by Tamim ad-Dari: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The first thing the slave will be questioned about on the Day of Judgment is prayer. If his prayer is complete, it is recorded as complete for him. And if there is deficiency in it, Allah the Exalted says to His angels: 'Look, does my slave have any voluntary (nafl) prayers? Complete for him what is lacking from his obligatory (fard) prayer.' Then comes zakah, and then the other deeds in that order."

I know the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, better than you all.” They said, “Why do you claim that?” He replied, “Because I was not the most devoted to following his prayer, nor was I the earliest to pray with him?” He said, “Yes.” They said, “Then demonstrate it.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would stand for prayer, raising his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then he would say Takbir until every bone in his body was in its proper place, then he would recite [the Quran], then he would say Takbir and raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then he would bow down and place his palms on his knees until every bone returned to its place, without turning his head or inclining it. Then he would raise his head and say, ‘Sami’ Allahu liman hamidah [May Allah hear those who praise Him]’, then he would raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, Abu ‘Aasim thinks that he said, ‘until every bone was in its proper place, straightened,’ then he would say, ‘Allahu Akbar [Allah is the Greatest]’, then he would prostrate, distancing his hands from his sides, then he would raise his head and bend his left leg and sit on it, opening the fingers of both his feet when he prostrates, then he would return and prostrate again, then he would raise his head and say, ‘Allahu Akbar’, and bend his left leg and sit on it, straightened, until every bone was in its proper place, straightened, then he would stand and perform in the second rak’ah in the same manner. And when he rose from the two prostrations, he would say Takbir and raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, as he did when beginning the prayer, then he would perform in the rest of his prayer in the same way, until he reached the prostration or sitting in which he would give the Salam. He would delay his left leg and sit leaning on his left side.” He said, “They said, ‘You have spoken the truth; this was the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.’”

I said, "I would certainly observe the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to see how he prays." So I observed him. He stood up, and said Takbir, then raised his hands until they reached his ears, and placed his right hand upon the back of his left hand. He said, "Then when he intended to bow, he raised his hands as he had done before, and placed his hands upon his knees. Then he raised his head, and raised his hands as he had done before. Then he prostrated, placing his hands beneath his ears. Then he sat down, stretching his left leg, and placed his left hand upon his thigh and knee, and placed his right elbow upon his right thigh. Then he made a fist with two fingers, and circled them in a ring, and I saw him moving them, invoking with them." He said, "Then I came after that in a time of cold, and I saw people moving their hands beneath their garments."

Abu Musa narrated: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and taught us our prayer and clarified our Sunnah to us. He said: 'When the prayer is announced (i.e., the adhan), let one of you lead the prayer. When he says Takbir (Allahu Akbar), you say Takbir. When he recites, "Ghafirun (The Forgiving), not including those who incur wrath, nor those who are astray," (Surah Al-Fatiha, verse 7), say "Ameen," and Allah will respond to you. When he says Takbir and bows down, you say Takbir and bow down. The Imam bows down before you and raises (up) before you.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “It is like that, like that.” Then he said: “When he says, ‘Sam’a Allahu liman hamidah (Allah hears those who praise Him),’ you say, ‘Allahumma Rabbana lakal hamd’ or ‘Rabbana walakal hamd.’ For Allah said on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ): ‘Sam’a Allahu liman hamidah.’ When he says Takbir and prostrates, you say Takbir and prostrate. The Imam prostrates before you and raises (up) before you.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “It is like that, like that.” Then he said: “When you reach the sitting position, let your first words be: ‘At-tahiyyatu l-tayyibatu was-salawatu lillahi, as-salamu,’ or ‘As-salamu ‘alayka ayyuha an-nabi wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu, as-salamu,’ or ‘As-salamu ‘alayna wa ‘ala ‘ibadi Allahis-salihin. Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan ‘abduhu wa rasuluhu.’”

Narrated Abu Qatada: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once went out to pray and he was carrying Umama bint Zainab on his neck. When he bowed (in prayer), he put her down, and when he stood up, he carried her.

Narrated Abu Qatada Al-Ansari: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried Umama bint Zainab bint the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying. When he prostrated, he placed her down, and when he stood up, he carried her.”

Abu al-Walid, that is al-Tayalisi, narrated to me, he said: Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: Bukayr, that is ibn al-Ashajj, narrated to me from Nabil, the companion of the cloak, from Ibn Umar, from Sahih, who said: "I passed by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was praying, so I greeted him, and he returned my greeting with a gesture." Layth said: I think he said: with his finger.

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to me, that Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Umar, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) entered the mosque of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Auf, and the people entered greeting him while he was in prayer. He (the Prophet) said: “I asked Suhail how he used to respond to them?” Suhail said: “Like this,” and he gestured with his hand.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Tasbih (glorification) is for men, and clapping (for women)."
"If something happens to you during prayer, then men should say SubhanAllah (Glory be to Allah), and women should say Astaghfirullah (I seek forgiveness from Allah)."

Narrated by Abu Nadhr from Busr bin Sa’id from Zaid bin Thabit, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Observe the prayer in your homes, for the best prayer of a man is in his house, except for the congregational (obligatory) prayer."

Narrated By Jabir bin Yazid As-Suwa’i from his father: He (the Prophet) صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم offered the Fajr (dawn) prayer. Then two men did not pray with him. So, he called them, and they were brought forth trembling with fear. He (the Prophet) صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم said, "What prevented you from praying?" They said, "We prayed in our dwellings." He (the Prophet) صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم said, "Do not do that. If you pray in your dwellings and then catch up with the Imam, pray, for it will be a Nafl (supererogatory) prayer for you." Then the people stood up and took hold of his hand, wiping their faces with it. I also took hold of his hand and wiped my face with it, and it felt colder than snow and smelled sweeter than musk.
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saw a man praying alone, and said, “Would there not be a man who would give charity to this [man] so that he could pray with him?”

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: A man entered the mosque while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was praying. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Is there anyone who will give charity for this man so that he may pray with us?” Abdullah (ibn Umar) said: “He prays the ‘Asr and Maghrib (prayers) but he intercedes.”
Narrated Abu Huraira: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, can a man pray in one garment?" He (the Prophet) said: "Does everyone of you find two garments, or does everyone have two garments?"
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Let none of you pray in one garment that does not cover his shoulders.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Muhammad ibn ‘Amr narrated to me, from Abu Salama, from Abu Huraira, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade two types of garments: that one of you should wear a single garment without anything between his private parts and the sky, and wearing a garment that covers the head, like the Jews.”
Narrated by Maymunah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray wearing a khumurah (a garment covering the head and chest).
Narrated Anas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) offered prayer upon a mat.

Narrated by Muawiya bin Abi Sufyan: He asked Um Habibah: Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) pray in the garment in which he sleeps with you? She said: Yes, if he did not see any harm in it.

Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), informed that he (the Prophet) asked her, "Did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) ever pray in the garment he had intercourse with you in?" She replied, "Yes, if he did not see any impurity in it."

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abu Muslim, who is Saeed ibn Yazid al-Azdi, that he said: I asked Anas ibn Malik: "Did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, pray in his shoes?" He said: "Yes."

While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying with his companions, he removed his sandals and placed them on his left side. They removed their sandals too. When he finished the prayer, he said, "What made you throw off your sandals?" They said, "We saw you remove yours, so we removed ours." He said, "Indeed, Gabriel came to me or came and informed me that there was harm or filth in them. So, when anyone of you comes to the mosque, let him turn his sandals over, and if he sees harm in them, let him shake them off and pray in them."
Abu Hurairah (RA) reported that he disliked the long, loose garment (as-saddl), and he raised this matter to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw me while I was prostrating and had braided my hair, or he said, “tied [it]”, so he released [it].

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Bakr, who is the son of Mudara, narrated to me, from ‘Amr, meaning Ibn al-Harith, from Bukayr, that Kuraib, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, informed him, that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) saw Abdullah ibn al-Harith praying, and the back of his head was shaved. So, Ibn Abbas stood behind him and began to untie it, and the other (person) acknowledged (it). Then he turned to Ibn Abbas and said: "What is the matter with you and my head?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: 'Its example is like that of one who prays while being tied up.'"

Narrated by Abu Sa’id al-Khudri: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "If one of you yawns, let him hold his hand over his mouth, for Shaytan enters." Abu Muhammad said: Meaning, over his mouth.
"If anyone of you feels sleep overcome him while praying, let him sleep until the sleep departs, for he may intend to seek forgiveness and then curse himself."
It has reached me that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The prayer of a man sitting is half a prayer."

I entered upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was praying sitting down. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, it has reached me that you said, ‘The prayer of a man sitting is half a prayer,’ and yet you are praying sitting?” He said, “Yes, but I am not like one of you.”

Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), said: "I did not see the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) praying while sitting, reciting (the Quran) in prostration, until a year or two before his death. Then I saw him praying while sitting, reciting a surah until it was longer than any other recitation of it."

Narrated by Mu'ayqib: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) regarding wiping over the shoes in the mosque, and he said: "If you must do it, then once."

Hisham said: I think he said, meaning wiping over the pebbles.
Narrated Abu Darr: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When any of you stands up for prayer, mercy turns towards him, so he should not sweep the pebbles (with his feet)."

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, saying: Sayyar narrated to me, saying: I heard Yazid al-Faqir say: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Five things were given to me that no prophet before me was given: The prophets were sent to their people specifically, but I was sent to all of mankind. Raids were made permissible for me, while they were forbidden for those before me. The earth was made pure and a place of prostration and purification for me. Our enemies are terrified of us for a month's journey. And I was given intercession."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The entire earth is a mosque except for the graveyards and the bathhouses."

It was said to Abu Muhammad: Is it permissible to pray in the graveyard? He said: If one is not upon the grave, then yes. And he said: The majority of narrators transmitted this Hadith through a mursal chain.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the time for prayer comes and you do not find anything but sheepfolds and the resting places of camels, then pray in the sheepfolds and do not pray in the resting places of camels."

Uthman related: "When I intended to build the mosque, the people disliked it. So I said, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build for him a similar one in Paradise."
"When any of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rak'ahs before sitting."

Narrated Abu Hurairah or Abu Usayd Al-Ansari: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When any of you enters a mosque, let him greet the Prophet (ﷺ), and then say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy. And when he exits, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask you for Your grace.'"
I asked Qatadah, "Did you hear Anas relate from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: 'Spitting in the mosque is an offense?'" He said, "Yes, and its expiation is burying it."

Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Verily, when a slave prays, he is engaged in supplication to his Lord, or his Lord is between him and the Qibla. And if one of you spits, let him spit to his left or beneath his foot, or let him say thus," and he spat in his garment and rubbed some of it with others.

While the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was delivering a sermon, he saw some mucus in the direction of the mosque (qibla). He became angry at the people of the mosque and said, “Indeed, Allah is before one of you when he is in prayer, so let him not spit, or he said, ‘let him not have mucus.’” Then he ordered it to be scraped away, and ordered it to be plastered over. Hammad said: I do not think he said anything except that it was with saffron.
