Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa’d narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Humaid ibn Abdur-Rahman, that Abu Sa’id and Abu Huraira informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw some phlegm in the wall of the mosque. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a small stone and wiped it, and then said: “If one of you sneezes, he should not sneeze towards his face or to his right, but should spit to his left or beneath his foot.”

Narrated Abu Dharr: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to me while I was sleeping in the mosque and struck me with his foot. He said, “Do I not see you sleeping in it?” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, my eyes overcame me.”

I used to spend the nights in the mosque, as I did not have a family. I saw in a dream as if I was being taken to a well in which there were men suspended. It was said, "Take him to Zul-Yamin." I mentioned the dream to Hafsa, and she narrated it to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He said, "Who saw this?" She said, "‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "What a good youth—or he said, ‘What a good man’—if he were to pray at night." I said, "I used to sleep and not get up until the morning." He said, "So, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar used to pray the night prayer."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you see someone selling or buying in the mosque, say to him: ‘May Allah not profit from your trade.’ And if you see someone seeking a lost item in the mosque, say to him: ‘May Allah not lead you to it.’”

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told me: I said to Amr ibn Dinār: Did you hear Jabir ibn Abdullah say: A man passed through the mosque carrying arrows, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: "Hold back their points." He said: Yes.

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas and ‘Aisha: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) was afflicted with a fever, he kept throwing a garment over his face. When he felt better, he would remove it and say, “May Allah’s curse be upon the Jews and the Christians, for they have taken their prophets’ graves as places of worship.” He warned against what they did.

K’ab ibn ‘Ajrah met me at Al-Balat while I was interlinking my fingers, and he said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘When one of you performs ablution and then goes forth deliberately for prayer, he should not interlink his fingers.’”
Narrated by K’ab bin ‘Ajra: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “When you perform ablution and proceed to the mosque, do not interlock your fingers, for you are in a state of prayer.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ablution and then goes out to pray, he is in a state of prayer until he returns home. So do not say like this," and he gestured, intertwining his fingers.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The angels will continue to pray for the servant as long as he remains in his place of prayer, as long as he does not stand up or perform an act of ritual impurity, saying: ‘O Allah, forgive him, O Allah, have mercy on him.’”
The Hour will not be established until people begin to boast in the mosques.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me, from Hakim bin Utaiba, who said: I heard Abu Jahifa saying: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went out to al-Bat'ha in al-Hajira, and he prayed the Dhuhr prayer two rak'ahs, and the Asr prayer two rak'ahs. A staff was before him, and the camels were passing between his hands."

Musaddad narrated to me, that Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from 'Ubaidullah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would have a goat tethered to a stake while he prayed towards it.
Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If any of you is praying, let him not allow anyone to pass between his hands. If he refuses, let him fight him, for he is a Satan."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray facing his camel.
Aisha informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray while I was between him and the Qibla, on his bed, due to a funeral procession passing by.

Abu al-Walid and Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: We were told by Shu'bah, that he told us from Humayd ibn Hilal, that he said: I heard Abdullah ibn As-Samit from Abu Dharr, who said: "A man's prayer is invalidated if there is not between him and the donkey, the black dog, and the woman, as there is between him and the last part of his baggage."

He said: I asked, "What is the matter with the black one compared to the red one and the yellow one?" He said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as I have asked you, and he said: 'The black one is a shaytan.'"

Abu Naim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, from Zuhri, from ‘Ubaidullah ibn ‘Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I and Al-Fadl came on a she-mule, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was praying in Mina or ‘Arafah. We passed by a part of the row, so I dismounted and let the she-mule graze, and I joined the row."

Yahya ibn Hasan narrated to me, from Ibn Uyayna, from Salim, father of An-Nadr, from Busr ibn Sa’id, who said: Abu Jahim Al-Anṣārī sent me to Zaid ibn Khalid Al-Juhani to ask him what he had heard from the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, concerning that which passes between the hands of the praying person. He said: The Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, said: "It is better for one of you to stand [in prayer] for forty [rak'ahs] than to pass between the hands of a praying person." He said: I do not know whether it is a year, a month, or a day.

Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani sent me to Abu Juhaym to ask him what he had heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the one who passes in front of the praying person. Abu Juhaym said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If the one passing in front of the praying person knew what was upon him because of that, it would be better for him to stand for forty [units of prayer] than to pass in front of him." Abu Nadhr said: I do not know whether forty days, or months, or years.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A prayer in my mosque is a thousand prayers, in comparison to a prayer offered elsewhere except for the Sacred Mosque."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers in any other than it, except for the Sacred Mosque."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except for the Sacred Mosque."
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not set out on journeys except for three mosques: the Mosque of the Ka’bah, and my mosque, and the Mosque of al-Aqsa.”
Whoever walks in the darkness of the night to prayer, Allah will grant him light on the Day of Resurrection.
Allah remains attentive to the servant as long as the servant remains attentive to Him; but when the servant turns away, Allah turns away from him.

Narrated by Abdullah bin Hubshi: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was asked, "Which deeds are best?" He said, "Faith without doubt, striving (jihad) without theft, and an accepted Hajj."

It was said, "Which prayer is best?" He said, "Prolonged standing (in prayer)."

It was said, "Which charity is best?" He said, "The effort of a meager person."

It was said, "Which emigration (Hijra) is best?" He said, "To abandon what Allah has forbidden upon you."

It was said, "Which jihad is best?" He said, "One who strives against the polytheists with his wealth and life."

It was said, "Which killing is most noble?" He said, "One whose horse is maimed and whose blood is spilled."
"Whoever prays the two coolings, he enters Paradise." It was said to Abu Muhammad: "What are the two coolings?" He said: "The morning and the afternoon prayers."

"Whoever prays the Fajr (dawn) prayer is under the protection of Allah, so do not offend Allah in His protected one. And whoever prays the Asr (afternoon) prayer is under the protection of Allah, so do not offend Allah in His protected one." Abu Muhammad said: "If he is trusted and then he betrays, then he has broken his promise and acted disgracefully."
"When the time for prayer approaches and a man needs to relieve himself, he should begin with that [need] first."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade a man from shortening his prayer.
Abu Barzah reported: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, disliked sleeping before the 'Isha' prayer and talking after it."

I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him forth, and he proclaimed four things until his voice became clear: “Verily, no soul except a believing one shall enter Paradise, and let no polytheist perform pilgrimage after this year, and let no one circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, his term is four months; and when those four months pass, then Allah and His Messenger are clear of the polytheists.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Teach the boy prayer at the age of seven, and discipline him for it at the age of ten."

"Wehbu bin Ja'r narrated to me, saying: Musa bin Ali narrated to me, saying: I heard my father say: I heard Uqba bin Amir say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade us from praying or burying our dead during three intervals: when the sun rises bright until it ascends, when the one who stands for the midday prayer stands until the sun declines, and when the sun weakens towards sunset until it sets."

Narrated Abu Al-Aliya, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Certain trustworthy men informed me – and among them was Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he was the most approved of by me – that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no prayer after the Fajr prayer until the sun rises, and no prayer after the Asr prayer until the sun sets."

Abu Ishaq said: I heard Al-Aswad ibn Yazid and Masruq testify that Aisha witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ always praying these two rak'ahs [after the afternoon prayer]. Abu Muhammad said: Meaning, after the afternoon prayer.
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) never left two rak'ahs after the Asr prayer."

Abdullah ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn Azhar, and Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama sent me to Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and they said, "Send her our greetings collectively, and ask her about the two rak'ahs after the Asr prayer, and say: We have been informed that you pray them, and it has reached us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade them." Abdullah ibn Abbas said: "I used to strike those who prayed them along with Umar ibn al-Khattab."

Kuraib said: "I entered upon her and conveyed to her what they had sent me with. She said: Ask Umm Salama." So I went out to them and informed them of her saying. They sent me back to Umm Salama with the same message they had sent me to Aisha.

Umm Salama said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbidding them, then I saw him praying them. As for when he prayed them, he prayed the Asr prayer, then entered and there were women from the Banu Haram of the Ansar with me, so he prayed those two rak'ahs. I sent a maid to him, and said: 'Go to his side and say: Umm Salama says: O Messenger of Allah, did I not hear you forbidding these two rak'ahs, and I see you praying them?' If he gestures with his hand, then stay away from him." She said: "So the maid did so, and he gestured with his hand, so she stayed away from him. When he left, he said: 'O daughter of Abu Umayya, did you ask about the two rak'ahs after Asr? Indeed, people from the Abd al-Qays came to me with Islam, along with their people, so they occupied me from the two rak'ahs after the Dhuhr prayer, so these are they.'"

Abu Muhammad was asked about this hadith, and he said: "I say according to the hadith of Umar from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): 'There is no prayer after Asr until the sun sets, and no prayer after Fajr until the sun rises.'"

Abu 'Aasim narrated from Malik, from Naf'i', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray two rak'ahs before Zuhr, two rak'ahs after Zuhr, two rak'ahs after Maghrib in his home, two rak'ahs after 'Isha', and two rak'ahs after Jumu'ah in his home.

"No Muslim slave performs twelve voluntary Rak'ahs every day, apart from the obligatory prayers, but a house is built for him in Paradise, or a house is built for him in Paradise." Um Habibah said, "So I never ceased to pray them after that." 'Amro said something similar. And Nu'man said something similar.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would regularly pray four Rak'ahs before the Zuhr (noon) prayer, and two Rak'ahs before the Fajr (dawn) prayer."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Between every two calls to prayer (adhan) there is a prayer, between every two calls to prayer there is a prayer, between every two calls to prayer there is a prayer for whoever wishes."

Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The muadhdhin would pronounce the call to the Maghrib prayer during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and the elite of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would stand up, hastening to the prayer mats until the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would come out while they were like that.” He said: “And it was rare that he would linger.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to whisper what he recited [in the two surahs], and she mentioned ‘Say, O disbelievers,’ and ‘Say, He is Allah, the One.’” Saeed said: [He used to do so] in the two rak’ahs of Fajr (dawn prayer).

Musaddad narrated to me, he said: Yahya narrated to me, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Naafi’ informed me, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: Hafsah informed me that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray two light prostrations after the Fajr had appeared. And it was a time during which I would not enter upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).

Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) would, after the muezzin had ceased calling the dawn adhan and the dawn had begun to appear, pray two light rak'ahs before the prayer was announced."
Narrated by Salim from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray two rak'ahs after the Friday prayer.
Hafsah informed him [the narrator], that he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) used to pray two rak'ahs when the dawn became bright.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, after praying the two rak'ahs before Fajr, if he had a need, he would mention it to me; otherwise, he would proceed to the prayer."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray between the Isha and Fajr prayers eleven rak'ahs, giving salam after every two rak'ahs, and performing the Witr prayer with one rak'ah. And when the mu'adhdhin ceased from the first adhan, he would pray two light rak'ahs, then lie down until the mu'adhdhin came to him, and he would then go out with him."

Abu Hurairah (RA) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the adhan (call to prayer) is announced, there is no prayer [obligatory prayer] except the obligatory prayer."

Another narration: Abu Hurairah (RA) said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said something similar.

Narrated Ibn Buhaynah: The prayer was announced, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw a man praying two rak'ahs. When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) finished his prayer, the people began to reproach him, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him, "Do you pray the Fajr (dawn) prayer four rak'ahs?"

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "When the prayer is announced, there is no prayer except the obligatory prayer." Abu Muhammad said: "If he is in his house, the house is preferable."
Allah (Exalted and Mighty) said, “O son of Adam, pray four rak’ahs for Me in the early part of the day, and I will suffice you for the rest of it.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: 'Amru ibn Murra informed me, he said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla say: No one has informed us that they saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, praying Duha (mid-morning prayer) except Ummu Hani’. She mentioned that it was on the day of the conquest of Mecca, he bathed in her house, then prayed eight rak'ahs. She said: I have never seen him pray a lighter prayer than that, except that he would complete the bowing and prostration.

Umm Hani bint Abi Talib reported: "I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the year of the conquest and found him bathing. Fatima, his daughter, was covering him with a garment. I greeted him, and it was midday. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'Who is this?' I said, 'I am Umm Hani.' When he finished his bathing, he stood up and offered eight rak'ahs, wrapped in a single garment, and then turned away."

I said, “O Messenger of Allah, my uncle’s son claims he killed a man I granted protection to, Fulān ibn Hubayrah.” He (the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him) said, “We have granted protection to whom you have granted protection, O Ummah Hanī’.”

Abu Hurairah (RA) said: "My beloved Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed me with three things which I will never abandon until I die: performing Witr prayer before sleeping, fasting three days of every month, and praying two rak'ahs of Dhuha (mid-morning prayer)."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) never prayed the Subh prayer (early morning prayer) while traveling or residing."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr: His father saw people praying the Duha prayer, and he said, “Indeed, they are praying a prayer that neither the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed nor did the generality of his companions.”
Narrated by Zaid ibn Arqam: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came upon them while they were praying after sunrise and said, "The prayer of the early devotees is when the young ones thirst."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shaiba: He narrated to us, saying: Abu Waqid and Ghunder narrated to us from Shu’bah, from Ya’la ibn ‘Ata’, from ‘Ali al-Azdi, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The night and day prayers are two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs.” And one of them said: Two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs.

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Naafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the night prayer. He said: "Pray in pairs, in pairs. And if one of you fears the dawn, then let him pray one rak’ah which will complete what he has prayed."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Salam: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Medina, the people were delighted by him and said, "The Messenger of Allah has arrived! The Messenger of Allah has arrived!" So I went out among those who went out. And when I saw his face, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. And the first thing I heard him say was: “O people, spread the greeting of peace, feed the poor, maintain the ties of kinship, and pray while people are asleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace.”

I entered the mosque of Damascus and saw a man prolonging his bowing and prostration. I said, “I will not leave until I see if he knows whether he has performed two rak'ahs or a witr prayer.” When he finished, I said to him, “O slave of Allah, do you know if you have performed two rak'ahs or a witr prayer?” He said, “If I do not know, then Allah knows.”

Then he said, “Indeed, I heard my close friend, Abu al-Qasim, peace be upon him, say, ‘No slave prostrates to Allah in a prostration except that Allah raises him by it a degree and removes from him a sin.’”

I said, “Who are you, may Allah have mercy on you?” He said, “I am Abu Dharr.”

Then my soul felt diminished in my eyes.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Salamah ibn Raja narrated to me, saying: Shaathaa’ said: I saw Ibn Abi Aufa pray two rak'ahs and say: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed the Duha prayer two rak'ahs when he was given the news of the conquest, or when the head of Abu Jahl was brought."

I came to Hira and saw them prostrating before their governor, so I said, “O Messenger of Allah, should we not prostrate for you?” He said, “If I were to order anyone to prostrate for anyone, I would order women to prostrate for their husbands, due to the rights Allah has imposed upon them.”

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Hizami narrated to me, he said: Habban ibn Ali narrated to me, from Salih ibn Habban, from Ibn Burayda, from his father, who said: An Arab man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, allow me to prostrate for you." He (the Prophet) said: "If I were to order anyone to prostrate for anyone, I would order a woman to prostrate for her husband."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) recited [a passage from] the stars and prostrated upon it. So no one remained but that he prostrated, except an elderly man who took a handful of pebbles and raised it to his forehead and said: "This is sufficient for me."

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) delivered a sermon to us one day and recited [Surah Al-Baqarah]. When he reached the prostration, he got down and prostrated, and we prostrated along with him. He recited it again, and when he reached the prostration, we prepared ourselves for the prostration. When he saw us, he said: “It is the prostration of a prophet, but I see that you have prepared yourselves for the prostration.” So he got down and prostrated, and we prostrated along with him.

'Amru bin Zurara narrated to me, saying: Isma'il (ibn 'Aliya) narrated to me, saying: Ayyub narrated to me from 'Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, who said: "He used to recite in the prostration during the [supererogatory] prayer: 'There is no obligation in the prostration,' and I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrate in it."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn ‘Amr narrated to me, from Abu Salama, who said: I saw Abu Huraira prostrating during the recitation of Surah Isra’. It was said to him: “You prostrate in a Surah in which prostration is not prescribed?” He said: “Indeed, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrating in it.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, that Al-Awza'i narrated to me, from Yahya, from Abu Salama, who said: I saw Abu Huraira prostrating during the eclipse (of the sun), and I said to him: "O Abu Huraira, I see you prostrating during the eclipse." He said: "If I had not seen the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, prostrate during it, I would not have prostrated."
Narrated Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) prostrated during the recitation of "When the sky is split open."
Narrated Abu Huraira: We prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the night when the sky split open, and he recited, "Read! (Qul) In the name of your Lord."
I recited (the Surah) An-Najm before the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and he did not prostrate in it.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray between the Isha and Fajr prayers eleven rak'ahs, giving salam after every two rak'ahs, and performing Witr with one rak'ah. He would prostrate in his tahajjud (night prayer) for as long as one of you reads fifty verses before raising his head. And when the mu'adhdhin ceased from the first adhan, he would pray two light rak'ahs, then lie down until the mu'adhdhin came, and he would go out with him.”

Yazid ibn Harun and Wahb ibn Ja'rir narrated to us, saying: We were told by Hisham, from Yahya, from Abu Salama, who said: I asked Aisha about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, at night. She said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pray thirteen rak'ahs. He would pray eight rak'ahs, then perform Witr, then pray two rak'ahs while sitting. If he intended to perform a bow (in the sitting prayer), he would stand and bow. And he used to pray two rak'ahs between the call (adhan) and the iqama of the Fajr prayer.

Sa'd ibn Hisaam divorced his wife and came to Medina to sell his property, intending to spend it on weapons and trinkets. He was met by a group of the Ansar, who said, "Six of us intended to do this during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, but he forbade them, and said, ‘Do you not have in me an example?’”

Then he came to Basra and narrated that he met Abdullah ibn Abbas and asked him about the Witr prayer. He (Ibn Abbas) said, "Shall I tell you about the most knowledgeable person regarding the Witr of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Aisha, the mother of the believers. Go to her and ask her, then return to me and tell me what she tells you.”

So, I went to Hakim ibn Hisham and said to him, “Come with me to Aisha, the mother of the believers.” He said, “I will not go to her; I have been forbidden from visiting these two groups (of people).” He refused except by my insistence.

I said, “I swear by you that you will come.” So, we set out, and we greeted her. She recognized Hakim’s voice and said, “Who is this?” I said, “Sa’d ibn Hisham.”

She said, “Who is Hisham?” I said, “Hisham ibn Amir.”

She said, “He was a good man; he was killed on the day of Uhud.”

I said, “Tell us about the character of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

She said, “Don’t you recite the Quran?” I said, “Yes.”

She said, “Then that is the character of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” I intended to stand up and not ask anyone about anything until I returned to Allah, and the inclination to leave arose within me.

I said, "Inform me about the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." She said, "Do you not recite, ‘O you who are wrapped in your garment’?" I said, "Yes." She said, "That was the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The first part of the Surah was revealed, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions stood until their feet swelled. The last part of it was withheld in the heavens for sixteen months, then it was revealed, so the night prayer became voluntary after it had been obligatory." Then I intended to stand and not ask anyone about anything until I joined Allah, but the Witr prayer was presented to me.

I said, "Inform me about the Witr prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him." She said, "The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, would, when he slept, place his siwak with me, and Allah would send it forth as He willed. He would pray nine rak'ahs, not pausing except in the eighth, wherein he would praise Allah and supplicate his Lord. Then he would stand and not greet, then sit in the ninth, wherein he would praise Allah and supplicate his Lord and greet with a greeting that we could hear. Then he would pray two rak'ahs while sitting. That was eleven rak'ahs, O my son. When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, grew old and his flesh weakened, he would pray seven rak'ahs, not pausing except in the sixth, wherein he would praise Allah and supplicate his Lord. Then he would stand and not greet, then sit in the seventh, wherein he would praise Allah and supplicate his Lord, then greet with a greeting. Then he would pray two rak'ahs while sitting. That was nine rak'ahs, O my son. And the Prophet, peace be upon him, if sleep or illness overcame him, would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day. And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, when he adopted a habit, he would love to persist in it. And the Prophet of Allah, peace be upon him, would not stand up at night until morning, nor would he recite the entire Quran in a night, nor would he fast a complete month other than Ramadan.”

So I went to Ibn Abbas and related it to him. He said, "You spoke the truth. Indeed, if I were to visit her, I would see her directly."

He said, "I said, 'Indeed, if I had realized that you would not visit her, I would not have told you.'"
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The best (voluntary) prayer after the obligatory prayers is the prayer in the middle of the night."

Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever sleeps and misses a portion of his [Quran recitation] or the whole of it, and then recites it between the Fajr and Zuhr prayers, it is recorded for him as if he recited it during the night."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah descends every night to the lower heaven until the last third of the night or half of it, and says: Who is it who calls Me, so that I may answer him? Who is it who asks Me, so that I may grant him? Who is it who seeks forgiveness from Me, so that I may forgive him? Until the dawn appears or the reciter turns from the Fajr prayer."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Our Lord, blessed and exalted be He, descends every night to the lower heaven when a third of the night has passed, and says: ‘Who is calling Me so that I may answer him? Who is asking for forgiveness so that I may forgive him? Who is asking so that I may grant him?’ until the dawn."

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Every night, Allah descends to the lower heaven and says: 'Is there anyone who will ask, so that I may grant him? Is there anyone who will seek forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?'"

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "When half or two-thirds of the night have passed, Allah descends to the lower heaven and says: Who is it that asks, so I may grant him? Who is it that seeks forgiveness, so I may forgive him? Who is it that calls upon Me, so I may respond to him, until the dawn breaks."
Narrated ‘Ali: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said: “When a third or half of the night passes…” then he mentioned (something about) the descent.

I have narrated to us Muhammad ibn Yahya; he narrated to us Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim; he narrated to us my father; from Ibn Ishaq; he narrated to me Sa’id ibn Abi Sa’id al-Maqburri; from Ata’a, the freedman of Umm Subayyah; from Abu Hurayrah, who said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: ‘If it were not difficult for my community, I would order them to use the siwak after every prayer. And I would delay the last night meal until a third of the night has passed. For when the first third of the night passes, Allah descends to the nearest heaven and remains there until dawn, and says: Who is asking for forgiveness so that I may forgive him? Who is asking for provision so that I may provide for him? Who is asking for healing so that I may heal him? Who is seeking forgiveness so that I may forgive him?’”

Muhammad narrated to us; he narrated to us Ya’qub; he narrated to me my father; from Ibn Ishaq; he narrated to me my uncle, Abdur-Rahman ibn Yasir; from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Raf’i, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; from his father; from Ali ibn Abi Talib; from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, a similar narration to that of Abu Hurayrah.

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to recite these words when he stood up for the night prayer (Tahajjud): “O Allah, all praise is due to You. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. And all praise is due to You, You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. And all praise is due to You, You are the King of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. You are the Truth, and Your word is the Truth, and Your promise is the Truth, and meeting You is the Truth, and Paradise is the Truth, and Hellfire is the Truth, and the Resurrection is the Truth, and the prophets are the Truth, and Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the Truth. O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, in You I have placed my trust, to You I turn, with You I argue, and to You I judge. So forgive me what I have done before and what I have done afterward, what I have declared and what I have concealed. You are the Forerunner and You are the Delayer. There is no god but You, and there is no power and no strength except in You.”
He (the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah in a night, that is sufficient for him."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah has not permitted anything as He has permitted a Prophet reciting the Quran, proclaiming it aloud."
Narrated Aisha: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) heard Abu Musa reading (the Quran), and said: “Indeed, this has been given to you from the Psalms of David.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "None of us is one of us who does not recite the Quran melodiously."

Narrated Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Allah has not permitted anything as He has permitted a Prophet to recite the Quran melodiously." Abu Muhammad said: He means by it, self-sufficiency.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me and said, “Did not Allah say, ‘O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when they call you to justice,’ [Quran 8:24]?” Then he said, “Shall I not teach you a surah which is the greatest surah in the Quran before I leave the mosque?” So, when he intended to leave, he said, “All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and it is the Seven Oft-Repeated [Surah Al-Fatiha], and the Great Quran which you have been given.”
Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "One who recites the Qur’an in less than three [years] does not understand it."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me, from Yahya, from Abu Salama, from Abu Huraira, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the call to prayer (Adhan) is announced, Satan turns away, emitting a sound like a donkey's braying, so that he may not hear the Adhan. When the Adhan is concluded, he returns. When the clothing is donned, he turns away. When the donning of the clothing is concluded, he returns, until he plants himself between a man and his heart, and says: 'Remember such and such, remember such and such,' things that he would not have remembered. Thus, a man remains uncertain how many Rak'ahs he has prayed. If any of you is unsure whether he has prayed three or four Rak'ahs, he should prostrate two prostrations while sitting."

"If one of you is unsure whether he has prayed three or four [rak'ahs], let him stand up, pray one rak'ah, then prostrate two prostrations after that. If he has prayed five [rak'ahs], they will suffice for his prayer. And if he has prayed four [rak'ahs], then those two [prostrations] will be a humiliation for Satan."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Muhammad, from Abu Huraira, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered one of the evening prayers, and he prayed two rak’ahs, then he greeted (peace) and stood up to a wooden beam placed across the mosque, and placed his hand upon it. Yazid said: Ibn ‘Awn showed us, and placed his palms, one upon the other, and inserted his upper fingers into the lower ones, placing them and standing as if he were angry. He said: The hasty people among the people went out and began to say: “The prayer has been shortened, the prayer has been shortened.”

Among the people were Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, and they did not speak. And among the people was a man with long hands, called “Dhu al-Yadayn,” who said: “O Messenger of Allah, did you forget the prayer, or has it been shortened?” He said: “I have not forgotten, nor has the prayer been shortened.” He said: “Is it so?” They said: “Yes.”

He said: “Then he returned,” and completed what remained, then greeted and said, “Allahu Akbar,” and prostrated, prostrating for a long time, then he raised his head, said, “Allahu Akbar,” and prostrated as he had prostrated, then he raised his head and left.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offered the Zuhr or ‘Asr prayer and he shortened the prayer (i.e., reduced the number of Rak'ahs) and gave Salam in two Rak'ahs of one of them. Then, Thu Al-Yadain bin ‘Amr bin Nadla Al-Khuzai, who was an ally of Banu Zuhra, said to him, “Did you shorten it or forget, O Messenger of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “I did not forget, and I did not shorten it.”

Thu Al-Yadain said, “Some of that was the case, O Messenger of Allah.” So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned towards the people and said, “Is Thu Al-Yadain truthful?” They said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and completed the prayer. None of them informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrated two prostrations while sitting in that prayer. And that was because the people were certain about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until they became convinced.
Narrated Abdullah: The Prophet (ﷺ) offered the Zuhr prayer with five Rak'ahs. It was said to him, "Pray (again)," so he prostrated two prostrations.

Narrated Ibn Buhaynah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered prayer with us for two rak'ahs, then he stood up without sitting. The people also stood up. When he finished the prayer, we looked at his greeting, and he said "Allahu Akbar" and prostrated two prostrations while sitting before giving the greeting, and then he gave the greeting.

Narrated Malik ibn Buhaynah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for the two rak'ahs of Zuhr or 'Asr, and he did not return until he had finished his prayer, then he performed the prostration of forgetfulness, and then he concluded (with the salaam).

Yazid ibn Harun narrated from Al-Mas’udi, from Ziyad ibn ‘Ilāqah, who said: “Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah led us in prayer. When he had recited two rak’ahs, he stood up without sitting. Those behind him began to say, ‘SubhanAllah [Glory be to Allah]’. He gestured to them to sit down. When he finished his prayer, he said the Salam and performed two prostrations of forgetfulness, said the Salam, and said: ‘Thus, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to do.’” Yazid said: “They authenticate it.”

While I was praying with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man among the people sneezed. I said, “May Allah have mercy on you.” The people stared at me, and I said, “May you perish! What are you looking at?” They then struck their hands on their thighs, and when I saw them silencing me, I said, “What is the matter with you, why do you silence me?” But I remained silent. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned around, and I said, “By my parents, I have not seen a better teacher before him or after him, and by Allah, he never struck me, scolded me, or cursed me. Rather, he said, “In this prayer of ours, nothing from the talk of the people is permissible. It is only glorification, exaltation, and recitation of the Qur’an.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Hisham, from Yahya, from Damdam, from Abu Huraira, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that the two black creatures be killed during prayer. Yahya said: "The two black creatures are the snake and the scorpion."

I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, "Allah has said, 'So there is no blame on you for that you shorten the prayer if you fear,' [Quran 4:101], so the people have been secure." He said, "I am amazed at what you are amazed at." Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "It is a charity which Allah has given to you, so accept it."

Narrated by Salim from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abu Bakr, and Umar, and Uthman prayed two rak'ahs at Mina at the beginning of Uthman's caliphate, and then they completed [the prayer] afterwards.
Narrated Anas bin Malik: We prayed the Dhuhr prayer with the Prophet (peace be upon him) in Medina four Rak'ahs, and we prayed with him at Dhi al-Halifah two Rak'ahs.

Uthman ibn Muhammad narrated to me, that Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, that they heard Anas ibn Malik saying: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed four Rak'ahs in Medina and two Rak'ahs at Dhi al-Halifah."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "Indeed, the prayer was first ordained as two rak'ahs, and the prayer of travel was confirmed, and the prayer of settlement was completed." I asked, "What was the matter with her that she would complete the prayer while traveling?" He said, "She interpreted [it] as Uthman interpreted [it]."

Narrated Anas bin Malik: We went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) and he used to shorten (the prayers) until we reached Mecca, and he stayed there for ten days shortening (the prayers) until he returned, and that was during his Hajj.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The stay of the emigrant after completing his ritual obligations is three [days]."

Narrated by Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Hadrami: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the Muhajirun (emigrants) to stay for three nights after the Sadar (the initial period) in Makkah.” Abu Muhammad said: “I testify to its authenticity.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Hisham al-Dustawa'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Katir, from Muhammad ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Thawban, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pray on his camel facing the East. But when he intended to pray the obligatory prayer, he would dismount and face the Qibla.

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: Abdullah bin Amir bin Rabi'ah told me that Amir bin Rabi'ah said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was on his mount, reciting the remembrance of Allah (SubhanAllah), and he would nod his head towards whichever direction he faced. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not perform this action during the obligatory prayer."

We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the campaign of Tabuk, and he would combine the prayers. He combined the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, then entered [his tent], and then he came out and combined the Maghrib and Isha prayers.

Yahya ibn Hasan narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered the Maghrib and Isha prayers together, combining them.
Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would combine the Maghrib and Isha prayers when the journey became pressing.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: Al-Hakam and Salama ibn Kuhail narrated to me, they said: "Sa'id ibn Jubair led us in prayer with the Maghrib (sunset) prayer, establishing it with the Iqama (call to prayer), three times. When he concluded, he stood up and prayed the 'Isha' (night) prayer, two rak'ahs." Then he narrated from Ibn Umar that he did likewise for them in that place, and Ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did likewise in that place.

Sa'id ibn al-Rabee' narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, with his chain of narration, in a similar manner.
Narrated by K’ab bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not return from a journey except during the forenoon, and then he would enter the mosque and pray two rak’ahs, and then sit for the people.

I narrated to me Hakim bin Naafi’, from Shu’aib, from Zuhri, who narrated to me Salim bin ‘Abdullah: that ‘Abdullah bin ‘Umar (RA) said: “I accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a campaign towards Najd. We faced the enemy and lined up against them. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up to pray for us, and a group of us stood with him. Another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with those who were with him one rak’ah and prostrated two prostrations, then he turned back. They took the place of the group that had not prayed, and the group that had not prayed came forward. The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed with them one rak’ah and prostrated two prostrations, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, ‘As-salamu alaykum.’ Every man among the Muslims then stood up and prayed one rak’ah and prostrated two prostrations for himself.”

Narrated by Sahl bin Abi Hathmah concerning the prayer of fear: “The Imam prays with a group, and a group faces the enemy. He prays with those who are with him one rak’ah, and these go to the ranks of their companions, and those come and he prays with them one rak’ah, and they pray one rak’ah for themselves.” Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated, “Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to me, Yahya bin Sa’id narrated to me, from Shu’bah, from Abdurrahman bin Qasim, from his father, from Salih bin Khuwat, from Sahl bin Abi Hathmah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), with a similar wording.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Ibn Abi Zayd, from Al-Maqburri, from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Sa’id Al-Khudri, from his father, who said: "We were detained on the day of the Trench until the darkness of the night had almost vanished, until we were exhausted. That was the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ‘And Allah would suffice the believers in fighting, and Allah is Powerful, Worthy of all respect.’ [33:25] So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) called Bilal and ordered him, and he stood up and performed the Dhuhr (noon) prayer, perfecting it as he used to perform it at its appointed time. Then he ordered him and he stood up and performed the Asr (afternoon) prayer, and then he ordered him and he stood up and performed the Maghrib (sunset) prayer. Then he ordered him and he stood up and performed the Isha (night) prayer. That was before the revelation of: ‘So if you fear, then (do it) in groups or on foot.’ [2:239]"

Narrated Abu Mas’ud Al-Ansari: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed due to the death of any person among the people, but they are signs of Allah. So, when you see them, stand up and pray.”

Narrated ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah al-Madini and Musaddad: Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id, who told me Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) prayed during an eclipse eight rak’ahs in four prostrations.

Aisha narrated: A Jewish woman came to her and said, "May Allah protect you from the torment of the grave." When the Prophet (ﷺ) came, she asked him, "Are people tormented in their graves?" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah." She said, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) rode one day and the sun eclipsed. So the Prophet (ﷺ) came and descended, and then proceeded to the place where he used to pray. The people stood behind him and he prolonged the standing, then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, then he stood and prolonged the standing, which was shorter than the first standing, then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, which was shorter than the first bowing, then he prostrated two prostrations, then he stood and did like that, and then the sun reappeared."
Then he entered upon me and said: "Indeed, I see you being tested in your graves with a trial like the trial of the Dajjal."
I heard him (the Prophet) saying: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the torment of the Fire."

Abu Ya’qub Yusuf al-Bawiti narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Idris – that is, ash-Shafi’i – that Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: “The sun eclipsed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed. Ibn Abbas recounted that his prayer ﷺ was two rak’ahs in each rak’ah, two rak’ahs. Then he addressed them in a sermon, saying: ‘Indeed, the sun and the moon are signs of Allah. They do not eclipse because of the death of anyone, nor because of his life. So, when you see that, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah.’”
She (Aisha) reported: "An eclipse occurred, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offered prayer, and she mentioned that he offered two rak'ahs, in each rak'ah two rak'ahs."

Narrated ‘Asma bint Abu Bakr: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the manumission of a slave when the sun was eclipsed. Abu Huraira reported that Mus’ab bin Mas’ud narrated to him from Zaidah, from Hisham bin ‘Urwah, from Fatima, from ‘Asma, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said something similar.

Narrated by Yazid ibn Harun: Yahya ibn Sa'id Al-Ansari narrated to me from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from 'Abbad ibn Tamim, that he heard 'Abdullah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with him) mention that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) went out with the people to seek rain, and he faced the Qibla and turned his garment.

Hakim ibn Nafi’ reported from Shu’aib from Zuhri, that ‘Ubaid ibn Tamim reported to him that his uncle informed him: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out with the people to the place of prayer, seeking rain for them. He stood and supplicated to Allah standing, then he faced the Qibla, and turned his garment, and they were given rain.
Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not raise his hands in supplication for anything except in asking for rain.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When any of you comes for the Friday prayer, let him bathe (ghusl)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The washing on the day of Friday is obligatory upon every adult male."

Narrated Abu Huraira: While Umar bin Al-Khattab was delivering a sermon, a man entered and criticized him. Umar said to him, "I have not done anything more than performing ablution when I heard the call to prayer." The man replied, "And the ablution too?" Umar said, "Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'When anyone of you comes for the Friday prayer, let him bathe.'"
"One who performs ablution for Friday, that is sufficient, and if one were to bathe, then bathing is better."

Narrated by Salman Al-Farsi, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday, purifies himself as much as he can, then applies oil from his own oil or touches something fragrant from his household's fragrance, and then sets out without intermixing with others and prays what has been ordained for him, and when the Imam begins [the Khutbah], he listens attentively, then his sins between that Friday and the next are forgiven."
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite during the Fajr prayer on Fridays, "Tanzil as-Sajdah" and "Hal ata 'ala al-insan."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who hurries to the Friday prayer is like the one who drives a camel to graze, then the one who follows him is like the one who drives an ox to graze, then the one who follows him is like the one who drives a sheep to graze. And when the Imam sits on the pulpit, the scriptures are folded, and they sit listening to the remembrance."

Narrated Abu Hurrah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When the Day of Jumu'ah comes, the angels sit on the doors of the mosque and record the names of those who come to Jumu'ah. When the Imam begins [the prayer], the angels roll up the scrolls and listen to the remembrance [Khutbah]."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "One who prepares himself for Friday is like one who offers a cow as a sacrifice, then a cow, then a sheep, then a hen, then a rooster, then an egg."

We used to pray with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) on Fridays, and then we would return and hasten to seek shade in the courtyard of Bani Ghanm, and it would not extend beyond the places of our feet.
"We used to pray Friday prayers with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and then return without any shade under which to take shelter."

"Whoever washes himself [thoroughly] on Friday, and then bathes, and goes forth early and sits close to the Imam and listens attentively, and does not speak until the Imam departs, then for every step he takes, it is equivalent to the reward of fasting and praying for a year."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If you say to your companion, 'Be silent, and the Imam is delivering the sermon,' then you have spoken frivolously."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If you say to your companion, 'Be silent,' while the Imam is delivering the sermon, then you have spoken frivolously."
"Whenever any of you comes while the Imam is delivering the sermon or has already set out [for prayer], let him pray two rak'ahs."

Sadqah narrated: Sufyan narrated to me from Ibn ‘Ajlan, from ‘Iyadh ibn ‘Abdullah, who said: Abu Sa’id and Marwan were delivering a sermon. [The Prophet] stood up to pray two rak’ahs. Then the guards came to prevent him, so he said: “I would not leave them, for I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordering them.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to me, from Rabi’ – he is Ibn Sabih al-Basri – that he said: I saw al-Hasan praying two rak’ahs while the Imam was delivering the khutbah.

Al-Hasan said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “If any of you comes [to the mosque] while the Imam is delivering the khutbah, let him pray two light rak’ahs, and let him hasten in them.”

Abu Muhammad said: I affirm this.
Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon one day and recited [Surah] Al-Hashr. When he reached the prostration, he dismounted and prostrated.

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: A man entered the mosque on the day of Jumu'ah while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering the Khutbah. He said, "Did you pray?" He said, "No." He (the Prophet) said, "Then pray two Rak'ahs." Abu Muhammad said: I testify to its authenticity.

Ammar ibn Yasir delivered a sermon to us, being both eloquent and concise. We said, "O Abu al-Yaqthan, if only you had elaborated further!" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: 'The length of a man’s prayer and the brevity of his sermon are a sign of his understanding.' So lengthen this prayer and shorten this sermon, for there is indeed in clarity a charm."
I prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and his prayer was concise, and his khutbah was concise.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to deliver two sermons while standing, and he would separate them by sitting.
Narrated by Jabir bin Samurah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had two sermons, and he would sit between them reciting the Quran and reminding the people.

Abu Zubayd narrated from Husam, who said: 'Umara ibn Ruwayba saw Bishr ibn Marwan on the pulpit raising his hands, so he said: "May Allah detest these two hands! I have indeed seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the pulpit, and he would not gesture except with his finger."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me, from Husayn ibn ‘Abd ar-Rahman, from ‘Amara ibn Ruwayba, who said: Bishr ibn Marwan was seen raising his hands supplicating on the pulpit on the day of Jumu’ah. So, he cursed him and said: “Indeed, I have seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the pulpit, and he would not say anything with his finger except like this,” and he gestured with his index finger towards the waist.

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to stand at a tree trunk before the pulpit was made. When the pulpit was made, that tree trunk lamented until we heard its lamentation. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) placed his hand upon it, and it became silent."

Narrated ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to deliver sermons to a tree trunk before he had a pulpit built. When he had the pulpit built, he moved to it. The tree trunk grieved and embraced him, and he settled down and said: “If I had not embraced it, it would have grieved until the Day of Resurrection.”

Narrated by Hajjaj, Hammad, Thabit, Anas, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), similar to this.

Sahlu bin Sa’d (RA) reported: When the people increased in Medina, a man would come and the people would come, and they could hardly hear the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) until they returned from him. So, the people said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, the people have increased, and the one who comes can hardly hear your words.” He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “As you wish.” So, they sent for a young carpenter from among the Ansar and to Tarfa’i al-Ghaba. They made for him two or three platforms. So, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) would sit on them and deliver sermons. When they did that, the wooden post that he used to stand by became affectionate (or softened). So, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up to it and placed his hand upon it, and it became still.

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated: Malik narrated to me from Damrah ibn Sa’id Al-Mazini from ‘Ubaidullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah that Dhahhak ibn Qais asked An-Nu’man ibn Bashir Al-Ansari: "What Surah did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite after Surah Al-Jumu’ah on Fridays?” He (An-Nu’man) said: “Has the story of Al-Ghashiyah reached you?”

Narrated by Nu'man bin Bashir Al-Ansari: We asked him (the Prophet) about what he used to recite with the Surah in which Friday is mentioned. He said, "He used to recite with it, 'Have you received news of the Sacking?'"

Narrated by Nu’man bin Bashir: “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite in the two ‘Eids and on Fridays, [Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4)] and [Surah Al-Ghashiyah (88:1-22)], and sometimes both would be recited with them.”

I met with Ka'b, and I began to relate to him what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, and he began to relate to me about the Torah, until we came to the mention of the Day of Jumu'ah. Then I said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'There is an hour in it that if a Muslim slave asks Allah for good in it, He will give it to him.'"
Some people will surely cease attending the Friday gatherings, or Allah will seal their hearts, and then they will be among the heedless.
"Whoever neglects the Friday prayer out of carelessness, Allah will seal his heart."

Narrated by Aws bin Aws: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “The best of your days is the Day of Friday; on it Adam was created, on it he was breathed into, on it the trumpet will be blown, and on it the earthquake will occur. So, increase (your prayers) for me on this day, for your prayers are presented to me.”

A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is our prayer presented to you when you have been worn out?" – meaning, afflicted. He said: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."
Narrated by Abu ‘Aasim, from Malik, from Naafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray two rak’ahs in his home after Jumu’ah (Friday) prayer.
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray two rak'ahs after the Friday prayer.
"Whoever is among you who prays after Jumu'ah (Friday prayer), let him pray four [rak'ahs] after it." Abu Muhammad said, "I pray two or four [rak'ahs] after Jumu'ah."

Narrated by Abu Al-Walid Al-Tayalisi: He narrated to me, Layth, who is Ibn Sa’d, narrated to me, Yazid Ibn Abi Habib, from Abdullah Ibn Rashid Al-Zoufi, from Abdullah Ibn Abi Murrah Al-Zoufi, from Kharijah Ibn Hudhafah Al-‘Adawi, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said: “Indeed, Allah has granted you a prayer that is better for you than red camels.” He made it for you between the prayer of Isha’ (night prayer) and the rising of the dawn.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari narrated to us, that Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban narrated to us, that Ibn Muhriz al-Qurashi, then al-Jumahi, narrated to us, and he resided in Syria, and he witnessed Muawiya, that al-Mukhadji, a man from Banu Kinanah, narrated to him, that a man from Syria, who had companionship (Sahaba), and was known as Abu Muhammad, narrated to him: That the Witr prayer is obligatory. So, al-Mukhadji went to 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and mentioned that to him. 'Ubadah said: Abu Muhammad lied. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Allah has enjoined five prayers upon the people. Whoever performs them without belittling any of their rights, then he has a covenant from Allah that He will enter him into Paradise. And whoever does not perform them, then he comes without having a covenant from Allah; if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He enters him into Paradise."

Yahyá ibn Hasan narrated to me, saying: Ismā’īl ibn Ja’far narrated to me, from Abū Suhail, Nāfi’ ibn Mālika, from his father, from Ṭalḥa ibn ‘Ubayd Allāh, that an Arab man came to the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) in a state of agitation, and said: “O Messenger of Allāh, what has Allāh imposed upon me of prayer?” He (the Prophet) said: “The five daily prayers and fasting.” Then the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) informed him of the rulings of Islām, whereupon he said: “By the One who has honored you, I will not perform any voluntary acts, nor will I diminish from what Allāh has imposed upon me.” The Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) then said: “He has prospered, and his father has prospered, if he speaks the truth, or he and his father have entered Paradise if he speaks the truth.”
"Indeed, the Witr prayer is not obligatory like the obligatory prayers, but it is a Sunnah. So do not abandon it."
Indeed, Allah is the Single One (al-Witr), and He loves those who practice the Single (prayer - Witir).

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me from his father, from 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray thirteen rak'ahs at night, performing Witr with five (rak'ahs). He would not sit in any of them until he sat in the last one, and then he would say the Salam.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: "Perform the Witr prayer with five [rak'ahs], and if you cannot, then with three, and if you cannot, then with one, and if you cannot, then gesture with a nod."

Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Nāfi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the night prayer. He said: "Pray two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs. And if one of you fears the dawn, then let him pray one rak'ah that will complete [what he has prayed]." It was said to Abu Muhammad: Do you act upon this? He said: Yes.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to pray between the Isha and Fajr prayers eleven rak'ahs, giving salam in every two rak'ahs, and performing Witr with one rak'ah."

Malik related to me, saying, "Abu Ishaq told me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said, 'The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to perform the Witir prayer with three [rak'ahs]: reciting 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,' and 'Say, O you who disbelieve,' and 'Say, He is Allah, the One.'"

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to perform Witr prayer every night, and his Witr prayer would extend until the Fajr (dawn) prayer time."
Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the Witir (prayer of odd number), and he said: "Offer the Witir before Fajr."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Sa’id: He said, “Abu Usama narrated to me, saying: Zakariya narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, from Sa’id ibn Jubair, from Ibn Abbas, who said, ‘The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to perform the Witr prayer with three [recitations]: he would recite ‘Subhan Rabbika al-A’la’ in the first [rak’ah], ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ in the second [rak’ah], and ‘Qul huwallahu ahad’ in the third [rak’ah]’.”

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, that Abu Bakr ibn Umar narrated to me, from Sa’id ibn Yasar, from Ibn Umar, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to recite (the Quran) while riding a camel. It was said to Abu Muhammad: Do you relate this? He said: Yes.

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: I narrated to me Shu'bah, from Buraid ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu al-Harawiy as-Sa'di, who said: I said to al-Hasan ibn Ali: "What do you remember from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him?" He said: "He carried me on his back, and I took a date from the dates of charity and put it in my mouth. He said to me: 'Throw it! Do you not realize that charity is not permissible for us?'"

He (Al-Hasan) said: “He used to supplicate with this supplication: ‘O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, and grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, and take me under Your care among those You have taken under Your care, and bless me in what You have given me, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed; indeed, You decree and are not decreed upon, and whoever You befriend, he is not humiliated. Blessed are You and Exalted.’”

He (Ubaydullah ibn Musa) narrated to me, from Israel, from Abu Ishaq, from Burayd ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu al-Harawi, from Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught me words to say in the Qunut, and he mentioned the same [supplication].”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught me words to say in the Qunut of Witr: "O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, and grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, and take me in charge among those You have taken in charge, and bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed, for You decree and no one decrees against You, and whoever You befriend, he is not humiliated. You are blessed and exalted."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “This night vigil is an exertion and a burden, so if one of you performs the Witr prayer, let him pray two rak’ahs. If he does not stand [for prayer] during the night, then these two rak’ahs are sufficient for him.”

Yahya ibn Hasan narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa’d narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyib, and from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Huraira, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to, when he wanted to invoke blessings upon someone or curse someone, recite the Qunut after the bowing (in prayer). He would sometimes say: When he said, "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah, Rabbana wa laka al-hamd, Allahumma anj al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and Salama ibn Hisham, and 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabia, and the weak among the believers. O Allah, intensify your impact upon Mudar, and make it years like the years of Joseph.” And he would say this aloud. He would say in some of his prayers, in the Fajr prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," (referring to) two living individuals from the Arabs. Then Allah revealed: [And never is his command except [that] He says, "Be," and it is.] Or they repent, or He punishes them. Indeed, they are a wrongdoer. (Surah Al-Imran, 3:128)

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to me, saying: ‘Asim narrated: I asked Anas ibn Malik about the Qunut, and he said: Before the bowing. I said: So-and-so claims that you said it after the bowing. He said: He lied. Then he narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) recited the Qunut for a month after the bowing, invoking curses upon a group of Banu Sulaim.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to supplicate in the Fajr prayer.

Musaddad narrated to me, he said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: Anas ibn Malik was asked, "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite the Qunut in the Fajr prayer?" He said, "Yes." It was then said to him, "Did I say to him, before the bowing or after the bowing?" He said, "After the bowing, a little."

Abu Muhammad said: I affirm it and act upon it, and I do not see that one should act upon it except in times of war.
"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would eat before going out on the day of Eid al-Fitr, and when it was the day of Eid al-Adha, he would not eat until he returned and ate from his sacrifice."
Jabir (RA) said: "I witnessed the prayer with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) on a day of Eid, and he began the prayer before the khutbah, without an adhan or iqama."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, and Ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, and Ayyub as-Sakhtiyani narrated to me, saying: I heard Ata’ saying: I heard Ibn Abbas saying: “I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began with the prayer before the sermon on the day of Eid, then he gave the sermon. It appeared that the women had not heard him, so he went to them, reminded them, and admonished them, and ordered them to give charity. Bilal was holding his garment, and the women would come with a handful of coins or something, and throw it into Bilal’s garment.”
I witnessed the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman praying before the Khutbah on the festival day.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: 'Adi ibn Thabit told me, he said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubair relating, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) went out on the day of al-Fitr and prayed two rak'ahs, and he did not pray before them or after them.

Narrated Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ammar, from his father, from his grandfather: “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would perform the Takbir in the two ‘Eids. He would perform seven Takbirs in the first ‘Eid and five Takbirs in the second ‘Eid, and he would begin with the prayer before the Khutbah.”

Narrated by Nu’man bin Bashir: “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite [the Surahs] ‘Subhan Rabbika al-A’la’ and ‘Hal ata laka hadith al-Ghashiyah’ on the two Eids and on Fridays, and sometimes both would be recited together.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Salamah, meaning Ibn Nubait, narrated to me, saying: My father or Nu'im ibn Abi Hind narrated to me: "I performed Hajj with my father and my uncle. My father said to me: 'Do you see that man who delivers the sermon, the one with the red camel? That is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.'"

Umm ‘Atiyyah reported that her father (peace be upon him) ordered them to bring out on the days of al-Fitr and al-Adha the women who were not menstruating, and those who were in seclusion. As for those who were menstruating, they should keep away from the ranks, but they should witness the goodness and the supplication of the Muslims. I said: “O Messenger of Allah, what if one of them does not have a jilbab?” He (peace be upon him) said: “Let her be covered by her sister from her jilbab.”

Yala ibn ‘Ubaid narrated to me, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Malik, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said: I witnessed the prayer with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on a day of Eid. He began with the prayer before the sermon, then he stood leaning on Bilal until he reached the women. He admonished them, reminded them, and ordered them to fear Allah. He said, "Give charity." Then he mentioned something about the punishment of Hell. A woman from among the lower class of women, with ruddy cheeks, stood up and said, "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Because you reveal complaints and curses, and you deny the rights of your husbands.” So they began to take from their jewelry, earrings, and rings, and throw them into the garment of Bilal, giving charity with it.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, he said: Shu’ba narrated to me, from ‘Adiyy ibn Thabit, from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, a similar narration.

Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to me from Isra’il, from ‘Utman ibn Mughira, from Iyas ibn Abi Ramla, who said: I witnessed Mu’awiya questioning Zayd ibn Arqam: “Did you witness with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, two festivals coinciding in one day?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “How did he proceed?” He said: “He performed the festival prayer, then permitted the Friday prayer, and said: ‘Whoever wishes to pray, let him pray.’”
Narrated by Abu Huraira: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would return from the Eid prayer by a different route.

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Mu'adh when he sent him to Yemen, "You will come to a people of the Book, so call them to testify that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If they accept that from you, then inform them that Allah has imposed upon them five prayers in every day and night. If they accept that from you, then inform them that Allah has imposed upon them charity from their wealth, taken from their wealthy and returned to their poor. If they accept that from you, then beware of their noble properties and beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no shield against Allah other than Him."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The poor person is not he who scrapes by on a few morsels or two, or a piece of bread or two, or a date or two. Rather, the poor person is he who has no means to suffice him, and who is too shy to ask (people) earnestly, or does not ask (people) earnestly."

Narrated by Jabir: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "No owner of camels, cows, or sheep fails to fulfill their rights, but he will be held accountable for it on the Day of Resurrection, and they will trample him with their hooves, and gore him with their horns, and there will be no fat or broken-horned animal among them that day.”

They said: O Messenger of Allah, what is their right? He said: "To let them drink from the watering trough, to lend out their pail, to give them charity, to milk them on the water’s edge, and to carry them in the way of Allah.”

"No one who possesses camels and does not treat them well will come on the Day of Resurrection except that they are more numerous than they ever were, and they will be stationed in a desolate place, stamping with their feet and shins. And no one who possesses cows and does not treat them well will come on the Day of Resurrection except that they are more numerous than they ever were, and they will be stationed in a desolate place, butting him with their horns and treading him with their feet. And no one who possesses sheep and does not treat them well will come on the Day of Resurrection except that they are more numerous than they ever were, and they will be stationed in a desolate place, butting him with their horns and trampling him with their hooves, without a lame one or a broken-horned one. And no one who possesses wealth and does not fulfill its due will come on the Day of Resurrection except that his wealth will come as a fierce, roaring beast, following him, opening its mouth. And when it reaches him, he will flee from it. Then it will call out to him, ‘Take your treasure that you concealed.’ He will say, ‘I am free from it.’ Then, when he sees that he cannot escape it, he will put his hand into its mouth and it will bite him like the bite of a stallion.” Abu Zubayr said, “I heard ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr say this statement. Then we asked Jabir ibn Abdullah, and he said the same statement as ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr.”

Abu Zubayr said: I heard ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr say: A man said: “O Messenger of Allah, what are the rights of camels?” He said: “To milk them over the water, to lend out their pail, to lend out their stallion, to give them as gifts, and to ride them in the way of Allah.”

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) wrote (a decree) concerning charity, stating: "For every forty female camels, one ram is to be given in charity, up to two hundred. If it exceeds that, then two rams are to be given in charity, up to two hundred. If it exceeds that, then three rams are to be given in charity, up to three hundred. If it increases by one ram, then only three rams are due in charity until it reaches four hundred. If it reaches four hundred sheep, then for every hundred sheep, one ram is to be given. Neither aged sheep, nor those with defects, nor those with blemishes are to be taken for charity.”

Narrated from my father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen along with ‘Amr ibn Hazm: “In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Prophet, to Surhabeel ibn ‘Abd Kulal, and Al-Harith ibn ‘Abd Kulal, and Nua’im ibn ‘Abd Kulal, concerning forty sheep, one sheep for every forty until it reaches two hundred. If it exceeds two hundred by one, then two sheep for every two hundred until it reaches two hundred. If it exceeds by one, then three sheep for every three hundred. And whatever exceeds that, one sheep for every hundred sheep.”

Narrated from Bishr ibn al-Hakam, he said: “We narrated from ‘Abd al-Razaq, who said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ wrote a letter to them, and mentioned a similar wording.

Mu'adh said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me to Yemen and commanded me to take from every forty cows, an old one, and from every thirty, a follower or a female follower."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me to Yemen and commanded me to take from the cattle thirty young cows annually, and forty old cows.
