Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Prophet (ﷺ) wrote down (instructions) regarding the Zakat (obligatory charity), but it was not given to his collectors until the Prophet (ﷺ) passed away. Then Abu Bakr took it and acted according to it after him. When Abu Bakr passed away, ‘Umar took it and acted according to it after them. By Allah, ‘Umar was killed and it was still attached to his sword or his will. And (the instructions) regarding the Zakat of camels contained: "For every five (camels) there is one female sheep; up to twenty-five. If they reach twenty-five, there is a female of the Makhaz breed; up to thirty-five. If there is no female of the Makhaz breed, there is a male of the Labun breed. If they increase, there is a female of the Labun breed; up to forty-five. If they increase, there is a Haqqa; up to sixty. If they increase, there is a Jad’a; up to seventy-five. If they increase, there are two females of the Labun breed; up to ninety. If they increase, there are two Haqqa; up to one hundred and twenty. If they increase, there is one Haqqa for every fifty, and one female of the Labun breed for every forty.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyayna narrated from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan ibn Hussein, from Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), a similar narration.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote with ‘Amr ibn Hazm to Sharhabil ibn ‘Abd Kulal, Al-Harith ibn ‘Abd Kulal, and Naim ibn ‘Abd Kulal: “For every five awaq of silver, five dirhams; and if it exceeds that, for every forty dirhams, one dirham. And there is nothing (due) for less than five awaq.”

Narrated ‘Ali: He transmitted from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: “I have pardoned the sadaqah (charity) of horses and slaves. Bring the sadaqah of silver from every forty dirhams, one dirham, and there is nothing (due) in ninety and one hundred until it reaches two hundred.”

Al-Aswad ibn ‘Amir narrated: “The collector of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to us. I took hold of his hand and read in his covenant: ‘Let not those who are united be separated, and let not those who are divided be brought together, out of fear of the charity.’”
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, when he sent Mu'adh to Yemen, "Beware of the noble possessions of their wealth."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "There is no charity due from the Muslim’s horse nor from his slave."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is no charity in that which is less than five wasq, and no charity in that which is less than five awaq, and no charity in that which is less than five dhawd." Abu Muhammad said: The wasq is sixty sa’s, and the sa’ is two man and a half in the saying of the people of Hijaz, and four amna’ in the saying of the people of Iraq.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no charity from grains or dates for less than five wasq, and no charity from less than five awaq, and no charity from less than five zawd.”

Narrated by Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin ‘Amr bin Hazm from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote with ‘Amr bin Hazm to Sharhabil bin ‘Abd Kullal, and Al-Harith bin ‘Abd Kullal, and Naim bin ‘Abd Kullal: “For every five awaq of silver, there are five dirhams, and no more than that. And for every forty dirhams, there is one dirham, and there is nothing (due) for less than five awaq.”

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Abbas asked the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) to hasten his charity before its due time, and he permitted that for him." Abu Muhammad said: "I follow this, and I do not see any harm in hastening the zakah.
Narrated by Fatima bint Qais: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "There is a right in your wealth other than Zakat."

I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, along with my father and grandfather. He proposed marriage to me and I married him. I argued a case before him, and my father, Yazid, would bring out dinars to give in charity and place them with a man in the mosque. I came and took them, and then brought them to him. He said, “By Allah, I did not intend for you to take them.” So I argued the case with him before the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, and he said, “You, Yazid, have what you intended, and you, Ma’n, have what you took.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Charity is not permissible for a wealthy person nor for a sound, able-bodied person." 

Abu Muhammad said: "Meaning, a strong person."

Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever asks for something over and above what he possesses, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with marks or blemishes or scratches on his face." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wealth?" He said: "Fifty dirhams or their value in gold." 

Abu ‘Aasim and Muhammad ibn Yusuf reported from Sufyan, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd ar-Rahman, from his father, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), with a similar narration.
Narrated Abu Huraira: Hasan took a date from the dates of charity and put it in his mouth. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Spit it out! Do you not know that we do not eat charity?"

I was with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and al-Hasan ibn Ali was with him. The Prophet took a date from the dates of charity and snatched it from him, and said, “Did you not know that charity is not permissible for us?”

Conveyed to me by Saeed ibn Mansur, he narrated to me that Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to me from Amr ibn Dinār, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from his brother, from Mu'awiyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not press me with questions. By Allah, no one will ask me for something and I give it to them while I dislike it, and it will be blessed for them."
"Whoever asks others a question when he is wealthy (or self-sufficient) regarding it, that is a mark of shame on his face."

Some people from the Ansar asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he gave them, and they asked him again, and he gave them, until what was with him ran out. Then he said: "Whatever good is with me, I will not withhold it from you. And whoever shows patience, Allah will grant him independence. And whoever is self-sufficient, Allah will make him self-sufficient. And whoever is patient, Allah will grant him patience. And no gift is given to anyone that is better and more extensive than patience."

Abdullah narrated: I heard Umar saying: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give me the allowance, and I would say, 'Give it to someone more in need than I am.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Take it, and whatever Allah has given you of this wealth while you are not extravagant or a seeker, take it, and if not, do not let your soul pursue it.' "

Al-Hakam bin Naafi’ narrated from Shu’aib bin Abi Hamza from Zuhri, that Sa’ib bin Yazid narrated to me that Huwaitib bin ‘Abd al-‘Uzza informed him that Abdullah bin as-Sa’di informed him from Umar, with a similar narration.

Abu al-Walid narrated, that Layth narrated from Bukair from Busr bin Sa’id from Ibn as-Sa’di, who said: "Umar employed me, and I mentioned something similar to this."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Al-Awza’i, from Ibn Shihab, from Saeed ibn Musayyib, and ‘Urwa ibn Al-Zubayr, that Hakim ibn Hizam said: I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and he gave me, then I asked him and he gave me, then I asked him and he gave me, then I asked him, and he said: “O Hakim! Indeed, this wealth is green and sweet. So whoever takes it with generosity of soul, blessings will be in it for him, and whoever takes it with a covetous soul, no blessings will be in it for him, and it will be like the one who eats but does not feel full.”
Narrated Abu Hurairah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "The best of charity is that which is given from wealth after prosperity, and let one of you begin by supporting his dependents."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "The upper hand is better than the lower hand, and the upper hand is the hand of the giver, and the lower hand is the hand of the receiver."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The best of charity is that given from wealth, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those you support.”
Narrated by Zainab, the wife of Abdullah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “O women, give charity even if it is from your jewelry.”

'Abdullah was a man of modest means. I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, asking him a question, and I found Zaynab, a woman from the Ansar, asking about the same thing. I said to Bilal, "Ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, where should I place my charity: with 'Abdullah or among my relatives?" So Bilal asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, "Which Zaynab?" Bilal said, "The wife of 'Abdullah." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "She has two rewards: the reward of kinship and the reward of charity."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talha, from Anas, who said: Abu Talha was the most wealthy of the Ansar in Medina in terms of date palms, and his most beloved possession was Birhaa, which faced the mosque. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to enter it and drink from its pure water.

Anas said: When the verse was revealed: "You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love..." [Surah Al-Imran 3:92] Abu Talha said: My most beloved possession is Birhaa, and I am making it a charity to Allah, hoping for His acceptance and preservation. So, O Messenger of Allah, dispose of it as you see fit.

The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Blessed is that wealth, profitable or destined for reward. I have heard what you said about it, and I believe it is best to allocate it to your relatives."

Abu Talha said: I will do so, O Messenger of Allah, and he divided it among his relatives.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never addressed us except that he ordered us to give charity and forbade us from mutilation.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me, he said: 'Amru ibn Murra narrated to me, he said: I heard Khaithama from 'Adi ibn Hatim, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who said: "Fear the Fire, even with a piece of date, and if you cannot, then with a kind word."

Abu Lubabah reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased with him, he said: “O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I abandon the home of my people, reside with you, and give a charity from my wealth to Allah and His Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A third is sufficient for you.”

While we were in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, a man came with a gold sphere, which he had found during some campaigns. Ahmad said: "Or in some mines," and that is the correct statement. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, accept it from me as a charity; by Allah, I have no wealth other than this." The Messenger of Allah turned away from him. Then the man came to him from his left side and said the same thing. Then he came before him and said the same thing. Then the Messenger of Allah said, "Bring it here," angrily, and he flung it at him with a throw that would have injured or maimed him had it hit him. Then he said: "One of you takes from his wealth, which he does not have more of, and gives it in charity, and then sits waiting for people to ask him. Charity should only be from surplus wealth; take what is yours, we have no need of it." The man took his wealth and left. Abu Muhammad said: Malik used to say: If a man places his wealth with the poor and gives a third of his property in charity.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, he said: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: I heard 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered us to give charity. I then had some wealth, and I said: Today I will outdo Abu Bakr if I ever outdo him in anything. He (the narrator) said: I came with half of my wealth, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "What did you leave for your family?" I said: Like this (half). He (the Prophet) then came and Abu Bakr brought everything he had. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "O Abu Bakr, what did you leave for your family?" He said: "I left them Allah and His Messenger." Then I said: "I will never outdo you in anything again."

"Narrated by 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ enjoined the Zakat al-Fitr from Ramadan, one sa' of dates or one sa' of barley, on every free person and slave, male or female, among the Muslims." It was said to Abu Muhammad: Do you say this? He said: Malik used to say it.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered Zakat al-Fitr from every small and large person, free person and slave, one sa’ of dates or one sa’ of barley.” Ibn Umar (RA) said: “The people then equated it with two mudds of wheat.”

"We used to pay Zakat al-Fitr during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from every small and large person, free and slave, one sa’ of food, or one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of dried raisins, or one sa’ of wheat. This remained so until Mu’awiya came to Medina as a pilgrim or visitor, and he said: ‘I see two mad of Syrian wheat equal to one sa’ of dates.’ So the people took that as their measure.” Abu Sa’id said: “As for me, I will continue to pay it as I used to pay it.” Abu Muhammad said: “I think one sa’ of everything is sufficient.”

"We used to pay Zakat al-Fitr during Ramadan: one Sa’ of food, or one Sa’ of dates, or one Sa’ of barley, or one Sa’ of raisins, or one Sa’ of dried figs."

We used to give [Zakat al-Fitr] during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he mentioned something similar.

Narrated by ‘Abd ar-Rahman bin Shimasah: I heard ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “The owner of a dye-house will not enter Paradise.” Abu Muhammad said: He means a dyer.

Mu'adh asked, "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me to Yemen, and commanded me to take one-tenth of the produce of irrigated land (baal), and half of the one-tenth of the produce of land irrigated by a water channel (saaniyah)."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "A wound inflicted by an animal with a white spot on its forehead is severe, a well is severe, a mine is severe, and one-fifth of the treasure found belongs to the state."

Abu Hurayrah al-Ansari, then al-Sa’idi, narrated: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a person to collect the Zakat. When the appointed person finished his work, he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, this is what is for you, and this was presented as a gift to me.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Would it not have been better for you to sit in your father’s and mother’s house and see if anything is presented to you?” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up one evening after the prayer on the pulpit, recited the tashahhud, praised Allah with what He deserves, and then said: “After this, should we appoint someone and he comes to us and says: ‘This is from your work, and this was presented as a gift to me?’ Would it not have been better for him to sit in his father’s and mother’s house and see if anything is presented to you?” And by the One whose soul is in my hand, none of you should take anything from it illicitly, but it will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying it: if it is a camel, it will come with its bleating; if it is a cow, it will come with its mooing; if it is a sheep, it will come bleating. I have conveyed [the message].” Abu Hurayrah said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands until we could see the armpits. Abu Hurayrah said: Zayd ibn Thabit heard that with me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so ask him.
"When the tax collector comes to you, let him not depart from you except while he is content."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “O Muslim women, do not belittle your neighbor, even if it is the burnt scraps of a sheep.”

Narrated by Sakhr bin al-‘Ilah: The aunt of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah was taken captive, and she came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). So, the Prophet (peace be upon him) asked about his aunt, and he said: "O Sakhr, when these people embrace Islam, they secure their properties and their lives, so return it to them.”

There was water belonging to the tribe of Banu Sulaim, and they embraced Islam, so they asked for it. The Prophet (peace be upon him) summoned me and said: "O Sakhr, when these people embrace Islam, they secure their properties and their lives, so return it to them.” So, I returned it to them.

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No person gives in charity from (lawful) earnings, and Allah accepts only that which is lawful, except that Allah places it in the Hand of the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman), and Allah fosters it for one of you as he fosters his foal or his mare, until it becomes like Mount Uhud."
"Charity does not diminish wealth, and Allah increases a person’s honor through forgiveness, and no one humbles himself before Allah except that Allah elevates him."

Narrated by Nadr bin Shu’ail, from Bahz bin Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "In every forty camels there is a female camel that produces milk (Laubun). No camels are separated from their reckoning. Whoever gives it (the female camel) as a gift, he will have its reward. And whoever withholds it, then We will take it and half of his wealth. This is a firm decree from Allah, and nothing from it is permissible for the family of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Musaddad and Abu Nu'aim narrated: Hammad bin Zayd narrated to us from Harun bin Ri'ab, that Kinanah bin Nu'aim narrated to me from Qabisah bin Mukharreq al-Hilali, that he said: “I carried a burden and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask him about it. He said: ‘Stand, O Qabisah, until the charity arrives, and then we will order it for you.’ Then he said: ‘O Qabisah, begging is not permissible except for one of three: A man who has undertaken a burden and begging is permissible for him until he obtains it, then he stops. And a man who has been afflicted by a calamity that has swept away his wealth, and begging is permissible for him until he obtains the means of livelihood. And a man who has been afflicted by poverty until three men of understanding from his people say: ‘So-and-so has been afflicted by poverty,’ and begging is permissible for him until he obtains the means of livelihood, then he stops. And whatever is other than these three is a futile pursuit, O Qabisah, and its owner eats it as futile pursuit.’”
Narrated by Hakim bin Hizam: A man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about charity, which is best? He (the Prophet) said: "To a close relative who cuts off ties with you."

Abu Hatim of Basra narrated to me, he said: Ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Hafsa bint Sirin, from Ummu Ar-Raihi bint Sulay’, from Salman ibn ‘Amir Ad-Dubbi, who mentioned that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Giving charity to a poor person is charity, and giving to a relative is two: charity and maintaining the family ties.”

Narrated from Salman ibn ‘Amir ad-Dabbi, who narrated it from the Prophet (peace be upon him): “Charity given to a poor person is a charity, and charity given to a relative is two: a charity and maintaining the family ties.”

We were with ‘Ammar ibn Yasir when a roasted sheep was brought to him. He said, “Eat.” Some of the people withdrew, saying, “I am fasting.” ‘Ammar ibn Yasir said, “Whoever fasts today, the day of doubt, has disobeyed Abu al-Qasim, peace be upon him.”

I awoke one morning in a day that was unclear to me, whether it was from Sha'ban or the month of Ramadan. I happened to be fasting, so I went to Ikrimah, and he was eating bread and vegetables. He said, "Come to breakfast." I said, "I am fasting." He said, "I swear by Allah that you will break your fast." When I saw him swear without exception, I went forward and excused myself, and I had only broken my fast earlier. Then I said, "Give me what you have now." He said, "Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'Fast on sighting it, and break your fast on sighting it. If clouds obscure it from you, then complete thirty days, and do not welcome the month with anticipation.'"

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Ubaydullah, from Malik, from Naf’i’, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, mentioned Ramadan and said: “Do not fast until you sight the crescent moon, and do not break your fast until you sight it. If it is obscured for you, then estimate it.”
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, or Abu Al-Qasim ﷺ said, "Fast on sighting it, and break your fast on sighting it. If the month is obscured from you, then count thirty days."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Sa’id: We were told by Sufyan, from ‘Amr, meaning Ibn Dinār, from Muhammad ibn Jubair, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was astonished at someone who anticipates the month (of Ramadan) and says, "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘If you see it, then fast, and if you see it, then break your fast. If it is obscured from you, then complete the count of thirty days.’”

Narrated by Ibn Umar: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) would, when he saw the new moon, say: “Allah is Most Great. O Allah, bring it to us with security, faith, peace, Islam, and guidance to that which You love and accept. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.”
Narrated by Talha (RA): The Prophet (ﷺ) would, when he saw the new moon, say: "O Allah! Bring it to us with security, faith, peace, and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah."
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not fast one day or two days before Ramadan, except for a man who has been fasting regularly."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The month of Ramadan is twenty-nine (days). Do not fast until you see it, and do not break your fast until you see it. If it is obscured from you, then estimate it."
The people saw the new moon, and I informed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that I had seen it. So he observed the fast and commanded the people to fast.

I was told by ‘Ismah ibn al-Fadl, who said: Hussain al-Ju’fi narrated to me, from Zaidah, from Simak, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a Bedouin came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “I have seen the new moon.” The Prophet said: “Do you bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and that I am His Messenger?” He said: “Yes.” The Prophet said: “O Bilal, announce to the people, and let them fast tomorrow.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: The companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "If a fasting person sleeps before the sunset (and misses the time of Iftar), he should not eat or drink until the night falls.” Qays bin Sarmama Al-Ansari was fasting, and when the time of Iftar approached, he came to his wife and asked, "Do you have any food?” She replied, “No, but I will go and look for it for you.” He was working during the day, and sleep overcame him, and his wife came and when she saw him, she said, "What a disappointment for you!" Then, he fainted at midday. This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and this verse was revealed: “It has been permitted to you to go to your wives on the night of fasting [Ramadan] as a relaxation for yourselves. They are, to you, a garment, and you are to them a garment. Allah knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has forgiven you and pardoned you. So now you may go to them, and seek that which Allah has prescribed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread [i.e., dawn]. Then complete your fast until the night [ends]. And do not have sexual relations with them while you are observing the fast - [it is] a restriction imposed by Allah. Thus does Allah clarify His signs for people that they may become aware.” (Quran 2:187) They rejoiced at this revelation and ate and drank until the white thread became distinct from the black thread.

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have placed a white thread and a black thread under my pillow, but I cannot distinguish between them." He said, "You are wide of the pillow, and that is the night from the day in His statement, ‘And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at dawn, then complete your fast until the night, and do not approach them while you are fasting in the mosques. Those are the limits set by Allah, so do not violate them. Thus does Allah make His verses clear to the people that they may become mindful.” [Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 187]

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "We broke our fast with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and then he stood up for prayer. I said: 'How much was the time between the Adhan (call to prayer) and the Suhur (pre-dawn meal)?' He said: 'The amount of reciting fifty verses.'"
Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Break your fast with the pre-dawn meal, for there is blessing in it."

Abu Qays, the freedman of ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, said: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As used to order us to prepare food for him to break his fast (suhur) with, but he would not eat much of it. We said: "Do you order us to do something and not partake of it yourself?" He replied: “I do not order you to do it because I desire it, but I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: ‘The difference between our fasting and the fasting of the People of the Book is the meal of suhur.’”
"Whoever does not observe the intention for fasting before dawn, then his fast is not valid." Abdullah said, "In obligatory matters, I speak with certainty."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The people will continue to be well as long as they hasten to break their fast.”
Narrated ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the night approaches and the day departs and the sun sets, then you have broken your fast.”
Narrated by Umm Salama: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said, “If any of you breaks his fast, let him break it with dates. If he does not find dates, let him break it with water, for water is purifying.”
One who provides sustenance for a fasting person, for him is recorded a reward equivalent to that of the fasting person, without diminishing anything from the reward of the fasting person.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of wasl (joining)." He repeated this twice. They said: Do you practice wasl? He said: "Indeed, my Lord feeds me and gives me drink."

Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Do not maintain continuous relations (with others).” It was said: “But you do that.” He said: “Indeed, I am like one of you; I am fed and given to drink.”

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Do not practice mutual visiting (i.e., prolonged sitting with each other). And whoever wants to practice it, let him practice it until dawn.” They said: “You too practice it, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Indeed, I have a servant who feeds me and gives me drink.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) forbade the wasl (joining of prayers without break). Some Muslims said to him, “But you join (the prayers).” Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said, “I am not like you; my Lord provides food for me and gives me drink.” When they persisted in doing the wasl, he joined them for a day, then another day. Then they saw the new moon, and he said, “If it had delayed, I would have added (more days).” He said this as a reproach to them when they refused to stop doing the wasl.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwa, from ‘Urwa, from Aisha, that Hamza ibn ‘Amr al-Aslami asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “O Messenger of Allah, I intend to travel. What do you command me?” He said, “If you wish, fast, and if you wish, break your fast.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the year of the Conquest (of Makkah) and people observed fasting. They continued fasting until the heat of the sun became intense. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast, and the people broke their fast too. They would take the new (day) after the new (day) following the practice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”

Hashim ibn al-Qasim and Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: "We were told by Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Anṣari, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn al-Hasan narrating from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who mentioned that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was on a journey and saw a crowd and a man shaded over. He said: "What is this?" They said: "This is a fasting person." So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "It is not from piety to fast while traveling."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is not considered an act of piety to observe fasting while traveling."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "It is not among piety that one fasts while traveling."

Abu Ammya al-Damri said: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from a journey and greeted him. When I was about to leave, he said: "Wait for the lunch, O Abu Ammya." I said: "I am fasting, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Come, I will inform you about the traveler. Indeed, Allah has lifted the obligation of fasting and half of the prayer from him." Abu Muhammad said: If he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break his fast.

I rode with Abu Basra al-Ghifari on a ship from Fustat during Ramadan. The ship lurched, and he brought his lunch closer. Then he said, "Come closer." I said, "Don't you see the houses?" Abu Basra said, "Are you averse to the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him?"

The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever breaks a fast during Ramadan without a valid excuse or illness, then no compensatory fasts for a lifetime, even if he fasts for a lifetime, will atone for it."
"Whoever breaks a fast during Ramadan without a valid excuse, and Allah permits it for him, then the fasts of a lifetime will not compensate for it."

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said, "I have ruined myself!" He said, "What ruined you?" He said, "I had intercourse with my wife in the month of Ramadan." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "Set a slave free." He said, "I do not have one." He said, "Then fast two consecutive months." He said, "I cannot." He said, "Then feed sixty poor people." He said, "I do not find [the means]." Then a jug of dates was brought to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, "Where is the questioner?" He said, "Give charity with this." He said, "Shall I give it to someone poorer than my family, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "By Allah, there is no household between the two lava stones poorer than ours." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "Then you are indeed [fortunate]," and he laughed until his teeth shone.

Another narration: Malik narrated to me from Ibn Shihab, from Humayd ibn Abdur-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah, that a man broke his fast in Ramadan, and he mentioned the same hadith.

A woman from the Ansar, Yahya ibn Sa'id, narrated to me, that Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Zubair narrated to me, that he heard 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Zubair, that he heard Aisha (RA) saying: A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), "Indeed, I was burned (by fire)." He asked him, "What happened?" He said, "I had intercourse with my wife during Ramadan." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a vessel called 'al-'Araq' containing dates. He said, "Where is the one who was burned?" The man stood up and said, "Give charity with this."
Narrated by Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to a woman, "Do not fast except with his permission."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A woman should not observe a voluntary fast on any day other than during Ramadan while her husband is present, except with his permission."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A woman should not fast on a day while her husband is present, except with his permission." He said: [This applies even] in fulfilling vows.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to kiss while fasting." 'Urwa said: "Indeed, she does not call to anything but good."
Aisha narrated: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to kiss me while he was fasting."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Layth ibn Sa’d narrated to me, from Bukayr ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashajj, from Abd al-Malik ibn Sa’id al-Ansari, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: “I was overcome by desire and kissed while fasting. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: ‘I have done a great thing today: I kissed while fasting.’ He said: ‘Have you considered if you were to rinse with water?’ I said: ‘Then it would not harm.’ He said: ‘Then what is the matter?’”
Abu Bakr reported from his father that Um Salama and Aisha informed him that the Prophet (ﷺ) would sometimes wake up in a state of janaba (sexual impurity) and then observe the fast.

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever forgets (and breaks his fast) while fasting, and then eats or drinks, he should complete his fast, for Allah has fed him and given him drink."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you eats or drinks while fasting and forgets (that he is fasting), then he should complete his fast, for Allah has fed him and given him drink." Abu Muhammad said: The people of Hijaz say: "He should make up (the missed fast)." And I say: "He should not make it up."

Abu ad-Darda narrated: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He performed ablution and broke his fast." I met Thawban in the mosque of Damascus and mentioned this to him. He said: "He spoke the truth. I poured water over him for his ablution." Abdullah said: "If he performs ablution…"

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If a vomiter vomits due to an uncontrollable urge and does not intend it, then he is not required to make up (the fast), and if he induces vomiting, then he must make it up." 

‘Isa said: The people of Basra claimed that Hisham was mistaken about it, and the point of disagreement is here.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ‘Asim narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani, from Abu Asma’ al-Rahabi, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: “I passed by with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the eighteenth of Ramadan, and he saw a man being cupped. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘The cupper and the one being cupped have broken their fast.’”

Narrated: Thawban: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was walking in Al-Baqi’, a man came to him who was cupping (performing Hijama). The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The cupper and the one being cupped have broken their fasts.” Abu Muhammad said: I avoid cupping during the fast in Ramadan.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Fasting is a shield, as long as it is not torn." 
Abu Muhammad said: Meaning, [it is torn] by backbiting.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn An-Nu'man, Abu An-Nu'man Al-Anṣārī, narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My grandfather was brought to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he wiped over his head and said: "Do not use kohl during the day while you are fasting, but use it at night with ithmid (a type of kohl), for it clarifies the sight and promotes hair growth." Abu Muhammad said: I do not see any harm in using kohl.

Narrated by Salamah: When the verse, "And [as for] those who are able to afford it – there is a fidyah – feeding of the poor [for] a specified number of days," was revealed, the people would break their fast and offer the fidyah. Then the verse that followed it was revealed, which abrogated it.

Umm Hanī’ reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her while she was fasting. An vessel was brought, and he drank from it, then gave it to her, and she drank. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If it was to fulfill the obligation of Ramaḍān, then fast another day. And if it was voluntary, then if you wish, fulfill it, and if you wish, do not fulfill it.”

Umm Hanī’ reported: When the day of the conquest of Mecca arrived, Fāṭimah came and sat on the left side of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I, Umm Hanī’, sat on his right. She said: A slave girl came with a vessel containing a drink, and she offered it to him (the Prophet ﷺ), and he drank from it, then he offered it to me, and I drank from it. Then she said: O Messenger of Allah, I have broken my fast, and I was fasting. He said to her: “Were you making up for something (missed)? She said: No. He said: “Then it does not harm you if it was voluntary.” Abu Muhammad said: I testify to its authenticity.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If one of you is invited to a meal while he is fasting, he should say, ‘I am fasting.’”

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Hammam narrated to me, from Habib al-Ansari, who said: I heard a female slave of ours, named Layla, relating from her grandmother, Umm ‘Amara bint Ka’b, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) visited her. She invited him for food, and he said to her, "Eat." She said: "I am fasting." So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Indeed, the fasting person, when food is presented to him, the angels pray for blessings upon him until they finish, and sometimes he says: until they complete their eating."

Um Salama reported: "I did not see the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) observe a complete month of fasting except for Sha'ban. He would link it with Ramadan so that it would be two consecutive months. And he would fast from the month until we would say, 'He will not break his fast,' and he would break his fast until we would say, 'He will not fast.'"
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the middle of Sha'ban arrives, refrain from fasting."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, he said: Al-Jariri narrated to me from Abu al-'Ala ibn ash-Shakhir from Mutarrif from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a man: "Did you fast from the latter part of this month?" He said: "No." He said: "If you break your fast from Ramadan, then fast two days." Abu Muhammad said: Its latter part is its end.

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace be upon him) never observed a complete month of fasting other than Ramadan. However, he used to fast occasionally, and when he fasted, people would say, “He will never break his fast,” and when he broke his fast, they would say, “He will never fast again.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from al-Awza’i, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ash-Shakhir, from his father, who said: A man who fasts perpetually was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he said, “He neither fasted nor broke his fast.”

Abu Hurairah said: “My beloved Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed me with three things which I will never abandon: performing Witr prayer, fasting three days of each month, and not neglecting the Fajr (morning) prayer.”

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Mu'awiyah ibn Qarra, from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Fasting on the middle three days of the month is like fasting the whole month."
I asked Jabir: "Did the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbid fasting on the day of Friday?" He said: "Yes, by the Lord of this House."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Busr from his sister, whose name was As-Sammaa, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Do not fast on the Sabbath day except for what is obligatory upon you. And if one of you finds nothing but a few dates or the bark of a tree, let him chew it.”

Narrated: A servant of Qudamah bin Maz’oon said: A servant of Usamah informed him that Usamah used to ride to his property in Wadi Al-Qura and used to observe the fasts on Mondays and Thursdays while on the road. I said to him, "Why do you observe the fasts on Mondays and Thursdays while traveling, and you are old and weak or frail?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to observe the fasts on Mondays and Thursdays, and he said, ‘Indeed, the deeds of people are presented on Mondays and Thursdays.’”

Abu 'Aasim narrated: Muhammad ibn Rifaa'ah narrated to me from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to observe fasts on Mondays and Thursdays. I asked him about this, and he said: "Indeed, the deeds (of people) are presented (before Allah) on Mondays and Thursdays."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him): "The most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dawud (David). He used to fast one day and break his fast one day. And the most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud. He used to pray half of the night, sleep a third of it, and glorify Allah a sixth of it."

Abu Muhammad said: "This last wording is an error or a mistake. Rather, it is that he used to sleep half of the night, pray a third of it, and glorify Allah with a single glorification."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no fasting on two days: the day of al-Fitr and the day of al-Adha.”
"Whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal, then that is a fast of the whole year."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Fasting the month of Ramadan is equivalent to fasting ten months, and fasting six days after them is equivalent to fasting two months, so that completes a year.” He meant the month of Ramadan and six days after it.

Narrated by Nu’man bin Sa’d: A man came to Ali and asked him about a month to fast after the month of Ramadan. Ali said to him, “No one has ever asked me about this after I heard a man ask the Prophet (peace be upon him): Which month should he fast from in the year after Ramadan? The Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered him to fast Muharram and said: “Indeed, Allah forgives a people on a day in it, and He forgives another people on a day in it.”
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The best of fasting after the month of Ramadan is the month of Allah, which you call Muharram."
"The best of fasting after the month of Ramadan is Muharram."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Abbas: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Medina, the Jews were observing the fast of Ashura. He asked them about it, and they said, "It is the day on which Moses was victorious over Pharaoh." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "You are closer to Moses than we are, so observe it."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to fast on the tenth of Muharram, and he would order us to fast it as well."

Abu 'Aasim narrated: From Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubaid, from Salama ibn Al-Akwa', that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) sent a man on the day of 'Ashura (the tenth of Muharram) from Aslam, saying: "Indeed, today is the day of 'Ashura'. So whoever has eaten or drunk, let him complete the remainder of his day. And whoever has not eaten or drunk, let him fast it."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is the day of ‘Ashura’, and the Quraysh used to observe it in the pre-Islamic period. So whoever wishes to observe it, let him observe it, and whoever wishes to leave it, let him leave it.” And Ibn ‘Umar would not observe it unless its fast coincided with his regular fasts.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The people of Quraysh used to observe the fast on the tenth of Muharram in the pre-Islamic period. When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to Medina, he observed it and ordered its observance, until Ramadan was prescribed. Then Ramadan became the obligatory fast, and the fast of ‘Ashura’ was left voluntary; whoever wishes observes it, and whoever wishes leaves it."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Day of ‘Arafah and the days of Tashriq are our Eid, O people of Islam, and they are days of eating and drinking.”

I was informed by Al-Mulla ibn Asad, that Ismail ibn Ulayyah narrated to me, that Ibn Abi Najih narrated from his father, that Ibn Umar was asked about fasting on the Day of Arafah, and he said: "I performed Hajj with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and he did not fast it. I performed Hajj with Abu Bakr and he did not fast it. I performed Hajj with Umar and he did not fast it. I performed Hajj with Uthman and he did not fast it. And I do not fast it, nor do I order anyone to fast it, nor do I forbid anyone from fasting it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him or a man to announce during the days of Tashriq: “No one enters Paradise except a believer, and these are days of eating and drinking.”

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Layth narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Abu Mura, the servant of Aqil, that he and Abdullah ibn Amr entered upon Amr ibn al-Aas. It was the day after Eid or the day following that. Amr presented food to them, and Abdullah said, "I am fasting." Amr said, "Break your fast, for these are the days that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to order us to break our fasts and forbade us from fasting them." So Abdullah broke his fast and ate, and I ate with him.

Sahal ibn Hammad narrated: “Tell me, Shu’bah narrated to me from Abu Bishr, from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that a woman vowed to fast, and then she died. Her brother came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about that. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: “If she had a debt, would you pay it?” He said: “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Then pay [the vow] to Allah, for Allah is more deserving of fulfillment.” So he fasted on her behalf.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The breath of the fasting person is more pleasing to Allah than the scent of musk, and the fasting person has two joys: a joy at breaking his fast, and a joy on the Day of Resurrection."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Allah the Exalted says: Every action of the son of Adam is for him, [i.e., multiplied in reward]. A good deed receives ten times its reward up to seven hundred times, except for fasting. Fasting is for Me, and I reward it. For he leaves food and desire for My sake, and he leaves drink and desire for My sake. So it is for Me, and I reward it.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Fasting is a shield."

Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would say when breaking his fast amongst people: “The fasting have broken their fast with you, and the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels have descended upon you.”

"No work is superior to that which is done in the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah." It was said, "Not even Jihad in the way of Allah?" He said, "Not even Jihad in the way of Allah, except for one who sets out with his person and his property and does not return with either."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Asbagh, from Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Saeed, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who said: "There is no deed greater with Allah, or with a more abundant reward, than a good deed done in the ten days of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha)."

It was said: "Is not Jihad in the way of Allah greater?"

He (the Prophet) said: "Not unless a man sets out with his person and his wealth and returns from it with nothing."

Saeed ibn Jubair would, when the ten days (of Dhul Hijjah) arrived, exert himself with intense effort, to the point that he could scarcely endure it.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained."
"Whoever spends Ramadan in faith and seeking (reward), all his past sins will be forgiven, and whoever spends the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) in devotion, all his past sins will be forgiven."

We fasted with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during the month of Ramadan. He did not stand with us during the month until seven nights remained. He then stood with us until a third of the night had passed. When it was the sixth [night], he did not stand with us. When it was the fifth [night], he stood with us until the latter half of the night had passed. We said, "O Messenger of Allah, grant us the remaining portion of this night [as a voluntary prayer]." He said, "Indeed, a man who stands with the Imam until he finishes his prayer has his night prayer counted for him." When it was the fourth [night], he did not stand with us. When it was the third [night], he gathered his family, his women, and the people, and he stood with us until we feared missing out on success. We said, "What is success?" He said, "The pre-dawn meal (suhur)." Then he did not stand with us for the remainder of the month.

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe ‘itikaf (seclusion in the mosque for worship) during the last ten nights of Ramadan. But in the year in which he died, he observed ‘itikaf for twenty days.

Safiyyah bint Huyayy informed me, that she came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to visit him during his seclusion (i'tikaf) in the mosque, in the last ten nights of Ramadan, and she spoke with him for a while, then she left.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Humayd narrated to me from Anas, from ‘Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us intending to inform us of the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). Then two men from among the Muslims began to quarrel. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I came out to you intending to inform you of the Night of Power, but a dispute arose between so-and-so and so-and-so, which was removed. Perhaps this is for the best. So seek it in the last ten nights: on the fifth, seventh, and ninth.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was shown the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), and then some of my family awakened me, so I forgot it. Therefore, I seek it during the last ten nights."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Seek the Night of Power in the last seven nights (of Ramadan)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever intends to perform Hajj, let him hasten."

Narrated Abu Umama: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is not prevented from performing Hajj by an unavoidable necessity, or an unjust ruler, or an illness that confines him, and he dies without performing Hajj, then let him die as he wishes – whether a Jew or a Christian."

Narrated by Mujahid bin Musa: Yahya bin Adam told us, and he said: Zuhair narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Zayd bin Arqam saying: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) performed Hajj after his Hijra."
Abu Ishaq said: "He [meaning Umar ibn al-Khattab] performed Hajj before his Hijrah."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Hammam narrated to me, he said: Qatadah said: I said to Anas: How many Hajj’s did the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) perform? He said: “One Hajj, and four Umrahs: his first Umrah when the polytheists prevented him from the House, his second Umrah when they made peace with him and he returned the following year, his Umrah from Ji’ranah when he distributed the spoils of Hunayn in Dhul-Qi’dah, and his Umrah with his Hajj.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said: “The Hajj has been enjoined upon you.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, every year?” He said, “No, and if I had said it, it would have become obligatory. Hajj once is sufficient, and whatever exceeds that is voluntary.”

Narrated by Ibn Umar: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Dhu al-Halifa for the people of Medina, Al-Juhfa for the people of Syria, and Qarn for the people of Najd.” He said: Ibn Umar said: “As for these three, I heard them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it reached me that he appointed Yalamlam for the people of Yemen.”

Narrated by Muslim bin Ibrahim, who said: Abu Taous narrated to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) appointed Dhu al-Halifa for the people of Medina, Al-Juhfa for the people of Syria, Qarn al-Manazil for the people of Najd, and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. These are for their people, and for every arrival who comes to them from outside their people, intending to perform Hajj or Umrah, or less than that. Then from wherever he originates, even the people of Mecca from Mecca.

Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Ibn Abbas disputed regarding the washing of the head of a pilgrim. So, they sent me to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, asking: "How did you see the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wash his head while he was in ihram?" I went to Abu Ayyub, and he was between the two horns of a well, and a garment had been drawn over him. I greeted him, and he pulled the garment closer to him. I said: "Your nephew, Ibn Abbas, sent me to you, asking: How did you see the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wash his head?" He then passed his hands over his head, facing forward and backward.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) disrobed for the ritual of ihram and performed ablution.
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "An accepted Hajj has no reward other than Paradise, and two Umrahs expiate whatever sins are committed between them."

Narrated Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever performs Hajj and does not indulge in lewdness or commit any unlawful act, he returns as his mother bore him."

Narrated Abu Bakr: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) being asked: "Which Hajj is best?" He said: "Al-'Ajju and ath-Thajju." Al-'Ajju means reciting the Talbiyah, and ath-Thajju means sacrificing (the animal)."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Yahya, who is Ibn Sa’id, narrated to me, from ‘Umar ibn Nafi’, from his father, from Ibn ‘Umar, that a man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): “What garments should we wear when we are in Ihram?” He (the Prophet) said: “Do not wear Qumis (tunic), nor Sirawilat (trousers), nor ‘Amā’im (turbans), nor Barānis (cloaks), nor Khiffāf (soft shoes), unless one does not have sandals; then he should wear Khuffain (shoe coverings) and place them below the ankles. And do not wear any garment that has been touched by war (dye) or saffron.”

Abu Sha'tha' reported: Ibn Abbas informed me that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Whoever does not find an izar (lower garment), let him wear sarawil (trousers), and whoever does not find sandals, let him wear khuffs (socks)." He said: I said or it was said: Should he cut them (the khuffs)? He said: "No."

Narrated by Ibn Umar: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about what an intending pilgrim (muhrim) should wear. He said: "He should not wear qamus (a type of shirt), nor ‘amā’im (turbans), nor siraawilat (trousers), nor barānis (a type of cloak), nor khiffāf (soft leather socks). Unless he does not find shoes; then he should wear khuffain (two socks) and cut them below the ankles."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I used to scent the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) before he would perform Ihram with the finest of perfumes." 'Urwa would say to us, "Perfume yourselves before you perform Ihram and before you leave (Mina) on the Day of Nahr."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I used to scent the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) during his state of ihram with the best of what I could find."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I perfumed the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) for his intimacy, and I perfumed him at Mina before he departed."
‘Aisha (RA) said: Asma bint Abu Bakr gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr at Ash-Shajara. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Abu Bakr to “bathe her and pronounce the declaration of Islam.”

Uthman ibn Muhammad narrated to me, that Jarir narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa’id, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir, concerning the story of Asma’ bint ‘Umays, when she menstruated at Dhul-Halifa. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Abu Bakr to order her to “bathe and proclaim [her declaration of purity].”
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Avoid sitting idly after the prayer.”
Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed 'Ihram' and 'Hal' in the rear of the prayer.

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to say, when saying "Labbaik," "Labbaik, O Allah, Labbaik, Labbaik, there is no partner with You. Labbaik, indeed all praise, blessings, and sovereignty are Yours, and there is no partner with You."
Yahyā said, and Nāfiʿ mentioned that Ibn ‘Umar would add these words: “Labbaik (Here I am, O Lord), and the longing (towards You), and the action; Labbaik, Labbaik.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Gabriel came to me and said: Instruct your companions or those with you to raise their voices [in reciting] the talbiyah or the ihlal.”

Dhuba’a, the daughter of al-Zubayr ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I want to perform Hajj, so what should I say?” He said: “Say: ‘Labbaik Allahumma labbaik, and my station is where You detain me.’ Indeed, you have a right upon your Lord for whatever you stipulate.”
Narrated by Aisha (RA) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I have singled out the Hajj."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Abu Hilal narrated to me, Qatadah narrated to me, from Mutarrif, who said: Imran ibn Husayn said: “I relate to you a hadith, perhaps Allah will benefit you by it later. I used to be greeted, and Ibn Ziyad ordered me [to do something], so I cauterized [myself]. I was withheld [from something] until the effect of the cauterization disappeared. And know that ‘temporary marriage’ is permissible in the Book of Allah, no Prophet forbade it, and no revelation came down concerning it.” A man then spoke based on his own opinion, whatever occurred to him.

Narrated by Muhammad bin ‘Abdullah bin Nawfal: I heard ‘Amr bin Shu’aib asking Sa’d bin Malik during the year when Mu’awiya performed Hajj: “How do you say that combining ‘Umra with Hajj is permissible?” Sa’d replied, “It is a good and beautiful thing.” Mu’awiya said, “‘Umar forbade it.” Sa’d replied, “‘Umar was better than you, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) did it, and he is better than ‘Umar.”

I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was halting at al-Batḥā’ during Hajj. He said to me, "Have you performed the pilgrimage?" I said, "Yes." He said, "How did you pronounce the declaration (of ihram)?" I said, "I said, 'Labbaik with a declaration like the declaration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" He said, "You have done well, go and circumambulate the House, and Safa and Marwa, then return (to your lodging)." I circumambulated the House, and Safa and Marwa, and then I came to a woman from the women of Banu Kays, and she began to clip my head, so I began to give legal opinions to the people about that. A man said to me, "O Abdullah ibn Qays, restrain some of your legal opinions, for you do not know what the Commander of the Believers has innovated in the ritual after you." I said, "O people, whoever we have given a legal opinion to, let him be cautious, for the Commander of the Believers is coming to you, so obey him in this matter." When he arrived, I came to him and mentioned this to him. He said, "If we take according to the Book of Allah, then the Book of Allah orders completion. And if we take according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not return (to his lodging) until the sacrificial animal reached its place."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There are five things in which it is permissible to kill: the crow, the rat, the viper, the scorpion, and the mad dog.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered that five types of animals be killed in both the sacred and profane land: the lizard, the crow, the mouse, the scorpion, and the mad dog.” Abdullah said: “The mad dog.” And some of them said: “The black dog.” Abdur-Razzaq reported that some of his companions said that Ma’mar used to mention it from Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, and from Urwa, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed hijama while in ihram.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ underwent cupping while in a state of ritual impurity (ihram).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ underwent cupping while in a state of ritual impurity (ihram).
Narrated by 'Abbas: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) married while in Ihram."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Naafi’, from Nubayh ibn Wahb: That a man from Quraysh requested marriage from Aban ibn ‘Utman while he was the governor of Al-Mawsim. Aban said: “I do not see him as anything other than a dry Iraqi; indeed, the one in Ihram does not marry nor is he married.” ‘Utman informed me about this from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). Abu Muhammad was asked: Do you say this? He said: Yes.
Maymunah said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, married me while we were both lawful (divorced) after his return from Mecca with Sirf."
Abu Rafia reported: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, married Maymuna in a lawful manner, and he resided with her in a lawful manner, and I was the messenger between them.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, on the authority of Hisham al-Dustawa’i, from Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, who said: My father accompanied the Prophet (ﷺ) during the year of Hudaibiya. His companions became pilgrims, but my father, Abi Qatadah, did not. He killed a wild donkey, and ate of its meat. I said: "O Messenger of Allah! I killed a wild donkey." He said to the people: "Eat," and they were pilgrims.

Narrated by Abu Al-Walid: He narrated to me, Shaybah narrated to me, from Uthman bin Abdullah bin Mahbub, from Abdullah bin Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: While we were traveling with them as pilgrims, and Abu Qatadah was not, I saw a donkey, so I mounted a horse and struck it, and they ate from its meat while in ihram, and I did not eat. Then they came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and asked him about it. He said, "Did you point (at it) and kill (it)? Or did he say, 'Did you strike it?'" They said, "No." He said, "Then eat."
Narrated by As-Sa’b bin Jaththama: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was brought some meat of a wild ass, and he rejected it, saying: “It is forbidden game, and we do not eat game.”

We were with Talha ibn Ubaidullah on a journey, and fowl was presented to him while they were in ihram and he was asleep. Some of us ate, and some of us refrained. When Talha awoke and was informed, he approved of those who had eaten, and said: “We ate it with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: Sa’b bin Jaththama said, “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was in Al-Abwa’ or Waddan. I presented to him the meat of a wild ass, but he returned it to me. When he saw the displeasure on my face, he said, ‘It is not because we dislike it being returned to you, but it is forbidden.’”

Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi narrated to me, he said: Zuhayr narrated to me, from Ma’mar, from Zuhri, from Suleyman ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas, from al-Fadl ibn Abbas, that he used to ride behind the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) during the Farewell Pilgrimage. A woman came from Khu’tham and said: “The obligation of Allah upon His servants regarding the pilgrimage has overtaken my father, an elderly man who cannot control himself on his mount, and he has not performed the pilgrimage. Can I perform it on his behalf?” He (the Prophet) said: “Yes.”

Abu Muhammad was asked: Do you say this? He said: Yes.

Narrated by Abu 'Aasim, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Shihab, from Sulaiman ibn Yasir, from Ibn Abbas, that al-Fadhl – who is Ibn Abbas – said that a woman asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said, "My father is an old man who cannot mount a camel. He has reached the age when Allah’s obligation (of Hajj) has become due upon him.” So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Perform Hajj on his behalf.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: A woman from the Banu Khath’am asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) during the Hajj of Farewell, and al-Fadl ibn ‘Abbas was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). She said: “O Messenger of Allah, Allah’s obligation upon His servants has overtaken my father as an old, elderly man who cannot mount an animal. Can I fulfill the pilgrimage on his behalf?” He said: “Yes.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, my father or mother is an old, feeble person. If I carry her, she will not be able to hold on, and if I tie her, I fear I will harm her.” The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, “Do you think if your father or mother had a debt, would you pay it?” He said, “Yes.” The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, “Then defend your father or mother.”

Narrated Abdullah ibn Zubair: A man from Khati'am came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "My father embraced Islam when he was an old man and could not travel, and Hajj is obligatory upon him. Shall I perform Hajj on his behalf?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Are you his eldest son?" He said, "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "If your father had a debt, and you paid it off for him, would that suffice for him?" He said, "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Then perform Hajj on his behalf."

Salidah ibn Abdullah narrated: Abdullah al-Aziz, who is the son of Abdus-Samad, narrated to me from Mansur, from Mujahid, from a servant of Ibn az-Zubayr, whose name is Yusuf ibn az-Zubayr or az-Zubayr ibn Yusuf, from Sawdah bint Zam’ah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "My father is an old man and he cannot perform Hajj." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you think if your father had a debt, and you paid it off for him, would it be accepted from him?" He said: "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more Merciful, perform Hajj for your father."

Musaddad narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to me, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Nafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “I have not left off touching these two pillars in hardship or ease since I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, touching them.” I asked Nafi’: “Did Ibn ‘Umar walk between the two pillars?” He said: “He only walked so it would be easier for him to touch them.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will send forth a stone on the Day of Resurrection, having eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, bearing witness against whoever grasped it rightfully.” Sulaiman said: “Against whom will it bear witness?”
Narrated Jabir: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) paced from one stone to another three paces.

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Sa’id, ‘Uqba ibn Khalid, ‘Ubaidullah, and Naafi’ from Ibn ‘Umar: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he performed the first round of the House (Ka’bah), would walk four steps and run three steps. And he would hasten in the Sa’i (running between Safa and Marwa) in the belly of the valley.

I asked Naafi’: Did ‘Abdullah (Ibn ‘Umar) walk when he reached the Yemeni corner? He said: No, unless there was a crowd on the corner; for he would not leave it until he touched it.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ran from the stone to the stone three times and walked four times.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “He was struck while stumbling.”

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever performs Hajj and ‘Umrah, one Tawaf is sufficient for both, and he does not become lawful until he has discharged himself from them.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Tawaf (circumambulation) of the Ka’bah riding a camel. Whenever he reached a pillar, he would point towards it with something in his hand and say, “Allahu Akbar.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I came to Mecca while menstruating and did not perform the sa’i between Safa and Marwa. I complained about this to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he said: 'Do everything that the pilgrim does, except that you do not circumambulate the House.'"

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The circumambulation of the House (Ka'bah) is prayer, except that Allah has permitted speech within it. So whoever speaks, let him not speak except with good."

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I have coincided with my Lord in three matters. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, if you were to take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer,' and Allah the Exalted revealed: '#And take from the Station of Abraham a place of prayer.' [Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 125]#"

Zayd b. ʿAwf > Abū ʿAwānah > ʿAbd al-Malik b. ʿUmayr > Muḥammad b. al-Muntashir > Ḥumayd b. ʿAbd al-Raḥman > Abū Hurayrah “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: ‘Which fasting is better after the month of Ramadan?’ He said: ‘The month of Allah which is called Muharram.’” (Using translation from Ibn Mājah 1742)

While a man was standing with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) at ‘Arafah, his camel stumbled, or it bucked him off, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Wash him with water and lote tree leaves, shroud him in two garments, do not apply perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for Allah, the Exalted, will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection proclaiming [the talbiyah].”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Indeed, the circumambulation of the House, the stoning of the Jamarat, and the running between Safa and Marwa were instituted to establish remembrance of Allah." Abu ‘Aasim said: He would raise it [the chain of narration].

Abu Nu’aim and Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated from Sufyan, from ‘Ubaidullah ibn Abi Ziyad, from Al-Qasim, from Aisha, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), with a similar wording.
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, is the cancellation [of certain rituals] of Hajj exclusively for us, or for those who come after us?" He said, "Rather, it is exclusively for us."

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "This is 'Umrah which we have enjoyed. So whoever has not with him a sacrificial animal (for Hajj), let him release himself to all that is permissible, for 'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Resurrection."

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, on the authority of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Rabi' ibn Sabra, that his father narrated to him: That they traveled with the Prophet (ﷺ) until they reached 'Usfan. A man from Banu Mudlij, named Malik ibn Surqa or Surqa ibn Malik, said to him: "Judge for us the judgment of a people born today." He (the Prophet) said: "Verily, Allah has entered into your pilgrimage this 'Umra. So, when you arrive, whoever performs the Tawaf of the House, and of Safa and Marwa, he has discharged [his obligation], except one who has a sacrificial animal with him."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed four ‘umras: the ‘Umra of al-Hudaybiyyah, the ‘Umra of Qada’ (or, as Shihab ibn ‘Abbad was unsure, the ‘Umra of Qisas), the third from al-Ji’ranah, and the fourth which was with his Hajj.

Narrated by Abu 'Aasim, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ataa, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a woman: "Perform 'Umrah during Ramadan, for an 'Umrah in Ramadan is equivalent to a Hajj."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “An ‘Umrah performed in Ramadan is equivalent to a Hajj.”

Narrated by Muzhim bin Abi Muzhim from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz bin ‘Abdullah from Muharish al-Ka’bi that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out from al-Ji’ranah when he intended to perform ‘Umrah. He entered Mecca at night, performed his ‘Umrah, and then left before the night ended, and he was found in al-Ji’ranah at dawn, exhausted.

Sadqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to me, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, from ‘Amru, that he heard ‘Amru ibn Aws say: “Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered me to equip Aisha and to provide her with comfort and enjoyment.” Sufyan said: Shu’bah liked a chain of narration like this one.

Narrated by Hafsa bint Abdurrahman bin Abi Bakr: Her father said, “The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abdurrahman bin Abi Bakr: ‘Ride with your sister (meaning Aisha) and give her enjoyment (of travel). And when you dismount from Al-Akama, order her to perform ‘ihram’, for it will be an accepted ‘umrah.’”
Umar said, "I kiss you, and indeed I know that you are a stone, but I have seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, kiss you."

Abu 'Aasim narrated: Ja'far ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utman said: I saw Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far "touching the Black Stone, then kissing it, and prostrating upon it." I asked him, "What is this?" He said: "I saw my uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, doing this." Then he said: "I saw 'Umar doing this." Then he said: "I know that you are a stone, but I have seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, doing this."

Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) entered Makkah, and Usaamah ibn Zayd was his mount. He halted at the base of the Ka’abah. The people rushed, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), Bilal, and Usaamah entered. I said to Bilal behind the door, ‘Where did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) pray?’ He said, ‘Between the two Maqams.’”

Ahmed ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated: Layth narrated to me from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) entered the House with Usaamah ibn Zayd, Bilal, and Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi. He then mentioned a similar account.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to me, "Had it not been for the recent association of your people with disbelief, I would have demolished the Ka’bah and rebuilt it upon the foundations of Abraham. Indeed, when the Quraysh built it, they did not complete it, and then they added to it behind."

Aisha (RA) said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Black Stone, “Is it from the House (Ka’bah)?” He said, “Yes.” I said, “Then why was it not included in the House?” He said, “Your people were impoverished.” I said, “Then what about its door being raised?” He said, “Your people did that so they could admit whoever they wished and prevent whoever they wished. And were it not that your people are newly emerged from the period of ignorance and I feared that their hearts would reject it, I would have moved the Black Stone and made it part of the House and fixed its door to the ground.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas saying: "Al-Tahseeb is nothing; it is merely a place where the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stayed." Abu Muhammad said: Al-Tahseeb is a place in Mecca, and it is a place in Batn al-Wadi.
Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed five prayers in Mina.

I asked Anas ibn Malik, "Recite to me something you have understood from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him: Where did he pray the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Tarwiya?" He said, "In Mina." I said, "And where did he pray the Asr prayer on the Day of Nahr?" He said, "At al-Abṭaḥ." Then he said, "Do as your leaders do."
Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered the Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha prayers, and then slept for a nap at Mina. Afterwards, he rode towards the Ka’bah and circled it.

Abdullah ibn Yazid said: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) prayed four rak'ahs with 'Uthman in Mina and said: "I certainly prayed with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in this place two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs; and with Abu Bakr, two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs; and with Umar, two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs. Then the ways parted amongst you. May my share of these four rak'ahs be two accepted rak'ahs."

Narrated by Salim from his father that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman (may Allah be pleased with them all) prayed two rak'ahs in Mina at the beginning of Uthman's caliphate, and then he completed [praying] them afterward.
