Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: We accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Mina, and some of us were reciting Takbir and some were reciting Labbaik.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Malik narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr ath-Thaqafi said: I asked Anas ibn Malik while we were traveling from Mina to Arafat about the utterance of the talbiyah: How did you do with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him? He said: "One would utter the talbiyah, and he would not be rebuked for it, and one would say Takbir, and he would not be rebuked for it."

Jabir narrated: "I lost a camel of mine, so I went searching for it. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing with the people at ‘Arafah. I said: ‘By Allah, this is surely a misfortune! What business has he here?’”

Narrated by Jabir: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) shot an arrow, then he sat for the people. A man came and said, “O Messenger of Allah! I shaved my head before slaughtering (the sacrificial animal).” He (the Prophet) said, “No harm.”

Then another came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, did I circumambulate before I prayed?" He said: "There is no harm." He said: "So I asked him about anything, and he said: 'There is no harm.'"

Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Every place in ‘Arafah is a standing place, and every place in Muzdalifah is a standing place, and Mina is all a place of slaughter, and every valley of Makkah is a way and a place of slaughter.”

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, Hisham ibn Urwa narrated to me from his father, from Usama ibn Zayd, that he used to ride behind the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), "and he would leave 'Arafa, and he would move the neck (of the camel) quickly, and whenever he passed a valley, he would say, 'Ayyuhā al-ḥajar'."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Zuhayr narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn ‘Uqba, who said: Kuraib informed me that he asked Usama ibn Zayd, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, on the evening I rode behind him: “How did you do or act?” He said: “We came to the valley where people halt for the night, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, halted his camel. Then he relieved himself, and he did not say, ‘I poured out the water,’ then he called for purification and performed ablution, not a very thorough one. Then I said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, the prayer?’ He said: ‘The prayer is before you.’ He then rode until we reached Mina, and he stayed for Maghrib. Then he halted, and the people were in their dwellings, and they did not leave until he stayed for the last ‘Isha’ prayer, and he prayed, then the people left.” He said: I said: “Tell me how you did when you became morning?” He said: “Al-Fadl ibn ‘Abbas rode behind him, and I went in the race of Quraysh on foot.” Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn ‘Uqba narrated to me from Kuraib ibn Abi Muslim from Usama, with a similar narration.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: 'Addiyy ibn Thabit informed me, saying: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Yazid from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, combined the Maghrib and 'Isha'.

Narrated by Salim from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed the Maghrib and Isha prayers at Muzdalifah, and he did not announce in either of them except with the Iqama, and he did not recite any supplications between them, nor after either of them.

Abu 'Aasim narrated to me from Ibn Jurayj from 'Ata from Ibn Shawwal: He informed me that Um Habibah informed him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered her to depart from a gathering at night.

Aisha (RA) reported: "Sawda bint Zam'a requested permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be allowed to precede [others] before they are allowed, and he gave her permission."

Qasim said: "She was a woman of heavy gait." Qasim said: "By 'heavy gait' is meant a woman who is slow and deliberate." She then preceded [others], and we were detained with him until we were allowed to proceed with her proceeding.
Aisha (RA) said: "I would prefer to seek permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as Sawda did, and then proceed before the people, to being delighted with it."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: Bukayr ibn 'Ata' said: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mur al-Dili say: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was asked about Hajj, and he said: "Hajj is 'Arafat," or he said: "'Arafat," and whoever spends the night of Jumu'ah before Fajr has completed it."

He (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: “The days of Mina are three days. So, whoever concludes (the stoning of Jamarat) in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him.”

Yala narrated: Isma'il narrated to me, from Amir, from Urwa bin Mudarris, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was standing on the heads of the people and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I have come from the mountains of Tayy, having exhausted my mount and fatigued myself. By Allah, if there remains any mountain, I will stand upon it. Can I perform Hajj?" He ﷺ said: "Whoever witnesses this prayer with us and has come to Arafat before that, whether at night or during the day, then he has fulfilled his obligation and his Hajj is complete."

Abu al-Walid narrated: Shu'ba narrated to me, from Abdullah bin Abi Saffar, from Al-Sha'bi, from Urwa bin Mudarris bin Haritha bin Lam, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and mentioned a similar account.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) said: "The people of pre-Islamic times would disperse from their gatherings after the sun had risen, and they would say, 'Let Thabir shine so that we may raid.' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) differed with them, and he advanced before sunrise by the time of the morning prayer of those who hasten (or those who rise early)."

Narrated Abu Az-Zubair: Abu Ma’bad, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, informed me that Ibn Abbas informed me from Al-Fadl that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said on the night of 'Arafah and the morning of Eid, as they set off, "Bestow peace upon yourselves," and he was restraining his camel until he entered Wadi Muhassir, whereupon he let it go.

Ahmed bin Abdullah narrated: Layth narrated to me from Abu Az-Zubair with a similar chain of narrators.

Abdullah said: “Iydha’ (letting go) is for camels, and Iyjaf (letting go) is for horses.”

Abdullah ibn Sa’id narrated: We were told by Abu Usama, from ‘Ubaidullah, from Nafi’, that Abdullah ibn ‘Abdullah and Salim spoke to Ibn ‘Umar on the nights when al-Hajjaj lodged with Ibn al-Zubayr, before he was killed. They said: “It does not harm you if you do not perform Hajj this year, for we fear that you will be prevented from reaching the House [Ka’aba].” He said: “We set out with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, intending ‘Umrah. Then the disbelievers of Quraysh blocked the way to the House. So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, slaughtered his sacrificial animals and shaved his head, then returned. I bear witness to you that I have obligated an ‘Umrah. If I am allowed to reach the House, I will perform the circumambulation [Tawaf], and if I am prevented from reaching it, I will do as the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did with me while I was with him.” He then performed the Ihram of ‘Umrah from Dhu al-Hulaifa, and set out. He said: “Their affairs are one.” He bore witness to them that he had obligated Hajj along with his ‘Umrah. Nafi’ said: He performed one Tawaf for them and one Sa’i for them. He did not become free [from the state of Ihram] until the Day of Nahr [Eid al-Adha] arrived, when he sacrificed [an animal]. He used to say: “Whoever combines ‘Umrah and Hajj should perform the Ihram for both together, and should not become free from them until he is free from both of them on the Day of Nahr.”
"Whoever has a bone broken or is afflicted with a limp, then he is excused [from fulfilling previous obligations], and he has another pilgrimage due upon him."
Narrated by Jabir: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw at the Jamrah on the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha) in the forenoon, and after that, when the sun began to decline.

Narrated by Abu Al-Badaa’s father: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted shepherds of camels to throw stones on the Day of Nahr, then the next day, and after the next day for two days, and then to throw stones on the day of departure. 

Abu Muhammad said: Some of them say: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from Abu Al-Badaa’.

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Uthman ibn Murra narrated to me from Abu Salama ibn Abdur-Rahman, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Uthman at-Taymi, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, to throw stones at Jamrat al-’Aqaba with pebbles like the pebbles of Khazf.”
Narrated by Jabir: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them to throw stones like the pebbles of Khadif, and he placed them in Wadi Muhassir, and said: "Maintain tranquility."

Narrated by 'Abd ar-Rahman bin Mu'adh that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to order us to "throw the pebbles at Jamarat with pebbles like the pebbles of al-Khazf."

It was said to Abu Muhammad: Does 'Abd ar-Rahman bin Mu'adh have companionship (Sahaba status)? He said: Yes.

Abu 'Aasim, Al-Mu'ammal, and Abu Naim narrated to me on the authority of Ayman bin Nabil, from Qudamah bin Abdullah bin Ammar Al-Kilabi, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ throwing stones at a white she-camel, and there was neither striking nor driving it away, nor saying 'to the right' or 'to the left'."
Narrated Abdullah ibn Abbas: Al-Fadhl said, "I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and he kept saying ‘Labbaik, Allahumma Labbaik’ until he threw the pebbles at Jamrat."

Narrated ‘Utman bin ‘Umar: Yunus narrated to me from Zuhri that Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) used to, when he threw at the Jamrah which is next to the Masjid of Mina, throw at it with seven stones, saying “Allahu Akbar” with each stone. Then he would advance forward and stand before it, facing the Qiblah, raising his hands, and he used to prolong the standing. Then he would come to the second Jamrah and throw at it with seven stones, saying “Allahu Akbar” each time he threw a stone. Then he would descend from the left side of the valley, raising his hands, invoking (Allah). Then he would come to the Jamrah of ‘Aqabah and throw at it with seven stones, saying “Allahu Akbar” each time he threw a stone, and then he would turn back and not stand at it. Zuhri said: I heard Salim bin ‘Abdullah narrating this Hadith from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ). He (the Prophet) said: “And ‘Abdullah bin ‘Umar used to do so.”

Aisha (RA) said: “We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioning nothing but the Hajj. When we reached Sirf, I began to menstruate. Then, when the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha) arrived, I became pure. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me, and I proceeded (to Mina). A cow was brought to me, and I said, ‘What is this?’ They said, ‘The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sacrificed the cow on behalf of his wives.’”

Ali ibn Abdullah al-Madini narrated to me, he said: Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, he said: Abdul Hamid ibn Jubayr informed me, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: Ummu Uthman, daughter of Abu Sufyan, informed me that Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is not permissible for women to have their hair completely shaved; rather, women should have their hair trimmed."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Allah have mercy upon the trimmers (of hair).” It was said, “And those who trim a little?” He said, “Allah have mercy upon the trimmers.” He said in the fourth instance, “And those who trim a little.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz, who is Ibn Abi Salama al-Majshun, narrated to me from Zuhri, from Isa ibn Talha, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Jamrah, while he was being asked questions. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have sacrificed before I have stoned [the Jamrah]?" He said: "Stone, and there is no harm."

Another said: "O Messenger of Allah, I shaved my head before I sacrificed [the animal]?" He said: "Sacrifice, and there is no harm." He said: "He was not asked about anything that was brought forward or delayed except that he said, 'Do it and there is no harm.'"

Musaddad narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to me, saying: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, saying: Zuhri narrated to me, from Isa ibn Talha, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood before the people during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and a man said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I have shaved my head before sacrificing?" He said: "There is no harm."

He said, "I felt no awareness; I slaughtered before I shot [the arrow]." He said, "No harm." On that day, he was not asked about anything that was presented or postponed except that he said, "No harm." Abdullah said, "I say this, and the people of Kufa are strict about it."

I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What should I do with a defective animal from the sacrificial animals?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Slaughter it, then throw its shoe into its blood, then let it be separated from the people, and let them eat it.”
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was once presented with some sheep as a gift."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Abu Hassan relating, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed the Dhuhr prayer at Dhul Halifah. Then he called for a sacrificial animal, and he shaved a portion from the right side of its hump. Then he licked the blood from it and put sandals on it. Then his riding animal was brought to him. When he mounted it and it stabilized on the open plain, he proclaimed, "Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik" for Hajj.

Abu Nadr, Hashim ibn al-Qasim, narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Qatadah informed me, saying: I heard someone narrating, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that he approached a man driving a cow, and said, "Mount it." He said, "It is a cow." He said, "Mount it." He said, "It is a cow." He said, "Mount it, by Allah!"

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Yunus ibn ‘Ubaid, from Ziyad ibn Ja’bir, from Ibn ‘Umar, that he saw a man having halted a female camel, and the man said, "Let it go forth standing and tied, following the practice of Muhammad, peace be upon him."

I have narrated to me Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, said: I read from Abu Qura, he is Musa ibn Tariq, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Khuzaim narrated to me, from Abu Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he returned from the Umrah of Ji’ranah, sent Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj. So we set out with him until we reached Al-’Arj, and dawn broke. When he straightened up to say Takbir, he heard the sound of a camel behind him, so he stopped the Takbir and said: “This is the sound of the Prophet’s camel, Al-Jud’aa.” “Indeed, something has appeared to the Prophet in Hajj, so perhaps the Prophet is present, and we will pray with him.” Then Ali was on her, and Abu Bakr said: “Is he an Amir or a Messenger?” He said: “No, but a Messenger. The Messenger of Allah has sent me with a declaration of innocence to recite to the people in the standing places of Hajj.”

So we arrived in Makkah. When the day before Tarwiyah arrived, Abu Bakr stood and addressed the people, informing them about their rituals. When he finished, Ali stood and recited the declaration of innocence to the people until he completed it.

Then we set out with him until it was the day of Arafah. Abu Bakr stood and addressed the people, informing them about their rituals. When he finished, Ali stood and recited the declaration of innocence to the people until he completed it.

Then came the day of Nahr, and we proceeded. When Abu Bakr returned, he addressed the people, informing them about their proceeding, about their slaughtering, and about their rituals. When he finished, Ali stood and recited the declaration of innocence to the people until he completed it.

When the day of the first departure came, Abu Bakr stood and addressed the people, informing them how to depart, how to throw stones, and teaching them their rituals. When he finished, Ali stood and recited the declaration of innocence to the people until he completed it.

Narrated by Abu Huraira: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "On the day of ‘Arafat, the month of Dhul-Hijjah, and in the city of Mecca, your blood, your wealth, and your honor are forbidden to one another.” Then he said, “Let the witness inform the absent (one), for the witness may inform someone who is more knowledgeable than him.”

Safiyyah menstruated. When the night of the departure [for Hajj] arrived, she said, "O ringlets! O bald ones!" – using their language. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "Are you not one who circled [the Ka'bah] on the Day of Nahr?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Then ride [the camel]."

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Bazzaz narrated to me, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: We asked Ali, "By what were you sent?" He said: "I was sent with four things: No soul believing will enter Paradise, nor will anyone circumambulate the House naked, nor will a Muslim and a disbeliever gather for pilgrimage after this year of theirs, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, his covenant is until its term. And whoever does not have a covenant, then it is four months. After the Day of Nahr, their term is the twentieth of Dhul-Hijjah, so kill them after the four months."

Narrated: 'Abidullah bin 'Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi: Narrated to me Shu'bah, who informed me Abu Qaz'ah, who said: I heard a migrant saying: Jabir bin 'Abdullah was asked about raising the hands at the House (Ka'bah), and he said: "They (the Jews) used to do that. We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Did we do that?"

Abu al-Walid and Hajjaj narrated: "We were told by Shu'bah, who told us that Ali ibn Mudrik said: I heard Abu Zur'ah narrating from Jarir ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The people have become listeners.' Then he said: 'Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another.'"

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, saying: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid narrated to me, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Aufa say: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ran between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and we were shielding him from the people of Mecca so that no one would harm him with a stone or a projectile."

Sahlu ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to me from Al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn, from Marwan ibn Al-Hakam, that he witnessed Ali and Uthman between Mecca and Medina, and Uthman forbade the mut'a (temporary marriage). When Ali saw that, he said, "Labbaik (O Allah, here I am) for Hajj and Umra together." He said, "Do you see me forbidding it and doing it?" Ali said, "I would not abandon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, because of the statement of any person."
Narrated by Anas: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saying: "Labbaik with 'Umrah and Hajj."

Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the ritual of Ihram for both (Hajj and 'Umrah) together. I met Ibn Umar and informed him of what Anas had said. He said, "He only performed Ihram for Hajj." So I returned to Anas and informed him of what Ibn Umar had said. He said, "They consider us nothing but boys."
"O Bani 'Abd Manaf, if you are entrusted with this affair [of leadership], then do not prevent anyone from circling [the Ka'bah] or praying at any hour they wish, be it night or day."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed at Dhul Tuwa until morning, then entered Mecca. And Ibn ‘Umar used to do likewise.
Narrated by Ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to enter Mecca from the upper side of the valley and exit from the lower side.
Narrated by Ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he would put his foot in the al-Ghariz (a valley) and his camel would level out with him, would pronounce the talbiyah from Masjid al-Huwayt.

Narrated ‘Uthman bin Muhammad bin Abi Shaybah and Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abi Khalaf: They said: We were told by Sufyan, from Ayub bin Musa, from Nubaih bin Wahb, from Aban bin ‘Uthman, from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said about a person who is in ihram and complains of an ailment in his eyes: "Let him apply patience to it."

Hashim ibn Qasim narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah narrated to me, from ‘Amr ibn Dinār, who said: I heard ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab saying: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived [in Mecca], then he circumambulated the House [Ka’bah] and prayed two rak’ahs at the Station [Maqam Ibrahim], then he proceeded to Mount Safa.” Shu’bah said: Shu’bah narrated to me, from Ayyub, from ‘Amr ibn Dinār, from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: “This is the Sunnah.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: The people used to disperse in every direction, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Let none depart until he makes his last farewell at the House (Ka’bah).”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Ibn Tawus narrated to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Permission was granted to a menstruating woman to depart if she is in ihram." He said: And I heard Ibn Umar in the year one, saying: "She does not depart," then I heard him saying: "She departs, indeed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, granted them permission."

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: I was told by Layth, who told me, from ‘Uqail, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Tawus al-Yamani informed me that he heard Abdullah ibn Umar being asked about the restriction of women from performing the Tawaf (circumambulation) of the House when menstruating before leaving, and having already completed the pilgrimage on the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha). He said: "Indeed, Aisha used to mention a concession for women." And that was a year before the death of Abdullah ibn Umar.

"Ya'la narrated to me, saying: Ismail, meaning Ibn Abi Khalid, narrated to me from Amir, from Masruq, that he said to Aisha: "O Mother of the Believers, some men send a sacrificial animal with a man, and they say to him: 'When you reach such and such a place, imitate him (in performing the ritual).' But when he reaches that place, he remains in the state of ihram until the people return." He said: "I heard the sound of her hands clapping behind the veil, and she said: 'I used to prepare the necklaces for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he would send sacrificial animals to the Ka'bah. Nothing was forbidden for him of what is permissible for a man of his family until the people returned.'"

"I used to spin the necklaces for the Prophet’s ﷺ sacrificial animals. He would send forth a portion of his sacrificial animals, each with a necklace, and he would remain in Medina, avoiding nothing, until his sacrificial animals were slaughtered."
Aisha (RA) said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, should we not build for you a structure in Mina that would shade you?" He said, "No, Mina is a resting place for whoever arrives first."

Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Mecca in the year of the Conquest, wearing a head covering (migfar). When he removed it, a man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Ibn Khatal clinging to the curtains of the Ka'abah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Kill him." Abdullah bin Khalid said: Malik was recited this statement: Ibn Shihab said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not in a state of ritual impurity (ihram) that day.

Narrated Jabir: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) entered Mecca when he conquered it, wearing a black head covering without being in the state of ihram. Isma'il said: I heard this from Abu Az-Zubair. He was with his father.

Musaddad narrated to me, he said: Yahya narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Hasan ibn Muslim and Abd al-Karim al-Jazari informed me that Mujahid informed them that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla informed him that Ali informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to stand guard over his sacrificial animal and to distribute its entirety – its meat, its skins, and its offal – and not to give anything from it to the butcher.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Ubaid ibn Umayr from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Ammar from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about the badger (ḍubba’), and he said: “It is game, and within it is a ram that the pilgrim (muḥrim) may take.”

I was told by Abu ‘Aasim, from Ibn Jurayj, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr, from ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi ‘Ammar, that he said: I asked Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah about the desert fox: Is it permissible to eat it? He said: Yes. I said: Is it game (prohibited during Hajj)? He said: Yes.

I said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him? He said: Yes.

It was said to Abu Muhammad: What do you say about the desert fox – is it permissible to eat it? He said: I dislike eating it.

Abdullah ibn Sa’id narrated: “Abu Usama narrated to me from ‘Ubaidullah from Nafi’ from Ibn ‘Umar: That al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib asked permission of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to set up a watering place at Makkah during the nights of Mina, for the purpose of providing water. So, he gave him permission.” Sa’id ibn al-Mughira narrated to me from ‘Isa ibn Yunus from ‘Ubaidullah ibn ‘Umar, a similar narration.

Narrated Anas: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) sacrificed two rams with black markings and horns. He used to name them and say, “Allahu Akbar” (Allah is the Greatest). I saw him sacrificing them with his own hand, placing his foot on their foreheads. I said: You heard it (from him)? He said: Yes.

Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed two rams on the day of Eid. When he turned them towards the qibla, he said: "Indeed, I have turned my face towards Him Who created the heavens and the earth, as a pure monotheist, and I am not of those who associate partners with Allah. Indeed, my prayers, my sacrifices, my life, and my death are all for Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. And with this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. O Allah, this is from You and for You, from Muhammad and his community.” Then he mentioned Allah’s name, said “Allahu Akbar,” and slaughtered them.
"Whoever intends to sacrifice [an animal], let him not trim his nails or shave any hair during the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah."
Narrated ‘Umm Salama: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “When the ten days (of Dhul-Hijjah) arrive, and anyone of you wants to sacrifice an animal, he should not cut his hair or nails.”

Narrated By Al-Baraa’ bin ‘Aazib: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about what is prohibited in sacrificial animals. He said: “The blind animal with an obvious defect, the lame animal with an obvious limp, and the sick animal with an obvious disease, and the emaciated animal that cannot fatten.”

I asked al-Bara’ about what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade concerning sacrificial animals, and he said: “Four are not acceptable: the one with a manifest defect, the one with a manifest limp, the one with a manifest disease, and the one with a broken bone that cannot heal.” I said to al-Bara’: “I dislike an animal with a deficiency in its teeth, a deficiency in its ear, or a deficiency in its horn.” He said: “Whatever you dislike, leave it, and do not forbid it upon anyone.”

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Salama ibn Kuhail, who said: I heard Hujayyah ibn ‘Adiyy say: I heard ‘Ali, and a man asked him a question. The man said: O Commander of the Believers, regarding the cow [for sacrifice]? He said: From seven [shekel]. I said: The horn? He said: It does not harm you. I said: A limp? He said: When it reaches the place of sacrifice. Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered us to look attentively with the eye and listen carefully with the ear."

Narrated by Ali (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered us to avoid sacrificing animals with split ears, or with a portion cut from the ear, or from the side of the ear, or with pierced ears, or with cracked ears. The ‘muqabila’ is what has a portion cut from its ear, the ‘mudabira’ is what has a portion cut from the side of its ear, the ‘kharqaa’ is the one with a hole, and the ‘sharqaa’ is the one with a crack.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, that Hisham narrated, from Yahya, from Baajidah al-Juhani, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, divided the sacrificial animals among his companions, and I received a young camel. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is just a young camel." He said: "Sacrifice it."

Abu al-Waleed narrated to me, that Layth narrated to me, that Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, from Abu al-Khair, from ‘Uqba ibn ‘Amir, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave me some sheep to distribute among his companions. I distributed them, and a young goat, a ‘atood,’ remained. I mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: ‘Sacrifice it.’” Abu Muhammad said: “The ‘atood’ is the young one of the goats.”

Yaa'la narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Abu Az-Zubair, from Jabir, who said: "We sacrificed seventy camels on the day of Hudaibiya, one camel for every seven people. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'Share in the sacrificial animals.'"

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, from Abu Zubeir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "We sacrificed a cow with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) for seven (people)." It was said to Abu Muhammad: Do you affirm this? He said: Yes.

Narrated by Abu ‘Aasim, from Ibn Jurayj, from Naafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals, or he said, “Do not eat the meat of sacrificial animals after three days.”

"We used to forbid you from eating the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days, so that it might suffice you. Then Allah has brought abundance, so eat, store, and trade." Abu Muhammad said: "Trade – seek reward in it."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) had forbidden eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days. Then, in the following year, when people sacrificed [animals], I said: “O Messenger of Allah, these sacrifices used to be beneficial to the people, as they would store some of their meat and fat.” He said: “What prevents them from doing that today?” I said: “O Messenger of Allah, did you not forbid them in the first year from eating their meat for more than three days?” He said: “I forbade it for the present [people] among the bedouins who were with them, so that they might distribute its meat among them. But now, let them eat and let them store [it].”

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, that Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Zubaydi narrated to me, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, that my father narrated to me, that he heard Thawban, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to me while we were in Mina, "Repair for us from this meat." So I repaired for him from it, and he kept eating from it until we reached Medina.
"We used to provision ourselves from Makkah to Madinah on the authority of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” Abu Muhammad said: meaning, the meat of the sacrificial animals.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, that Sufyan narrated, from Mansur and Zubayr, from Al-Sha'bi, from Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that Abu Burdah ibn Niyar sacrificed before the prayer. Then, when the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed, he called him and mentioned to him what he had done. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed, your sacrifice is a sheep of meat." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a young goat which is dearer to me than two sheep." He said: "Sacrifice with it, and it should not suffice for anyone after you." Abu Muhammad said: It was recited to Muhammad from Sufyan: And whoever sacrifices after the prayer and the Imam is delivering the sermon, it is sufficient.

Abu Ali al-Hanafi narrated to me, Malik narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Bushair ibn Yasar, from Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, that a man slaughtered an animal before the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had departed. So he ordered him to repeat [the slaughter].
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no divination and no (reliance on) omens."
Luqait ibn ‘Amir said: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, we slaughter in Rajab, so what do you see (regarding that)?” He said, “There is no harm in that.” Wakee’ said: I will never abandon it.

Habiba, daughter of Maysara ibn Abi Khuthaym, from Um Kurz, narrated: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said concerning ‘Aqiqah: “For a boy, two sheep that are similar, and for a girl, one sheep.”
Narrated by Salman ibn ‘Amir Ad-Dubbi: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For every boy there is ‘Aqiqah, so shed blood for him and remove the impurity from him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For a boy, two sheep, and for a girl, one sheep."

Narrated by Samura, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Every boy is held as a pledge by his ‘aqiqa (sacrifice); it is slaughtered on the seventh day, and his head is shaved and he is bled.” And Qatada would describe the bleeding, saying: “When the ‘aqiqa is slaughtered, a tuft of wool is taken and brought forward to the temples of the sacrificed animal, then it is placed on the boy’s chest until the amount resembling a thread flows, then his head is washed, and then he is shaved afterwards. 

Narrated by ‘Affan, he said: Aban narrated this hadith, saying: “And he is named.”

Abdullah said: And I do not think it is obligatory.

Narrated by Shaddad ibn Aws: I memorized two things from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: He said, "Indeed, Allah has enjoined upon you excellence in all matters. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let one of you sharpen his blade, and then let him spare the suffering of the slaughtered animal."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: That a woman who was tending sheep for the people of Ka'b ibn Malik in Sal'a feared for a sheep that it would die, so she took a stone and slaughtered it with it. And that was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. So he ordered them to eat it.

Abu al-Ushra narrated from his father, that he said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, is Zakat (religious charity) only due on sheep and camels?" He said, "If you pierced it in the thigh, it would suffice for you." Hammad said: We interpreted it as pertaining to the animal that falls from a height.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Al-Minhal ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr saying: I set out with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab on a road outside Medina, and we saw some young boys throwing stones at a chicken. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asked, "Who did this?" and they dispersed. He said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, cursed whoever mocks or imitates an animal."
Abu Ayyub al-Ansari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade restraining animals unnecessarily. Abu Ayyub said: If it were a hen, I would not restrain it.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the "Mujaththama." Abu Muhammad said: "The Mujaththama is the one who endures [hardship]."

Narrated ‘Aisha, the mother of the believers, that some people said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), “Some people bring us meat, and we do not know whether the name of Allah has been mentioned over it or not.” He (ﷺ) said, “Mention (the name of Allah) yourselves and eat.” And they were recent converts from paganism.

Narrated Abu Rafi’a, from his grandfather Rafi’ ibn Khadij: That a camel ran wild and there were only a few horses among the people. A man shot it with an arrow and stopped it. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: “Indeed, these beasts are like wild animals, so if you overpower any of them, treat it in this way.”

Narrated ‘Abdu’llāh ibn ‘Amr: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever kills a sparrow without right, Allah will question him about it on the Day of Resurrection.” It was said: “What is the right (to kill it)?” He said: “That he should slaughter it and eat it.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The purification of the fetus is the purification of its mother." It was said to Abu Muhammad: Is it permissible to eat [the fetus]? He said: Yes.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating every animal with fangs from the species of lions.
Narrated Abu Thallabah Al-Khushani: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade snatching, mutilating, plundering, and eating every animal with tusks from the lions.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the eating of every animal with tusks from the lions, and every bird with talons.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade using the skins of lions as mats.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Wa’ila, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the al-Asqiya’ (skins of animals). He said: I do not know what to say to you, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whenever a skin is tanned, it is purified."

Ya'la narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Al-Qaa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Wa'la, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the skins of dead animals, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Its tanning purifies it." It was said to Abu Muhammad Abd Allah: Do you say this? He said: Yes, if its meat is eaten.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered that benefit be derived from the hides of slaughtered animals if they are tanned."

Ubayy ibn 'Abbas reported: A sheep died for Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Would you not have enjoyed its hide?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, it is dead (and thus impure).” He said: “It is only its flesh that has been prohibited.”

Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa reported: Bqiyyah narrated to me from al-Zubaydi from al-Zuhri from 'Ubaydullah from ibn Abbas from the Prophet (ﷺ), a narration similar to this hadith.

It was said to Abu Muhammad: What do you say about foxes if they are tanned? He said: I dislike them.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade the temporary marriage of women on the day of Khaybar, and forbade the consumption of asses."

Narrated Anas bin Malik: A man stood up on the day of Khaybar and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the asses have been eaten or destroyed." Then he said, "O Messenger of Allah, the asses have been destroyed or eaten." So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ordered a man to announce, "Indeed, Allah and His Messenger forbid you from the meat of asses, for they are impure."
Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with her) said: “We ate the meat of a horse during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) in Medina.”
Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) narrated: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the consumption of domesticated donkeys on the day of Khaybar, and permitted the consumption of horses."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No one plunders a valuable possession that elevates the Muslims’ vision in it while he is a believer when he plunders it.”
Narrated by Abdur-Rahman bin Samura: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade plundering.” Abu Muhammad said: “This refers to raiding (in war) when they gain spoils before they are divided.”

We said: O Messenger of Allah, we are in a land where poverty prevails, so what is permissible for us regarding carrion? He said: "If you do not eat in the morning, nor at night, and do not conceal beans, then do as you wish [regarding it].” He said: The people say it with ‘ha’ (ح), and this was said with ‘kha’ (خ).
I presented to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, a female goat. He ordered me to milk it, and I milked it. I struggled in milking it, and he said, "Leave the milker of the milk."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade killing frogs.
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of four types of animals: ants, bees, the hoopoe, and the lark.
Narrated from Um Sharik that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered the killing of lizards.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade (people) from the Mujathamah, from the milk of al-Jallalah, and from drinking from the mouth of the water skin.

I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about hunting with dogs, and he said: "Whatever your dog catches for you, eat, for taking it is its slaughter. And if you find another dog with it and fear that it may have taken it and killed it, do not eat it, for you only mentioned the name of Allah upon your dog, and you did not mention it upon the other."

I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about hunting with a trained falcon, and he said the same.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever acquires a dog except for hunting or herding, two qirats are deducted from his reward every day."

Malik narrated to me from Yazid ibn Khuzaifa from As-Sa’ib ibn Yazid, that he heard Sufyan ibn Abi Zuhair addressing a group of people near the door of the mosque, saying: “I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ‘Whoever acquires a dog that is of no use for guarding crops or livestock, his reward diminishes by one qirat every day.’” They said: “Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?” He said: “Yes, by the Lord of this mosque.”
Abu ad-Darda narrated: The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that dogs be killed, then he said: "What does it matter to me about the dogs?" Then he permitted dogs for herding and hunting.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of dogs.

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Mughaffal: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Were it not that dogs are a community among communities, I would have ordered their complete slaughter. But kill from them every black, fierce one." Saeed ibn ‘Amir said: "By ‘fierce’ he meant every black one."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Abi Safar from Al-Sha'bi, who said: I heard 'Adi ibn Hatim say: I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) about the mir'ad (a type of trap), and he said: "If it catches with its boundary, then eat. But if it catches with its breadth and kills, then it is a waqid (a harmful thing), so do not eat it."
Narrated Abdullah ibn Abi Aufa: We accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on seven campaigns, and we ate locusts.

Narrated Abu Huraira: A man asked the Prophet (peace be upon him): "We sail on the sea and carry with us little water. If we perform ablution with it, we become thirsty. Can we perform ablution with seawater?" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Its water is purifying, and its dead creature is permissible (to eat)."

Narrated Jabir: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) sent us in an expedition of three hundred (men). We were afflicted with hunger until we reached the sea. We saw a creature cast up on the shore. We ate of it until our bodies became firm. Abu Ubaidah took a rib from it and placed it (back). Then, the tallest man in the army was mounted on the biggest camel in the army and passed beneath it. This is its meaning.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Hisham ibn Zayd ibn Anas narrated to me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: “We were on a journey when we startled a rabbit, and the people began to chase and play. I took it and brought it to Abu Talha. He slaughtered it, and sent [to the Prophet] Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, the haunches or thighs – Shu'bah was unsure – and [the Prophet] accepted it.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to me from Amir from Muhammad ibn Sufyan, that he passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was looking at two rabbits suspended. He said: “O Messenger of Allah, I entered the flock of my family and hunted these two rabbits, and I did not find an iron implement with which to slaughter them, so I slaughtered them with a stone. Can I eat them?” He (the Prophet) said: “Yes.”
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about the desert hare, and he said: “I do not eat it, nor do I forbid it.”
Narrated by Thabit ibn Wudai’ah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was brought a desert hare, and he said: “A community transformed, and Allah knows best.”

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Layth narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me from Ibn Shihab, who said: He informed me Abu Umama ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf al-Ansari, that Abdullah ibn Abbas informed him, that Khalid ibn al-Walid, who was called "the Sword of Allah," informed him, that he entered with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, upon Maymuna, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who was his aunt and the aunt of Abdullah ibn Abbas. He found there a roasted desert hare that his sister, Hafida bint al-Harith, had brought from Najd. So, she presented the hare to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. It was rare that he would extend his hand to food until he was informed about it and its name was mentioned to him. So, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, extended his hand towards the hare, when a woman among the women present said: "Inform the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, what you have presented to him." They said: "This is a desert hare." So, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, withdrew his hand and Khalid ibn al-Walid said: "Do you forbid the desert hare, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, but it was not in the land of my people, so I find myself avoiding it." Khalid said: "So, I dragged it and ate it, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was looking, and he did not forbid me."

Narrated Abu Waqid Al-Laythi: When Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) came to Medina, the people were cutting off the humps of camels and the udders of sheep. So Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said: “Whatever is cut off from an animal while it is alive is carrion.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to him, "Mention the name of Allah and eat from that which is before you."

Narrated ‘Aisha: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to eat with six of his companions. An Arab Bedouin came and ate the food in two bites. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Indeed, if he had mentioned the name of Allah, it would have been sufficient for you. So, when anyone of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah. And if he forgets to mention the name of Allah, let him say, ‘In the name of Allah, its beginning and its end.’”

Narrated by Bundar: He said, I narrated to me Mu’adh bin Hisham from his father, from Budail, from Abdullah bin ‘Ubaid bin ‘Umir, from Ummu Kultum, from Aisha, with this Hadith.

My father told my mother, "Would you prepare some food for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?" So she prepared a porridge, and he gestured with his hand, indicating a small portion. My father then went and called him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, placed his hand upon the top of it, and then said, "Take in the name of Allah." So they took from its sides, and when they tasted it, he invoked blessings upon them, saying, "O Allah, forgive them, have mercy on them, and bless their provision."

Narrated Abu Umama: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say when he ate or drank: "All praise is due to Allah, abundant praise, pure praise, blessed praise, praise that is not rejected, nor concealed, and not from one who is independent of his Lord."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The eater who is grateful is like the one who fasts with patience."
"When one of you eats, let him lick his three fingers."
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When one of you eats, let him not wipe his hand until he licks his fingers or has them licked."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Yaman al-Barra’ – and he is Mu’alla ibn Rashid – said: My grandmother, Umm ‘Asim, told me that Nubaysha, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), entered upon us while we were eating, so we invited him, and he ate with us. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) told me, "Whoever eats from a bowl and then licks it clean, the bowl will seek forgiveness for him."
Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If a morsel falls from anyone amongst you, let him wipe it off with the dust, and mention the name of Allah, and then eat it."

Ma'qil ibn Yasar was having lunch when a piece of his food fell. He picked it up, removed any impurities from it, and then ate it. Some of the nobles began to glance at him and said to him, "What do you think about what these foreigners say? They say, 'Look at what is in front of him of food, and look at what he does with this piece.'" He replied, "I would not abandon what I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, because of the words of these foreigners, 'We are commanded when a piece of food falls from one of us to remove any impurities from it and then eat it.'"
"When one of you eats, let him eat with his right hand, and let him drink with his right hand. For the devil eats with his left hand and drinks with his left hand."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Ikrimah ibn ‘Ammar narrated to me, he said: Iyasu ibn Salama narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw Busr ibn Ra’i al-‘Ir eating with his left hand. He said: “Eat with your right hand.” He said: “I cannot.” He said: “You cannot.” He said: “Then his right hand did not reach his mouth.”
Narrated by Ibn Ka'b from his father: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to eat with three fingers and would not wipe his hand until he licked it.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to eat with his three fingers, and when he finished, he would lick them.

One who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. And one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. And one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest, providing for him for a day and a night, and the hospitality is for three days, and anything beyond that is charity.

"Narrated Abu Shuraih Al-Khuzai: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him treat his neighbor well. And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent."

"Whoever hosts a Muslim guest and the guest is left deprived in the morning, then it is incumbent upon every Muslim to support him until he obtains sustenance for the night from his produce and wealth."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If a fly falls into the drink of one of you, let him dip it in all of it, then remove it, for indeed in one of its wings is sickness, and in the other is healing."
"When a fly falls into the vessel of any of you, let him not repel it, but rather dip it (in the vessel), for in one of its wings is disease, and in the other is healing."
The believer eats with one stomach, and the disbeliever eats with seven stomachs.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The believer eats one meal, and the disbeliever eats seven meals."

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The food of one person is sufficient for two, the food of two persons is sufficient for four, and the food of four persons is sufficient for eight."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to him, "Mention the name of Allah and eat from that which is before you."

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a dish of porridge, or he said: a bowl of porridge. He said: "Eat from its edges or its sides, and do not eat from its center, for the blessing descends upon its center."

Asma bint Abu Bakr (RA) narrated: Whenever a loaf of bread was brought to her, she would order it to be covered until the intensity of its smoke subsided, and she would say: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'It is more blessed.'"

Jabir ibn Abdullah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) took my hand one day and led me to his home. He said, "Is there anything for breakfast or dinner?" Talha hesitated. Then, he brought out two pieces of bread, and said, "Is there anything to go with it?" They said, "Nothing, except a little vinegar." He said, "Bring it to me, for vinegar is a good accompaniment." Jabir said: I have loved vinegar ever since I heard him say that from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). Then Abu Sufyan said: I have loved it ever since I heard it from Jabir.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Vinegar is a good accompaniment to food."
Narrated Anas: I saw the Prophet (peace be upon him) being brought a broth containing dates and dried meat, and I saw him following the dates, eating them.
Hudhaifa narrated: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to like pumpkins." He said: "It was presented to him, and I began to take them and place them before him."
Narrated Abu Asa’id Al-Ansari: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Eat olive oil, for it is a blessing, anoint yourselves with it, and use it for massage, for it comes from a blessed tree.”

Narrated by ‘Abdullah, that Naafi’ informed him, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said during the expedition of Khaybar, "Whoever eats from this tree – meaning garlic – should not come to the mosques."

Narrated by Umayya ibn Abi Salit, his mother informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited them, and they prepared a meal for him containing some of these beans. When they brought it to him, he disliked it and said to his companions, "Eat it, for I am not like one of you; I fear that my companion might be harmed." Abu Muhammad said: If it does not harm anyone, then there is nothing wrong with eating it.

Narrated by Zadam al-Jarmi: We were with Abu Musa, and his food was presented, and it included the meat of a chicken. There was a man from Banu Taym among the people, who was red-faced, and he did not approach. Abu Musa said to him, "Approach, for I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eating from it."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Zayd ibn Jad’am al-Jarmi, from Abu Musa, that he mentioned chickens and said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, eating them.”
Do not associate with anyone except a believer, and let no one eat your food except a righteous person.
Narrated by Abdullah ibn Ja'far: I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) eating dates with cucumbers.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah narrated to me, he said: Jabalah ibn Suhaym narrated to me, that we were in Medina and a year of famine afflicted us. Ibn al-Zubayr used to distribute dates, and Ibn Umar would pass by us and say: “Do not compare [your portions], for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade comparison except that a man asks permission of his brother.”

Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me, "O Aisha, a house in which dates are not present, its people experience hunger, or its people become hungry." He said it twice or three times.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The household of which dates are present will never experience hunger."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Mu'adh ibn Sulaym narrated to me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: "Dates were presented as a gift to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he began to distribute them as gifts."
He said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, eating dates, bending his back from hunger." Abu Muhammad said: He was sending them (meaning: sending them here and there)."

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever sleeps with the scent of camphor on his hand, and a cloud appears to him, let him not blame anyone but himself."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Anas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to Abdur-Rahman ibn ‘Auf, and saw a yellowish tinge on him: "What is the matter?" He said: "I have married." He (the Prophet) said: "Observe an Aqiqah, even if it be with a sheep."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Uthman ath-Thaqafi from a one-eyed man from the Thaqif tribe, who was called Maaruf (meaning he was praised), or perhaps his name was Zuhair ibn ‘Uthman, and I do not know his name, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The feast on the first day is a right (obligation), the second day is generosity, and the third day is showing off and hypocrisy."

Qatadah said: A man told me, from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib, that he was invited on the first day and accepted, and he was invited on the second day and accepted, and he was invited on the third day, so he disregarded the Messenger (peace be upon him) and did not respond, and said: "These are people of showing off and hypocrisy."

Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated: "The worst of foods is the food of a feast, to which the wealthy are invited and the poor are left out. And whoever refuses an invitation, he has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."

Narrated Anas: A man brought food to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is like this," gesturing with his hand. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him, "Like this," and pointed to Aisha. He said, "No," so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) turned away from him. Then the man gestured to him again, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) gestured to him again, and he turned away from him. Then the man gestured to him a third time, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him, "And this?" He said, "Yes," so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and Aisha went with him and ate from his food.

Narrated Abu Mas’ud: There was a man named Abu Shu’aib who had a young slave. He said, "Prepare food so I may invite the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) as the fifth of five." He (the Prophet) was invited as the fifth of five, and a man followed them. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "You invited me as the fifth of five, and this is a man who has followed me. If you wish, you may allow him, and if you wish, you may leave him.” He (Abu Shu’aib) gave him permission.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The superiority of Aisha over the women is like the superiority of the dates over all other food.”

Abu Umayya, reported from Abdullah ibn Harith ibn Nawfal: My father married me during the governorship of Uthman. He called a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and Safwan ibn Umayya was among those he called, and he was an elderly man. He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Eat the meat quickly, in large bites, for it is more delicious and easier (to swallow)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I do not eat with a recliner."

Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) used to say when a first fruit (of the season) was brought to him: “O Allah! Bless our city, our fruit, our measure, and our scales with blessings upon blessings.” Then he would give it to the youngest among those present.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you asks his servant to bring food, let him seat him. If he refuses, let him hand it to him."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "When any of you is served food, let him seat his servant with him, or give him a morsel or two, or a bite or two, for he is his companion in heat and smoke."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) loved sweets and honey."

Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) emerged from the privy, and food was presented to him. They said to him, "Do you not perform ablution?" He said, "Do I perform ablution before praying?"

Abu Muhammad said: It is Saeed ibn Abi Huwairith.

Abu Naim narrated, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinār, from Saeed ibn Abi Huwairith, from Ibn Abbas.

He said: I heard Abu ‘Āsim narrating, from Ibn Jurayj, from Amr ibn Dinār, from Saeed ibn Abi Huwairith, from Ibn Abbas, with his chain of narration.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was in a state of ritual impurity (janabah) and wanted to eat or sleep, he would perform ablution."

Abu Dharr (RA) said: My beloved Khalil (Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him) gave me counsel, saying: "If you prepare soup, make its water abundant, and then look to the people of your household from among your neighbors and give them from it."
Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the food is set, take off your shoes, for it is more refreshing for your feet."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Worship the Most Merciful (Allah), spread peace, and give food, and you will enter the gardens of Paradise."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Respond to the caller when you are invited." He said: And ‘Abdullah used to attend invitations whether at weddings or other than weddings, and he would attend them while fasting.

Narrated ‘A’isha:

Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) was asked about a mouse that fell into the clarified butter. He said, "Throw it and what is around it, and eat (the rest)."

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was asked about a mouse that fell into clarified butter and died. He said: "Take it and what is around it and throw it away."

Zayd ibn Yahya narrated: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubaidullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Maymunah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said something similar.

Abu Muhammad said: If it is molten, pour it out.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one eats, let him clear (the food from between his teeth), and if he does not clear it, let him spit it out, and if it sticks to his tongue, let him swallow it."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was presented with two vessels, one containing wine and the other milk, on the night of his ascension. He looked at them and then took the milk, and Gabriel said: "Praise be to Allah who has guided you to the natural disposition (fitrah). Had you taken the wine, your community would have gone astray."

Anas (RA) narrated: I was the server of drinks at a gathering in the house of Abu Talha. He (Abu Talha) said: "The prohibition of alcohol was revealed." He ordered a crier to announce it, and Abu Talha said, "Go and see what this is." I went out and said, "This is a crier announcing: ‘Verily, alcohol has been forbidden!’" He told me, "Go and pour it out." So, it flowed in the streets of Medina. At that time, their drink was al-Fadikh. Some of the people said, "People have died while it was still in their bellies." So Allah revealed: [It is not a sin for those who believe and do good work that they eat what they are permitted, if they observe their duty and believe.] (Surah Al-Ma’idah, 5:93)

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world and does not repent from it, it will be forbidden for him in the Hereafter, and he will not be given to drink."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related from al-Awza’i, who said: Rabi’ah ibn Yazid told me from Abdullah ibn ad-Daylami, who said: I entered upon Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-‘As in a garden of his in Ta’if, called al-Wahṭ. There he was engaged in a discussion with a young man from Quraysh, who was being reprimanded for drinking wine. I said to him, “Traits have reached me from you that you relate, concerning the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that whoever drinks wine, forty mornings of his prayers are not accepted for him.” When the young man heard the mention of wine, he withdrew his hand from Abdullah’s, and then turned away.

Then Abdullah said: “O Allah, I do not permit anyone to say anything about me that I have not said. And I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: ‘Whoever drinks wine, forty mornings of his prayers are not accepted for him. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. I do not know whether it is on the third or the fourth [morning]: it is incumbent upon Allah to give him a drink of the foulest of pus on the Day of Resurrection.’”
Narrated by Jabir: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table where wine is being consumed."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Neither a child born out of wedlock, nor a boastful person, nor an ungrateful person, nor an habitual drinker of wine will enter Paradise."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "One who is ungrateful to his parents, one who is boastful, and one who is addicted to wine will not enter Paradise."

Suwaid ibn Tariq asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about wine. He forbade him from making it, and Suwaid said, "It is a medicine." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "It is not a medicine, but it is a disease."

Narrated by Abu Mughira, from Al-Awza'i, who said: I heard Abu Kathir say: I heard Abu Huraira say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Intoxicants come from these two trees: the palm tree and the grape."
Narrated by Aisha: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about al-bit’; he said, "Every intoxicant is forbidden."
Narrated Abu Hurda bin Abi Musa: My father said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me and Mu’adh bin Jabal to Yemen, and said: “Drink, but do not drink intoxicants, for every intoxicant is forbidden.”
I forbid you from consuming little of that which its abundance intoxicates.

Aisha (RA) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "The first thing that was overturned [abolished] in Islam was as the container [vessel] is overturned [abolished], meaning wine." It was said: How so, O Messenger of Allah, when Allah has clarified it therein? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They give it a name other than its name, and thus they deem it permissible."

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to me, saying: Abu Wahb narrated to me, from Makhul, from Abu Thallabah al-Khushani, from Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The first of your religion is prophethood and mercy, then kingship and mercy, then a dusty kingship, then kingship and power wherein wine and silk are permitted." Abu Muhammad was asked about 'a'far (dusty), and he said: It is like dust, and there is no goodness in it.

Narrated on the authority of Sa'hl bin Hammad, who said: He told me, Mu'tima, who said: He told me, 'Amru bin Bayan al-Taghlibi, from 'Urwa bin al-Mughira bin Shu'ba, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever sells wine, let him shear the swine." Abu Muhammad said: It is 'Umar bin Bayan who narrated.

I asked Ibn Abbas about the sale of wine, and he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had a close companion from the Thaqif or Daws tribe. He met him in Mecca during the year of the Conquest, bringing a container of wine as a gift. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “O so-and-so, did you not know that Allah the Exalted has forbidden it?” The man turned to his servant and said, “Go and sell it.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “What did you order him to do, O so-and-so?” He said, “I ordered him to sell it.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Indeed, He who has forbidden its consumption has forbidden its sale.” He then ordered that it be overturned in al-Batḥā’.

It was reported to 'Umar that Samura sold wine. He said, "May Allah kill Samura! Did he not know that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'Allah cursed the Jews, for they were forbidden from eating fat, so they melted it down and sold it.' " Sufyan said, "Melted it down: they liquefied it."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If he becomes intoxicated, then flog him. If he becomes intoxicated, then flog him. If he becomes intoxicated, then flog him. If he becomes intoxicated, then behead him." – meaning on the fourth [occurrence].

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does the thief steal while he is a believer, nor does the drinker drink wine while he is a believer.”
Jabir narrated: "Wine used to be put for the Prophet (ﷺ) in a sāqiyyah (skin container), and if there was no sāqiyyah, it was put for him in a tawr from birām."

Narrated Abdullah bin ad-Dailami, from his father, or a man from his people, that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ): “O Messenger of Allah, we have come from a place you know, and settled among people you know. Who is our guardian?” He (ﷺ) said: “Allah and His Messenger.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, we used to have grapes and wine, and Allah has forbidden wine. What should we do with the grapes?” He (ﷺ) said: “Make them raisins.” They said: “What should we do with the raisins?” He (ﷺ) said: “Soak them in water, soak them with your lunch, and drink them with your dinner, and soak them with your dinner and drink them with your lunch. When the two afternoons pass, they become permissible before they become wine.”

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from 'Azrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubair, who said: I asked Ibn 'Umar about jar wine, and he said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade it." Then I met Ibn 'Abbas and informed him of Ibn 'Umar's statement, and he said: "Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman spoke truthfully."
Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not eat or drink from vessels made of palm fiber and asphalt."

Abu Zayd narrated: Shu'bah narrated to me from Salama bin Kuhail, who said: I heard Abu al-Hakam say: I asked Ibn Abbas, or I heard him being asked, about nabidh al-jarr (a type of fermented drink), and he said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade nabidh al-jarr and ad-dubba’." And I asked Ibn az-Zubair, and he said the same as Ibn Abbas.
Ibn Abbas said: "Whoever desires to violate what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, or whoever is violating what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, let him forbid the wine."

He [the narrator] said: My brother narrated to me from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade [mentioning] the jar, the dubba', and the muzaffat, and [forbade mentioning] the busr and the dates.

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to me, saying: 'Asim narrated to me, from Fudayl ibn Zayd ar-Raqashi, that he came to Abdullah ibn Mughaffal and said: "Inform me of what is forbidden for us regarding drinks." He said: "Wine." I said: "Is that in the Qur'an?" He said: "I do not tell you except what I heard Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) begin with the mention of [Allah's] Name or the Message." He said: "He forbade the dabb, the hantum, and the naqir."

Yazid ibn Harun and Saeed ibn Amir narrated to me, and the wording is that of Yazid, they said: Hisham narrated to us from Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Do not both consume dates and fresh fruits together, and do not both consume raisins and dates together, but consume each of them separately."

Narrated by ‘Alqama bin Wail, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not say 'al-karam' (the noble grape), but say 'al-‘inab’ (the grape) or ‘al-habala’ (the vine)."

Abu Talha had orphans under his care. He bought them wine, and when the prohibition of wine was revealed, he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and mentioned this to him. The Prophet said, "Shall I turn it into vinegar?" He said, "No." So he poured it out.

Abu Mughira narrated: The narrator, Al-Awza'i, narrated to me: The narrator, Zuhri, narrated to me from Anas bin Malik, that he saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drinking milk, with Abu Bakr on His left and an Arab man on His right. He gave the remainder of the milk to the Arab man, and then said: "The right one, then the right one."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade drinking from the mouth of the water skin.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade drinking from the mouth of the water skin.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade the excessive jingling of water pitchers.
Anas narrated: Anas used to breathe into the vessel two or three times, and he claimed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to breathe into the vessel two or three times.

I was with Marwan when Abu Sa’id came and said: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I do not get satisfied with a single breath.” He (the Prophet) said: “Then separate the vessel from your mouth, and then breathe.” He said: “I see something (dirt/debris)?” He (the Prophet) said: “Pour it out.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Qatadah: My father informed me that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "When anyone of you urinates, let him not touch his private part with his right hand, nor perform istinja (cleansing after urination or defecation) with his right hand, and let him not breathe into the vessel."

Narrated by Jabir bin Abdullah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) visited a man from the Ansar who was ill. There was a stream flowing nearby. He said: "If you have water that remained in the bucket overnight, then give it to him, and if not, we will drink from this (stream)."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) drank from the mouth of a standing waterskin.
"We used to drink while standing and eat while walking, during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Qatadah narrated to me, from Anas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade drinking while standing. I asked him about eating, and he said, “That is even more impure.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to a man whom he saw drinking standing: "Vomit." The man said: "Why?" He (the Prophet) said: "Do you like to drink with a donkey? He (the devil) has drunk with you worse than that."
The one who drinks in vessels of silver, he is but pouring the fire of Hell into his belly.

Hudhaifa and I set out with a group to al-Madain. He asked for water, and a dignitary brought him a vessel of silver. Hudhaifa threw it in his face. We said, "Be silent, for if we question him, he will not tell us." Later, he said, "Do you know why I threw it?" We said, "No." He said, "I was forbidding him, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade drinking in vessels of gold and silver, and forbade wearing silk and brocade, and said, 'These are for them in this world, and for you in the Hereafter.'"
Abu Hurayrah al-Sa’idi narrated: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with milk. He said: “Why didn’t you curdle it? Or at least expose it to a stick?”
Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered us to cover the water during ablution, to turn down the edges of the pitcher, and to balance the vessel.

Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, that Mālik narrated to me, from Ayyūb ibn Habbīb, from Abū al-Muthannā al-Juhani, who said: Marwān said to Abū Sa’īd al-Khudri: “Did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbidding blowing into drinks?” He said: “Yes.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade blowing into drinks.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The cupbearer of the people is the last of them to drink."

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Aban narrated to me, he said: Yahya narrated to me, from Abu Salama, from ‘Ubada ibn as-Samit, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, the statement of Allah: “They receive good news in this world’s life, and in the Hereafter” (Surah Yunus, 10:64), so he said: “You have asked me about something that no one has asked me about before you or anyone from my community. It is the good dream, which a Muslim sees or is seen for him.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The vision of a believer is a part of the sixty-six parts of prophethood."
