Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, from his father, from Sibah ibn Thabit, from Um Kurz al-Ka’biyyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Prophethood has passed away, but the glad-tiders remain."
Narrated Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever sees me in a dream, he has indeed seen me, for the Satan does not appear in my form."
Narrated Abu Qatada: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever sees me in a dream, he has seen the truth."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Qatadah from his father: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A true dream is from Allah, and a delusion is from Satan. So, if one of you sees a dream that he fears, let him spit to his left three times, and seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for it will not harm him."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abd Rabbih ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman saying: "I used to see dreams that made me ill. I mentioned this to Abu Qatada, who said: I too used to see dreams that made me ill until I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The good dream is from Allah. So, if one of you sees something he likes, let him praise Allah and not relate it to anyone except those he loves. And if he sees something he dislikes, let him spit to his left three times, seek refuge in Allah from its evil, and not relate it to anyone, for it will not harm him.'"

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "There are three types of dreams: A good dream is a glad tiding from Allah, a dream that causes sadness is from Satan, and a dream that is a result of a person talking to himself – so if one of you sees something he dislikes, let him not mention it to anyone, and let him stand up and pray."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the time draws near, the vision of a believer will scarcely be false, and the most truthful of them in vision is the most truthful of them in speech."
Narrated ‘Ali: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Whoever lies in his dream, he will be tasked with tying a knot of a sheep’s hair on the Day of Resurrection.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The most truthful dreams are those seen during the early morning hours."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "Do not recount dreams except to a scholar or one who gives sound counsel."

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', who said: I heard Wakee' ibn 'Adus relating from his uncle, Abu Razeen al-'Uqaili, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A vision is but a flash of a bird's wing until it is explained; once it is explained, it comes to pass."

Narrated By Khalid bin Al-Jalaj, and Makhool asked him to narrate it, he said: I heard Abdur Rahman bin Auf saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form. I asked: 'About what do the highest assembly dispute?' I said: 'You are the Knower.' He said: 'He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what was in the heavens and the earth,' and recited: 'Thus We show Ibrahim the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be of the certain believers.' [Surah Al-An'am 6:75]"
Narrated Ibn Sirin: Whoever sees his Lord in a dream, he has entered Paradise.

While I was asleep, I saw people being presented before me, and they were wearing garments, some of which reached the bosom, and others less than that. And ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab was presented, and he was wearing a garment that trailed [behind him]. So those around me asked, “What did you interpret that to be, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “The religion.”

Ubaydullah narrated from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: “I was in the company of the Prophet (ﷺ) and I did not have a night’s stay except in the Masjid of the Prophet (ﷺ). And the Prophet (ﷺ) used to, every morning, be visited by people who would recount their dreams to him. I said: ‘Why don’t I see anything?’ Then I saw as if people were being gathered and thrown upon their feet into a pit, and I was taken. When it drew near the well, a man said: ‘Take him to the right.’ When I awoke, my dream was fresh in my mind, and I feared it, so I asked Hafsa about it. She said: ‘You have seen a good thing.’ I said to her: ‘Ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about it.’ So she asked him, and he said: ‘‘Abdullah is a good man; if only he prayed at night.’”

Musai ibn Khalid narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Fazari, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, with this narration.

Ibn Umar said: “And I would not rise until morning when I slept.”

Nafi’ said: “And Ibn Umar used to pray the night prayer.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saying: “While I was asleep, I was brought a container of milk, and I drank from it until I saw the whiteness (of milk) in my fingernail or they said, in my fingernails. Then I passed the remainder to ‘Umar.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is its interpretation?” He said, “Knowledge.”

The narrator, one of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Milk is purity, a ship is safety, a camel is sorrow, greenery is paradise, and a woman is goodness."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say to his companions, "If anyone of you sees a dream, let him tell it to me so that I may interpret it for him." A man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw a shade between the sky and the earth, dripping with honey and clarified butter. I saw a rope extending from the sky to the earth, and I saw people taking from it, some taking much and some taking little. I grasped it and ascended, and Allah elevated me. Then the one who came after me grasped it and ascended, and Allah elevated him. Then the one who came after him grasped it and ascended, and Allah elevated him. Then the one who came after him grasped it and it was cut, then it was joined and connected." Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, allow me to interpret it." He said, "Interpret it." It was said that he was the most one who interpreted dreams after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said, "As for the shade, it is Islam, and as for the honey and clarified butter, it is the Qur'an - the sweetness of the honey and the softness of the clarified butter. And as for those who take from it, some taking much and some taking little, they are the carriers of the Qur’an. And as for the rope extending from the sky to the earth, it is the truth that you are upon, by which you ascend, and Allah elevates you with it. Then a man from after you grasps it and ascends with it, and Allah elevates him. Then another man grasps it and ascends with it. Then another man grasps it and it is cut off with him. Then it is joined to him and he ascends with it. So tell me, O Messenger of Allah, by my father, have I hit the mark or have I erred?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "You have hit the mark and you have erred." He said, "What is it that I have hit the mark in, and what is it that I have erred in?" But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to tell him.

Muhammad ibn Mihran narrated to me, he said: Muskin the Harani narrated to me, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from al-Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib, who said: “I saw in a dream as if a sun or a moon – Abu Ja’far was unsure which – was being raised from the earth to the sky by strong ropes. I mentioned this to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: ‘That is the death of your nephew,’ meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, referred to himself.”

"I saw in my dream that I shook a sword, and its sheath broke. Then I saw it as those of the believers who were wounded on the day of Uhud. Then I shook it again, and it returned as it was in its finest condition, and it was as what Allah brought of victory and the gathering of the believers. And I also saw in it a good cow, and by Allah, the good is better. And it was the group of believers on the day of Uhud, and the good was what Allah brought of goodness and the reward of truth which He gave us after the day of Badr."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to us on the authority of Hammad ibn Salama, who narrated from Abu Zubair, from Jabir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw in a dream that I was in a strong armor, and I saw cattle being slaughtered. I interpreted the armor as Medina, and the cattle as tribes. By Allah, we are better, and if we stayed in Medina, they would come upon us, and we would fight them.” They said: “By Allah, we were never attacked in pre-Islamic times, so will we be attacked in Islam?” He said: “Then you may do as you wish.” The Ansar said to one another: “Let us return the Prophet (ﷺ) his opinion.” So they came and said: “O Messenger of Allah, you do as you wish.” He said: “Now? It is not for a Prophet to put off his armor until he fights.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "I dislike the shackles (of debt), and I love the restraints (of commitment), for the restraint is stability in the religion."

Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi narrated to me, that Ibn Abi Zinaad narrated to me, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Salim ibn Abdullah, from his father, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "I saw in a dream a black woman, with disheveled hair, spitting, being expelled from Medina and settled in Mahya. I interpreted it as a plague of Medina, which Allah would transfer to Mahya."

On a certain day, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "I saw in a dream a man bringing me a mass of dates, so I ate them, and I found a pit in it, which hurt me when I chewed it. Then he gave me another mass, and I said, ‘Indeed, I found a pit in what you gave me, and it hurt me, so I ate it.’"

Then Abu Bakr said, "Your eye slept, O Messenger of Allah. This is the company you sent, they gained spoils twice, and both times they found a man seeking sanctuary with you."

So I asked Mujahid, "What does he seek sanctuary with you?" He said, "He says, ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

A woman from the people of Medina had a husband who was a merchant and traveled. She would have a dream every time her husband was away from her, and he rarely left her except when she was pregnant. She would come to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and say, “My husband has left as a merchant and has left me pregnant.” She said, “I saw in my dream, as a person sees in sleep, that the gate of my house broke and that I gave birth to a one-eyed boy.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “That is good. Your husband will return to you, if Allah wills, as a righteous man, and you will give birth to a pious son.” She would see this dream two or three times, and each time she would come to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and tell him about it, and he would say to her, “That is good,” and her husband would return and she would give birth to a son. One day, she came as she used to come, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was absent. She had seen that dream, so I said to her, “What are you asking the Messenger of Allah, O slave of Allah?” She said, “It is a dream that I used to see, and I would come to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and ask him about it, and he would say something good, and it would be as he said.” I said, “Then tell me what it was.” She said, “Until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, comes, so that I may present it to him as I used to present it to him.” By Allah, I did not leave her until she told me. I said, “By Allah, if your dream is true, then your husband will die, and you will give birth to a wicked son.” She sat weeping and said, “What is the matter with me when I presented my dream to you?” Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered while she was weeping, and he said to her, “What is the matter, O Aisha?” I told him the story and did not interpret it for her. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Enough, O Aisha! When you pass a dream along to a Muslim, pass it along with goodness, for a dream is as its owner interprets it.” By Allah, her husband died, and I do not see her but she gives birth to a wicked son.
Narrated Abu Najih: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever is able to marry and does not, he is not one of us."

We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as young men who possessed nothing. He said: "O assembly of young men, whoever is able to afford marriage, let him marry; for it is most likely to avert the gaze and guard the chastity. And whoever is not able, let him observe the fast; for the fast is a shield."

Narrated Abdullah: 'Uthman met me while I was with him and said to me, "O Abu Abdur-Rahman, what do you say about a virgin girl who would remind you (of his wife)?" I said, "You have said it." Then I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "O assembly of the young men, whoever is able to marry, let him marry; for it is most guarding of the eyes and most protective of chastity. And whoever is not able, let him fast; for fasting is a restraint."

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said, "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, rebuked Uthman for something, and if he had permitted him to practice asceticism, we would have had ourselves castrated."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade celibacy."

Narrated by Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas: Concerning the affair of ‘Utman bin Maz’un, who neglected his wives, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for him and said, “O ‘Utman! I have not been commanded to practice monasticism. Have you abandoned my Sunnah?” He said, “No, O Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “Indeed, part of my Sunnah is that I pray, sleep, fast, feed, marry, and divorce. So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not from me, O ‘Utman. Indeed, your family has a right over you, and you have a right over yourself.” Sa’d said: By Allah, the Muslims were more united in their opinion that if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confirmed ‘Utman in his state, they would separate and devote themselves (to seclusion).

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Women are married for four reasons: for their religion, their wealth, their beauty, and their family. So, you should seek one who is pious, for wealth disappears, beauty fades, and family connections are broken."

Narrated Jabir: The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned this Hadith.

Umar ibn Shabah narrated: "I proposed marriage to a woman from the Ansar. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'Go and look at her, for it is more likely that compatibility will be found between you.'"

Muhammad ibn Kathir al-‘Abdi of Basra narrated to me, that Sufyan narrated to me, from Yunus, who said: I heard Hasan say: Aqil ibn Abi Talib came to Basra and married a woman from the tribe of Jusham. They said to him, "May you have well-being and children." He said, "Do not say that, for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade us from saying it, and ordered us to say: 'May Allah bless you and bless upon you.'"
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would say, “May Allah bless you and bless upon you, and may He join you both in goodness,” when he blessed someone.
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade a man from proposing marriage while another man was already proposing to the same woman.
Do not bid against your brother’s bid, nor sell where your brother is selling, until he permits you.

Fatima bint Qais reported: That she was married to a man from Quraysh, of the Banu Makhzum, and he divorced her definitively. She sent to her people seeking maintenance, but they said, "You have no maintenance from us." This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he said, "You have no maintenance, and you must observe ‘Iddah (waiting period), and go to the house of Um Sharik, and do not neglect yourself." Then he said, "Indeed, Um Sharik is a woman who is visited by her brothers from the Muhajireen (emigrants). But go to the house of Ibn Um Maktum, for he is a blind man. If you remove your garments, he will see nothing, and do not neglect yourself." So she went to the house of Ibn Um Maktum. When her ‘Iddah was completed, she mentioned that Muawiya and Abu Jahm had proposed marriage to her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "As for Muawiya, he is a man who has no wealth, and as for Abu Jahm, he does not remove his stick from his shoulder. So what about Usama?" It seemed that her people disliked it, so she said, "By Allah, I will not marry anyone except the one the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has mentioned." So she married Usama.

Muhammad ibn ‘Amr said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim said to Fatima, "Fear Allah, for you know in what matter this was." He (Ibn Abbas) said: Allah the Exalted said: #O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their ‘Iddah and count the ‘Iddah accurately and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not drive them out of their homes, nor should they leave [their homes] unless they commit a clear act of immorality. (Surah At-Talaq, 1) # And the immorality is that she openly exposes herself to her husband’s relatives, so if she does that, it is permissible for them to drive her out.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a woman to marry her maternal aunt, or an aunt to marry the daughter of her brother, or a woman to marry her paternal aunt, or a paternal aunt to marry the daughter of her sister, and forbade a younger woman to marry the older woman’s husband, or an older woman to marry the younger woman’s husband.
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a woman from being married to her maternal aunt and to her paternal aunt.

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated: Malik narrated to me from Naafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade *shighaar*.” Malik said: And *shighaar* is that a man marries another man’s daughter on the condition that the other man marries his daughter without a dowry. It was said to Abu Muhammad: Do you see a marriage between them? He said: It does not please me.

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Marry the righteous men and the righteous women." 
Abu Muhammad said: And it was related to me from the Hadith, "And whatever follows them is good."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no marriage except with a guardian."
"There is no marriage except with a guardian."

"Any woman who is married without the permission of her guardian, her marriage is invalid, her marriage is invalid, her marriage is invalid. If they dispute about it, Abu ‘Aasim said, and he once said: If they quarrel, then the ruler is the guardian of one who has no guardian. And if she is harmed thereby, she is entitled to the dowry according to what she has permitted of her private parts."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The orphaned girl is consulted about herself; if she remains silent, then she has given consent, and if she refuses, she is not compelled."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A widow should not be married until she is consulted, and a virgin should not be married until she gives her permission, and her permission is her silence."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “A woman who has been widowed is more deserving of her own self than her guardian, and a virgin must be asked for permission regarding herself, and her permission is her silence.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A virgin female is granted permission, and her permission is her silence."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “A divorced woman has more control over her affairs than her guardian, a virgin woman must be consulted regarding herself, and her silence is an acknowledgement [of consent].”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, that he heard Qasim ibn Muhammad say: He heard Abdur-Rahman ibn Yazid and Mujamma' ibn Yazid al-Ansari narrate that a man among the Ansar, named Khidham, married his daughter to him, but she disliked marrying her father. So she came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and he forbade her from marrying her father. Then she married Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir. Yahya said: It reached him that she was a divorcee.
Khansa bint Khizim came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) after her father had married her while she was a widow, and she disliked it. So he annulled her marriage.
"Any woman whom two guardians marry her, she belongs to the first of them, and any man who sells a sale from two men, it is for the first of them."

Narrated By Rabiah bin Sabrah: That his father informed him: That they accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Hajj of Farewell, and he said, "Enjoy yourselves with these women." And enjoyment with us means marriage. So we presented this to the women, and they refused unless we set a term between ourselves and them. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do so."

So I and my cousin went out with a garment, and I had a garment with me, and his garment was finer than mine, and I was younger than him. We came upon a woman and she was impressed by my youth and impressed by his garment, and she said, "A garment like his garment." The term between me and her was ten [days]. I spent the night with her, and then I went out in the morning, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing between the pillar and the door, and he said, "O people, I had permitted you to enjoy yourselves with the women, but Allah has forbidden it until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever has anything of them, let him release her, and do not take back from what you have given them.”
Narrated by Rabia bin Sabra Al-Juhani from his father: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade temporary marriage (mut’ah) in the year of the conquest.”

Muhammad narrated to me, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Zuhri, from Hasan, and Abdullah, from their father, that he said: I heard Ali saying to Ibn Abbas: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the mut'ah (temporary marriage), the mut'ah of women, and the meat of domesticated donkeys, in the year of Khaybar."
The one in ihram neither marries nor is married.

Narrated by Abu Salama: I asked Aishah about the dowries of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and she said: "His dowry for his wives was twelve awqiyahs and a nash." She said: "Do you know what a nash is?" I said: "No." She said: "Half an awqiyah. This was the dowry of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) for his wives."

Umar ibn al-Khattab delivered a sermon, praising and glorifying Allah. Then he said: “Indeed, do not exaggerate in the dowries of women, for if there were any honor in the world or piety before Allah, your Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, would have been the most generous to them. No woman was given a more generous dowry than his wives, and no daughter of yours would be given a dowry exceeding twelve awqiya. Indeed, one of you may exaggerate in his wife’s dowry until animosity remains in his heart, to the point where he says, ‘You are obligated to me with the weight of a waterskin or the sweat of a waterskin.’”

A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said, “Indeed, I have devoted myself to Allah and His Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “I have no need for women.” A man said, “Marry her.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Give her a garment.” He said, “I do not have [any].” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Give her even a ring of iron.” He said, “I am ill for him.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “What of the Quran do you have?” He said, “Such and such [portions].” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “I have married her for what you have of the Quran.”

Abu al-Walid and Hajjaj narrated: We were told by Shu'bah, who said: Abu Ishaq told me, that he heard Abu 'Ubaidah narrating from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught us the Khutbah (speech) of need: "All praise is due to Allah. Indeed, all praise is for Allah. We praise Him and seek His help and forgiveness. We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of our souls. Whoever Allah guides, there is no misguider for him, and whoever He misguides, there is no guide for him. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger." Then he recites three verses: #O you who believe, fear Allah in the manner He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims. [Surah Al-Imran, 3:102]#, #O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from one soul, and from him He created his wife, and from them both He created men and women. And fear Allah, whom you will be questioned about. And [fear] the ties of kinship. Indeed, Allah is over all things Aware. [Surah An-Nisa, 4:1]#, #O you who believe, fear Allah and speak a sound statement [i.e., correct and truthful words]. [70] He will amend your works and forgive your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, he has achieved a great success. [71] [Surah Al-Ahzab, 33:70-71]# Then he speaks his need.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The most binding of agreements is that by which you have permitted yourselves [conjugal relations]."

Abu Nu'man narrated: Hammad bin Zayd narrated to me from Thabit, from Anas: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saw a yellowish tinge on Abdur-Rahman bin ‘Auf. He said: “What is this yellowness?” He said: “I married a woman for the weight of a date-stone of gold.” He said: “May Allah bless you, and have a feast even if it be with a sheep.”

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Sa’id, from ‘Uqba ibn Khalid, from ‘Ubaidullah, from Nafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If anyone is invited to a feast, he should accept it."

Abu Muhammad said: He should accept the invitation, but eating is not obligatory upon him.
"Whoever has two wives and inclines to one of them, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of his body tilted."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would distribute (charity) and be just, and he would say: ‘O Allah, this is my distribution in that which I possess. So do not reproach me for that which You possess and that which I do not possess.’”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) traveled, he would draw lots between his wives, and whichever of them her arrow came out for, she would travel with him."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "For a virgin (baker) there are seven (days of purity), and for a widow (thayyib) there are three (days)."

Umm Salama (RA) narrated: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Umm Salama, he stayed with her for three days and said: "It is not befitting for your people that they feel humiliated because of you. If you wish, I will do that for you seven times, and if I do that for you seven times, I will do that for all my wives."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) married me in Shawwal, and I was brought to him in Shawwal. So which of his wives was dearest to him than I?" She said: "And she preferred that the women be brought to him in Shawwal."

Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "What prevents any of you from saying when he enters his wife, 'In the name of Allah, O Allah, protect us from Satan, and protect what You have provided us from Satan,'? If Allah decrees a child, Satan will not harm it."

Narrated by Huraymi bin Abdullah: I heard Khuzayma bin Thabit saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “Indeed, Allah does not feel shame because of the truth. Do not approach women in their ‘ajuz.”

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: The Jews said to the Muslims, "If a man comes to his wife from behind, their child will be cross-eyed." So Allah revealed: "Your wives are fields for you, so go to your fields as you will." [Surah Al-Baqarah (2):223]

Narrated Abdullah ibn Mas’ud: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a woman and she pleased him. So he came to Sawda while she was making perfume and women were with her. He excused himself [from them], and then he fulfilled his need. Then he said: “Whoever of you sees a woman who pleases him, let him go to his wife, for she has that which she has.”

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey. When we were returning, I hurried. A rider overtook me, and I turned around, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said to me, "What made you hurry, O Jabir?" I said, "I have recently returned from a wedding." He said, "Did you marry her as a virgin or a widow?" I said, "A widow." He said, "Would it not have been better for you to play with a virgin and she with you?" Then he said to me, "When you arrive, be wise, be wise." When we arrived, we went to enter (the wedding celebration). He said, "Wait until we enter at night (evening), so that the disheveled may become tidy and the shy may become modest."

Hudayfah ibn ‘Abdullah al-Salami reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was about to prohibit the practice of Ghilah until I remembered that the Persians and Romans do it, and it does not harm their offspring.” Abu Muhammad said: Ghilah is that a man has intercourse with a woman while she is breastfeeding.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) never struck a servant, nor struck anything with his hand ever, except in Jihad in the way of Allah."

Narrated ‘Iyās bin ‘Abdullāh bin Abī Dhubb: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Do not strike the female slaves of Allah.” Then ‘Umar bin al-Khuttāb came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, “They have become aggressive towards their husbands.” So, he permitted them to strike them, but then many women surrounded the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) complaining about their husbands. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: “Indeed, many women have surrounded the family of Muhammad complaining about their husbands; these are not among the best of you.”

Narrated Abdullah ibn Zam’a: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed the people one day and gave them a sermon about women. He said: “How does it befit a man that he beats his wife like a slave? And perhaps he will lie with her at the end of the day?”

Narrated by Abu Darr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A woman is created from a rib; so if you try to straighten it, you will break it, but if you leave it as it is, then it will remain crooked. Indeed, in her is crookedness and perversity."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “A woman is like a rib; she is inclined, so if you straighten her, you break her, and if you leave her as she is, you get enjoyment from her, but she has a crookedness.”

Narrated Abu Sa’id: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about coitus interruptus (contraception). He (the Prophet) said: “Do you do that? It is alright for you not to do that, for Allah has decreed every soul that He will create.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Ibn ‘Awn narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn Bishr, who relates the Hadith back to Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: We said, “O Messenger of Allah, a man has a female slave and has relations with her, and he dislikes her becoming pregnant. Should he abstain from her?” And a man has a wife who is breastfeeding, and he has relations with her and dislikes her becoming pregnant. Should he abstain from her?” He said, “It is not permissible for you to do that, for it is only destiny.” Ibn ‘Awn said: I mentioned this to Hasan, and he said: By Allah, it seems this is a deterrent! By Allah, it seems this is a deterrent!

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No one is more protective of privacy than Allah, and for that reason He forbade indecent acts. And no one loves praise more than Allah does."

Narrated by Abu Al-Mughirah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is jealousy that Allah loves, and there is jealousy that Allah hates. The jealousy that Allah loves is jealousy in matters of suspicion (doubt), and the jealousy that Allah hates is jealousy in matters other than suspicion."

It was narrated to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) that Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah said: “If I found a man with her, I would strike her with a sword, not lightly.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “Do you wonder at Sa’d’s jealousy? I am more jealous than Sa’d, and Allah is more jealous than I. Because of this, He forbade blatant and concealed immoralities. No one is more jealous than Allah, and He loves excuses the most. Because of this, He sent prophets as bearers of good news and warners. No one loves praise more than Allah, and because of this, He promised Paradise.
"Whenever a woman leaves the bed of her husband during the night without a valid reason, the angels curse her until she returns to it."

Narrated by Sahl bin Sa’d: ‘Uwaimir Al-‘Ajlani said, “O Messenger of Allah, what about a man who finds his wife with another man? Should he kill him, and they kill him, or what should he do?” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Allah has revealed (a ruling) concerning you and your wife, so go and bring her to me.” Sahl said, “So we cursed each other, and I was with the people at the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). When they finished cursing each other, I said, ‘I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah. If I retain her, I divorce her three times.’” He (the Messenger of Allah) did not order him before that. Sahl said, “Ibn Shihab said, ‘That became the practice of those who curse each other afterwards.’ Muhammad bin Yusuf narrated from Al-Awza’i, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl bin Sa’d, that ‘Uwaimir came to ‘Asim bin ‘Adiyy, who was the chief of Banu ‘Ajlan, and he mentioned the same story, but he did not mention, “I divorce her three times.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, and Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulaiman narrated to us, saying: I heard Sa’id ibn Jubayr say: “I was asked about the mutually cursing (couple) during the governorship of Mus’ab ibn Zubayr: Should they be separated? I did not know what to say, so I went until I reached the home of Abd Allah ibn Umar. I told the servant to announce me, and he said, ‘He is occupied and you cannot enter.’ I heard Ibn Umar’s voice and he said, ‘Ibn Jubayr?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Enter,’ and he said, ‘You have not come to me this hour except for a need.’ So I entered and found him reclining on a saddle blanket, using a pillow of a cushion or a bolster – Abd Allah was unsure whether the stuffing was wool or not. I said, ‘O Abu Abd al-Rahman, the mutually cursing (couple), should they be separated?’ He said, ‘Glory be to Allah, yes! The first to ask about this was so-and-so, who said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, should a man see his wife committing a shameful act, what should he do?’ If he remains silent, he remains silent over a great matter, and if he speaks, it is like that?’ The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, remained silent and did not answer him. Then he stood up for a need, and after that, he came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, the matter I asked you about, I have been afflicted by it.’ So Allah revealed these verses in Surah An-Nur: ‘And those who accuse their wives of immorality, and have no witness except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies that he is truthful. And the fifth [testimony] is that the wrath of Allah would be upon him if he is of the liars. And [as for] the wife, [it is] that she avoids punishment by testifying four times that he is truthful. And the fifth [testimony] is that the wrath of Allah would be upon her if he is of the truthful.’ Then he called the man and recited these verses to him, reminding him of Allah, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said, ‘I have not lied against her.’ Then he called the woman and admonished her and reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said, ‘By the One who sent you with the truth, he is
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced the divorcée and attached the child to his mother.
"Anyone who marries without the permission of his master or his family is a fornicator."
"Any slave who marries without the permission of his master, he is a fornicator."
"The child belongs to the bed (marriage bed), and the fornicator has the stone (social disgrace)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “A child belongs to the bed.”

‘Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas entrusted his brother, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, to take custody of the son of Zam’a’s slave girl. Utbah then claimed, “He is my son.” When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) arrived during the time of the conquest, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas took the son of Zam’a’s slave girl, and he was the most like Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas in appearance. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “He is yours, O ‘Abd ibn Zam’a, because he was born on his father’s bed.” And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “O Sawda daughter of Zam’a, conceal yourself from him due to the resemblance he bears to Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas.” Sawda daughter of Zam’a.

Narrated Abu Huraira: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying when the verse of the curse (relating to false accusations of lineage) was revealed: “Any woman who introduces a kinship among a people that is not theirs, she is not from Allah in anything, and Allah will not admit her to His Paradise. And any man who denies his child while looking at him, Allah will conceal Himself from him and disgrace him among the first and the last.” Abdullah said: Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi said, and Sa’id was narrating to him about it, in this manner: And this Hadith has reached me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

Narrated ‘Adiyy bin Thabit from his father: I met my uncle with a banner, and I asked him, “Where are you going?” He said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me to a man who married his father’s wife, and ordered me to strike his neck and take his wealth.”

Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated: Wahb narrated to me from Dawood ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from a man from the Ansar named Ziyad, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Suppose the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed away, would it be permissible for him to marry?" He said: "Yes, Allah has only permitted for him a specific type of women, and described a characteristic to him." Then he said: "Women are not permissible for you after this characteristic."
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did not die until Allah permitted him to marry as many women as he wished."
Narrated Anas: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed Safiyyah and made her manumission her dowry.
Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed Safiyya and married her, and made her manumission her dowry.

Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, from Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayy al-Hamdani, who said: I was with Al-Sha’bi, and a man came to him from Khurasan. He said: “O Abu ‘Amru, the people of Khurasan say about a man: if he emancipates his slave girl and then marries her, is he like a rider on his female camel?” Al-Sha’bi said: “Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa narrated to me from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ‘Three are given their reward twice: a person from the People of the Book who believes in his prophet, then he finds the Prophet (ﷺ) and believes in him and follows him, and a slave who fulfills his obligation to Allah and the obligation to his masters, then he has two rewards, and a man who has a slave girl, so he provides for her, and improves her provision, and educates her, and improves her education, then he emancipates her and marries her, then he has two rewards.’” Then he said to the man: “Take this hadith without anything, for people used to travel to Medina for less than this.” Hushaym said: “They informed me in Basrah, so I went to him and asked him about it.”

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to me, from Shu’bah, from Salih ibn Hayy, from Al-Sha’bi, from Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), a narration similar to this hadith.

Narrated Abdullah: A man married a woman and did not impose a dower upon her, and did not consummate the marriage with her, and he died. He said about her: She is entitled to the dower of other women, she must observe the waiting period ('iddah), and she is entitled to inheritance. Ma’qil Al-Ashja’i said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged the case of Birwa bint Washiq, a woman from Banu Ruwasa, in the same way as you have judged.” He (Abdullah) said: Then he rejoiced at that. Muhammad and Sufyan said: We follow this.

Aisha narrated: She was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in Hafsa’s house, and she heard the voice of a man. She said: “O Messenger of Allah, I heard the voice of a man in your house.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “I think it was so-and-so, a foster brother of Hafsa.” Aisha said: “O Messenger of Allah, if so-and-so were alive as a foster brother of her, would he enter upon me?” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Yes, what is forbidden by foster relationship is forbidden by blood relationship.”

Aisha related: Her maternal uncle, the brother of Abu al-Qais, came to ask for permission to enter her presence after the hijab had been imposed. She refused to grant him permission until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and asked for permission. When the Prophet (ﷺ) came, she mentioned this to him, saying: "My uncle, the brother of Abu al-Qais, came and I sent him away until I asked your permission." He said: "Is he not your uncle?" She said: "It is only a woman who suckled me, not a man." He said: "He is your uncle, let him enter upon you." Aisha used to say: That which is forbidden by suckling is forbidden as that which is forbidden by birth.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "That which is forbidden by breastfeeding is forbidden as that which is forbidden by lineage." Malik said: And he told me, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from ‘Amrah, from Aisha, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), with a similar wording.
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Do not forbid the single date and the two dates."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Abu Khalil, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ummu al-Fadl: That a man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have married a woman and I have another (wife). The first one claimed that she suckled my other wife." The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Do not forbid [her] the fosterling, or the two fosterlings."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Revelation of the Qur'an began with ten known sucklings which would render [women] unlawful [to a man], then they were abrogated by five known sucklings. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed away while they were among that which was recited from the Qur'an."

Uthman ibn Muhammad narrated: 'Abdah narrated to me from Hisham from his father, from Hajjaj ibn Hajjaj al-Aslami, from his father, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, what removes the reproach of foster feeding from me?" He said: "The Ghurrah: a slave or a female slave."

I married the daughter of Abu Ihhab, and a black slave woman came and said, “I have breastfed you both.” So I went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and mentioned this to him, and he turned away from me. Abu ‘Aasim said: He said this in the third or fourth instance. He said: How could that be, when it has been said? And he forbade me from her. Abu ‘Aasim said: And ‘Umar ibn Sa’id ibn Abi Husayn reported from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: “How could that be?” And he did not say, “He forbade me from her.” Abu Muhammad said: This is how it is with us.

Aisha narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me while a man was with me. He changed his countenance, as if he disliked it. I said: He is my brother from breastfeeding. He (the Prophet) said: "Let your womenfolk look to their foster brothers, for breastfeeding is [a relationship established] due to hunger."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: Sahla bint Suhayl ibn Amr, who was a wife of Abu Hurayfa ibn Utba ibn Rabia, came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said, "Indeed, Salim, the slave of Abu Hurayfa, enters upon us, and I am breastfeeding. We only see him as a child." And Abu Hurayfa had adopted him as the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) had adopted Zayd. So Allah the Exalted revealed: "Call them by their fathers, that is more just in the sight of Allah." [Quran 33:5] Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered her at that time to suckle Salim. 

Abu Muhammad said: This is specifically for Salim.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who brings about a divorce and the one who legalizes it.

Hind, the wife of Abu Sufyan, came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a miser, and he does not give me and my children enough unless I take it from him without his knowledge. Is there any sin on me in that?” He said: “Take what is sufficient for you and your children in a good manner.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The best of you are those who are best to their families, and when your companion dies, leave him [alone]."

Aisha said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, married me when I was a girl of six years old. We then migrated to Medina and settled among the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj. I fell ill, and my head split open. Then Jumaima applied a plaster. Um Ruman came to me while I was in a cradle, and I was with my female companions. She shouted at me, and I went to her, not knowing what she wanted. She took my hand and stopped me at the door of the house. I was bleeding until some of my breath subsided. Then she took something of water and wiped my face and head with it. She then brought me into the house, and there were women of the Ansar in the house. They said, ‘May it be good and blessed, and may it be a good omen.’ So they handed me over to them, and they took care of my condition. I did not realize anything until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came on the morning of the day, and he handed me over to him, and I was then a girl of nine years old."

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, that Malik narrated to me, from Naafi’, from Ibn Umar: That he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. So Umar mentioned this to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he said: "Order him to take her back and retain her until she is purified, then menstruates, then is purified, and then if he wishes, he may retain her, or divorce her before intercourse. That is the waiting period that Allah has commanded to be given to women who are divorced."

Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Abdur-Rahman, who said: I heard Salim mentioning, from Ibn Umar: That Umar said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when Ibn Umar divorced his wife, "Order him to take her back, then divorce her while she is pure." Abu Muhammad said: Ibn al-Mubarak and Waqi' narrated: "Or while she is pregnant."
Umar said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, divorced Hafsa, then he reconciled with her."

Narrated by Anas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) divorced Hafsa, and then took her back. 

Abu Muhammad said: Ali ibn al-Madini disliked this Hadith and said: We do not have this Hadith in Basra from Humayd.

Al-Hakam narrated to me, he said: Yahya ibn Hamza told me, from Sulaiman ibn Dawud, that Zuhri narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: Al-Hakam said: Yahya ibn Hamza told me, “That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: ‘Let none touch the Quran except one who is pure, and let there be no divorce before a waiting period, and let there be no manumission until a purchase price is agreed upon.’”

Abu Muhammad was asked about Sulaiman. He said: I believe he was a scribe from the scribes of Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Aziz.

Narrated Aisha: A woman from the tribe of Quraza came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while Abu Bakr and Khalid bin Sa’id bin Al-’Aas were present at the door, waiting to be allowed to enter the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She said: “O Messenger of Allah! I was with Rifa’a Al-Qurazi and he divorced me irrevocably.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Do you want to go back to Rifa’a? No, not until your back and his back taste (i.e., you both experience the pain of separation).” Khalid bin Sa’id called out to Abu Bakr: “Do you not see what this woman is saying openly before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: A man from the Banu Qurayza divorced his wife, and Abdur-Rahman ibn Zubair married her. She then came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of Allah, he has nothing with him except what is like this eyelash.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to her: “Perhaps you want to return to Rifaa’a? No, until your ‘usayla’ tastes it, or he tastes your ‘usayla.’”
I asked Aishah about the khirar (divorce option), and she said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has given us the choice, so is it a divorce?"
"Whoever of the women asks her husband for divorce without justification, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

Habiba bint Sa’hl reported that Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas married her, and she mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had intended to marry her. She was a neighbor of his, and Thabit struck her. So she appeared at the door of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the darkness of night. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out and saw her and asked, "Who is this?" She said, "I am Habiba bint Sa’hl." He said, "What is the matter with you?" She said, "Neither I nor Thabit." Then Thabit came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "Take from her and let her go." She said, "O Messenger of Allah, he takes everything I give him." So he took from her, and she returned to her people.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me from Zubayr ibn Sa’id, a man from Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib, who said: A report reached me of a tradition from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Ali ibn Yazid ibn Rukana, while he was in a village he owned, so I visited him and asked him. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather that he divorced his wife outright. Then he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and mentioned this to him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "What did you intend?" He said: One [divorce]. He said: "By Allah?" He said: "By Allah." He said: "That is what you intended."

I was a man who was afflicted by women more than others. Then, when the month of Ramadan approached, I feared being afflicted during the night, and that would continue until morning. So, I feigned [abstinence] until the month passed. One night, while she was serving me, something was revealed to me from her, and I did not long before I had intercourse with her. When morning came, I went out to my people and told them, and said, "Accompany me to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." They said, "By Allah, we will not go with you, for we fear that the Qur'an will be revealed concerning you, or that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, will say something about you that would bring us shame. And we will deliver you to [the consequences of] your deed."

So, I went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and recounted my story to him. He said, "O Salama, are you doing this?" I said, "I am doing this." He said, "O Salama, are you doing this?" I said, "I am doing this." He said, "O Salama, are you doing this?" I said, "I am doing this, and here I am, restraining my soul. So, judge for me as you see Allah guiding you." He said, "Manumit a slave." I struck the neck of a slave, and said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, I do not possess any slave other than him." He said, "Fast two consecutive months." I said, "Has anything afflicted me except during fasting?" He said, "Feed a wasq of dates to sixty poor people." I said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, we spent the night in fear, and we had no food." He said, "Go to the keeper of the charity of Banu Zurayq, and let him give it to you, and feed sixty poor people a wasq of dates, and you and your family eat the remainder."

I came to my people and said, "I found narrowness and bad counsel among you, and I found spaciousness and good counsel with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he has ordered me to your charity."

Fatima bint Qays said, "Her husband divorced her three times, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not order him to provide her with maintenance or lodging." Salama said, "I mentioned this to Ibrahim, and he said, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said, 'We will not abandon the Book of our Lord or the Sunnah of His Prophet because of the statement of a woman.' So he ordered her to be provided with lodging and maintenance."

Fatima bint Qais said, "My husband divorced me three times. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered her to observe 'iddah (waiting period) at the home of her cousin, the son of Um Maktum."
"‘Umar (RA) said: “We will not abandon the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of His Prophet because of the statement of a woman: ‘The divorced thrice has maintenance and lodging.’”

ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad narrated: Hafs narrated to me from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, who said: ʿUmar said: “We do not accept the statement of a woman regarding a matter of Allah’s religion: ‘The woman divorced three times is entitled to lodging and sustenance.’” Abu Muhammad said: “I do not see lodging and sustenance for the divorced woman.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sulaiman ibn Yasar informed him, saying: Abu Salama ibn Abdur-Rahman informed him, that he and Ibn Abbas gathered at the home of Abu Huraira, and they discussed a man’s death and a woman subsequently giving birth after a few nights. Ibn Abbas said: "Her waiting period ends after the end of the two periods (of waiting)." And Abu Salama said: "When she gives birth, her waiting period is over." They argued about this matter between them. Then Abu Huraira said: "I side with the son of my brother," meaning Abu Salama. So they sent Kuraib, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, to Umm Salama and asked her. Umm Salama mentioned that Subay'a bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyya’s husband died, and she gave birth after a few nights. A man from the Banu Abd ad-Dar, known as Abu Sanebal, proposed marriage to her and informed her that her waiting period had ended, so she intended to marry someone else. Then Abu Sanebal said to her: "You have not become permissible." So Subay'a mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he ordered her to marry.

Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The husband of Subay'a bint al-Harith passed away, and she gave birth after a few days following his death. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered her to marry."

Subay’ah bint al-Harith gave birth to her child twenty-three nights after the death of her husband. When she recovered from her post-natal bleeding, she began to seek intimacy with her husband. This was criticized, and her matter was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: “If you do so, her waiting period has ended.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Al-Aswad: That Subay’ah gave birth a few days after her husband’s death and she inquired [about something]. Abu Sannabla criticized her, so she asked or mentioned her matter to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he ordered her to marry.

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "It is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn over anyone other than her husband for more than three days."

Zaynab bint Abi Salama reported from Um Habibah, daughter of Abu Sufyan, that a brother or close friend of hers died, and she went to a yellow plant and began to rub her hands on it, saying: "I do this only because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'It is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days except for her husband, in which case she mourns four months and ten days.'"

Hashim ibn Qasim narrated: I was told by Hashim ibn Qasim, that Shu'bah told me, from Humaid ibn Nafe', who said: I heard Zaynab bint Um Salama narrating from her mother or a wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), in a similar manner.

Narrated ‘Umm ‘Atiyyah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “A woman should not observe ‘iddah (waiting period) for more than three days except for a husband, for whom she observes ‘iddah for four months and ten days. During this period, she should not wear dyed clothes except the clothes of ‘Asb (a type of garment), nor use kohl, nor apply perfume except in the least amount of purity when she bathes from her menstrual period – a handful of kasturi (musk) and fingernails.”

Al-Furay'a bint Malik informed me that she asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for permission to return to her family, for her husband had gone in search of his slaves who had run away, and he overtook them until he was at the edge of al-Qudum, when they killed him. So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "Remain in your home until the decree is fulfilled." I said, "He has not left me in a home I own, nor has he provided me with sustenance." So he said, "Remain until the decree is fulfilled." So she observed ‘iddah within it for four months and ten days. She said, "Then when ‘Uthman was in power, he sent for me and asked me about that, so I informed him, and he followed that and ruled according to it."

Abu 'Asim narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me from Abu Zubayr from Jabir who said: "My maternal aunt was divorced and she wanted to prune her palm trees. A man forbade her from doing so. She said, 'So I went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and mentioned this to him. He said: 'Go out and prune your palm trees, for you might give in charity or do a good deed.'"

Aisha related: She intended to buy Barira, and her masters wanted to stipulate her manumission. She mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: "Buy her, for manumission belongs to the one who sets her free." So she bought her and freed her, and gave her a choice between her husband and herself, and he was free. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was brought some meat, and he said: "From where is this?" It was said: "It was given as a gift to Barira." He said: "It is a sadaqah for her, and a gift for us."

Aisha (RA) said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) came to me and I presented to him food that contained no meat. He said: "Did I not see a pot set up for you?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is meat which Barira has testified to (as a gift)." She had presented it as a gift to us. He said: "It is a sadaqah (charity) on her behalf, and it is a gift from her to us." She had a husband, and when she was freed, she was given a choice.

Aisha related: When Aisha freed Barira, her husband was a slave. So Allah’s Messenger (peace be upon him) encouraged her regarding him. She kept saying to Allah’s Messenger (peace be upon him), "Does it not behoove me to leave him?" He (the Prophet) said, "Yes." She said, "Then I have left him."

Ibrahim reported: 'Abdullah b. 'Umar said, "I heard 'Umar (RA) say: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Woman who asks her husband for more rights than what is due to her, will not be allowed to enter Paradise.'"

Abu ‘Aasim narrated to me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. He said: Ziyad ibn Sa’d informed me from Hilal ibn Usama from Abu Maymuna Sulayman, a servant of the people of Medina, that he was with Abu Huraira. A woman came to him and said: “My husband wants to take my son away.” Abu Huraira said: “I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a woman came to him and said: ‘My husband wants to take my son away, or he wants to take my child. He has benefited me and given me water from the well of Abi ‘Inaba.’” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Let them cast lots.” Abu ‘Aasim said: “Or he said: ‘Let them draw lots.’” Then her husband came and said: “Who will argue with me about my son or my child?” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “O boy! This is your father, and this is your mother. Take the hand of whichever you wish.” Abu ‘Aasim said: “And follow whichever they choose.” So he took his mother’s hand and they left.

Abu 'Aasim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, he said: Muzahir, the son of Aslam, informed me that he heard Qasim ibn Muhammad relate from 'Aisha, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who said: "A slave woman has two divorces, and her 'idda is two menstrual courses." Abu 'Aasim said: I heard it from Muzahir.

Narrated by Abu Sa’id, he said regarding the captives of Autas: “No pregnant woman should be harmed until she delivers her burden, and no woman who is not pregnant until she observes a menstrual course.”

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The pen has been lifted from three [persons]: the sleeping until he awakens, the minor until he reaches puberty, and the insane until he regains sanity." Hammad also said: "And from the bewildered until he regains sanity."

Narrated Abu Amama: 'Uthman said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'It is not permissible to shed the blood of a Muslim man in any of three ways: (1) committing disbelief after having professed faith, (2) committing adultery after having been chaste, or (3) killing a person without a just cause, in which case he must be killed."

Narrated ‘Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “It is not permissible to shed the blood of a person who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am His Messenger, except for one of three: a soul for a soul, a married adulterer, and one who abandons his religion, separating from the community.”

Safwan ibn Umayya was sleeping in the mosque, and a man came to him while he was asleep and pulled his garment from beneath his head. He awoke from it and pursued the man, seized him, and took him to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). Safwan said, “O Messenger of Allah, I was sleeping in the mosque, and this man came to me and pulled my garment from beneath my head. I pursued him and seized him.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered him to be cut [his hand]. Safwan said, “O Messenger of Allah, my garment was not sufficient to warrant this punishment.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “Would it not have been so before you brought it to me?”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The hand is to be cut off for stealing a quarter of a dinar or more."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off the hand of a thief, and its value was three dirhams.

Aisha narrated: The Quraysh were concerned about the affair of the Makhzumite woman who stole. They said, "Who will speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about her?" They said, "Who would dare to speak to him except Usama ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" So Usama spoke to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Are you interceding in a matter concerning a limit set by Allah?" Then he stood up and delivered a sermon, saying, "Your people perished because when a noble person stole among them, they would leave him, but when a weak person stole among them, they would apply the punishment. By Allah, if Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad, were to steal, I would cut off her hand."

Narrated by Abu Ammya Al-Mazumi: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought a thief who confessed his theft, and no property was found with him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I do not think you stole.” He said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “I do not think you stole.” He said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “Go, cut off his hand, then bring him to me.” So they cut off his hand, then they brought him to him. He said, “Seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.” He said, “I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “O Allah! Forgive him, O Allah! Forgive him.”
"There is no cutting (of a tree) in fruit or a cluster (of grapes)."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "There is no cutting [of a tree] in fruit or in clusters."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There is no cutting [of a branch] in a fruit tree, nor in [a plant with] excessive growth.”

Narrated Rafi' ibn Khadij: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying: "There is no cutting (of dates) in a thamar or kathir." He (the narrator) said: "And thamar is the fruit of the palm tree, and kathir is the jummar (the date before it ripens)."
I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "There is no punishment of cutting off [a hand] in abundance."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no cutting off [of the hand] for the one who seizes [something], nor for the one who steals a small amount, nor for the one who betrays [a trust]."

Narrated Anas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was brought a man who had consumed wine, and he struck him with two palm leaves. Then Abu Bakr did the same. When Umar became caliph, he consulted the people, and Abdur-Rahman bin ‘Auf said, “The lightest punishment is eighty [lashes].” So Umar acted accordingly.

Hudhaifa ibn al-Manadhir al-Raqashi said: I witnessed Uthman ibn Affan and al-Walid ibn Uqba was brought before him. Ali said: "The Prophet ﷺ flogged forty, Abu Bakr flogged forty, and Umar flogged eighty; and each was a practice (sunna)."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn ‘Urwah ibn Mas’ud ath-Thaqafi from ‘Amr ibn ash-Sharid from his father: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "If anyone of you drinks [alcohol], strike him, then if he returns, strike him, then if he returns, strike him, then if he returns for a fourth time, kill him."
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “It is not permissible for anyone to strike another person more than ten strokes, except as a penalty prescribed by Allah.”

Abu 'Asim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from Abu Salama, from Jabir: That a man from the Banu 'Uslam came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and informed him that he had committed adultery and confessed that he had committed adultery four times. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered him to be stoned, and he had already been married.

Narrated Jabir bin Samura: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was brought a man named Ma’iz bin Malik, a short man wearing only an izar (lower garment) and no cloak. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was reclining on a cushion on his left side, and he spoke to him, but I did not know what he was saying to him, and I was far from him, with people between me and him. Then he said, "Take him and stone him." Then he said, "Bring him back." He spoke to him again, and I heard him, though there were people between me and him, and he said, "Take him and stone him." Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) stood up and delivered a sermon, and I heard him. Then he said, "Whenever we set out for the path of Allah, one of us leaves behind a ram’s ewe that gives milk to a woman, is it possible that we can leave behind any of them without punishing him?” By Allah, I cannot control anyone among them except by punishing him.”

Narrated Abu Huraira, Zaid ibn Khalid, and Shibl: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "I implore you by Allah, judge between us according to the Book of Allah.” His opponent, who was more knowledgeable than him, said, “He has told the truth, judge between us according to the Book of Allah, and allow me to speak, O Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “Speak.” He said, “My son used to be unkind to my family, and he committed adultery with my wife. I ransomed him with one hundred sheep and a servant. I asked some men of knowledge, and they informed me that the penalty for my son is one hundred lashes and exile for a year, and the penalty for this woman is stoning.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will judge between you according to the Book of Allah: the one hundred sheep and the servant are returned to you, and your son will receive one hundred lashes and exile for a year, and O ‘Unays, go to the wife of this man and question her. If she confesses, stone her.” She confessed, and she was stoned.

I was among those who stoned him. Abu Muhammad said: meaning Ma’iz ibn Malik. When he felt the impact of the stones, he trembled with intense fear. We mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: “Why didn’t you leave him alone?”

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Set out to Ma’iz bin Malik and stone him.” So we set out with him to Baqi’ Al-Gharqad. By Allah, we neither secured him nor dug a grave for him, but he stood up and we stoned him with stones, pottery, and thorns.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Bashir ibn al-Mujahir narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Buridah narrated to me from his father, who said: I was sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when a man named Ma'iz ibn Malik came to him and confessed to adultery. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) dismissed him three times. Then he came for the fourth time and confessed. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered that a grave be dug for him and he was placed in it up to his chest, and the people were ordered to stone him.

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a man and a woman among them who had committed adultery. He (ﷺ) said, "How do you deal with those who commit adultery among you?" They said, "We find nothing (to punish them with)." Then ‘Abdullah ibn Salam said, "You lie. In the Torah, there is stoning." So, they said, "Bring the Torah." They brought it, and one of their scholars placed his hand over the verse of stoning and said, "What is this?" They said, "This is the verse of stoning." So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them to be stoned, and they were stoned near where the bodies are placed near the mosque. ‘Abdullah said, "I saw her companion shielding her from the stones."

Umar said, "Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, with the truth, and revealed to him the Book, and within what He revealed was the verse of stoning. We recited it, memorized it, and understood it. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stoned, and we stoned after him. I fear that if time prolongs for the people, someone will say, ‘We do not find the verse of stoning in the Book of Allah.’ Stoning is indeed in the Book of Allah, a right upon those who commit adultery among men and women if they are married, when there is clear evidence against them, or if there is pregnancy or confession."

Narrated by Zayd ibn Thabit: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit adultery, then stone them both, without fail."

I was sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when a woman from the Banu Ghamid came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery, and I want you to purify me.” He said to her, “Go back.”

The next morning, she came to him again and confessed her adultery in his presence, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, purify me, perhaps you will restore me as you restored Ma’iz ibn Malik.” She said, “By Allah, I am pregnant.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to her, “Go back until you give birth.”

When she gave birth, she came to him carrying the baby in a cloth and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have given birth.” He said, “Go, breastfeed him, then wean him.”

When she weaned him, she came to him with the baby in her hand holding a piece of bread, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have weaned him.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) ordered the baby to be given to a Muslim man, and ordered a grave to be dug for her, and she was placed in it up to her chest. Then he ordered the people to stone her, and Khalid ibn al-Walid came forward with a stone and threw it at her head, and the blood splashed on Khalid ibn al-Walid’s cheek. He cursed her, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) heard him cursing her, so he said, “Enough, O Khalid, do not curse her. By the One in whose hand is my soul, she has repented a repentance that if the owner of a garment repented like her, he would be forgiven.”

Then he ordered that she be prayed over and buried.

A woman from the Banu Jahina tribe came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) while pregnant as a result of adultery. She said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have committed a transgression, so impose the punishment upon me.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) called for her guardian, and he said, “Go and treat her well, and when she gives birth to her child, bring her to me.” He did so, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered that her clothes be loosened, then ordered her to be stoned (with pebbles), and then he prayed for her. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, “O Messenger of Allah, do you pray for her after she has committed adultery?” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “Indeed, she has repented with a repentance that, if it were divided among seventy people from the people of Medina, it would suffice them. And have you found anything better than her offering herself to Allah?”

Narrated by Khalid bin Makhlad, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaidullah bin ‘Abdullah bin ‘Utbah, from Zaid bin Khalid Al-Juhani and Abu Hurairah: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was asked about a female slave who commits adultery and is not chaste. He said: "If she commits adultery, flog her, and if she commits it again, flog her." He said: "What about the third or the fourth time?" He said: "Sell her, even for a braid."

Narrated ‘Ubada bin As-Samit: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Learn from me, learn from me. Allah has made a way for them: The virgin with the virgin, and the married woman with the married woman. The virgin (is to be punished with) one hundred lashes and exile for one year, and the married woman (is to be punished with) one hundred lashes and stoning.”

Yahyá ibn Hammád narrated to me, he said: Abán ibn Yazíd narrated to me, from Qatádah, who said: Khalid ibn ‘Urfutah wrote to me from Habib ibn Salím: That a young man who was nicknamed Qurqúr had relations with the wife of a man’s wife. The matter was referred to Nu‘mán ibn Bashír, who said: “I will judge this case with a just judgment: If she had permitted it to him, I will flog him one hundred lashes. And if she had not permitted it to her, I will stone him.” It was said to her: “Your husband!” She said: “I have permitted it to him.” So he was flogged one hundred lashes. Yahyá said: It is a marfū‘ (elevated narration).

Sadqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to me, from Shu‘bah, from Abí Bishr, from Khalid ibn ‘Urfutah, from Habib ibn Salím, from Nu‘mán ibn Bashír, from the Prophet (ﷺ), a narration similar to this.

Marwan ibn Muhammad of Damascus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to me, from Usama ibn Zaid, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Ibn Khuzaima ibn Thabit, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever has a punishment imposed upon him, that sin is forgiven for him."

Sahal ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: That a woman vowed to perform Hajj and then died. Her brother came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and asked him about that. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to him: "If she had a debt, would you pay it?" He said: "Yes." He (the Prophet) said: "Then pay (her vow) to Allah, for Allah is more deserving of fulfillment."

'Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated: Hafs narrated to me: 'Ubaydullah narrated to me: From Naafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I made a vow in pre-Islamic times, then Islam came?" He said: "Fulfill your vow."

My sister vowed to perform Hajj for Allah on foot, without covering her head. I mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and he said: "Tell your sister to cover her head, and to ride, and to fast three days."
