Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Hammam narrated to me, he said: Qatadah narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the sister of Uqba made a vow to walk to the House (Ka'bah). So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah is free from need of the vow of your sister, let her ride and let her offer a Hadi (a sacrifice during Hajj)."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once encountered an elderly man walking between his two sons. He asked, "What is the matter with this old man?" His sons replied, "He has vowed to walk (thus)." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Ride, for Allah is free from need and free from your vow."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There is no validity in a pledge that involves disobedience of Allah, or in something that Adam’s son does not possess.”
The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever makes a vow to obey Allah, let him obey Him, and whoever makes a vow to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him."

A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I vowed that if Allah grants you victory, I would pray in the Holy Land (Bayt al-Maqdis)." The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Pray here." He repeated it to him three times, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Then do as you wish."
Umar ibn Muarrrah narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Vows do not avert anything, but they extract from the miser."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once encountered Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was traveling with a caravan and taking an oath by his father. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Indeed, Allah has forbidden you from swearing by your fathers. So, whoever was swearing, let him swear by Allah, or remain silent.”
One who swears an oath, then says, "If Allah wills," has nullified it.
Narrated by Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then says, 'If Allah wills,' then he has the option to do it or not to do it."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Salih: He told me, Yazid narrated to me, Yazid narrated to me from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaidullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to Abu Bakr, "Do not swear oaths." Abu Muhammad said: The Hadith is lengthy.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me from 'Amru, who said: Ibn Murra said: I heard a man, they said his name was Abdullah ibn 'Amru, during the time of the Jamajim, recounting a report. He said: A man asked 'Adi ibn Hatim, and he swore he would not give him anything. Then he said: "Were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: 'If someone swears an oath and then sees something better than what he swore, let him take what is better and atone for his oath.'"

Narrated ‘Abdullah bin Samura: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said to ‘Abdullah bin Samura, “Do not ask for the position of leadership, for if it is given to you after asking for it, you will be held accountable for it, and if it is given to you without asking, you will be assisted in it.” And when you take an oath, and then you see something better than it, then redeem your oath and go for the better thing.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr, from Abu Salama, from al-Sharid, who said: “I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: ‘My mother has a slave to pay, and I have a black Sudanese maidservant. Will she suffice as payment?’ He said: ‘Call her.’ So I called her, and he said to her: ‘Do you bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah?’ She said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Set her free, for she is a believer.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Your oath is upon that which your companion accuses you of.”
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Musa, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, who said: “The hand that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would swear with was, ‘No, and He who turns hearts.’”

"Narrated Abu Shuraih Al-Khuzai: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'Whoever is inflicted with bloodshed or injury (al-khabl - meaning an injury), then he has the choice between three options: If he desires a fourth, then restrain his hands; either he takes retribution, or he forgives, or he accepts compensation. If he takes something of this (compensation) and then transgresses thereafter, then the Fire is his abode, eternally dwelling within it.'"

The narrator, al-Hakim ibn Musa, reported from Yahya ibn Hamza, from Sulaiman ibn Dawud, who reported from Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wrote to the people of Yemen. And in his letter was the statement: "Indeed, whoever unlawfully kills a believer with clear evidence, then his hands and feet should be cut off, unless the relatives of the slain accept compensation." Abu Muhammad said: "‘Ibtata’ means to kill without a justifiable reason."

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ar-Raqashi narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Zura’i narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Bashir ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, who said: Abdullah ibn Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, one of the Banu Haritha, went to Khaybar with a group of his people, intending to seek provisions from Khaybar. It happened that Abdullah was attacked and killed; his neck was slit until it dislocated, and he was then thrown into a spring of the springs of Khaybar. His companions then called for help, and they extracted him and concealed him. Then they came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in Medina. His brother, Abdullah ibn Sahl, who was of long standing with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, accompanied by his cousin, Huwaith ibn Mas’ud and Muhaisa, advanced forward. Abdullah ibn Sahl spoke, and he was the youngest of them, and he was the master of the blood debt and of long standing among the people. When he spoke, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Old age, old age.” He then retreated, and Huwaith and Muhaisa spoke, then he. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You will name your killer, then swear fifty oaths upon him, then we will hand him over to you.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, we would not swear to something we do not know. We do not know who killed him, except that the Jews are our enemies, and he was killed among them.” He said: “They will swear to you by Allah that they are innocent of the blood of your companion, then they will be acquitted from it.” They said: “We would not accept the oaths of the Jews; there is nothing in them more than swearing an oath of sin.” So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, redeemed him from his own wealth with one hundred camels.

The narrator, al-Hakim ibn Musa, reported from Yahya ibn Hamza, from Sulaiman ibn Dawud, who reported from Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wrote to the people of Yemen, and it was in his letter: "A man is killed because of a woman."

Narrated Anas: A Jewish girl was crushed between two stones. They said to her, "Who did this to you? So-and-so? So-and-so?" Until the Jew was named. She nodded her head. He was sent for and brought, and he confessed. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered that his head be crushed between two stones.

I said to Ali: "O Commander of the Believers, did you acquire any knowledge of revelation other than what is in the Book of Allah?" He said: "No, by the One who splits the grain and creates the soul, I do not know anything except understanding which Allah grants a person in the Qur’an, and what is in the scroll." I said: "And what is in the scroll?" He said: "Reason, manumitting the slave, and no Muslim is killed for the sake of a polytheist."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Punishments should not be carried out in the mosques, and a father should not be led by his son."

Narrated by Samura ibn Jundub: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever kills his slave, we kill him, and whoever maims him, we maim him." He said: Then Hasan forgot this hadith, and he used to say: A free person is not killed for a slave.

I witnessed the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) when a murderer was brought to him, being led by a rope. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the avenger of the slain: “Will you pardon him?” He said, “No.” The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “Will you take the blood money (diyah)?” He said, “No.” The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “Will you kill him?” He said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Indeed, if you pardon him, he will bear your sin and the sin of your companion.” He then abandoned the matter. I saw him dragging his rope, having pardoned him.

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, and unlawful killing – the one who kills a soul whose life Allah has made sacred."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The cursing of a believer is like his murder, and whoever kills himself with something in this world, he will be punished for it on the Day of Resurrection.”

"Whoever kills himself with a blade, that blade will be in his hand, with which he will be impaled in the belly in the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. And whoever poisons himself, the poison will be in his hand, with which he will be poisoned in the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. And whoever throws himself from a mountain and kills himself, he will throw himself into the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: A man killed a man during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) set his blood-price at twelve thousand [dirhams]. That is [referring to] the statement: “They swear by Allah that they did not say [what is alleged], and indeed they have said a word of disbelief, and they rejected faith after their acceptance of it, and they harbored thoughts of what they did not attain, and they resented only that Allah and His Messenger enriched them out of His grace.” (Surah At-Tawbah, 74) [referring to] their taking the blood-price.

Narrated by Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin ‘Amr bin Hazm from his father, from his grandfather: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: "And upon the people of gold, a thousand dinars."

Narrated by Al-Zuhri from my father, from his father, from his grandfather: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Prophet ﷺ, to Surhabeel ibn ‘Abd-Kulal, Al-Harith ibn ‘Abd-Kulal, and Nua’im ibn ‘Abd-Kulal, known as Dhi Ru’ayn and Mu’afir, and Hamadan. And it was in his writing: ‘Indeed, the blood-wit for a soul is one hundred camels.’”

Al-Hakim ibn Musa narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to me, from Sulaiman ibn Dawud, saying: Zuhri narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from his grandfather: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen, and in his letter was: "The retribution for injury to the nose, if it is broken, is a diyah (blood money); and for injury to the tongue, a diyah; and for injury to the lips, a diyah; and for injury to the two front teeth, a diyah; and for injury to the male organ, a diyah; and for injury to the spine, a diyah; and for injury to the eyes, a diyah; and for injury to one leg, half a diyah; and for injury to the abdomen, a third of a diyah; and for injury to the loin, a third of a diyah; and for injury to the flank, fifteen camels."
Narrated by Abdullah: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "divided the diyya (blood money) for unintentional killing into five shares."

Narrated ‘Imran ibn Husain: That a slave of some poor people cut off the hand of a slave of some wealthy people. So his family came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said, “O Messenger of Allah, he is for some poor people?” So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did not impose anything upon him.

Narrated Abu Al-Walid: He told me, that Shu'bah narrated to me from Ghaleb Al-Tammar, from Masruq bin Aus, from Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The fingers are equal." He (Abu Musa) said: I said: Ten (in number)? He (the Prophet) said: "Yes."
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “These two are equal,” and he pointed with his little finger and index finger.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: "And upon every finger of the hand and foot are ten [portions] of camels."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, decreed that five camels be sacrificed in the open spaces.

Narrated from my grandfather: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: "And upon every finger of the hand and foot there are ten camels, and upon the palm of the hand there are five camels."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ruled regarding the teeth of a camel that five teeth equal five camels.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: "And [regarding Zakat] five camels in the fifth year [of the camel’s age]."

Narrated ‘Imran bin Husain: A man bit another man, and he pulled his hand away, causing two of his teeth to fall out. They contested before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: “Does one of you bite his brother as a stallion bites? There is no penalty for you.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The wild ass is a fierce beast, a well is formidable, a mine is formidable, and a fifth of the treasure trove is due [to the state]."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A wound inflicted by an aggressive animal is a noble cause, a well is a noble cause, a mine is a noble cause, and one-fifth of the treasure found belongs to the state."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The mine is formidable, the grazing animal is formidable, the well is formidable, and one-fifth of the treasure trove is due to the state."

Two women were under the guardianship of a man, and they quarreled. One of them struck the other with a wooden beam, killing her and what was in her womb. They contested [the matter] to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he judged in favor of the one who had been struck and imposed a diya (blood money) upon the woman who had struck [the other].

Umar implored the people to uphold the judgment of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, concerning the fetus. Then Hamal ibn Malik ibn al-Nagigh stood and said, "I was between two women, and one of them struck the other with a flat stone." So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, judged that the fetus should be killed because of it, and that she should be executed.

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Yunus narrated to me from Zuhri from Saeed ibn Musayyib and Abu Salama, from Abu Huraira, that two women from the tribe of Hudhaila quarreled. One of them threw a stone at the other, killing her and what was in her womb. They disputed about the blood money (diyah) and came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He judged that the blood money for the fetus was a slave or a female slave, and he judged the blood money for her to be paid by her heir, her inheritors, her son, and those with her. Then Hammal ibn an-Nabigha al-Hudhaali said: "How can I make someone who did not drink, eat, speak, or babble bear responsibility? Is such a thing dismissed?" The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "He is one of the companions of soothsayers, because of his rhyming."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The diyya (blood money) for the killing of a person by mistake is like that of intentional killing, and whatever is inflicted by a whip or stick is one hundred [dirhams] from it: forty of them being for those who carry [babies] in their wombs."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, that Al-Awza'i narrated to me, from Zuhri, from Sahl ibn Sa'd As-Sa'idi, who informed him that a man peeped from a hole in the wall of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) chamber, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was using a comb to arrange his hair. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saw him and said: "If I had known that you were looking at me, I would have pierced your eyes with it." And the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Permission was only granted for looking."

Narrated by Sahl bin Sa’d: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a chamber and had a comb with which he was combing his head, a man looked at him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "If I knew that you were looking, I would have stood up and pierced your eyes with it. Permission [to enter] was granted only for looking."

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Zakariyya, from Ash-Sha'bi, from Abdullah ibn Muti', from Muti', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "No Qurayshi shall be killed with premeditation after this day until the Day of Resurrection."

Ya'la narrated to me, Zakariyya narrated to me from Amir, who said: Abdullah ibn Muti' said: I heard Muti' saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [The narration continued similarly.]

Abu Muhammad said: Its interpretation is that no Qurayshi shall be killed for disbelief. That is, it is not meant that a Qurayshi should revert to disbelief after that day. However, in cases of legal retribution (qisas), they may be killed.

Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to me, and Jarir (meaning Ibn Hazim) narrated to me, saying: I heard Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr say: Iyad ibn Laqit narrated to me from Abu Rimtha who said: I came to Medina with my son, and we had not seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. So I went to him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out wearing two green garments. When I saw him, I recognized him by description. I approached him, and he said: "Who is this with you?" I said: "My son, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" He said: "Your son?" I said: "I testify to that." He said: "Indeed, this son of yours will not wrong you, nor will you wrong him."

Abu Rimtha reported: I set out with my father towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He (the Prophet ﷺ) said to my father, "Is this your son?" My father replied, "Yes, by the Lord of the Ka'bah." He (the Prophet ﷺ) said, "Truly?" He (my father) said, "I bear witness to that." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, smiling because of the firmness of my resemblance to my father and because of my father's oath. He (the Prophet ﷺ) said, "Your son will not wrong you, and you will not wrong him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: "And no burdened one will bear the burden of another." [Surah Al-An'am, 164]

A group of the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, sat together and discussed. They said, "If we knew which of the deeds was most beloved to Allah, we would do it." So Allah revealed, "Glorify [Allah] for whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He is the Mighty, the Wise," [Quran 59:1] until it was concluded. Abdullah said, "The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, recited it to us until it was concluded." Abu Salama said, "Ibn Salam recited it to us." Yahya said, "Abu Salama recited it to us." Al-Awza'i recited it to us, and Muhammad recited it to us.

Allah has undertaken to guarantee for the one who leaves his home with no intention other than striving in the way of Allah and confirming His words, that He will either admit him to Paradise or return him to his dwelling from which he set out, along with whatever reward or spoils he has earned.
Narrated Jabir: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said, "One whose horse is crippled and whose blood is spilled."

Narrated Abu Huraira: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what deeds were best. He said, "Belief in Allah and His Messenger." I said, "Then what?" He said, "Then striving in the way of Allah." I said, "Then what?" He said, "Then performing a Hajj that is accepted (Mabrur)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever fights in the way of Allah, equivalent to the milk yield of a she-camel, Paradise becomes obligatory for him."

Narrated Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came out to them while they were sitting, and said, "Shall I not tell you about the best of people in status?” We said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “A man who holds the reins of his horse’s head in the path of Allah until he dies or is killed.” He said, “Shall I tell you about the one who follows him?” We said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “A man who secludes himself in a valley, performs the prayer, pays the zakah, and avoids the evils of people.” He said, “Shall I tell you about the worst of people in status?” We said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “The one who is asked by Allah, the Mighty, and does not give (anything) with Him.”
"A man remaining in the ranks (of the army) in the path of Allah is better than 'ibaadah (worship) of a man for sixty years."

Malik ibn Abdullah passed by Habib ibn Maslama, or Habib passed by Malik while he was leading a horse and walking, and said, "Why don't you ride your beast of burden?" Malik said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'Whoever’s feet are covered in dust in the path of Allah, Allah forbids the Fire upon him.'"
"A morning or evening excursion in the path of Allah is better than the world and all that is in it."
"No servant (slave) fasts a day in the way of Allah, seeking the countenance of Allah, but Allah distances his face from the Fire seventy autumns."

Al-Qasim ibn Kathir narrated: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih narrating from Abu al-Subah Muhammad ibn Shumair, from Abu Ali al-Hamdani, from Abu Rayhanah, that he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during a campaign, and he heard him one night saying: "The fire is forbidden to an eye that kept vigil in the cause of Allah, and the fire is forbidden to an eye that shed tears out of fear of Allah." He said: And he said it a third time, and I forgot it. Abu Shuraih said: I heard someone say that: "The fire is forbidden to an eye that averted itself from the prohibitions of Allah, or an eye that was plucked out in the cause of Allah."

Narrated by 'Uqba bin 'Amir Al-Juhani: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "May Allah have mercy on the guardian of the guard." Abdullah said: Umar bin 'Abd al-'Aziz did not meet 'Uqba bin 'Amir.

Narrated Abu Mas’ud Al-Ansari: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a tamed she-camel and said, “I have presented this in the way of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, “You will have seven hundred she-camels, all tamed, for it on the Day of Resurrection.”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Hisham narrated to me from Hasan from Sa’sa’ah ibn Muawiyah, who said: I met Abu Dharr while he was leading a camel for him, or driving it, with a waterskin on its neck. I said to him: O Abu Dharr, what is your wealth? He said: My deeds. I said: What is your wealth? He said: My deeds. I said: Recite to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: “No Muslim spends a pair of anything in the way of Allah, except that the veil of Paradise is drawn for him.” Abu Muhammad said: [It refers to] two dirhams, or two female servants, or two male servants, or two animals.
Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir: That he recited this verse: “And prepare against them whatever you can of strength.” (Al-Anfal 8:60) Then he said, “Verily, strength is archery.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, Allah allows the three to enter Paradise with a single arrow: its maker, intending good in his craft, the one who provides the arrows, and the one who shoots it.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Shoot and ride, for I love shooting more than riding."
He (peace be upon him) said: "Every amusement a man has is vanity, except for a man shooting with his bow, training his horse, and amusing himself with his wife, for these are from the truth."
He (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: "Whoever abandons archery after having been taught it, he has disbelieved that which he was taught."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "No wounded person is wounded in the way of Allah, but Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection with his wound oozing, the scent of which is the scent of musk and the color of which is the color of blood."

Narrated by Sahl bin Abi Amama from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks Allah for martyrdom sincerely from his heart, Allah will attain for him the ranks of the martyrs, even if he dies in his bed."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The martyr feels no pain from the agony of being killed except as one of you feels from the pain of a scratch."

Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "No soul dies and enters Paradise but that it wishes it had returned to you and possessed the world and all that is in it, except for the martyr; for he wishes he were killed again, due to what he sees of the reward."

We were asking Abdullah about the spirits of the martyrs. Had it not been for Abdullah, no one would have informed us. He said: "The spirits of the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection are with Allah in the entrails of green birds, which have chandeliers suspended from the Throne. They graze wherever they will in Paradise, then return to their chandeliers, and their Lord overlooks them, and says, ‘Do you need anything? Do you desire anything?’ They say, ‘No, except that we return to the world and be killed once again.’”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The martyrs are three: a believer who strives with his life and property in the way of Allah, and when he meets the enemy, he fights until he is killed. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said about him: “He is the tested martyr in the tent of Allah, beneath His Throne, and the prophets do not surpass him except by the degree of prophethood.” And a believer whose righteous deeds are mixed with evil deeds, who strives with his life and property in the way of Allah, and when he meets the enemy, he fights until he is killed. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said about him: “His sins and faults are sucked away; indeed, the sword obliterates sins, and he is admitted into Paradise through whichever of its gates he wishes.” And a hypocrite who strives with his life and property, and when he meets the enemy, he fights until he is killed; that one is in the Fire, for indeed the sword does not obliterate hypocrisy.” Abdullah said: It is said to a garment when it is washed: ‘Sucked clean.’”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Qatada from his father: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and delivered a sermon, praising and glorifying Allah. Then he mentioned Jihad and did not leave anything superior to it except the obligatory duties. A man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the one who is killed in the way of Allah? Does that expiate his sins?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, if he is killed while patient, seeking reward, facing the enemy and not turning his back, except for the debt, for indeed it is taken from it, as Jibril informed me."

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The plague is a martyrdom, drowning is a martyrdom, fighting in the way of Allah is a martyrdom, and dying of abdominal illness is a martyrdom, and a woman who dies in childbirth is a martyr."

Narrated ‘Ubadah bin As-Samit: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Killing in the way of Allah is martyrdom, and dying of plague is martyrdom, and dying of abdominal distress is martyrdom, and a woman who dies giving birth is a martyr."

We used to campaign with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and we had nothing to eat but smr (a type of coarse grain) and the leaves of the lote tree. Sometimes one of us would lie down as a sheep does, without any bedding. Then the Banu Assad began to reproach me! Indeed, I was ruined then, and my deeds went astray.

Jabalah ibn ‘Atiyyah narrated from Yahya ibn al-Walid ibn ‘Ubadah ibn as-Samit, from ‘Ubadah ibn as-Samit, who said: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ‘Whoever wages war in the path of Allah and intends nothing in his expeditions except a rope (i.e., a small gain), then he will get what he intended.’”

Narrated by Mu'adh bin Jabal: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There are two kinds of expeditions (ghazw): One is for him who goes forth seeking the countenance of Allah and obeys the Imam, spends generously, and is lenient with his companion, and avoids corruption. His sleep and wakefulness are rewarded. And the other is for him who goes forth seeking glory, showing off, and reputation, disobeys the Imam, and spreads corruption on earth. He will not return with sufficiency."

"Whoever does not participate in fighting (ghazw), nor equip a fighter, nor support a fighter in his family affairs with kindness, Allah will afflict him with a calamitous event before the Day of Resurrection."
One who equips a warrior for the path of Allah or supports his family, Allah writes for him the like of that warrior’s reward, without diminishing anything from the warrior’s reward.

Narrated Abu Al-Walid: Abu Ishaq told me that he heard Al-Bara’ saying, “When this verse was revealed: ‘Those who sit and those who stand [in prayer] are not equal,’ (Surah An-Nisa, 95), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for Zayd, and he brought a shoulder [of parchment], and he wrote it. Then Ibn Umm Maktum complained about his weakness, so this verse was revealed: ‘Those who sit and those who stand [in prayer] are not equal, except those who have an excuse.’ (Surah An-Nisa, 95)"

Narrated Anas bin Malik: Umm Haram bint Milhan informed me that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was once in her house when he awoke laughing. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what made you laugh?" He said, "I was shown a people from my Ummah riding the sea like kings on thrones.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to include me among them.” He said, “You are among them.” Then he slept again and awoke laughing. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what made you laugh?” He said, “I was shown a people from my Ummah riding the sea like kings on thrones.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to include me among them.” He said, “You are among them.” Then he slept again and awoke laughing. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what made you laugh?” He said, “I was shown a people from my Ummah riding the sea like kings on thrones.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to include me among them?” He said, “You are among the first.” Then ‘Ubada bin As-Samit married her, and he raided the sea, so he took her along. When they returned, a female donkey was brought for her to ride, but she threw it and broke her neck, and she died.
"I accompanied the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on seven campaigns, tending to the wounded, preparing food for them, and taking care of their households."

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would go out, he would draw lots between his wives, and the lot would fall on Aisha and Hafsa, so they would both go out with him."

Uthman said on the pulpit, "Indeed, I concealed a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) out of aversion to your separation from me. Then it became apparent to me to relate it to you, so that a person may choose for himself what appears good to him. Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: ‘A day’s guarding [ribat] in the path of Allah is better than a thousand days in other than that [ribat] from dwellings.’”

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “Every deceased person’s work is sealed except for the one who is engaged in jihad (fighting) in the way of Allah; his work continues to be recorded for him until he is resurrected.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The horses are tied to their manes with goodness until the Day of Resurrection: [meaning] reward and spoils of war."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The horses are tied to their manes with goodness until the Day of Resurrection: [meaning] reward and spoils of war."

Abu Qatadah al-Ansari reported: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, I intend to buy a horse. Which one should I buy?" He (the Prophet) said: "Buy a dark horse, strong, with a white blaze, swift of the right foreleg, or one from the Kumait tribe, having this mark [pointing to his shoulder], may you prosper and be safe."

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to me, Malik narrated to me, from Naafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to race with horses, the harnessed ones from al-Ḥafya’ to ath-Thaniyah, and the unharnessed ones from ath-Thaniyah to the mosque of Banu Zurayq, and Ibn Umar was among those who raced with him.”

Abu Lubayd said, "During the time of al-Hajjaj, and al-Hakam ibn Ayyub was in charge of Basrah, we came to the racecourse. When the horses arrived, we said, 'Let us go to Anas ibn Malik and ask him if they used to wager during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?' So, we went to him while he was in his palace in the corner. We asked him and said, 'O Abu Hamzah, did you used to wager during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him? Did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ever wager?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, he did wager on a horse called Sahba, and it outran the others, so he was delighted with that and admired it.'" Abu Muhammad said, "Anhashahu means he was delighted with it."
Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Strive against the polytheists with your wealth, your lives, and your tongues."
"There will always be a group from my community dominant over the people until the command of Allah comes, and they are dominant."
"There will always be a group of my community upholding the truth."

Narrated Abu Darr: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "After me, there will be people from my Ummah who recite the Qur'an, but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will go out of the religion as an arrow goes out of the bow, and they will not return to it. They are the worst of the creatures and the creation."

Sulaiman said: Humayd said: Abdullah ibn As-Samit said: I met Rafi’, the brother of Hakim ibn Amr al-Ghifari, and I narrated this Hadith to him.

Rafi’ said: And I too heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

"Narrated by Sakhr al-Ghamidi: That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘O Allah, bless my community in their early morning endeavors.’ And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would dispatch raiding parties from the early part of the day. He said: This man was a merchant, and he would send his servants out from the early part of the day, so his wealth increased."
Narrated by his father: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would scarcely set out on a journey but on a Thursday."
The best of companions before Allah is the one who is best to his companion, and the best of neighbors before Allah is the one who is best to his neighbor.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of companions are four, the best of armies are four thousand, the best of raiding parties are four hundred. And if [their number] reaches twelve thousand, then let them persevere and be truthful, for they will be overcome due to their fewness.”

Narrated by Sulaiman bin Burida from his father: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he appointed a man to lead an army, would advise him in private with taqwa (God-consciousness) and to treat those with him of the Muslims well. And he would say: "Go forth in the name of Allah and in the path of Allah, fight those who disbelieve in Allah, go forth and do not betray, do not hoard spoils, do not mutilate, and do not kill infants."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not wish for meeting the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. And if you meet them, stand firm, and increase the remembrance of Allah. And if they create a clamor, then maintain silence."
Sahib reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate during the days of Hunayn: “O Allah, with You I strive, with You I contend, and with You I fight.”

Narrated By Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to give the following advice to those whom he appointed as leaders of armies: "Invite (the people) to Allah, and if they accept, then fight for those who accept with you. Invite (them) to Islam, and if they accept, then accept their conversion and refrain from fighting them. Invite them to migrate from their homes to the homes of the emigrants, and inform them that they will have the same rights and obligations as the emigrants. If they refuse, then they will be like the Arab Muslims, subject to the laws of Allah which apply to the believers, but they will have no share in the war booty or spoils of war unless they participate in the fighting along with the Muslims. If they refuse to embrace Islam, then ask them to pay the Jizya (poll tax), and if they do so, accept it from them and refrain from fighting them. If they refuse, then seek Allah’s help and fight them. And if you besiege a fortress and its people ask you to guarantee them Allah’s protection and the protection of His Messenger, do not guarantee them Allah’s protection or the protection of His Messenger, but guarantee them your own protection and the protection of your father and your companions. Verily, if you relax your protection, it will be easier for you than relaxing Allah’s protection and the protection of His Messenger. And if you besiege a fortress and its people ask you to submit to the rule of Allah, do not submit them to the rule of Allah, but submit them to your own rule, for you do not know whether you will apply Allah’s rule correctly or not. Then, judge them as you please." Alqama said: I narrated this to Muqattal bin Hayyan, who said: Muslim bin Hisam narrated to me on the authority of Nu’man bin Muqrin, from the Prophet (ﷺ) with the same wording.
Narrated Abdullah: Sufyan said that he did not hear Ibn Abi Najih mention this Hadith. Ibn Abbas said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never fought a people after inviting them [to Islam]."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Thabit, from Anas: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to go out scouting at the time of Fajr prayer, and he would listen. If he heard the Adhan (call to prayer), he would stop, and if he did not hear the Adhan, he would continue scouting.

Hashim ibn Qasim narrated to me, saying: Shu’bah narrated to me from Nu’man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Aws ibn Abi Aws Ath-Thaqafi say: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with the delegation of Thaqif. I was at the bottom of the tent, and there was no one in it except the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who was sleeping. Then a man came to him and spoke in confidence, and he said, "Go and kill him." Then he said, "Does he not testify that there is no god but Allah?" Shu’bah said: I doubt whether Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah? He said: Yes. He (the Prophet) said: "Indeed, I have been commanded to fight people until they say, ‘There is no god but Allah.’ When they say it, their blood and wealth become forbidden for me except justly.” He said: And he was the one who killed Abu Mas’ud. He said: And he did not die until he killed the best person of Ta’if.

Narrated Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “It is not permissible to shed the blood of a person who testifies that there is no deity except Allah, except in one of three situations: a person who takes the life of another, a married adulterer, or one who abandons his religion and severs ties with the community.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Hammad ibn Shaybah narrated to me from Khalid ibn Sumayr, who said: Abdullah ibn Rabah al-Anṣārī came to us, and the Anṣār used to seek religious knowledge from him. He said: He narrated to me Abu Qatadah: That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent forth a company of commanders. They departed and remained for as long as Allah willed. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ascended the pulpit, and he ordered [that] the call to the congregational prayer be announced: “Prayer is congregational.”
The one who seeks counsel is trustworthy.
Narrated by K’ab bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he intended to set out on an expedition, would feint at another (place) before setting out.
I challenged a man and killed him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave me his spoils of war. Our battle cry with Khalid ibn al-Walid was: "Kill."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal and ‘Affan said: “We narrated from Hammad ibn Salama, from Ya’la ibn ‘Ata’, from ‘Abdullah ibn Yasir, Abu Hammam, from Abu ‘Abd ar-Rahman al-Fihri, who said: ‘We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the campaign of Hunayn. We were in a scorching, intensely hot day, and we took shelter under the trees... [The narrator continued the story], then he took a handful of dust and said: “He narrated to me the one who was closest to him than I, that he struck their faces with it and said, "May ruin be upon the faces!" And Allah defeated the polytheists.’ Ya’la said: “He narrated to me their sons that their fathers said: ‘No one among us remained except that his eyes and mouth were filled with dust.’”

Narrated ‘Abadah bin As-Samit: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a gathering when he said to us: “Give me a pledge that you will not associate anything with Allah, not steal, not commit adultery, not kill your children, and not come with false statements fabricating them between your hands and feet. Whoever fulfills this pledge, his reward is with Allah, and whoever violates it, Allah will conceal his fault, and his matter is up to Allah - if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him. And whoever is punished for something in this world, that is an expiation for it.” He (the narrator) said: We pledged to him on that.

We were a thousand four hundred on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. We pledged allegiance to him, and Umar was holding his hand beneath a tree, which was a sumrah tree. He said, "We pledged allegiance to him not to flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him for death."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, saying: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, carried earth with us on the day of al-Ahzab, and [the earth] covered the whiteness of his armpits. He was saying: "O Allah! If it were not for You, we would not be guided, nor would we give charity, nor would we pray. So send down tranquility upon us and strengthen our feet if we meet them. Surely, those who disbelieved have committed aggression against us. And if they intend to create a disturbance, we will refuse." And he would raise his voice with it.

Narrated Anas: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) entered Mecca in the year of the Conquest, wearing a head covering (migfar). When he removed it, a man came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah! This is Ibn Khatal clinging to the curtains of the Ka'aba." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Kill him."

Anas (RA) said: "The sheath of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was of silver."

Abdullah, Hisham ad-Dustawa'i, contradicted him.

Qatadah said: From Saeed ibn Abi al-Hasan, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and the people claim that this is the preserved (version)."
Abu Talha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would, when he overcame a people, like to remain among them in their dwellings for three days.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Sa’id, from ‘Uqba ibn Khalid, from ‘Ubaidullah, from Nafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ burned the date palms of the Banu Nadir.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us on a campaign, and he said, “If you find Fulān and Fulān, burn them with fire.” Then, the following morning, he sent for us and said, “Indeed, I had ordered you to burn these two men, but then I saw that no one should punish with fire except Allah. So, if you find them, kill them.”

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: It is mentioned in some accounts of the battles of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) that a woman was found killed. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade the killing of women and children.

We set out with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on an expedition. He confronted the polytheists, and the people hastened to kill, even killing the children. This reached the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: "What is the matter with people who were carried away by killing until they killed the children? Indeed, do not kill children three times over."

Narrated ‘Attiya Al-Qurazi: “We were presented before the Prophet (ﷺ) on that day, and whoever grew hair was killed, and whoever did not grow hair was left (unharmed).” I was among those who did not grow hair, so they did not kill me. (Meaning: the day of Qurayza.)
Narrated Abu Musa: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Release the indebted, and feed the hungry."
Narrated by ‘Imran ibn Husain: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man ransomed himself with two men.”

Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Abu Awana narrated to me from Sulaiman from Mujahid from ‘Ubaid ibn ‘Umayr from Abu Dharr: That the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I was given five things that no prophet before me was given: I was sent to the red and the black people, and the earth was made a mosque and a place of purification for me. Spoils of war were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me. I was given support through terror, for a month, so that the enemy would be terrified by me for a month's journey. And it was said to me: ‘Ask, and you shall be given.’ So I concealed my supplication as intercession for my community, and it will be attained by you, if Allah wills, for whoever does not associate anything with Allah."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, divided the spoils of Hunayn at al-Jirranah.

I witnessed the conquest of Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the polytheists were routed. We entered their tents, and the people rushed to seize whatever livestock they found. He said: It was not long before the pots boiled over, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them to be tilted. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided amongst us, giving every ten [men] a sheep. He said: Some of the sons of so-and-so were with me, numbering nine, and I was alone, so I turned to them, and we became ten, sharing one sheep. Abdullah said: It reached me that your companion says, from Qays ibn Muslim: as if he says, he did not remember it. Zakariya ibn ‘Adi narrated to us, from ‘Ubaidullah ibn ‘Amr, from Zayd, who is the son of Abu Unaisa, from Qays ibn Muslim, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, in a similar manner. He said: I was made friendly towards them. Abu Muhammad said: The correct account, in my opinion, is what Zakariya stated regarding the chain of narrators.

Narrated by Yazid bin Hurmuz: Najdah bin ‘Amir wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about certain matters, and Ibn Abbas wrote to him: “You have inquired about the share of the relatives that Allah mentioned, and we consider the relatives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) to be them, but our people reject this.”
Umar ibn 'Abdullah reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, distributed arrows at Khaybar: three arrows for the rider and one arrow for the pedestrian.

"I did not witness with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, any booty being divided for me, except on the day of Khaybar. It was specifically for the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. Abu Musa and Abu Hurayrah came between al-Hudaybiyyah and Khaybar."

Isma'il ibn Khalil narrated to me, Hafs narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from 'Umayr, the freedman of Abu al-Lahm, who said: I witnessed Khaybar while I was a slave. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, gave me provisions and a sword, and said to me: "Put this around your neck."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade the following of arrows until they are distributed.

"Ahmed ibn Khalid narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu Marzuq, a servant of Tujib, who said: Hanash the San'ani narrated to me: We marched to the Maghrib under the leadership of Ruwaif ibn Thabit al-Ansari, and we conquered a village called Jarbah. Then Ruwaif ibn Thabit al-Ansari stood up among us as a preacher and said: I do not stand before you except with that which I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. He stood among us on the day of Khaybar when we conquered it, and he said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not take anything from the captives until he purifies it."

Narrated Abu ad-Darda’: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saw a woman in labor at the door of a tent. He said, “Perhaps something has happened to her?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “I was about to curse him – a curse that would enter his grave – how can he inherit from her when it is not permissible for him, and how can he utilize her when it is not permissible for him?”

Abu Ayyub was once in an army, and the children were separated from their mothers. He saw them weeping, so he began returning each child to its mother, saying: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Whoever separates a mother from her child, Allah will separate him from the beloved on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Abu Muhammad said, and among them is one who says, "The Ghilah." He said, "I took the aunt of Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and brought her to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, questioned his aunt, and he said, "O Sakhr, when the people embrace Islam, they safeguard their wealth and their lives, so return it to them." And there was water belonging to the Banu Sulaim, and they embraced Islam, so they came to him and asked him about it. He called me, and said, "O Sakhr, when the people embrace Islam, they safeguard their wealth and their lives, so return it to them." So I returned it to them.

Narrated by Ibn Umar: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) sent forth a raiding party in which Ibn Umar was included. They captured a large number of camels, and their arrows captured twelve or eleven camels, and they were given one camel each as a reward.

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amamah Al-Bahili from ‘Ubadah ibn As-Samit, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he raided the territory of the enemy, would grant a quarter [of the spoils], and whenever he returned, and all the people were with him, he would grant a third.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) "appointed the third [as an additional inheritance] after the fifth [i.e., the share of the fifth relative]."

Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever kills a disbeliever, his spoils are his." On that day, Abu Talha killed twenty (disbelievers) and took their spoils.
Abu Qatadah said, "I challenged a man and killed him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave me his spoils of war."
Narrated ‘Ubadah ibn As-Samit: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) disliked the spoils of war and said: "Let the strong Muslim return [a portion] to the weak Muslim."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "Give the tailor his wages and the seamstress her payment, and avoid dealing in concealed goods, for it is a disgrace upon its possessor on the Day of Resurrection."

Harunah narrated: Ahmad ibn Khalid narrated to me, that Muhammad narrated to me, he being Ibn Ishaq, and Yazid narrated to me, he being Ibn Abi Habib, from Abu Marzuq, a servant of Tujib. He said: Hanash the San’ani narrated to me: “We went out to conquer the Maghrib under the leadership of Ruwaif’ ibn Thabit al-Ansari. We conquered a village called Jarbah. Then Ruwaif’ ibn Thabit al-Ansari stood up among us as a preacher and said: ‘I do not stand before you except with what I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, standing among us on the day of Khaybar when we conquered it: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not ride an animal from the spoils of the Muslims until he has compensated for its use.”’ Abu Muhammad said: ‘I doubt the return of the spoils in this regard.’ And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not wear clothing from the spoils of the Muslims until he has returned it when it becomes worn out.”

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, he said: Ikrimah ibn ‘Ammar narrated to me, he said: Abu Zumail narrated to me, he said: Ibn Abbas narrated to me, that Umar ibn al-Khattab said: Some people were killed on the day of Khaybar, and they said: So-and-so is a martyr, so-and-so. They mentioned every man until they mentioned a man, and they said: So-and-so is a martyr. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “No, indeed! I saw him in the Fire, wearing a cloak or a garment.” Then he said to me: “O Ibn al-Khattab, stand up and announce to the people that none enter Paradise except the believers.” So I stood up and announced to the people.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever you find possessing wool, strike him and burn his possessions."

Narrated from his grandfather: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no looting, no enslavement, and no [issal]. And whoever commits theft, he will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection." Abu Muhammad said: [Issal] is theft.

Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah said: Were it not that I heard Ibn Arta’h say, “I have heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say, ‘Hands would not be cut off in military expeditions.’”

Abu Hurayrah narrated: The Prophet (ﷺ) appointed a person to collect the Zakah. The appointed person came to him after completing his work and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is for you, and this was presented as a gift to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Why did you not sit in your father’s and mother’s house and see if anything would be presented to you?" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) stood up one evening after the prayer on the pulpit, recited the Tashahhud, praised and glorified Allah as He deserved, and then said, "Indeed, what is the matter with the appointed person who comes to us and says, ‘This is from your work, and this was presented as a gift to me?’ Why did he not sit in his father’s and mother’s house and see if anything would be presented to him? By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you should appropriate anything of it, but it will come to him on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck, if it was a camel, it would come with its bleating; if it was a cow, it would come with its mooing; and if it was a sheep, it would come bleating. Have I conveyed (the message)?" Abu Hurayrah said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) raised his hands until we could see the white underarms. Abu Hurayrah said: Zayd ibn Thabit heard that with me from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so ask him.

Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, ‘Umarah ibn Zadhan narrated to me from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik: “That the king of Dhi Yazin sent a garment to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), which he had acquired for thirty-three camels, or thirty-three she-camels, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) accepted it.”

Abu Humayd al-Sa’idi narrated: The ruler of Aylah sent a letter to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and presented him with a white mule. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to him and presented him with a brocade garment.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We do not seek assistance from a polytheist.”

Narrated By Saad bin Samura bin Jandub, from his father, from Abu Ubaida bin Al-Jarrah: He said, "Among the last things that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke was: 'Expel the Jews from Al-Hijaz and the people of Najran from the Arabian Peninsula.'"

Abu Tha'laba said: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are among the people of the Book, and we eat from their vessels." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If you are in a land as you have mentioned, then do not eat from their vessels unless you find no alternative. And if you find no alternative, then wash them and eat from them."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Maslama: Sulaiman, that is Ibn al-Mughira, narrated to me from Humaid, from Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: "A bag full of fat was brought forth on the day of Khaybar. He (Abdullah ibn Mughaffal) said: So I went to it and clung to it. He (Abdullah ibn Mughaffal) said: Then I said: ‘I will not give anyone anything from this today,’ and I turned around, and there was the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) smiling at me.” Abdullah said: I hope Humaid heard this from Abdullah.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me, from ‘Amr, from Bajalah, who said: I heard him say: “‘Umar did not take the Jizyah from the Zoroastrians until ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Auf testified that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had taken it from the Zoroastrians of Hajar.”

Narrated by Um Hanih bint Abi Talib: That she went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of the conquest and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my nephew claims that he has killed a man whom I had given protection to, Fulān ibn Hubayrah." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "You have given protection to whom you have given protection, O Um Hanih."

I went out early one morning riding a horse I owned and passed by a mosque of the Banu Hanifa. I heard them testifying that Musaylama was the Messenger of Allah. I returned to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and informed him, and he sent a patrol to them, and they were arrested and brought before him. The people repented and retracted from their statement, so he released them. However, a man among them, named Abdullah ibn Nawaha, was brought forward and his neck was struck. They said to him, "You left the people and killed this one?" He said, "I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when these two men, envoys from Musaylama, entered. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to them, ‘Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?’ They said to him, ‘You bear witness that Musaylama is the Messenger of Allah.’ He said, ‘I believe in Allah and His Messengers. If I were to kill envoys, I would have killed you both.’ So, for that reason, I killed him. And he ordered their mosque to be demolished.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills a treaty-protected person (mu'ahid) unjustly, Allah will forbid Paradise upon him."

A man from Banu ‘Aqil owned a swift camel. He was captured, and the swift camel was taken as well. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed by him while he was in captivity and said, “O Muhammad, on what grounds do you take me and take my camel, which is a possession of a pilgrim, when I have become Muslim?” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Had you said so while you were in control of your affairs, you would have achieved all success.” Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “We will take you for the transgression of your allies.”

The Thaqif tribe had captured two companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came riding a camel with a saddlecloth upon it. He said, “O Muhammad, I am hungry, so feed me, and I am thirsty, so give me to drink.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “This is your need.”

Then the man was ransomed for two men, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) kept the swift camel for his travel, and it was among the possessions of the pilgrims.

Then the polytheists raided the outskirts of Medina and took the swift camel with them, and they captured a woman from among the Muslims. Whenever they camped, Abu Muhammad said, “Then he mentioned a word about their camels in their courtyards.”

So when one night came, the woman stood up after they had fallen asleep, and she kept placing her hands on each camel until it reared up, until she reached the swift camel. She mounted it and headed towards Medina, vowing that if Allah saved her, she would slaughter it.

He said, “When she arrived at ‘Arafat, the camel was recognized, and it was said, ‘It is the camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)!’ So they brought it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and the woman informed him of her vow. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, ‘How badly you have rewarded her, or how badly she has rewarded you! Does Allah save her so that she will slaughter it? No, there is no fulfillment of a vow in disobedience of Allah, nor in that which a son of Adam has no power over.’”

I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him forth, and he proclaimed four announcements so that his voice rose high: “Indeed, no soul except a Muslim will enter Paradise, and no polytheist shall perform pilgrimage after this year, and no one naked shall circumambulate the House [Ka’bah]. And whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his term is four months; and when those four months pass, then Allah and His Messenger are clear of the polytheists.”

Narrated By Al-Baraa’ bin ‘Aazib: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) performed ‘Umrah in Dhul-Qa’dah, but the people of Makkah refused to let him enter Makkah unless he agreed to stay for three days. So they wrote: “This is what Muhammad (ﷺ) (Allah’s Messenger) has agreed upon.” They said, “We would have agreed to this had we known that you were a Messenger of Allah. But you are Muhammad, son of Abdullah.” So he said, “I am Allah’s Messenger and I am Muhammad, son of Abdullah.” Then he said to Ali, “Erase ‘Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah.’” But Ali said, “By Allah, I shall never erase it.” So Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) took the paper, though he did not write well, and wrote instead of “Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah”: “This is what Muhammad, son of Abdullah, has agreed upon: that he should not enter Makkah with any weapon except his sword in its sheath, and that he should not take out any of its people who wish to follow him, and that he should not prevent any of his companions who wish to stay behind.” When he entered Makkah and the term expired, they came to Ali and said, “Tell your companion to leave us, for the term has expired.”
"Two men, ‘Abdan and Abu Bakrah, from Tā’if came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and manumitted themselves. One of them was Abu Bakrah."

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was wounded on the day of Al-Ahzab. They cut off his veins, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) cauterized them with fire, so they swelled. He bled from his hand, and the Messenger cauterized it again, and it swelled. When he saw that, he said: "O Allah, do not take my soul until You grant my sight [satisfaction] concerning the Banu Qurayza." His vein held firm and did not drip a drop until they descended upon Sa'd's judgment.

He sent for him, and he judged that their men should be killed, and their women and children taken as captives so that the Muslims might benefit from them. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "You have struck the judgment of Allah concerning them."

They were four hundred in number. When they were finished killing them, his vein burst, and he died.

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: Layth narrated to me, and he said: ‘Uqail narrated to me from Ibn Shihab, who informed me, on the authority of Abu Salama bin ‘Abd ar-Rahman: That Abdullah bin ‘Adi bin al-Hamra’ al-Zuhri said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing on his camel at al-Hazwara, and he said: “By Allah, you are the best land of Allah, and the most beloved land of Allah to Allah. If I had not been driven out of you, I would not have left.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Do not curse the deceased, for they have passed away to what they have put forward."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Musa, from Isra’il, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the day of the conquest of Mecca arrived, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: “There is no migration after the conquest, but there is striving (jihad) and intention. And if you are called to arms, then respond.”

Narrated by Abu Hind Al-Bajali, who was among the early generations: We were discussing the Hijrah (migration) with Mu'awiya while he was on his throne. He said: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Migration will not cease until repentance ceases, and repentance will not cease until the sun rises from the west."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Were it not for Hijrah (migration), I would have been a man among the Ansar."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "No ruler of ten (men) but will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, his hands tied to his neck, until the truth releases him or he perishes."
Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah supports this religion with the sinful man."

Narrated by Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and said: “Indeed, those who came before you from the People of the Book divided into seventy-two sects, and this community will divide into seventy-three: seventy-two of them will be in the Fire, and one of them will be in Paradise.” Abdullah al-Haraz said: Al-Haraz is a tribe from the people of Yemen.
"Whoever witnesses something objectionable from his ruler, let him be patient, for none abandons the community even a hand's breadth and dies, but dies a pagan death."

He narrated to us Abu al-Walid, he said: Ikrimah ibn ‘Ammar narrated to us, he said: Iyass ibn Salama narrated to us from his father, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who said: "Whoever draws his sword against us, he is not one of us."

Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mat'im would relate from Mu'awiyah, while he was in his presence with a delegation from Quraysh, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Indeed, this affair [meaning Islam] will remain within Quraysh, and whoever opposes them, Allah will throw him face down, as long as they uphold the religion."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Quraysh, the Ansar, Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam, Ghafar, and Ashja’, they have no master other than Allah and His Messenger.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr from his father: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Tell me, what if ‘Aslam and Ghifar were better than Al-Halifayn (Asad and Ghatafan)? Would you consider them to have lost [their reward]?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then they are better than them." He said: "Tell me, what if Muzayna and Juhaina were better than Tamim, ‘Amir ibn Sa’sa’a, and he raised his voice with them? Would you consider them to have lost [their reward]?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then they are better than them."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ghafar, Allah forgave her; and Aslam, Allah granted her safety.”
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ghafar, Allah forgave her; Aslam, Allah granted her safety; and ‘Uсайyah, she disobeyed Allah and His Messenger.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to me, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. It was said to Sharik: Did you narrate this from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him? He said: Yes. "There is no oath in Islam, and the oath in the pre-Islamic era did not increase Islam except in severity and harshness."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: I said to Mu'awiya ibn Qurra: Did Anas report that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to An-Nu'man ibn Muqrin: "The brother's daughter of a people is from them?" He said: Yes.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The mawla of a people is from them, and the halif of a people is from them, and the brother of a people’s sister is from them.”

I was beneath the Prophet’s camel, and I heard him say: “Whoever claims descent other than his father or claims affiliation to a group other than his own, seeking to distance himself from them, then the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people is upon him. Neither a gift nor justice will be accepted from him.”
One who claims lineage other than his father while knowing he is not his father, then Paradise is forbidden to him.

Narrated by Nu’man bin Bashir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “The lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear, and between them are matters which are doubtful. Many people do not know them. So whoever doubts about these doubtful matters, he has not safeguarded his religion and his honor. And whoever falls into these doubtful matters, he falls into the unlawful. Like a shepherd grazing his flock around a protected enclosure, he is likely to graze into it. Verily, every king has a protected enclosure, and verily, Allah’s protected enclosure is His prohibitions. Verily, there is an organ in the body which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt, and it is the heart.”

Sa'id bin Amir narrated to me, that Shu'bah narrated to me from Buraid bin Abi Maryam, from Abu al-Harawiy as-Sa'di, who said: I asked Hasan bin Ali, "What do you remember from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?" He said: A man asked him about a matter, and I do not know what it was, and he said, "Leave that which causes you doubt to that which causes you no doubt."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Az-Zubayr ibn ‘Abd As-Salam, from Ayyub ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Mikraz Al-Fihri, from Wabisa ibn Ma’bad Al-Asadi: That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Wabisa: "Have you come to ask about piety and sin?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he gathered his fingers and struck his chest with them and said: 'Examine yourself. Examine your heart, O Wabisa, three times.' Piety is that which the soul finds peace in and the heart finds peace in, and sin is that which causes disquiet in the soul and hesitation in the chest. Even if people give you a fatwa and give you a fatwa."

I was holding the reins of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)’s camel during the middle days of Tashriq, warding off people from it, when he said: “Indeed, all interest that was taken in the pre-Islamic period is annulled. And indeed, Allah has decreed that the first interest to be annulled is the interest of Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib. Your principal amounts are yours; do not wrong [others], and do not be wronged.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed those who consume ribā (interest/usury) and those who pay it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There will surely come a time when people will not care whether they acquire wealth through lawful or unlawful means."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the most lawful that a man eats is from his best earnings, and indeed his child is from his best earnings."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Al-Baqi’ and said, “O merchants!” until they turned their faces towards him. He said, “The merchants will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection as wrongdoers, unless they fear Allah, act righteously, and speak truthfully.”

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The truthful and trustworthy merchant is with the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs." Abdullah said: I have no knowledge of this. Hasan heard from Abu Sa’id, and Abu Hamza said: This Abu Hamza is the companion of Ibrahim, and he is Maymun the one-eyed.
I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to establish the prayer, pay the zakah, and give sincere advice to every Muslim.

Narrated by Muhammad bin Salih, from Yahya bin Muawiyah, from Qasim bin ‘Abdullah, from Salim, from Ibn Umar: That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed by some food in the market of Medina and was pleased with its appearance. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) put his hand into its interior and brought out something that was not apparent, and rebuked the owner of the food, and then said: “There should be no deceit among Muslims. Whoever deceives us is not one of us.”
Each betrayer will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be proclaimed: “This is the treachery of so-and-so.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No one commits monopoly except a sinner, and he does so twice.”
The one who brings (goods) to the market is provided for, and the one who withholds (goods) is cursed.

Anas (RA) reported: Prices rose during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and the people said, "O Messenger of Allah, prices have risen, so set prices for us." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah is the Creator, the Seizer, the Expander, the Provider, the One who sets prices. And I hope that I will meet my Lord and none of you will reproach me for an injustice I have done to him in blood or wealth."

Narrated from Hudhaifa: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The angels received the soul of a man from among those who passed before you. They said, ‘Did you do any good deeds?’ He said, ‘No.’ They said, ‘Do you remember?’ He said, ‘I used to lend to people and order my young men to give respite to the indebted and overlook the wealthy.’” He said, “Allah said, ‘I have overlooked it for him.’”

The two parties in a transaction have the right to reconsider it until they separate. If they are truthful and clarify [the terms], blessings will be bestowed upon their transaction. But if they lie and conceal [information], the blessing of their transaction will be removed.

Narrated Abdullah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "The two parties in a transaction, if they dispute and the commodity is present before them, and there is no clear evidence between them, then the statement is that of the seller, or they should abandon the transaction."

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Abdullah ar-Raqashi that Yazid ibn Zura’ narrated to me, that Muhammad – that is, Ibn Ishaq – narrated to me from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Shimasah, from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) saying: "It is not permissible for a believer in Allah and the Last Day to sell over the sale of his brother until he leaves him (i.e., until he completes his sale)."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The period of grace for a slave is three days."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Hasan, from ‘Uqbah ibn al-’Amir, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The trial period for a slave is three days." Qatadah explained: If a defect is found within those three days, he should return him without a witness, but if a defect is found after three days, he should not return him except with a witness.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever buys a speckled sheep or a speckled milch-beast, he has a choice of three days. If he returns it, he returns with it a sa’ of food, without dates."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling on terms of uncertainty.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling fruits until their goodness becomes apparent, forbidding both the seller and the buyer.

Narrated by Jabir: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If someone purchases fruit and a plague afflicts it, then he should not take anything from him. How would you take your brother’s wealth without right?"
Narrated Abu Sa’id: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the muhāqalatu and muzābanatu. Abdullah said: Muhāqalatu is selling crops for barley. And they said: Ibn al-Musayyib says the same.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, permitted the sale of dates and fresh dates (rutab) for camels, but did not permit it for anything other than that.
Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he takes possession of it."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade lending (salf), selling, and two conditions in a sale, and profit on something that is not guaranteed.
Narrated by Salim from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever buys a slave and does not stipulate his price, then he has nothing."

Umar ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to me, from Zuhri, from ‘Atta ibn Yazid, from Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade two types of sales and two types of clothing: the sale of al-Munabadha and al-Mulamasah.” Abdullah said: “Al-Munabadha is when one throws [an item] to the other, and the other throws [something] back.” He said: “This was in the pre-Islamic period.”

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling on credit with uncertainty and forbade selling pebbles. Abdullah said: If one throws pebbles and says, "Sell," then the sale is obligatory.
