Narrated by Samura bin Jundub: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) forbade selling an animal for an animal, on installment. Then Hasan forgot this Hadith, and Ja’far did not say: “Then Hasan forgot this Hadith.”

Abu Rafia, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) borrowed a young lamb. Then some camels from the sadaqah (charity) arrived. Abu Rafia said: “He ordered me to return the lamb with its equivalent. I said: ‘I do not find anything among the camels except a choice, four-year-old camel.’ So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘Give it to him, for the best of people are those who settle matters best.’ Abdullah said: “This strengthens the statement of those who say: ‘An animal is equivalent to an animal.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not engage in price-raising, and whoever engages in it, and buys from him something, then he has the option [to return it] when he enters the market."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Let not some of you sell on the sale of another, and do not purchase goods until they have been brought down to the marketplaces, and do not engage in price bargaining.”

Narrated Abu Mas’ud: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the use of the fat of the dog, the earnings of a prostitute, and the diviner’s gains. Abdullah said: “The diviner’s gains refer to what is given for his divination.”

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: When the verse concerning riba was revealed at the end of Surah al-Baqarah, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) went out and recited it to the people, then he forbade trade in wine.

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: When the verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah were revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) went out and recited them to the people, then he forbade trading in wine.
I asked Ibn Abbas about the skins of the slaughtered animals, and he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Their tanning purifies them."

I asked him about selling wine from the people of the covenant, and I said to him: “We have grapevines, and we make these wines from them, and we sell them to the people of the covenant?” He [Ibn Abbas] said: A man from the Thaqif or Daws tribe presented the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with a skin of wine during the Farewell Pilgrimage. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: “Didn’t you know, O Abu Fulān, that Allah has forbidden it?” He said: “By Allah, I didn’t know.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Indeed, Allah has forbidden it.” Then he turned to his servant and said: “Go forth with it to the market and sell it.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: “Didn’t you know, O Abu Fulān, that He who forbade its drinking, forbade its selling?” He said: So he ordered it to be poured out in the Batḥā’.

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of manumission contracts and the gifting of them. ‘Abdullah said: “The matter remains as it is, [manumission contracts] are neither sold nor gifted.”

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah narrated to me from ‘Amr ibn Dinār, who said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah al-Anṣārī say: A man among us freed a slave of his from behind. He then called for him the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he sold him. Jabir said: And he died in the first year. It was said to ‘Abdullah: Do you say this about him? He said: Some people say so.
"When a woman slave gives birth to a man’s child, she is freed from his possession after that birth."
Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, bless them in their measures and bless them in their sa’s and mudds." Meaning (referring to) Medina.

I had one mod of dates belonging to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). I found dates that were better than those, two sa’s for one sa’. So I bought them, and I brought them to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he said: “From where did you get this, O Bilal?” I said: “I bought one sa’ for two sa’s.” He said: “Return it and return our dates to us.”

Narrated By Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri and Abu Huraira: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a brother of the Banu ‘Adiy of the Ansar and appointed him as governor of Khaybar. He came with some excellent dates. Abdullah bin Maslama said: meaning, good. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Are all the dates of Khaybar like this?" He said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah! We buy a sa’ of dates for two sa’s from the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not do that. Rather, equal for equal, or sell this and buy from this with its price, and thus is the balance.”

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Gold for gold, silver for silver, dates for dates, barley for barley, and wheat for wheat – equal measure and equal weight, and there is no excess between them."

Narrated ‘Amru bin ‘Awn, from Khalid, from Khalid Al-Hazza’i, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Al-Ash’ath As-Sana’ani, who said: Some people used to sell gold and silver vessels for the stipend (during the governorship of Mu’awiya). Then ‘Ubadah bin As-Samit stood up and said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade selling gold for gold, silver for silver, dates for dates, barley for barley, salt for salt, except like for like, equal for equal. So whoever increases or someone increases on him, then he has committed usury.

Usamah ibn Zaid informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Riba (interest/usury) is only in debt." Abdullah (ibn Abbas) said: Its meaning is: one dirham for two dirhams.

I was selling camels in al-Baqi’ and I would sell for dinars, taking dirhams, and sell for dirhams, taking dinars. Sometimes he would say, "I would hold [the money] and then come to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and say: ‘O Messenger of Allah, wait, I ask you about something. I sell camels in al-Baqi’ and I sell for dinars, taking dirhams, and sell for dirhams, taking dinars.’ He said: “There is no harm in you taking the price of the day, as long as you do not disagree, and there is nothing between you.’”
Narrated by Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, and his armor was pledged with a Jew for thirty sa’s of barley."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Kathir from Abu Minhal, from Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Medina while they were practicing deferred payment in fruits for two or three years. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘Practice deferred payment in fruits, on a known measure and a known weight.’ Sufyan used to mention a specific time limit for it, but ‘Abbad ibn Kathir disputed it.”
Sa'id ibn al-Rabee' reported: Shu'bah narrated to me from Muḥārib who said: I heard Jabir (RA) say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) weighed dirhams for them and they proved to be heavier.

I and Makhrama, the ‘Abdi slave, brought some fish from the two seas to Mecca. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us walking. He bargained with us for trousers or bought trousers from us, and there was a weight-keeper weighing with reward. He said to the weight-keeper, "Weigh and be just." When he began to walk, they said, "This is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Demanding payment from someone wealthy is injustice, and if anyone pursues another who is well-off, let him pursue."

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Yunus narrated to me from Zuhri from Abdullah ibn Ka’b from his father that he sued Ibn Abi Hadrad for a debt that he owed him in the mosque, and their voices rose until the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) heard them while he was in his house, so he came out to them and called out, "O Ka’b!" He said: "Labbayk, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Reduce your debt," and he gestured to him, meaning half of it. He said: "I have done so." He said: "Get up and pay it."

"Whoever grants respite to a debtor, or remits his debt, Allah will shade him with His shade on the Day when there will be no shade but His." He (the narrator) said: He spat in his paper and said, "Go, it is for you to give to his creditor," and mentioned that he was a debtor.
One who relieves a debtor or waives his debt, he will be under the Shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.
"Whoever finds his property with his own eyes in the possession of a bankrupt or with a man who has become bankrupt, then he is more deserving of it than others."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The soul of the believer is suspended as long as he has a debt."
"One who departs from the body, free from three things, enters Paradise: arrogance, consuming illicit gains, and debt."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abi Qatada from his father: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a deceased person to be prayed upon. He said, "Pray upon your companion, for he had a debt." Abu Qatada said, "It is upon me, O Messenger of Allah." He ﷺ said, "By fulfilling it?" He said, "By fulfilling it." So, he ﷺ prayed upon him.

By Him in Whose Hand My Soul Is, there is not a single believer on earth but I am closer to him than his own relatives. So whoever leaves behind debts or dependents, let him invoke me [to settle them], for I am his guardian. And whoever leaves behind wealth, it belongs to his relatives who are deserving. 

‘Abdullah said, “By ‘dependents’ he means ‘children.’”

He said, “Let him invoke me [to settle them] means: Invoke me, and I will settle it for him.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah is with the indebted person until their debt is paid, as long as they are not engaged in something Allah dislikes." He (Abdullah ibn Ja'far) would say to his treasurer: "Go and bring me a debt, for I dislike spending a night without Allah being with me, after I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Upon the hand is what it has taken until it fulfills it.”
"Fulfill the trust of those who trust you, and do not betray one who has betrayed you."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Humayd narrated to me from Anas, who said: One of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) presented to him a bowl containing thrīd (a dish of wheat and meat). He was in the house of one of his wives. The bowl was struck and broke. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) began to take the thrīd and return it to the broken bowl, saying: "Eat, for your mother has been angered." Then he waited until a sound bowl arrived. He took it and gave it to the owner of the broken bowl. Abdullah said: We rely on this.

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to me, he said: Abu Usama narrated to me, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, who said: Muhammad ibn Shu'aib narrated to me, from 'Amr and 'Aasim, sons of Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah ibn Rabia'a al-Thaqafi, that Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah found a stray animal and brought it to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. He said, "Identify it for a year. If it is recognized, then it is theirs; otherwise, it is yours." It was not recognized, so he met him with it the following year during the season and reminded him of it. 'Umar said, "It is yours, for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered us to do so." He said, "I have no need for it." So 'Umar took it and placed it in the public treasury.

Narrated Abu Hurairah that when Mecca was conquered, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) stood up and said: "Verily, Allah withheld the elephant from Mecca and empowered me and the believers. Know that it was never lawful for anyone before me, nor will it be lawful for anyone after me. Know that this hour of mine is sacred, so no one should hunt in it, nor should any tree be felled, nor should anything fallen be picked up except by a reciter (of poetry)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The loss of a Muslim is the burning of Hellfire."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Al-Jariri narrated to me from Abu al-'Ala, from Abu Muslim al-Jarmi, from al-Jarud, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The loss of a Muslim is the burning of Hell, the loss of a Muslim is the burning of Hell, the loss of a Muslim is the burning of Hell. Do not approach it." He said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, do we find lost items (luqatah)? He said: "Announce it, and do not conceal it, and do not hide it. If its owner comes, return it to him, otherwise, it is the property of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills."

Narrated Abu Umama: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes the right of a Muslim with his hand, Allah has obligated Hellfire for him and forbidden Paradise upon him.” A man said: "Even if it is something trivial, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: "Even if it is a twig from an Araak tree.”

Narrated Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik from his brother Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, that Abu Umama Al-Harithi told him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) … (and then mentioned a similar account).

Narrated Abu Al-Walid and Hajjaj: They said, "Tell us, Shu'bah said, 'He told me, Ali ibn Mudrik said, 'I heard Abu Zarrah narrating from Kharsah ibn al-Hurr from Abu Dharr who said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Three people whom Allah will not speak to, nor look at, nor purify on the Day of Resurrection, and for them will be a painful torment." I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who are they – those who fail and lose?' He repeated it. I said, 'Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: "The one who trails his garment (in arrogance), the one who gives gifts boastfully, and the one who sells goods with false oaths."
"Whoever wrongs someone over a span of land (even as little as) a handspan, it will be encircled around him from seven earths."
"Whoever revives a dead land, then he has reward in it, and whatever the healthy creatures eat from it, then he has charity in it."

Abu Dharr narrated: "I cut a portion of the salt lands from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which was called 'Milh Shadha' in Ma'rib. Then Al-Aqra' bin Habis Al-Tamimi said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I used to frequent Milh in the pre-Islamic period, and it was in a land without water. Whoever frequented it, took it, and it was like the water of 'Idd.' So, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) inquired of Abu Dharr about his cutting of the salt lands. I said: 'I have cut it on the condition that you make it a charity from me.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'It is a charity from you, and it is like the water of 'Idd. Whoever frequents it, takes it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then cut for him a piece of land and some palm trees, and so it is in Jauf, the place where he cut it from him." Al-Faraj said: "It is still so: whoever frequents it, takes it."

Narrated by Alqama bin Wail: My father said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted him land." He said, "Then Mu'awiya was sent with me." He said, "Give it to him." Yahya said: Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to me, Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to me, through Gundar, with this narration.

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: Umm Mubahir, the wife of Zaid bin Harithah, informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered a garden of mine. He said: "O Umm Mubahir! Did a Muslim plant this (tree), or a non-Muslim?" I said, "A Muslim." He (ﷺ) said: "It is not possible that a Muslim plants a tree or sows a seed, or cultivates a garden, or a bird eats from it, or an animal, without it being charity for him."

Abu Dhaybah narrated: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the grazing land of the wild donkeys, and he said: “There is no inviolable pasture in the grazing land of the wild donkeys.” I said: “But there are wild donkeys in my enclosure?” He (ﷺ) said: “There is no inviolable pasture in the grazing land of the wild donkeys.” Faraj said: The son of Abu Dhaybah means by ‘my enclosure’ the land which contains crops surrounded by a fence.

Narrated by Iyas ibn ‘Abd al-Muzani, who was among the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): “Do not sell water, for I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbidding the sale of water.” And ‘Amru ibn Dinaar said: “We do not know which water.” He (Iyas) said: “He (the Prophet) said: ‘I do not know, is it running water or the drawn water?’”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Kahmas narrated to me from Sayyar, a man from Fazara, from his father, from Buhaisa, from his father, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): That a man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and asked for permission to enter, and he entered between him and his garment. Uthman said: He clung to him, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "What is the thing that is not permissible to withhold?" He said: "Salt and water." The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "What is the thing that is not permissible to withhold?" He said: "If you do good, it is better for you." He said: "What is the thing that is not permissible to withhold?" He said: "If you do good, it is better for you," and he reached the point of salt and water. It was said to Abdullah: Do you say it (the Hadith)? He nodded his head.
Narrated Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a treaty with Khaybar, granting them half of what comes out of its fruits or produce.

Abu al-Hasan narrated to us from Zakariyya ibn Ishaq, who said: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us that he heard Jabir say: We used to exchange news before the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade us from exchanging news, for two or three months. We would mention a third, a half, and some straw. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to us: "Whoever has land, let him cultivate it. If he dislikes cultivating it, let him grant it to his brother. If he dislikes granting it to his brother, let him leave it."

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Musahir from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani from ‘Abdullah ibn as-Sa’ib, who said: I asked ‘Abdullah ibn Ma’qil about muzara’ah (partnership in agriculture), and he said: Thabit ibn ad-Dahhak al-Ansari informed me that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade muzara’ah. He said to ‘Abdullah: Do you testify to it? He said: I do not testify to the first statement.
Narrated by Jabir: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of white land for two or three years.

We used to lease land during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, based on what was planted on the irrigation channels and what water was available from it. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, forbade us from that, and permitted us – or he said, allowed us – to lease it for gold and silver.

Sahal ibn Abi Hathmah came to our gathering and narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "If you are eager (to acquire wealth), then take and leave, leave a third. If you do not leave a third, then leave a quarter."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade earning from female slaves.
Narrated by Sa’ib bin Yazid from Rafiq bin Khadij: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The earnings of a barber is impure, the dowry of a prostitute is impure, and the price of a dog is impure."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad al-Jawali narrated to me, from Anas ibn Malik: That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was bled by Abu Taybah, and he ordered two sa’s of food for him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the plucking of the sheaths of young male animals.
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the castration of male animals and the earnings of a prostitute.

Narrated by Abu Nu'aim, he said: Isma'il narrated to us, he said: He is Ibn Ibrahim Ibn Muhajir, he said: I heard 'Abd al-Malik Ibn 'Umayr narrating, he said: I heard 'Amr Ibn Hurayth narrating, from his brother, Sa'id Ibn Hurayth, who was among the companions, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saying: "Whoever sells a house or property among you, then it is possible that the blessing is withheld from him unless he makes it in its like."
"Whoever digs a well, then no one has the right to dig around it forty paces for his livestock."

Yalaa narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Malik narrated to me from Ata, from Jabir, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) spoke about intercession, saying: "It is looked into (whether it is permissible), if their path is one?." He said: "It is looked into (whether it is permissible), even if its owner is absent."

Narrated by Jabir: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ decreed that a partner in a joint ownership (of property) has the right of pre-emption in every partnership that was not divided, whether it be a quarter or a plot of land. It is not permissible for him to sell it without the permission of his partner. If his partner wishes, he may take it (the right of pre-emption), and if he wishes, he may leave it. If he sells it without informing him, then he (the partner) has a greater right to it.”

It was said to Abu Muhammad: Do you say this?

He said: Yes.

Abu Sa’id al-Khudri narrated: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari asked ‘Umar for permission three times, but was not granted it. He returned and said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: ‘If one who seeks permission is granted permission three times, then he should be allowed in, or he should return.’” ‘Umar said, “You shall bring someone to bear witness with you, or I shall do something, and I shall do it.” Abu Sa’id said: He came to us while we were with a group of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the mosque, and he was frightened by ‘Umar’s threat to him. He stood up and said, “I seek Allah’s protection from among you, a man who heard this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), except that he bear witness to it for me.” I raised my head and said, “Inform him that I am with you on this.” Others said the same, and Abu Musa was relieved.
Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and knocked at his door. He said, "Who is that?" I said, "It is I." He said, "It is I? It is I?!" And he disliked that.

Narrated by Jabir bin Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man from striking his wife at night, or causing her distress, or seeking out her faults. Sufyan said: Sufyan said about the statement, "or causing her distress, or seeking out her faults," I do not know what that means. Muḥārib said: or it is something in the Hadith.

Narrated Abdullah ibn Salam: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Medina, the people were eager to see him, and they said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has arrived." So I went out with those who went out, and when I saw his face, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing I heard him say was: "O people, spread the greeting of peace, feed the poor, maintain the ties of kinship, and pray while people are asleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There are six things a Muslim must fulfill for another Muslim: returning his greeting, saying ‘May Allah have mercy on you’ when he sneezes, visiting him when he is sick, answering his call, attending his funeral, and loving for him what he loves for himself, and advising him in secret.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The rider greets the pedestrian, the standing person greets the seated person, and the few greet the many."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, when one of the Jews greets another, he only says, ‘May the curse be upon you.’ You [Muslims] should say, ‘Upon you.’”

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from Siyar, who said: I was walking with Thabit al-Bunani, and we passed by some young boys, and he greeted them. Thabit narrated that he was with Anas, and they passed by some young boys, and he greeted them. Anas narrated that he was with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and they passed by some young boys, and he greeted them.

Narrated by Asma bint Yazid bin Sakin, one of the women of Banu Abd al-Ashhal: That while she was in a Sawiq (a type of barley preparation), the Prophet (peace be upon him) passed by them and greeted them.

Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “O Aisha, this is Gabriel, sending you greetings.” She said: “And upon him be peace, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings.” She said: “And he sees what I do not see.”

Abu Dharr (RA) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed, and I approached him when he finished his prayer. I was the first to greet him with the greeting of Islam. He said: “Peace, mercy of Allah be upon you! From where are you?” I said: “From Ghifar.” He then gestured with his hand. I thought to myself: He disliked that I belonged to Ghifar.

Narrated ‘Imran ibn Husain: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said, “As-salamu alaykum.” He responded and said, “Ten.” Then a man came and said, “As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi.” He responded and said, “Twenty.” Then a man came and said, “As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu.” He responded and said, “Thirty.”

Mujaahid ibn Qunfudh reported: I greeted the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was urinating. He did not return my greeting until he performed ablution. Then, when he performed ablution, he returned my greeting.

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Do not visit women.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, except the muhrim (female relatives)?”. He (ﷺ) said: “The muhrim is death.” Yahya said: The muhrim means the relatives of the husband.
I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about the accidental glance, and he said: "Turn away your gaze."

Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about the length of a woman’s garment, and he said, "An ell." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will their feet then be exposed?" He said, "Then an arm’s length, they should not exceed that." Abdullah said: The people say: From Naafi’, from Sulayman ibn Yasir.

Narrated by her husband, from Rib'i bin Hirash, from his wife, from a sister of Hudhaifa: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon to the women and said: “O women, do you not have (enough) silver with which to adorn yourselves? Indeed, no woman adorns herself with gold and displays it, but she will be punished for it.”

Narrated by Abu Musa: “Any woman who applies perfume and then goes out to have her scent noticed, she is a fornicatress, and every eye that looks at her is also a fornicator.” Abu ‘Aasim said: Some of our companions relate it with a chain of narration that elevates it.

Narrated Abdullah: Allah curses the women who get their faces tattooed, pluck their eyebrows, and make incisions in their skin to beautify themselves, changing the creation of Allah. A woman from the tribe of Assad, named Um Yaqub, heard this and came to him and said, "It has reached me that you have cursed so-and-so and so-and-so." He said, "And why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) cursed, and it is in the Book of Allah?" She said, "I have recited what is between the two tablets (the preserved knowledge), and I did not find therein what you say." He said, "If you have recited it, you have certainly found it. Have you not recited, 'And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is severe in punishment' [Al-Hashr 59:7]?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Then he has forbidden it." She said, "But I see the women of my family doing it." He said, "Then enter and see." She entered and looked, but she did not find what she was looking for. Then he said, "If it were like that, I would not have married her."

Uthman ibn Muhammad narrated to me, that Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to me, that Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Hadrami narrated to me, that Ayyash ibn Abbas al-Himayri narrated to me, from Abu al-Husein al-Hajri, from Abu Amir, who said: I heard Abu Rayhana, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), saying: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade ten things: a man lying with a man in the same garment without anything between them, and a woman lying with a woman in the same garment without anything between them. Also, plucking (eyebrows), tattooing, cutting (hair), riding lions, and wearing silk robes here (on the shoulders) and below the garments." Abdullah said: Abu Amir was a shaykh among them, and al-mukama'a means lying together.

Yazid ibn Harun and Wahb ibn Ja'rir narrated to me: that Hisham, who was ad-Dustawa'i, narrated to us from Yahya, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) cursed the effeminate men and the women who act like men, and said: "Expel them from your homes." He (the Prophet) then expelled so-and-so, and Umar expelled so-and-so or so-and-so. Abdullah said: "I doubt (about this incident)."

Malik narrated from Abu Nadr from Zurra bin ‘Abd ar-Rahman from his father, who was among the companions of the Suffa, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat with us and my thigh was exposed. He said: "Cover it, do you not know that the thigh is ‘awrah (a part of the body that must be covered)?"

A group of women from the people of Hims came to Aisha seeking a legal opinion. She asked, "Are you perhaps among the women who enter bathhouses?" They replied, "Yes." She said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: 'No woman places down her garments except in a place other than her husband's house but she has unveiled what is between her and Allah.'"
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Let not a man displace his brother from his seat, and then sit in it, but rather accommodate one another and be generous.”
"When one of you rises from an assembly and then returns to it, he is most deserving of it."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me from al-Bara’: That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a group of people sitting from the Ansar, and said: "If you must [do something], then pave the way [to goodness], spread greetings, and assist the oppressed." Shu'bah said: Abu Ishaq did not hear this hadith from al-Bara’.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khālif narrated to me, Sufyān said: I heard Zuhri narrating, from ‘Abbād ibn Tamīm, from his uncle, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, reclining in the mosque, placing one leg upon the other.

"Narrated by Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If you are three (persons), let not two of you speak privately without the consent of their companion, for that grieves him."

Yalaa ibn ‘Ubayd narrated to me, he said: Hajaaj – meaning Ibn Dinaar – narrated to me from Abu Hashim from Rufe’ ibn Abi ‘Aliyah from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the later part of his life, whenever he sat in an assembly and intended to rise, he would say: “Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ash-hadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk (Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I turn to You).”

So they said: O Messenger of Allah, you are now saying words that you used not to say before. He (ﷺ) said: “This is an expiation for what occurs in the assemblies.”

Narrated Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The one who sneezes should say: 'Alhamdulillah 'ala kulli halin (Praise be to Allah in every condition).’ And the one who hears him should say: ‘May Allah have mercy on you.’ And he (the one who sneezed) should reply: ‘May Allah guide you and set your affairs straight.’”

Narrated Anas: Two men sneezed before the Prophet (peace be upon him), and one of them said, “May Allah bless you,” and the other did not. It was said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, you blessed this one and not the other?” He said, “Indeed, this one praised Allah, and this one did not.” Abdullah said: Sulaiman is At-Taymi.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, he said: Ikrimah, who is Ibn ‘Ammar, said to me: Iyasu ibn Salama narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me: A man sneezed in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he said: “May Allah have mercy on you.” Then he sneezed again, and he said: “The man is afflicted with a cold.”

Aisha (RA) said: "We had a garment with pictures on it, and I spread it out before the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was praying. He forbade me or said, 'I dislike it.' She said: So I made it cushions."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The angel does not enter a house containing a dog, an image, or a person in a state of ritual impurity (janabah)."
The Muslim who spends on his family while seeking reward (for it) – it is a charity for him.

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to me, saying: He (Thabit) narrated to me that ‘Asim al-Ahwal narrated to me from Mu’awwidh ibn ‘Abdullah, from ‘Abdullah ibn Ja’far, who said: “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would, when setting out, take me and either al-Hasan or al-Husayn with him. He said: And I think he said: al-Hasan. So he carried me in front of him and al-Hasan behind him, until we arrived in Medina while we were on the mount that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was riding.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi, who was the governor of Kufa: We came to Qays ibn Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah in his house. The muezzin announced the call to prayer, and we said to Qays, "Stand and lead us in prayer." He said, "I would not lead a people over whom I am not their leader." A man said, "There is a hadith concerning this." He was identified as Abdullah ibn Hanza’l ibn al-Ghasil, who said, "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: ‘A man is most deserving to lead (prayer) in the front of his mount, in the front of his bed, and to lead (prayer) in his travel.’” Upon this, Qays ibn Sa’d said, “O so-and-so,” addressing a servant of his, “Stand and lead them in prayer.”

Narrated by Muhammad bin Hamza bin ‘Amro Al-’Aslami, who said: My father accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: I heard my father say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the ridge of every camel is a devil, so when you mount it, mention the name of Allah and do not fall short in fulfilling your needs."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Mount these beasts sound (unburdened), and do not make them seats.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Traveling is a portion of punishment, it deprives one of his sleep, food, and drink. So, when one of you has satisfied his need (or desire) from his face, let him hasten his return to his family.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, and Saeed ibn Abi K’ab narrated: Abu al-Hasan al-‘Abdi said: Musa ibn Maysarah al-‘Abdi narrated to me from Anas ibn Malik who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, I intend to travel.” He said to him: “When?” He said: “Tomorrow, if Allah wills.” So he came to him, and the Prophet took his hand and said to him: “You are under the protection of Allah, and in His care. May Allah grant you piety, forgive your sins, and direct you to goodness wherever you seek it or wherever you turn.” Saeed hesitated about one of the words.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, and ‘Asim narrated to me, he being Al-Ahwal, saying: Shu’bah strengthened my memory of the following narration from Abdullah ibn Sarjis, who said: Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) used to travel, he would say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from weariness of travel, sadness of return, and from being overtaken by misfortune after good fortune, and from the supplication of the oppressed, and from bad sights concerning my family and possessions.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he traveled and mounted his mount, would say Takbir three times and say: “Glory to the One who has subjugated this for us, and we could not have subjugated it ourselves, and indeed, we are returning to our Lord.” [Quran 43:13-14] He would also say: “O Allah, I ask you for goodness in this journey of mine, and for piety, and for work that You are pleased with. O Allah, make this journey easy for us, and shorten the distance for us. O Allah, You are the companion in the journey, and the caretaker of our families. O Allah, accompany us in our journey, and replace us with goodness in our families.”
Narrated Jabir: "Whenever we ascended a hill, we would say Takbir (Allahu Akbar), and whenever we descended a hill, we would say SubhanAllah."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The caravan that contains bells is not accompanied by the angels."
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The angels do not accompany a group in which there is a dog or a bell."

Narrated ‘Imran ibn Husain: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was on a journey when he heard a curse. He asked, “What is this?” They said, “Fulana cursed her camel.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Put her down, for she is cursed.” So they put her down. ‘Imran said, “I can almost see her, a lean female camel.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A woman should not travel for a journey of three days or more except in the company of her father, or her brother, or her husband, or a mahram from among them."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If people knew what was in solitude, no rider would travel alone at night ever again."

"Narrated by Khawla bint Hakim: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: ‘If any of you, when he sets down at a place, says: ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,’ nothing would harm him in that place until he departs from it.’”

Abu 'Aasim narrated from 'Uthman ibn Sa'd from Anas ibn Malik: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, when he settled at a place, not depart from it until he had prayed two rak'ahs, or bid farewell to the place with two rak'ahs.

'Abdullah said: 'Uthman ibn Sa'd is weak.

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would say when he returned from a journey, "Returning, if Allah wills, repentant, worshippers, praising our Lord."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, saying: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded a man, when he takes his place of rest, to say: "O Allah, I have submitted my soul to You, and I have directed my face towards You, and I have entrusted my affairs to You, and I have sought refuge with You, out of hope and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed, and Your Prophet whom You have sent. If he dies, he dies upon the natural disposition [fitrah]."

"When one of you goes to bed, let him shake his bed with the inside of his garment, for he does not know what he leaves behind in it, and let him say: ‘O Allah, with You I lay my side down, and with You I raise it. O Allah, if You take my soul, then forgive it, and if You send it back, then keep it safe by that which You keep safe the righteous.’”

Narrated by ‘Ali: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us until he placed his foot between me and Fatima, and taught us what to say when we retire to our beds: “Thirty-three times Tasbih (saying Subhanallah), thirty-three times Tahmid (saying Alhamdu lillah), and thirty-four times Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar).” ‘Ali said: I have never left it since. A man said to him: Not even on the night of Siffin? He said: Not even on the night of Siffin.

Narrated by Hudhaifa: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would, when he awoke from sleep, say: “All praise is due to Allah who has given us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the return.”

"Whoever rises during the night and says: 'There is no deity but Allah, alone without any partner; to Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things powerful; Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is the greatest; and there is neither power nor strength except in Allah,' and then says, 'O Lord, forgive me,' or he supplicates, his supplication will be accepted. And if he then performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abdur-Rahman ibn Abza from his father: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would say every morning: "We have risen upon the fitrah of Islam, the word of sincerity, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, and the way of our father Abraham, a true monotheist and a Muslim."

Abu Hurairah said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, instruct me with something I can say when I rise in the morning and when I retire in the evening." He (the Prophet) said: "Say: 'O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the manifest, Lord of everything and its Sovereign, I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of the devil and his partnership.'" He (the Prophet) said: "Say it when you rise in the morning, when you retire in the evening, and when you take your place to sleep."

Narrated by Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wears a garment and says: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi kasani hadha warazaqanihi min ghairi hawlin minni wa la quwwatin,' (All praise be to Allah Who has clothed me with this and provided it for me without any ability or power from me), his past sins will be forgiven."

Narrated Abu Hurairah or Abu Usayd: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When any of you enters a mosque, he should say: 'Allahumma iftah li abwab rahmatika,' and when he exits, he should say: 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlika.'"

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Azhar ibn Sinan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Wasiq, who said: "I came to Mecca and met my brother Salim ibn Abdullah there, and he narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather: That the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever enters a marketplace and says: "There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, alone without any partners. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise. He gives life and He causes death, and He is the living, who never dies. In His hand is all goodness, and He is over all things capable," Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds, and erases a thousand thousand bad deeds, and raises him a thousand thousand degrees.'" He said: "I then came to Khurasan and met Qutaiba ibn Muslim, and I said to him: 'I have come to you with a gift,' so I narrated it to him. And he would ride in his procession, and come to the marketplace, stand, and say it, then return."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunya (nickname)."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and the names of your fathers, so beautify your names."
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The most beloved names to Allah are ‘Abdullah and ‘Abd ar-Rahman.”
Narrated by Samura: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade naming our slaves four names: Afalḥ, Nāfi‘, Ribāḥ, and Yasār.
Narrated by Ibn Umar: Um 'Asim was called 'Asiya, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) named her Jamila.

Musaddad narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, Shu'bah narrated to me, Ata' ibn Abi Munaabah narrated to me, from Abu Rafia', from Abu Hurairah, who said: "The name of Zainab was Barrah. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) named her Zainab."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Tufayl, the brother of 'Aisha, who said: A man from amongst the polytheists said to a man from amongst the Muslims: "You are a good people, were it not that you say, 'What Allah wills, and what Muhammad wills.'" The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) heard this, and said: "Do not say, 'What Allah wills, and what Muhammad wills,' but say, 'What Allah wills, then what Muhammad wills.'"

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Muhammad, who is Ibn Ishaq, narrated to me from Salih ibn Ibrahim, from Abdur-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not call a vineyard 'the grape vine,' for the grape vine is the Muslim man."

Abu 'Aasim narrated: Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd narrated to me from Anas, who said: A young boy used to lead the Prophet’s wives (peace be upon him). He said: "O Anjasha, slow your pace with the glass flasks."
"Woe to him who speaks and tells lies to make the people laugh; woe to him! Woe to him! Woe to him!"

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Sulaiman narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Ya’qub ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, affirmed the truthfulness of Ummayyah ibn Abi Salit in two couplets of poetry, saying: “A man and a bull beneath his right leg, and an eagle to the other, and a lion lying in wait.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “He has spoken the truth.” He said: “And the sun rises every last night, red, its color becoming rosy.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “He has spoken the truth.” Then someone said: “It does not refuse, but it does not rise for us in its course except as being tormented, or being lashed.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “He has spoken the truth.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, there is wisdom in poetry."
The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: It is better for one of you to be filled with pus or blood than to be filled with vanity.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever Allah intends good for, He grants him understanding in the religion."
Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, health and free time are two blessings from Allah, in which many people are deceived."
"Whoever listens to the talk of a people while they dislike it, then molten lead is poured into his ears."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not follow a look with a look, for the first one is for you, and the second is against you.”

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Sufyan from his father: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a deed in Islam about which I will not ask anyone else." He said, "Fear Allah, and then be upright." I said, "Then what?" He pointed to his tongue.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, he said: Ibrahim narrated to me, meaning Ibn Ismail ibn Mujahid, said: Ibn Shihab told me, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Mu'adh, from Sufyan ibn Abdullah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, command me with something I may hold fast to." He said: "Say: 'My Lord is Allah, then keep to the straight path.'" I said: "O Prophet of Allah, what do you fear most for me?" He said: The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, took hold of his tongue and said: "This."
Jabir narrated: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, which form of Islam is best?" He said, "That from which the Muslims are safe from the harm of your tongue and hand."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever fasts, is saved."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked, "What is backbiting?" He said, "Mentioning your brother with something he dislikes." It was said, "What if I am saying the truth about him?" He said, "If he has that which you mention, then you have backbitten him; and if he does not have that, then you have lied against him."

Narrated by Abu Al-Ahwas: That Abdullah transmits the Hadith to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) who said: "Indeed, the worst of narrators is the narrator of falsehood. Neither seriousness nor jest is permissible from falsehood. And a man should not promise his son and then fail to fulfill it. Indeed, truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. And falsehood leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. And it is said to the truthful person: ‘You have spoken truthfully and acted righteously,’ and it is said to the liar: ‘You have lied and committed wickedness.’ And indeed, a man may continue to speak the truth until he is recorded with Allah as a truthful person, and he may continue to lie until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.” And he said: "Should I tell you what the 'Adh' is? Indeed, the 'Adh' is the gossip that corrupts between people."
The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O people, indeed Allah is Pure and He does not accept anything but that which is pure. Indeed, Allah has commanded the believers to what He commanded the messengers. [He ﷺ recited]: ‘O messengers, eat from the good and pure things and work righteousness. Indeed, I am Aware of what you do.’ [Surah Al-Mu’minun, 51] And He ﷺ recited: ‘O you who believe, eat from the good things which Allah has provided you and be grateful to Allah if you are His worshippers.’ [Surah Al-Baqarah, 172]. Then he ﷺ described a man who travels far, his hair unkempt and dusty, stretching his hands towards the sky, saying: ‘O Lord, O Lord!’ But his food is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and his drink is unlawful. He has been nourished with the unlawful. How can such a prayer be accepted?”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is sufficient for one of you from this world a servant and a riding beast."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The righteous ones will pass away like the foregone strands of barley husk, and what remains will be chaff, like the chaff of barley."
"How many are the fasting persons who gain nothing from their fast but hunger, and how many are the ones who stand [in prayer] but gain nothing from their standing but sleeplessness?"

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Yazid: Saeed, who is Ibn Abi Ayyub, said: He told me Ka'b ibn Alqama, from Isa ibn Hilal As-Sadufi, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) mentioned the prayer one day and said: "Whoever maintains it, it will be a light, a proof, and salvation from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever does not maintain it, it will not be a light for him, nor salvation, nor a proof, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be with Qarun, Pharaoh, Haman, and Abi ibn Khalaf."

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: He said, “I was told by Layth, who said, ‘I was told by Ibn ‘Ajlan, from Husayn bin Abdullah bin ‘Ubaydullah bin Abbas, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to desire to perform the night prayer so much that he would say, ‘Even if it is one rak’ah.’”

I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), for I used to be harsh in my speech towards my family, and I would not direct them to anyone else. He said: "What about seeking forgiveness? Verily, I ask forgiveness from Allah one hundred times every day."

Abu Ishaq said: I informed Abu Burdah and the sons of Abu Musa, Bakr and his brother, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "I seek forgiveness from Allah every day one hundred times, saying: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah and I turn to Him in repentance.'"

Narrated by Anas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited: "He is the one worthy of being feared, and the one worthy of forgiveness." (Surah Al-Muddathir, 56). He said: "Your Lord says: ‘I am worthy to be feared, and whoever fears Me, I am worthy to forgive him.’”

Narrated Abu Darr: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Indeed, I know a verse that, if people were to adhere to it, it would suffice them: ‘And when they reach the term prescribed, then either retain them according to what pleases you or release them with generosity. And witness – before Allah – two witnesses from among your people. And restrain not yourselves from bringing forward evidence, even if it is from your own family, so that you may rule justly. Allah wants to teach everyone who believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, He will provide for him a way out.’” [Surah At-Talaq, verse 2]
Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to me: “O Aisha, beware of the trivial sins, for they have a claimant from Allah.”
Every son of Adam commits error, and the best of those who err are the repentant.

Narrated by Nu’man bin Bashir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man traveled in a barren land and said, 'I shall rest under this tree with my camel, which carries my provisions and food.' Then he awoke and found his camel gone. He climbed a high place but saw nothing. Then he climbed another high place but saw nothing. Then he climbed yet another high place but saw nothing. He turned around and there it was, dragging its reins. He was not more delighted with it than Allah is delighted with the repentance of His slave when he turns to Him in repentance."

Narrated Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew for us a square, then drew a line in the middle of it, then drew lines around it, and drew a line outside of the line. He then said: "This is the human being for the middle line, and this is the decree which encompasses him, and these are the afflictions for the lines. So if one of them misses him, the other bites him, and this is hope for the outer line.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two hungry wolves released into a flock of sheep could not cause more damage than a person’s eagerness for wealth and status causes to his religion."
Allah, blessed and exalted, said: “I am as My servant expects Me to be. Let him then think (of Me) as he wishes.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) stood up when Allah revealed, "And warn your close relatives." (Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:214) and said: "O Quraysh, buy your souls from Allah; I cannot avail you against Allah in anything. O Bani 'Abd Manaf, I cannot avail you against Allah in anything. O Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you against Allah in anything. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you against Allah in anything. O Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, ask of me whatever you wish, for I cannot avail you against Allah in anything."

Narrated Jabir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be moderate and upright, and know that none of you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, not even you?" He said: "Not even me, except if Allah covers me with His Mercy and favor."

Narrated Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Each of you has a companion from the jinn and a companion from the angels." They said: As for you (O Messenger of Allah)? He said: "Yes, as for me too, but Allah has helped me against him and he has become a Muslim." Abu Muhammad said: Some people say, 'He has become a Muslim,' meaning 'He has surrendered.' They say: 'He has become humiliated.'"
"Were you to know what I know, you would laugh little and weep much."

Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Abu al-Muhaizmi, from Abu Huraira, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed by a discarded, barren female goat. He said: "Do you consider this insignificant to its people?" They said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, the world is lighter to Allah than this is to its people."

Narrated Jabir ibn ‘Awn, he said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwa narrated to me from his father, from Abu al-Murawih, from Abu Dharr, who said: A man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), "Which deeds are best?" He said: "Belief in Allah and striving in the way of Allah."
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "The best of deeds in the sight of Allah is faith without doubt in it." Abu Muhammad, Abu Ja'far, said: A man from the Ansar.
"None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself."
None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his children, and all of humankind.

A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the best of people?” He said, “Those whose lives are long and whose deeds are good.” He said, “And who are the worst of people?” He said, “Those whose lives are long and whose deeds are bad.”

Abu al-Mughira reported: I was told by al-Awza'i, he said: I was told by Asid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Khalid ibn Durayk, from Ibn Muhayriz, who said: I said to Abu Jum'a, a man of the Companions, "Recite to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)." He said, "Yes, I will recite a good hadith to you: We broke our fast with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and Abu Ubaida ibn al-Jarrah was with us. He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, is anyone better than us? We embraced Islam and fought alongside you?' He (the Prophet) said: 'Yes, there will be people after you who believe in me but did not see me.'"

Narrated by Abu Wail, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) who said: "It is bad for one of you to say, 'I have forgotten an ayah such as and such.' Rather, it was forgotten, so remind yourselves of the Quran, for it departs from the memories of men faster than sheep depart from their enclosures."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Let none of you say: 'I am better than Yunus (Jonah) ibn Matta.'"

Narrated Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "It is obligatory on every Muslim to give charity." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if he is unable or does not do it?" He said: "He should help himself with his hands and eat from it and give charity." They said: "What if he does not do that?" He said: "He should help a person in distress." They said: "What if he does not do that?" He said: "He should order what is good." They said: "What if he does not do that?" He said: "He should refrain from evil, for that is charity for him."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid: He narrated to me Hiyyah, who said: He narrated to me Abu Sakhr, that he heard Makhul saying: He narrated to me Abu Hind ad-Dari, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saying: "Whoever stands for a posture of showing off and seeking reputation, Allah will see him with it and make him hear it on the Day of Resurrection."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The example of a believer is like that of a young plant of the cultivated land; it bends with the wind sometimes, and is prostrated at other times, until death comes to it. And the example of a disbeliever is like that of a strong, deeply-rooted tree; it does not befall it anything until it collapses in a single fall.” Abu Muhammad said: “Al-Khamah refers to the weak [plant].”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Al-Awza’i, from Ibn Shihab, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyib, and Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, that Hakim ibn Hizam said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and he gave to me, then I asked him and he gave to me, then I asked him and he gave to me, then I asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "O Hakim, indeed this wealth is green and sweet. So whoever takes it with generosity of soul, blessings will be in it for him, and whoever takes it with a stingy soul, no blessings will be in it for him, and it will be like one who eats but does not feel full. And the upper hand [i.e., the giver] is better than the lower hand [i.e., the receiver]."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the killing of female infants, disrespecting mothers, preventing [someone from] giving [charity], demanding [it], idle talk, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I only fear for my community the misleading scholars."

Narrated by Jabir: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Let a man support his brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. If he is an oppressor, then he should restrain him (from oppression), and if he is oppressed, then he should support him."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us, “The religion is sincerity (nasiha).” We said, “For whom, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “For Allah, for His Messenger, for the Book, and for the leaders and the entire generality of the Muslims.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to us: “Indeed, Islam began as a stranger, and it will return as a stranger, I think.” Hafs said: “So blessed are the strangers.” It was said: “And who are the strangers?” He said: “The one who disputes from amongst the tribes.”

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, he said: Hammam narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas, from ‘Ubadah ibn As-Samit, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him, and whoever hates meeting Allah, Allah hates meeting him."

‘Aisha (or one of his wives) said: "Indeed, we hate death."

He (the Prophet) said: "That is not the case. Rather, when death approaches a believer, he is given the good news of Allah’s pleasure and honor, so nothing is more beloved to him than what lies ahead, so he loves meeting Allah and Allah loves meeting him. And when death approaches a disbeliever, he is given the good news of Allah’s punishment and retribution, so nothing is more hateful to him than what lies ahead, so he hates meeting Allah and Allah hates meeting him."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, Allah the Exalted says on the Day of Resurrection: ‘Where are the mutual-lovers because of My Majesty?’ Today I will shade them with My Shade on a Day when there is no shade but My Shade.”
Do not wish for death, whether you are one increasing in good deeds, for you may increase in goodness, or one decreasing in good deeds, for you may repent.
Narrated Anas: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour (Day of Judgement) have been sent forth like these two (fingers)." And Wahb gestured with his index and middle fingers.
Narrated by Abu Hurairah: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Indeed, you (the Muslims) have followed seventy nations, and you are the last of them and the most noble in the sight of Allah.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Where is so-and-so?" A man among them gestured and said, "He is here, he is here!" The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Is he not one who witnessed Badr?" They said, "Yes." The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Perhaps Allah looked at the people of Badr and said, 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'"

"If Allah withheld rain from my community for ten years and then sent it down, a group of my community would become disbelievers, saying, ‘It is due to the star al-Mijdhah.’” It is said that al-Mijdhah is a star, and it is called ad-Dabaran.
We visited Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah to check on him, and he said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: ‘A good deed is rewarded tenfold.”
"Whoever has two faces (displays duplicity) in the world, he will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection."

"Allahumma, I am only a human being, so whoever among the Muslims I curse, or revile, or strike, then make it for him prayer and mercy and a closeness that brings him nearer to You on the Day of Resurrection.” Another narration is similar, except it contains “zakat (charity) and mercy.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Hammad narrated to me from Amr ibn Murra, who said: I heard Suwaid ibn al-Harith from Abu Dharr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saying: "I do not desire that Mount Uhud were gold for me, that I die and I have a dinar or half a dinar, except for a debt."

"Indeed, you (people) come with matters that are finer in your eyes than hair. We used to consider them, during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, among the ruinous things. Then this was mentioned to Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sirin, and he said, 'He has spoken the truth.' So I see the dragging of the izar (lower garment) as being from that."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Fever is from the heat of Hell or a blast from Hell, so cool it with water."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “No Muslim is afflicted by a calamity that befalls his body, but Allah commands the guardians who protect him, [and says]: ‘Record for My servant each day and night whatever he does of good, as long as he remains confined within My decree.’”

I entered upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was experiencing a severe fever. I placed my hand upon him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, you are experiencing a severe fever.” He said, “I experience a fever as do two of you.” I said, “That is because you have two rewards?” He said, “Yes, and no Muslim is afflicted by an ailment or illness without his sins being forgiven, just as the tree sheds its leaves.”
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever offers one prayer of blessing upon me, Allah will offer ten blessings upon him."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) came one day and there was brightness in his face. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, we see brightness in your face that we have not seen before." He said, "Yes, indeed, an angel came to me and said, ‘O Muhammad, your Lord says to you: Are you not pleased that none of your community sends blessings upon you except that I send blessings upon him ten times, and none greets you except that I greet him ten times?’” He said, “I said, ‘Yes.’”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah has angels who travel the earth, bringing me the greetings of my Ummah."

Narrated by Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mat'im from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: "Indeed, I have names: I am Muhammad, and I am Ahmad, and I am the Eradicator by whom Allah eradicates disbelief, and I am the Assembler upon whose feet the people will be resurrected, and I am al-'Aqib, and al-'Aqib is he after whom there will be none."
Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “O Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah, no flesh grown from illicit gains will enter Paradise.”

While the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was sitting, he laughed. He said, "Will you not ask me about what made me laugh?” They said, “What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “I am amazed at the case of the believer: whatever befalls him, it is all good for him. If something he likes befalls him, he praises Allah for it, so it becomes good for him. If something he dislikes befalls him, he is patient, so it becomes good for him. Not everyone’s case is good for him except the believer.”

I used to listen to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and I did not know whether what he said was a revelation or his own words. And he said: “If two valleys of wealth were given to the son of Adam, he would desire a third, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except earth, and Allah will forgive those who repent.”

Narrated by Abu Nu’aim, from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir, from ‘Amru ibn Shu’aib, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Let no one announce (news of war) except an Amir, or someone authorized, or a herald.” I said to ‘Amru ibn Shu’aib: We used to hear those who exaggerate. He said: This is what I heard.

Narrated from Kirdus, who was a storyteller: A man from the people of Badr informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "I would prefer to sit in a gathering like this over freeing four slaves." He said: I said: I said: What gathering did he mean? He said: It was when he was recounting a story. Abu Muhammad said: The man from the companions of Badr is Ali.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A believer is not bitten from the same hole twice."

Narrated Jabir: Sometimes, Jabir was silent. He (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: "Do not enter upon those who are secluded, for Satan courses through the veins of the son of Adam as blood does." They said: "And you?" He said: "Yes, but Allah has helped me against him, and I have submitted [to Allah]."

Narrated by Sa’d: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: "Who among the people are subjected to the most severe trials?" He said: "The prophets, then those closest to them in character, then those who resemble them. A person is tried in proportion to his religion. If his religion is strong, his trial is increased, and if his religion is weak, his trial is lessened. A person’s trials continue until he walks upon the earth without any sin remaining."

Narrated ‘Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians exaggerate in praising ‘Isa, the son of Maryam; but say, ‘Abdullah (Allah’s servant) and His Messenger.’”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him) saying: “Allah has made mercy a hundred parts, and He retained ninety-nine parts with Him, and sent down one part to the earth, by which the creatures show their mercy to each other, even the horse lifts its hoof for its foal, fearing that it may harm it.”

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, relating from his Lord: “Indeed, your Lord is Most Merciful. Whoever thinks of doing a good deed and does not do it, it is recorded for him as a good deed. And if he does it, it is recorded for him as ten good deeds, or seven hundred times, or even more. And whoever thinks of doing a bad deed and does not do it, it is recorded for him as a good deed. And if he does it, it is recorded as a single bad deed, or it is erased. And none perishes except a destroyer.”

Narrated by Abu Dharr: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, a man loves a group of people but is unable to do exactly as they do?" He said, "You, O Abu Dharr, are with those whom you love." I said, "Then I love Allah and His Messenger?" He said, "You are with those whom you love."

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said from his Lord: “O son of Adam, you called upon Me and hoped in Me, so I have forgiven what was within you. O son of Adam, if you come to Me with sins as numerous as the grains of the earth, if you do not associate anything with Me, I will meet you with forgiveness equal to them. O son of Adam, if your sins reach the clouds, then you seek forgiveness of Me, I will forgive you and I care not.”

I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about piety and sin. He said: "Piety is good character, and sin is that which you harbor in yourself and dislike people knowing about."
Abu Dharr (RA) narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah wherever you may be, and follow every evil deed with a good one to erase it, and interact with people in a good manner."
The most complete of believers in faith is the one with the finest character.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Indeed, Allah is gentle and loves gentleness, and He gives because of it what He does not give because of harshness.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah loves gentleness in all matters."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever I take away his two beloved ones and perseveres with patience and hopes for reward [from Allah], I will not be content with a reward for him less than Paradise."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ashhab narrated to me: Ja'far ibn Hayyan narrated to me from Hasan: That 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad visited Ma'qil ibn Yasar while he was sick, the sickness in which he died. Ma'qil said to him: "Indeed, I will tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). If I knew that there was life in me, I would not have told you. Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: 'No servant whom Allah has entrusted with a responsibility over a flock, and he dies while oppressing them, except that Allah has forbidden Paradise upon him.'"

"The best of your leaders are those whom you love and who love you, and you pray for them and they pray for you. The worst of your leaders are those whom you hate and who hate you, and you curse them and they curse you.”

We said: Should we not make war against them, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “No, as long as they maintain the prayer [among you]. If a ruler is appointed over a person and he sees him doing something from the disobedience of Allah, then let him dislike that disobedience of Allah, and let him not remove his hand from obedience.”

Ibn Jabir said: I said: By Allah, O Abu al-Miqdam! By Allah, did you hear this from Muslim ibn Qarah? He faced the Qiblah, and knelt on his knees, and said: By Allah, I heard this from Muslim ibn Qarah, who said: I heard my uncle, Auf ibn Malik, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say it."
Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr: I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about the Trumpet, and he said: "It is a horn that is blown into."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “Allah will seize the earth and fold the heavens in His right hand, and then He will say: ‘I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?’”

Narrated by Ibn Mas’ud: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: It was said to him, "What is the Praised Station?" He said, "That is a Day when Allah, the Exalted, descends upon His Throne, swaying as the new saddle sways from its tightness. And it is as vast as the space between the heavens and the earth. And you will be brought forth barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. And the first to be clothed will be Ibrahim. Allah, the Exalted, will say, 'Clothe My intimate friend.' Then two white garments will be brought forth from the gardens of Paradise. Then he will be clothed after him, and then I will rise up from the right of Allah in a station where the first and the last will envy me."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The people asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) whether they would see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "Would you dispute about seeing the full moon without any clouds between you and it?” They said, “No, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “Would you dispute about seeing the sun without any clouds between you and it?” They said, “No.” He said, “So you will see Him like that.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me, he said: Al-Mughirah ibn Nu'man said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubair relating, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, delivered a sermon and said: “O people, indeed you will be resurrected before Allah, barefoot, unclothed, and uncircumcised.” Then he recited: “As We began the first creation, We will return it. [It is] a promise upon Us. Indeed, We are capable.” (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:104)

Narrated Abu Hurairah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "When Allah gathers the people in a single place, a caller will announce, 'Let every group follow what they used to worship.' So every group will follow what they used to worship, and the people will remain in their state. Then Allah will come to them and say, 'What is the matter with the people that they have gone and you are here?' They will say, 'We are waiting for our Lord.' He will say, 'Do you know Him?' They will say, 'If He shows Himself to us, we will recognize Him.' So He will reveal His leg to them, and they will fall down in prostration. That is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'On the Day when He will reveal His leg (to them), and they will call to their Lord in humility.' (Surah Al-Qalam, 42) And every hypocrite will remain, unable to prostrate, then He will lead them to Paradise."

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir Al-Juhani: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “When Allah gathers the first and the last, and judges between them and finishes the judgment, the believers will say: ‘Our Lord has judged between us, so who will intercede for us to our Lord?’ They will say, ‘Go to Adam, for Allah created him with His own hand and spoke to him.’ So they will come to him and say, ‘O Adam, stand up and intercede for us to our Lord.’ Adam will say, ‘Upon you is Noah.’ So they will come to Noah, and he will direct them to Ibrahim. So they will come to Ibrahim, and he will direct them to Musa. So they will come to Musa, and he will direct them to ‘Isa. So they will come to ‘Isa, and he will say, ‘I will direct you to the Ummiyyah Prophet.’ So they will come to me, and Allah will allow me to stand before Him. Then my place will erupt with the sweetest scent anyone has ever smelled. Then I will come before my Lord, and He will grant me intercession and make light from the hair of my head to the nails of my feet. At that time, the disbelievers will say to Iblis, ‘The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so stand up and intercede for us to your Lord, for you have led us astray.’ Then Iblis will stand up, and his place will erupt with the foulest scent anyone has ever smelled, and then he will grow immensely towards Hell. At that time, he will say, “And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, ‘Indeed, Allah has promised you a promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you.’” (Quran 2:22)

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Every prophet has a supplication, and I intend, if Allah wills, to reserve my supplication as intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Seventy thousand from my Ummah will enter Paradise without being questioned (about their deeds)."
