'Ukkasha said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to include me among them." So he prayed, and another said: "Pray for me, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Ukkasha preceded you in this."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Abi Jad’a: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) saying: “A man from my Ummah will enter Paradise through my intercession, more than the tribe of Banu Tamim.” They said, “Other than you, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Other than me.”

Masruq said: I said to Aisha, "O Mother of the Believers, I have reflected upon the words of Allah, the Exalted: 'On the Day when the earth and the heavens will be exchanged, and they will appear before Allah, the One, the Almighty,' [Surah Ibrahim (14:48)], where will the people be on that Day?" She said: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about this, and he said: "Upon the Sirat."

Narrated ‘Abidullah from Isra’il, from As-Suddi, who said: I asked Mura about the words of Allah, “And there is not among you anyone but that he will enter it. It is surely a matter decreed by your Lord.” (Surah Maryam 19:71). He informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud narrated to them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “The people will enter the Fire, and then they will depart from it according to their deeds. The first of them to leave will be like the flash of lightning, then like the wind, then like the gallop of a horse, then like a rider in his travel bag, then like the stretching of a man, then like his walking.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Death will come in the form of a black, shaggy ram and will be presented between Paradise and Hell. Then it will be announced, ‘O people of Paradise!’ and they will strain their necks and look, and it will be announced, ‘O people of Hell!’ and they will strain their necks and look. They will think that relief has come, and then it will be slaughtered, and it will be announced, ‘Eternity without death.’”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated: “I was informed by Shu’bah, from Simak, from Nu’man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivering a sermon, and he said: ‘I warn you against the Fire, I warn you against the Fire, I warn you against the Fire.’ He kept repeating it until, if he were in my position now, the people in the marketplace would hear him, and even the cloak he was wearing would fall from his shoulders.”

Narrated by his grandfather: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "There was a servant of Allah who did not owe allegiance to Allah. He remained until his life diminished and his age increased. Then he realized that he had not secured any goodness with Allah. So, he summoned his sons and said, 'Which of you knows me best?' They said, 'You are the best, O father.' He said, 'I will not leave any wealth of mine with anyone of you except that I will take it back, or you will do as I command you.' So, he took an oath from them by Allah and said, 'As for me, when I die, take me and burn me in the fire. When I become embers, crush me, then scatter me in the wind.' So, they did that to him by the Lord of Muhammad (ﷺ) when he died. Then he was brought in the best form he had ever been, and he was presented before his Lord. Allah said, 'What made you enter the fire?' He said, 'Your fear, O Lord.' Allah said, 'I hear you reciting the Quran like a pious man.' So, Allah forgave him." Abu Muhammad said: "Yabt'iru" means "to hoard."

Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: A woman was punished in Hellfire because of a cat, which she had kept as a pet and had neither fed nor given water, nor had she set it free to hunt for food.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ninety-nine dragons will be unleashed upon the disbeliever in his grave, tearing at him and biting him until the Hour is established. And if one of them were to blow into the earth, no green thing would grow."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Azhar ibn Sinan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Wasiq, who said: I entered upon Bilal ibn Abi Burdah, and I said to him: My father narrated to me from his father, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), who said: "In Hell there is a valley called Habbah, inhabited by every arrogant tyrant.” So beware that you not be among them.

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “The people of the Fire who are truly the people of the Fire do not die in the Fire. But some people are afflicted by the Fire according to the measure of their sins, and they are burned within it until, when they become ashes, intercession is permitted. Then they emerge from the Fire in groups, in bundles. They are scattered upon the rivers of Paradise. Then it is said to the people of Paradise: ‘Pour water upon them.’ So they pour water upon them, and their flesh grows as a grain grows in a flood plain.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Paradise has eight gates."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who enters Paradise will enjoy bliss and will never suffer distress; his clothes will never wear out, and his youth will never fade. In Paradise there is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has conceived."

"Narrated Abu Hurrah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'A space occupied by the handle of a whip in Paradise is better than all that is in the world and in it. And recite, if you wish: 'Every soul will taste death, and you are certainly given your reward in the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is removed from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, then he has succeeded. And the life of this world is not but a provision of deception.' [Quran 3:185]"

We said, "O Messenger of Allah, of what is the structure of Paradise?" He said, "Of bricks of gold and silver, its mortar is musk, its pebbles are rubies and pearls, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it never leaves it, enjoying without suffering, their youth never fades, and their garments never wear out."

Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays reported from his father that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The gardens of Firdaus are four: two of gold, their adornments and vessels and what is in them, and two of silver, their adornments and vessels and what is in them. And between the people and seeing their Lord are only the garments of pride upon their faces in the gardens of Eden. And these rivers burst forth from the gardens of Eden in a valley, and then ascend afterwards as rivers.” Abdullah said: "A valley is that from which the earth is filled."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first group of my Ummah to enter Paradise will be like the brightness of the full moon, and then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky.” ‘Ukkasha stood up and said: “O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to include me among them.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Allah, include him among them.” Then another man stood up and said: “O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to include me among them.” The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “‘Ukkasha has preceded you in that.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa’id: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: “And they will be told, ‘Enter therein in peace, and enter the Garden in tranquility.’” (Surah Al-A’raf, 7:43) He (the Prophet) then said: “They will be called out: ‘Be healthy and do not fall ill, be prosperous and do not become impoverished, be young and do not grow old, and abide eternally and do not die.’”

Narrated by Zayd ibn Arqam that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man from the people of Paradise is given the strength of a hundred men in eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse, and desire." A man from the Jews said: "Does he have a need (for that) because he eats and drinks?" He (the Prophet) replied: "Sweat flows from his skin, and when his belly is full."
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise are young, unblemished, free from calluses, with kohl-lined eyes, their garments do not wear out, and their youth never diminishes."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The people of Paradise neither urinate, nor defecate, nor have carnal desire. Rather, it is presented to them as a complete, nourishing drink. They eat, they drink, and they are inspired with glorification and praise, just as they are inspired with breath.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah says: ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and which has not occurred to the mind of any human being. And recite, if you wish: “No soul knows what is hidden for them of joy as a reward for what they used to do.” [Surah Al-Sajdah, verse 17]’"

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lowest status of the people of Paradise is the one who wishes to Allah, and it is said to him: ‘You have it, and its like with you.’ Except that he is met with something other than this and this, and it is said to him: ‘You have it, and its like with you.’” Abu Sa’id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Then it is said to him: ‘You have it and ten times its like.’”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, the people of Paradise see the inhabitants of the chambers in Paradise as you see the brilliant stars in the sky.” Abu Hazim said: I narrated this hadith to Nu’man ibn Abi Ayyash, and he narrated it to me from Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: “The brilliant stars in the sky are those in the east and the west.”

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no one in Paradise but he has two wives, and he sees the marrow of their legs behind seventy garments, and there is no celibate among them."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Abu Imran al-Jawni narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The tent is a pearl, hollowed out, its length in the sky is sixty miles, and in each of its corners there is a family for the believer that the others do not see."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, when a believer desires a child in Paradise, his conception, birth, and growth will occur in a single hour, as he desired."

Narrated by Sulaiman bin Burida, who said: I think that his father said, “The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘The people of Paradise will be two hundred and one groups: eighty of them will be from my Ummah, and forty will be from the rest of the people.’”

Narrated by Hakim bin Muawiya from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a sea of milk, a sea of honey, and a sea of wine, and from it rivers branch out."

Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: When the verse, "Indeed, We have granted you abundance," (Surah Al-Kawthar, 108:1) was revealed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is a river in Paradise, its banks are of gold, it flows over pearls and rubies, its soil is more fragrant than the scent of musk, its taste is sweeter than honey, and its water is whiter than snow."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, in Paradise is a tree whose shade a rider covers in one hundred years without traversing it, and recite if you wish: ‘And [He provides] a shade extended.’” (Surah Al-Waqi’ah, verse 30)

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "There is a tree in Paradise, under the shade of which a rider may travel for a hundred years without traversing its extent; it is the Tree of Eternity."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The 'Ajwa dates are from Paradise, and they are a cure for poison."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Anas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who said: "Indeed, there is a market in Paradise." They said: "What is it?" He said: "It is dunes of musk, to which they go out and gather. Then Allah sends a wind upon them which carries them into their homes, and their families say to them: 'Indeed, you have become more fragrant after us,' and they say to their families the same." Saeed ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) with a similar narration.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Paradise is encompassed by difficulties, and Hell is encompassed by desires."

While I was sitting in the mosque, a group of the poor emigrants were seated, when the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) entered and sat among them. I stood up to them, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to them: “Let the poor emigrants be given glad tidings of that which pleases their faces, for they will enter Paradise forty years before the wealthy.” He (Abdullah ibn Amr) said: “I have seen their faces brighten.” Abdullah ibn Amr said: “Until I wished to be among them.”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Fire complained to its Lord, saying: ‘O my Lord, I have consumed myself, (eaten away my own substance).’ So Allah permitted it two breaths: a breath in the winter and a breath in the summer. It is the hottest of what you feel and the coldest of what you feel.”

Narrated similarly by the Prophet (peace be upon him).
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, this fire [you have] is but a portion—one of seventy portions—of the Fire of Hell."
Narrated by Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The lightest of the people in punishment is the one whose brain boils in his shoes."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “The people of the Fire will be thrown into it, and it will say, ‘Are there any more? Are there any more? Are there any more?’ three times, until her Lord, the Exalted and Almighty, comes to her and places His foot upon her, so she will be straightened and say, ‘Cut, cut, cut.’”
"Learn the rulings of inheritance, the subtleties of Arabic grammar, and the authentic narrations (Sunnah) just as you learn the Quran."
"Learn the rulings pertaining to inheritance, for they are part of your religion."

Narrated Ibn Shihab: Had Uthman and Zaid died at one time, the knowledge of inheritance (Faraidh) would have perished. Indeed, a time will come upon the people when none would know it except them (Uthman and Zaid).

Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Learn the Qur'an and the rulings of Islamic law, for it is nearing a time when a man will be in need of knowledge he once possessed, or he will remain among a people who do not know [it]."
Abu Musa reported: "Whoever knows the Qur'an but does not know the rulings (of Islamic law), then his example is like a burnoos (a cloak) without a face; or, he has no face."
I said to al-Hakam: "I do not know what I am asking you about." He said: "Revive the kinship ties."
Learn about inheritance laws, divorce, and pilgrimage, for they are part of your religion.
They were encouraged to teach the Quran, inheritance laws, and rituals of pilgrimage.

Narrated Abdullah: "Whoever recites the Qur'an, let him learn inheritance (al-fara'idh). If an Arab Bedouin meets him and says, 'O emigrant, do you recite the Qur'an?' and he says, 'Yes,' he says, 'Do you know inheritance?' If he says, 'Yes,' then it is an increase and goodness. And if he says, 'No,' he says, 'Then what is your superiority over me, O emigrant?'"

Abdullah ibn Sa’id narrated: We were with Masruq, and we asked him, “Did Aisha possess knowledge of inheritance?” He said, “By the One who is not worshipped besides Him, I have seen prominent companions of Muhammad asking her about inheritance.”

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Shu'bah, from 'Asim, from Abu 'Uthman, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and from Abu Bakrah. Shu'bah said: "This (Sa'd) was the first to shoot an arrow in the way of Allah, and this (Abu Bakrah) hung down from the fortress of Ta'if to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)." They both narrated: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'Whoever claims lineage to someone other than his father while knowing that he is not his father, then Paradise is forbidden to him.'"

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "Disbelief in Allah is claiming a lineage that is unknown, and disbelief in Allah is disavowing a lineage, however slight it may be."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan narrated to me from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murra, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "Disbelief in Allah is claiming a lineage that is unknown, and disbelief in Allah is disavowing a lineage, however slight it may be."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated: Sufyan narrated to me from Zakariyya, Abu Yahya, who said: I heard Abu Wail recounting, from Ibn Mas'ud, a similar statement.

I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) to pledge allegiance to him, but I arrived and he had passed away, and Abu Bakr was standing in his place. He gave a lengthy praise and wept much, and said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: Disavowal from kinship, however slight it may be, is disbelief in Allah, and claiming a kinship that is unknown.”

"Whoever claims lineage other than his father’s, or allies himself with those other than his masters who emancipated him, then upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people until the Day of Resurrection; nor will any rectification or justice be accepted from him."
Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: "Whenever Umar took us along a path, we found it easy. And he said concerning a wife and parents: 'The wife takes half, and the mother takes a third of what remains.'"

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Yazid al-Rishk narrated, saying: I asked Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib about a man who abandoned his wife and his parents, and he said: "Zayd ibn Thabit divided it into four parts."
Uthman ibn Affan said concerning a woman and her parents: "The woman receives a fourth [of the inheritance], and the mother receives a third of what remains."

Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "A woman receives a fourth of four shares, the mother receives a third of what remains from that share, and the father receives two shares."

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me from Hajjaj from Umayr ibn Sa’id: That he asked Al-Harith Al-A’war about a woman, and parents, and he said the same as what Uthman said.
He (Zayd ibn Thabit) stated concerning a woman who abandoned her husband and parents: "The husband is entitled to half, and the mother is entitled to a third of what remains."
Narrated ‘Ali: Concerning a woman and her parents, he said, "It is divided among four: the woman gets a quarter, the mother gets a third of what remains, and the father gets what remains."

Narrated Abdullah: Umar, when he took a path with us, we found it easy. And he judged a case concerning a woman and her parents from four (shares), giving the woman a quarter, the mother a third of what remained, and the father two shares. 

Narrated Muhammad ibn Yusuf: We were told by Sufyan from ‘Isa from Al-Sha’bi from Zayd ibn Thabit, a similar account.
Abdullah (RA) said: "Allah would not allow me to favor a mother over a father."

"Abdullah ibn Abbas sent to Zayd ibn Thabit, asking: "Do you find in the Book of Allah that a mother is entitled to a third of what remains [of the inheritance]?" Zayd replied: "You are a man who speaks based on your opinion, and I am a man who speaks based on my opinion."

Hudhaifa, Hammad ibn Salamah, Hajjaj, Ash-Sha'bi, Hajjaj, Ata', and Ibn Abbas reported: That they said concerning a wife and parents: "The wife receives half, the mother receives a third of the entire wealth, and whatever remains is for the father."
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "A woman and her parents are entitled to one-third of the entire inheritance, and a husband and his parents are also entitled to one-third."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, and Ibn Idris narrated to me from his father, from al-Fudayl ibn ‘Amr, from Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Abbas opposed the people of the Qibla regarding a woman and her parents, saying: "The mother is to receive a third from all of the property."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ash’ath ibn Abi Ash’ath, from Al-Aswad ibn Yazid, who said: “Mu’adh ibn Jabal passed judgment in Yemen concerning a daughter and her sister, and he gave the daughter half and the sister half.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to me, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Al-Aswad ibn Yazid: that Ibn al-Zubayr did not inherit for the sister from the father, and the mother with the daughter, until Al-Aswad informed him that Mu'adh ibn Jabal gave half to the daughter and half to the sister. So he said: "You are my messenger to Abdullah ibn Utbah, and inform him of this." And he was his judge in Kufa.

Bishr ibn Umar narrated: I asked Ibn Abi Zinaad about a man who left behind a daughter and a sister. He said: "The daughter receives half, and the sister receives what remains." He said: And my father informed me, from Kharija ibn Zaid: That Zaid ibn Thabit used to consider sisters with daughters as heirs, and would not give them anything except what remained.

Narrated Muhammad bin Yusuf: Muhammad said, "I narrated to me Sufyan from Mansur and Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim: [regarding] a wife, a mother, and brothers and sisters from the same parents, and brothers and sisters from the mother's side. He said: Umar, Abdullah, and Zaid used to share [inheritance]. And Umar said: "The father did not but increase their closeness."
Narrated ‘Ali: He used to say, “There is no partner to Him.”
Muhammad narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Sulaiman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz: That Uthman used to associate [partners with Allah], and Ali used not to associate.
Narrated by Muhammad: Narrated by Sufyan: From Ibn Dakwan: That Zayd used to associate [others with Allah].
Narrated to me Muhammad, narrated to me Sufyan, from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Shurayh: “That he used to say…”
Umar said concerning partnership: “It only brought them closer.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Harith Al-A'war, who said: Abdullah was presented with a case concerning the inheritance of cousins, one of whom was a brother through the mother. He said, "The property is entirely for his brother through the mother." So, he placed him in the category of a brother [from the perspective of] the father and mother. When Ali arrived, I asked him about it and informed him of Abdullah’s statement. He said, “May Allah have mercy on him; he was indeed a jurist. As for me, I will not increase for him over what Allah has prescribed for him: a sixth share, and then he will share with them as one of them.”

Narrated by Muhammad bin Yusuf: He said, "Sufyan narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Harith, from Ali, that he was informed about two cousins, one of whom was a brother through the mother. They said to Ali: "Indeed, Ibn Mas'ud used to give him all the wealth." Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If he did, then he was certainly a jurist. And if I were he, I would give him one-sixth, and whatever remained would be between them."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, and Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to me, from Abu Qays al-Awdi, from Huzayl ibn Surhabil, who said: A man came to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari and Salman ibn Rabia and asked them about a daughter, a granddaughter, and a sister of the same mother and father. They said: "The daughter takes half, and whatever remains goes to the sister." Then they said: "Go to Ibn Mas’ud, for he will follow our judgment." So the man came to Abdullah, and asked him about that. He said: "I have certainly gone astray, and I am not of those who are rightly guided. I judge according to what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, judged: 'The daughter takes half, the granddaughter takes a sixth, and whatever remains goes to the sister.'"

Narrated by Abdullah: That he used to say concerning sisters who are daughters of the same father and mother, and brothers and sisters who are children of the same father: "The sisters (daughters of the same parents) are to inherit two-thirds, and whatever remains is for the males over the females.” Then Masruq came to Medina and heard the statement of Zayd therein, and it pleased him. So one of his companions said to him, "Do you abandon the statement of Abdullah?” He said, “I came to Medina and found Zayd ibn Thabit among those firmly rooted in knowledge.” Ahmad said: So I said to Abu Shihab, “And how did Zayd say it?” He said, “He shared between them.”

Sa'id ibn al-Mughira narrated to me from Isa ibn Yunus, from Ismail, who said: We mentioned to Hakim ibn Jabir that Ibn Mas'ud said concerning sisters who have the same father and mother, and brothers and sisters who have the same father: that he would give to the sisters who have the same father and mother two-thirds, and whatever remained would go to the males, with females receiving a lesser share. Hakim said: Zayd ibn Thabit said: "This is from the practices of pre-Islamic times, that men inherit more than women. Indeed, their brothers have been returned to them."
Aisha (RA) narrated: "That she used to divide between two daughters and a granddaughter and a grandson; she would give the two daughters two-thirds, and whatever remained, they would share it."
ʿAbdullāh would not associate partners with Allah, and he would give to males more than to females, and he said: “Sisters are like daughters.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Abu Sahl, from Al-Sha'bi: That Ibn Mas'ud used to say, concerning a daughter and the daughters of a son, and the grandchildren: "If their share of the inheritance is less than one-sixth, he would give them one-sixth. And if it is more than one-sixth, he would give them one-sixth."

Masruq said, "I used to associate [in marriage] with women. Alqama asked him, 'Is anyone among them more reliable than Abdullah?' He replied, 'No, but I have seen Zayd ibn Thabit and the people of Medina associating with two daughters, and a daughter of a grandson, and a grandson, and two sisters.'"

Narrated: Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Shurayh: “Concerning a woman who left her husband, her mother, her sister (through her father’s side), and her brothers (through her mother’s side), she was considered among six heirs, then their number was raised to ten. The husband receives half of three shares. The sister from the father and mother receives half of three shares. The mother receives one-sixth of a share. The brothers from the mother receive two-thirds of a share. And the sister from the father receives one share, completing the two-thirds.”
Ali and Zayd would not screen out (from sitting with) non-believers or slaves, nor would they bequeath anything to them.
'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) used to screen himself off with the disbelievers and the slaves, and he would not bequeath anything to them.
Ali and Zayd said: "Slaves and the People of the Book neither attain legal guardianship nor inherit."
Abdullah (RA) said: "They are veiled and they do not inherit."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, and Yahya narrated to me, from Saeed: That Umar (RA) used to write about the inheritance of the grandfather, until when he was wounded, he summoned it and erased it, then he said: "You will see your opinion about it."

Yazid informed me, telling me that Ash'ath narrated to me from Ibn Sirin, who said: I said to 'Abidah, "Relate to me about the remembrance of Allah (Jad)." He said, "Indeed, I recall eighty different states within the remembrance of Allah."

Abu Ghassan narrated to me, he said: Israel narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Ubaid ibn Amr, from Ali, who said: A man came to him and asked him about a legal obligation (fard). He said: "If there is no grandfather, then give it (the inheritance)."

Narrated by Muhammad bin Yusuf, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ubaid bin 'Amr, that a man came to 'Ali and asked him about an inheritance. 'Ali said to him: "If there is no grandfather, then bring it forth."
He heard Ali (RA) say: "Whoever desires to be plunged into the boils of Hell, let him judge between brothers with falsehood."

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and 'Ikrimah, reported: That Abu Bakr al-Siddiq made the grandfather like a father. 

Abu Musa reported: That Abu Bakr al-Siddiq made the grandfather like a father.
Abu Musa reported that Abu Bakr stipulated that a grandfather is like a father.
Abu Bakr would grant the grandfather the status of a father.
Abu Bakr would treat the serious (or diligent) as a father.

Al-Aswad ibn Amir narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Amr ibn Murra, from Abu Burda, who said: I met Marwan ibn al-Hakam in Medina. He said: "O son of Abu Musa, were you not informed that a grandfather does not take the position of a father among you, and you do not deny this?" I said: "Even if you were, you would not deny it." Marwan said: "Then I bear witness that Uthman ibn Affan witnessed that Abu Bakr declared, 'A grandfather takes the position of a father if there is no father below him.'"
Abu Bakr would treat his grandfather as a father.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Ayyub narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This is what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If I were to take a close friend, I would have taken him as a close friend, but brotherhood in Islam is better. Meaning, he made Abu Bakr his father, meaning: the grandfather."
Abu Bakr declared, "The grandfather is like a father."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Al-Ash'ath, from Hasan, who said: "The practice regarding grandfathers has passed away, and Abu Bakr made the grandfather like a father, but the people became perplexed."
Muhammad ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to me from Ali ibn Musahir from 'Asim from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "The first person to inherit according to Islam was Umar."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Hasan narrated to me, from 'Asim, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "The first inheritance to be established in Islam was for 'Umar. He took his father's property. Then 'Ali and Zayd came to him and said: 'You have no right to that. You are like any other brother.'"

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Musa, from ‘Isa the Tailor, from Al-Sha’bi, that ‘Umar (RA) would divide inheritance with the grandfather alongside the brother and the brothers. If they increased, he would give him a third. And he would give him a sixth with the child.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Zuhayr narrated to me, he said: Hisham ibn Urwa narrated to me from his father, from Marwan ibn al-Hakam: That when Umar ibn al-Khattab was stabbed, he consulted them about the matter. He said: "Indeed, I had an opinion about this matter, and if you see fit to follow it, then follow it." Then Uthman said to him: "If we follow your opinion, then it is sound guidance, and if we follow the opinion of the elder, then he was indeed one of those with sound judgment."

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Muhsir from Ash-Sha’bi who said: Ibn ‘Abbas wrote to ‘Ali and Ibn ‘Abbas in Basrah: “I was brought a grandfather and six brothers.” So ‘Ali wrote to him: “Give the grandfather a sixth, and do not give anyone after him.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hasan narrated to me, from Ismail, from Al-Sha'bi concerning six brothers and a grandfather, who said: "Give the grandfather one-sixth." Abu Muhammad said: It appears that Al-Sha'bi is relating this from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) would consider the paternal grandfather as a brother when he was the sixth in line of descent.
Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan: That Ali used to include the grandfather with the brothers, to one-sixth.
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) would distribute inheritance between the paternal grandfather and brothers until he would be the sixth [heir].

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) would include the grandfather up to one-sixth with the brothers, giving each heir their due share. He would not inherit a brother or sister through the mother along with the grandfather, nor would he inherit a sister through the mother. He would not increase the grandfather’s share with the children beyond one-sixth, unless there were others. He would not divide with a brother through the father alongside a brother through both parents. And if there was a sister through both parents and a brother through the father, he would give the sister half, and the other half between the grandfather and the brother, divided equally. And if they were brothers and sisters, he would include them with the grandfather up to one-sixth.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated from Sufyan, from Al-Absi - he is Abdullah ibn Khalid, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Ma’qil, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about genealogy. He said, "Which of your fathers is greater?" I said, "I am Adam." He said, "Did you not hear the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'O children of Adam' [Surah Al-A'raf, verse 26]?"
"I wish that I and those who disagree with me regarding jesting would curse one another, so that we may know who speaks the worst."
Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Ibn Tayus narrated from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said, "He [the Prophet, peace be upon him] made the grandfather like a father."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Zuhayr narrated to me from Abu Ishaq, who said: I entered upon Shurayh, and with him were 'Amir, Ibrahim, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah, concerning the inheritance of a woman from among us, Al-'Aliya, who left her husband, her mother, her brother on her father’s side, and her grandfather. He asked me, "Is there a sister (among the heirs)?" I said, "No." He said, "The husband takes half, and the mother a third." I exerted myself to have him answer me, but he did not answer me except with that. Then Ibrahim, 'Amir, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah said, "No one has come with a more difficult inheritance than the one you have come with." I then went to 'Abidah as-Salmani, for it was said that no one in Kufa was more knowledgeable about inheritance than 'Abidah and al-Harith al-'Awar. 'Abidah would sit in the mosque, and whenever Shurayh received an inheritance involving a grandfather, he would refer them to 'Abidah, who would then determine the inheritance. I asked him, and he said, "If you wish, I will inform you of the inheritance of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud in this matter: He gave the husband three shares, which is half; the mother a third of what remains, which is a sixth of the total; the brother one share, and the grandfather one share." Abu Ishaq said: "The grandfather is the father’s father."
Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan: That Zayd used to include his grandfather with his brothers to the extent of a third.

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to me, my father narrated to me, he narrated to me from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Zayd ibn Thabit: That he used to share with his grandfather along with his brothers to one-third, and then he would not diminish it.

Sa'id ibn al-Mughira narrated to me from Isa ibn Yunus, from Ismail, who said: 'Amir said: "Take from the saying of the grandfather what the people have agreed upon." Abu Muhammad said: "He means the saying of Zayd."

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Hammam from Qatadah: That Zayd ibn Thabit said concerning a sister, a mother, a wife, a grandfather, "He made them of twenty-seven: six for the mother, nine for the wife, eight for the grandfather, and four for the sister."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Al-Ash’ath narrated to me from Ibn Sirin from Ibn Mas’ud, who said: "The first woman to be fed (in Islam) was Sahm, the mother of Abu (a man), while her son was alive."
Narrated by Abu Naim: He said, "I narrated to me Shareek, from Layth, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) fed a grandmother a sixth [of food]."
Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) bequeathed inheritance to a maternal grandmother alongside her son.

Narrated: Mansur bin Al-Mu'tamir, he said: I heard Ibrahim say: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fed three grandmothers a sixth of a measure." He said: I said to Ibrahim: "Who are they?" He said: "Your grandmothers from your father's side, and your grandmother from your mother's side."
Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: He informed me Hasan, who said: "The grandmother inherits [a share] even if her son is alive."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Dawud, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "The mother does not inherit from her father's mother, nor does her son who is descended through her inherit. So how can she inherit?"
"’Imran ibn Husayn said: “The maternal grandmother inherits [a share] even when her son is alive.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Ash’ath, from Zuhri, who said: A grandmother (mother of one’s father or mother) came to Abu Bakr and said: “My grandson or granddaughter has died, and it has reached me that I have a share (in inheritance). What is my share?” Abu Bakr said: “I have not heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say anything about it, but I will ask the people.” When the Zuhr prayer was performed, he said: “Which of you heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say anything about the grandmother?” Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba said: “I did.” He said: “What did he say?” He said: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave her a sixth.” He said: “Does anyone else know that?” Muhammad ibn Maslama said: “He is truthful.” So Abu Bakr gave her the sixth. Then she came to Umar, and he said: “I do not know. I have not heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say anything about it, but I will ask the people.” They told him about the account of Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba and Muhammad ibn Maslama. Umar said: “Whoever was alone with him, she gets the sixth; if you both were together, it is between you.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Al-Ash'ath narrated to me from Al-Sha'bi, from Ali and Zayd, who said: "If grandmothers are equal, then three grandmothers inherit: the paternal grandmother (mother of the father), the maternal grandmother (mother of the mother), and the grandmother of the mother. If one of them is closer (in degree of relationship), then the share is for those closest in kinship."
Ali and Zayd related: "That they did not leave an inheritance for the maternal grandmother (grandmother on the father’s side) along with the father."
Uthman would not inherit for the granddaughter while her son was alive.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Al-Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Grandmothers have no inheritance; they are merely sustenance that we provide for them. The closest and the farthest grandmothers are equal in this regard."
'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "The maternal grandmother inherits [a share] even if her son is alive."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Al-Ash'ath, from Al-Sha'bi, who said: "Four maternal aunts came to Misruq seeking inheritance. He disregarded the mother of the grandfather and bequeathed to three: the maternal grandmothers of his father - his grandmother, his mother's mother, and his father's mother."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Sharik narrated to me, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, concerning a daughter and a granddaughter, that he said: "Half, a sixth, and whatever remains, is to be returned to the daughter."

Narrated Abdullah: That he was brought a case concerning brothers and a mother, and he gave the brothers who were siblings by mother one-third of the inheritance, and the mother the rest of the property, and said: "The mother is a protector for one who has no protector."
I asked al-Sha'bi about a man who died leaving his daughter, and no other heir was known besides her. He said, "She inherits all the property."

Narrated by Muhammad ibn Yusuf: Sufyan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Salim from Al-Sha'bi that Ibn Mas'ud would not respond to a brother of his mother in her presence, nor to a grandmother if another person who has a right over her was present, nor to a granddaughter in the presence of a daughter of his own loins, nor to a woman and her husband.
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) would respond to every person who had a claim or grievance, except for a woman and a husband.

Narrated: Zaid ibn Thabit: That he was brought a deceased person, and he gave half to the deceased's daughter or sister, and he placed what remained in the treasury. Yazid ibn Harun said: From Muhammad ibn Salim, from Al-Sha'bi, from Kharija.
"Regarding the inheritance of the child of a cursed woman, 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) stated: "His inheritance belongs to his mother."

Mu'adh ibn Han'i narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to me, saying: I heard a man ask Ata' ibn Abi Rabah about the inheritance of the child of divorced parents. Ata' said: "It belongs to his mother and her family."

Ali (RA) said concerning the son of the cursed woman: “He abandoned his brother for his mother, and his mother for his brother a sixth, and for his mother a third. Then it is returned to them, so the brother receives a third, and the mother receives two-thirds.”

Ibn Mas’ud (RA) said: “A sixth for his brother, and whatever remains is for his mother.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hasan narrated to me, from Abu Sahl, from Al-Sha'bi, concerning the son of the cursed woman: He abandoned his brother and his grandfather, and said, "The wealth is for the brother."
"For his mother is a third, and two-thirds are for the Bayt al-Mal (public treasury)."

Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Its inheritance is for his mother, and his mother’s relatives are her as guardians." Qatadah narrated from Hasan: "The mother receives a third, and the remainder of the wealth belongs to the mother’s relatives."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama said to us, Qatada narrated to us: That Ali and Ibn Mas'ud said concerning the child of a woman cursed (mulā‘anah), abandoning his maternal grandmother and his maternal brothers. He [the narrator] said: "The grandmother takes a third, and the maternal brothers take two-thirds." And Zayd ibn Thabit said: "The grandmother takes a sixth, and the maternal brothers take a third, and whatever remains belongs to the Bayt al-Mal (public treasury)."
Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, Yunus and Humaid narrated to me from Hasan, who said, "His mother inherits him, meaning the son of the cursed woman."
Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, Hajjaj narrated: That Nafi’ and Al-Sha’bi said: "His mother inherits from him."

I wrote to a brother of mine from the tribe of Zurayq, asking him about the judgment of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the son of a cursed woman. He wrote to me: “The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ruled that he belonged to his mother; she is in the position of both his mother and his father.” Sufyan said: “All the property belongs to the mother; she is in the position of his father and mother.”

Narrated from Muhammad, he said: Sufyan narrated to me from Hisham, from Hasan, concerning the son of the cursed woman (who was cursed by the Prophet), who abandoned his mother and her relatives. He said, "One-third is for his mother, and whatever remains is for her relatives."
"‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us from Ibn Abi Layla, from ‘Amir, from ‘Ali and Abdullah concerning the son of the cursed woman, they said: ‘His kinship is through his mother’s side.’”

Abu al-Walid al-Halabi, Musa ibn Khalid, narrated to me, from al-Mu'tamir, from Yunus, from Hasan, that he used to say: "The inheritance of the child born out of illicit relations belongs to his mother. I said: What if he has a brother from his mother? He said: He gets a sixth."

Abu al-Mughira reported: I narrated to me al-Awza'i, he narrated to me Zuhri, who said: "The child of a woman cursed (through divorce) belongs to her mother, she inherits his prescribed share from him, and the rest of it goes to the public treasury."

Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Musa, from Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah, from Naafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: "If two people exchange mutual accusations of adultery, they will be separated and will not reunite. The child will be assigned to his mother, and it will be said, 'The son of so-and-so,' and she will be his relative (asabah), inheriting from him and he inheriting from her. And whoever calls someone to adultery, he will be flogged."

Mu'adh ibn Han'i narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to me, Ash-Shaibani narrated to me, from Ash-Sha'bi, concerning the child of those who mutually curse each other (i.e., divorced due to mutual animosity): "His inheritance belongs to his mother's relatives, and they are responsible for him."

Sahil ibn Hammad narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, from Qatadah, from ‘Azrah, from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the child of a woman cursed (through slander), “He is the one who has no father. His mother and his maternal brothers inherit him, and his mother’s relatives (cousins). If someone falsely accuses him, the one who falsely accused him is flogged.”

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, and Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to me, from An-Nu'man, from Makhul: That he was asked about the inheritance of the child born of a woman cursed (mulā'anah), for whom is it? He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, decreed, "It is for his mother, to compensate her for what she has suffered of affliction, and for his brothers from the same mother." Makhul said: "If the mother dies and leaves her son, and then her son, for whom she was designated, dies, then his entire inheritance goes to his brothers from the same mother, because it was for their mother and their grandfather. And the father inherits one-sixth from the daughter’s son, and the grandfather does not inherit except in this situation, for he is only the father of the mother. And the brothers from the mother inherited their mother, and the grandfather inherited his daughter because she was designated for him. So the wealth that belongs to the child belongs to the heirs of the mother, and it is in the possession of the grandfather alone if there is no one else."

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: Some people disputed before ‘Ali (RA) regarding the inheritance of the child of divorced parents. The paternal relatives came seeking his inheritance, and ‘Ali (RA) said, “His father disowned him, so you have no claim to his inheritance.” He then ruled that his inheritance belonged to his mother and made her his relatives.

Narrated ‘Ubaidullah ibn Musa, from Isra’il, from ‘Abd al-‘Ala: That he heard Muhammad ibn ‘Ali narrating, from ‘Ali: Concerning a man who possesses what belongs to a man and what belongs to a woman, from which of them inheritance is taken, he said, "From which of them does he urinate?"
Narrated ‘Ali: Concerning the Khuntha (hermaphrodite), he said, "He is inherited from the side of his sexual organ."

Abu Naim narrated to me, saying: Abu Hani narrated that ‘Amir was asked about a child who was born, neither male nor female, not possessing what a male has, nor what a female has. It discharges from its navel in the form of urine and stool. He was asked about its inheritance, and he said: "Half of the share of a male, and half of the share of a female."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ‘Asim narrated to me from Al-Sha’bi, who said: Abu Bakr was asked about the Kalalah (inheritance of a deceased person who leaves neither a son nor a daughter). He said: “I will give my opinion on it; if it is correct, then it is from Allah, and if it is incorrect, then it is from me and from Satan. I see them as excluding the father and the son.” Then, when Umar was appointed Caliph, he said: “I am too shy before Allah to reverse anything Abu Bakr said.”
Nothing afflicted the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, with more distress than the hardship caused by poverty.
Ibn 'Abbas said, "Kalalah is that which remains excluding the parent and the child."

Sa'd narrated: "That he used to recite this verse: 'And if a man or a woman has no son nor daughter, but has a brother or a sister, then (the property belongs) to their mother.' [Surah An-Nisa, verse 12]… for his mother."
Umar sought someone to inherit for Ibn al-Dahdah, but he found no heir. So, he gave the wealth of Ibn al-Dahdah to his maternal uncles.
Allah and His Messenger are the patron of one who has no patron, and the uncle inherits from one who has no heir.

Narrated: Ziyad said: 'Umar was consulted about the inheritance of an uncle on the mother’s side and an aunt. He gave the uncle on the mother’s side two-thirds of the inheritance and gave the aunt one-third.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Yunus, from Hasan: That Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) gave the aunt a third [of the inheritance], and the paternal aunt two-thirds.

Narrated by Qays bin Habtar Al-Nadhali: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was presented with a female relative (khala) and an aunt (‘ammah). A senior man stood up and said, "I witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab give the khala one-third and the ‘ammah two-thirds." Abd al-Malik intended to write it down, then said, "Where is Zayd regarding this?"

"’Abdullah (RA) said: ‘The aunt is like the mother, the maternal aunt is like the father, the daughter of the brother is like a brother, and every relative is like the kinship relationship from which inheritance descends if there is no closer relative.’”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Hisham, from Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Utbah, who said: Dhahhak ibn Qais informed me that Umar judged regarding the people of the plague of ‘Amwas that if they were equal in terms of their paternal lineage, then the children of the mother were more entitled, and if some of them were closer in terms of their paternal lineage, then they were more entitled to the wealth.
Salim, the servant of Abu Dhuffa, was killed at the Battle of Yamama. His inheritance amounted to two hundred dirhams. Umar said, "Withhold it for his mother until it is completely spent."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Brothers from the same mother inherit from one another, excluding the offspring of uterine relations. A man inherits from his brother through his father and mother, excluding his brother through his father alone.”
Sahlu ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to me from Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: "Do you think a man who abandons his grandson inherits from him?" He said: "No."
Abdullah (RA) said, "The mother is the supporter of one who has no supporter, and the sister is the supporter of one who has no supporter."
"Distribute the obligatory inheritances to their rightful recipients, and whatever remains, it belongs to the closest male relative."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to me: That Sulaiman ibn Yasar informed him, from Muhammad ibn al-Ash’ath: That an aunt of his died a Jewess in Yemen. So he mentioned that to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: “She is inherited by the closest of the people to her from among her people of religion.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to me, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: The aunt of Ash’ath ibn Qays died while she was Jewish. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab came and said: "Her people of religion inherit from her."
'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The people of polytheism neither inherit from us, nor do we inherit from them."

Narrated by Abu Nu'aim, he said: Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hasan narrated to me, from Isa the Tailor, from Al-Sha'bi: That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), Abu Bakr, and Umar said: "People of two religions do not inherit from one another."
Umar (RA) said: "People of two religions do not inherit from each other."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to me, from Al-Ash'ath, from Hasan, from Jabir, who said: "We do not inherit from the People of the Book, nor do they inherit from us, except when a man dies leaving a slave or a female slave."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “We do not inherit from the People of the Book, nor do they inherit from us, except for a man who inherits his slave or his female slave.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me from Dawud, from Al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "Mu'awiya would inherit from a Muslim from a disbeliever, and would not inherit from a disbeliever from a Muslim." Masruq said: "And no judgment that occurred in Islam was more beloved to me than this." It was said to Abu Muhammad: "Do you say this?" He said: "No."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Hind from Amir: That al-Mu’zila bint al-Harith died in Yemen while she was Jewish. So, al-Ash’ath ibn Qays, who was her maternal uncle, rode to Umar concerning her inheritance. Umar said: “That is not for you. She is inherited by those closest to her from among her people of the same religion; two religions do not inherit from each other.”
"Two different religions shall not be inherited, and he who does not inherit shall not be a barrier."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim.”
"When a deceased person dies, their rights become due to their heirs, and no portion is allotted to anyone who embraced Islam or was freed [as a slave] before the inheritance is divided."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Muslim does not inherit from the disbeliever, nor does the disbeliever inherit from the Muslim.”
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim."
Ibrahim said: "The mukatab has no inheritance, as long as anything remains due from his agreement."

Narrated Ya'la: Ya'la narrated from Abd al-Malik, from Ata: “Concerning a man who has children and has emancipated some of them by half, others by a third, and others by a quarter, he said: ‘They do not inherit until they are emancipated.’”

Narrated Abdullah ibn Ja'far Ar-Raqi and Saeed ibn Al-Mughira, from Ibn Al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: Concerning a man who purchased his son while he was ill, he said, "If he recovers and comes out of one-third [of his wealth], then he inherits [from him]. But if the illness overcomes him, he does not inherit."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hasan narrated to me from his father, from Ash-Sha'bi, who said: "The limit of the mukatab (one who buys his freedom) is the limit of the slave, until he is set free."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The freed slave is a brother in religion and a blessing. The closest of the people to the deceased in terms of kinship is most deserving of his inheritance."

Narrated: Muhammad ibn Isa, he said: Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: Narrated to me by Hisham, from Mansur, from Hasan and Muhammad ibn Salim, from Al-Sha'bi, concerning a man who freed a slave, then the freedman and the slave both died, and the man who freed him left his father and his son. They said, "The property belongs to the son."
Narrated by Zayd ibn Thabit concerning a man who abandoned his father and his grandson, he said: "Loyalty belongs to the grandson."

Narrated by Ziyad bin Abi Maryam: A woman freed a slave she owned, then she died leaving her son and her brother. Then her freed slave died and her son and brother came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) regarding his inheritance. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "His inheritance is for the woman's son." The brother said: "O Messenger of Allah, if he committed a transgression, who would be held accountable?" The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "You."

Muhammad ibn Salit narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, saying: Mughirah said: I asked Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who freed a slave he owned, and both the man and the slave died. The man who freed the slave left behind his father and his son. He said to his father, "This much is yours," and what remained was for his son.
He (the Prophet) said to the son.

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Al-Ash’ath, from Hasan: that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) went out to Al-Baqi’ and saw a slave being sold. He approached him and bargained for him, then left him. Then a man saw him and bought him and manumitted him, then brought him to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and said: “I bought him and manumitted him, so what do you see in this?” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “He is your brother and your mawla.” He said: “What do you see in his companionship?” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “If he is grateful to you, it is good for him and bad for you, and if he is ungrateful to you, it is good for you and bad for him.” He said: “What do you see in his wealth?” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “If he dies without leaving a relative, you are his heir.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Ash'ath, from Al-Hakam and Salama ibn Kuhail, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad, that the daughter of Hamza freed a slave of hers. The slave died and left behind his daughter and his mistress, the daughter of Hamza. So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, divided his inheritance equally between his daughter and his mistress, the daughter of Hamza.

Shumus the Kindiyya related: "I presented a case to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning a father who died and left no one as his heir except me and his slave. He gave me half and gave the slave half."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: "A daughter and a slave-girl were brought to him [the Prophet, peace be upon him]. He gave the daughter half, and the slave-girl half. Al-Hakam said: Thus, this is the share of the slave-girl that she inherited from her master."

Narrated by Ibrahim ibn Musa, from Ibn Idris, from Ash'ath, from Al-Hakam, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Mudlij: That he died leaving his daughter and his clients, so Ali gave his daughter half and his clients the other half.
Narrated from Ibrahim, from Ibn Idris, from Ash-Shaybani, from Al-Hakam, from Ash-Shumus: "Her father died, and Ali gave her half and gave half to his dependents."

Narrated: Ibrahim (may Allah be pleased with him) that he was asked about two sisters whose one bought their father and manumitted him. Then their father died. He (Ibrahim) said to them: "Two-thirds of the inheritance are their prescribed shares in the Book of Allah, and whatever remains belongs to the one who manumitted [their father], excluding the other."

Narrated ‘Abdullah: Al-Ash’ath narrated to me from Al-Sha’bi: “Concerning a woman who manumitted her father, and her father died leaving four daughters, and she was one of them, it was said: She is not indebted to him, and they are entitled to two-thirds of the inheritance, and she is with them.”

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Hayyan ibn Salman, who said: I was with Suwaid ibn Ghafla when a man came and asked him about the inheritance of a man who left behind a daughter and a wife. Suwaid said: I will tell you what Ali judged. The man said: Ali’s judgment is sufficient for me. He said: Ali judged that the wife receives one-eighth, and the daughter receives half, then he returned the remainder to the daughter.
Narrated by Ibrahim: That a female slave of Ibrahim died and left property. I said to Ibrahim, and he said, "Indeed, she has relatives."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Ash'ath narrated to me, from Al-Sha'bi, from Umar, and Ali, and Zayd, that they said: "Loyalty is to the closest in kinship; they meant by 'closest' that which is nearest through father or mother."

Yazid narrated to me, he said: Ash'ath narrated to me from Ibn Sirin from Abdullah ibn Utbah, who said: "‘Umar wrote to me concerning Fakīha bint Sam‘an that she died and left her brother’s son to her father and mother, and her brother’s son to her father. So ‘Umar wrote: ‘Indeed, manumission (wala’) is for the elder.’”
Ali and Zayd said: "Manumission is for the eldest [among the slaves]." And Abdullah and Shuraih said: "It is for the heirs."
Umar, Abdullah, Ali, and Zayd decreed that seniority be determined by age.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sharik narrated to me, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "Fukayha bint Sam'an died and left her brother's son to his father, and her brother's sons to his father and mother. So 'Umar bequeathed the brother's sons to his father."
Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Isa, narrated to me Abdus Salam ibn Harb, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Umar, and Ali, and Zayd: that they said, "Loyalty belongs to the eldest."

Narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Awana, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: "Concerning two brothers who inherited a freed slave their father had manumitted, and one of them died leaving a son. Ali, Zaid, and Abdullah used to say: 'Walā' is for the elder.'"
Muhammad ibn Isa reported: Hammad ibn Zayd said: I heard Matar al-Warraq say: Umar and Ali said: "Loyalty belongs to the elder."
"Loyalty belongs to the elder."
Narrated from Ibrahim: "Manumitting a slave is for the benefit of the eldest [son/member]."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me from Mutarrif from Al-Sha'bi, and Sufyan narrated to me from Yunus from Hasan, concerning a man who supports another (man), they said: "He is among the Muslims." Sufyan said: "And likewise we say."

Abu Nu'aim narrated: Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to me from Abd Allah ibn Mowhab, who said: I heard Tummam al-Dari saying: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the practice regarding a person from among the people of disbelief who embraces Islam under the hand of a man from among the Muslims?" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He is most deserving of being given life and death by him."
Narrated from Ibrahim: That he was asked about a man from the people of Al-Sawad who embraced Islam under the care of a man. They said, "He is considered his guardian and inherits from him."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Shu'bah narrated to me, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "A woman inherits from the diyya (blood money) of her husband, whether it be due to intentional killing or error."
"The Diyah (blood compensation) is according to the ordinances of Allah."
Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Ayyub narrated to me, from Abu Qilaba, who said, "The legal penalty (diyya) follows the path of inheritance."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me from Humaid and Dawud ibn Abi Hind: that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote: “The uterine brothers are to inherit from the Diyah (blood money).”

"‘Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Layth narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Intelligence (or sound judgment) is a legacy among the heirs of the deceased, according to the Book of Allah and His prescribed duties.'"
"Indeed, he has wronged who does not give the brothers and sisters from the mother their share from the Diyah (blood money)."

"‘Abdullah ibn Sa’id narrated to me, that Abu Khalid narrated to me, that Ibn Salim narrated to me, from Al-Sha’bi, from ‘Umar, and ‘Ali, and Zayd, that they said: “The Diyah (blood money) is inherited just as wealth is inherited, whether it is due to error or intentional act.”

Ali would not distribute any portion of the blood money (diyah) to brothers and sisters from the same mother, nor to a spouse, nor to a woman. Abdullah said: Some people insert a man between Ismail and Amir.
Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me from Hammad ibn Salama from Ziyad al-A'alami from Hasan who said, "Brothers from the mother do not inherit from the Diyah (blood money)."
"Every community that inherits [property] dies through destruction or drowning; they do not inherit [from each other], but the living inherit [from them]."

Yahyá ibn Hasan narrated to me, Hammád ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Yahyá ibn ‘Atíq, who said: I read in some of the books of ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azíz, concerning people upon whom a house falls, and it is not known who died before the other, [that he said]: "The deceased do not inherit from one another; rather, the living inherit from the deceased."

Narrated by Nu'aim bin Hammad, from 'Abd al-'Aziz bin Muhammad, that Ja'far reported from his father: That Umm Kulthum and her son, Zayd, died on the same day. The two wailers met on the road, and neither inherited from the other. And the people of al-Harra did not inherit from each other, and the people of Siffin did not inherit from each other.

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, and Ibn Abi Layla narrated to me, from Ash-Sha'bi: "That a house in Syria fell upon some people, and 'Umar bequeathed a portion of their inheritance to others among them."
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: "That he bequeathed to two brothers who were killed at Siffin, one being killed by the other."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani: That a man died, leaving his aunt and his maternal aunt. Umar gave the aunt the share of a brother, and gave the maternal aunt the share of a sister.
One who maintains and honors kinship ties, he will be given favor through that very kinship.

Narrated: 'Abdu-Allah ibn Ahmad, from Abu Shihab, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani told me, from al-Sha'bi: "Concerning a man who abandoned his aunt and his brother's daughter, it was said: 'The inheritance belongs to his brother's daughter.'"
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “The uncle is an heir.”
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Hasan narrated to me, from 'Ubaydah, from Ibrahim: That 'Umar and Abdullah considered (or discussed) inheriting for a maternal uncle.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hasan narrated to me, from Sulaiman, Abu Ishaq, from Al-Sha'bi: concerning a maternal aunt and a niece through a brother, he said: "The wealth belongs to the niece through a brother."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Hasan narrated to me, from Sulaiman, from some of them, from Ibrahim, who said: "Regarding an aunt…"

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Ash-Sha'bi, concerning a daughter of a brother and an aunt: He (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: "Give the wealth to the daughter of the brother."

Narrated Masruq: A man died without any heirs except his sister’s daughter and his uncle. He said, "The uncle inherits the share of his sister, and the sister’s daughter inherits the share of her father."
Masrouq said: "He (Masrouq) would treat his maternal uncle as he would treat his father if he had no father, and his maternal aunt as he would treat his mother if he had no mother."

Yalaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Habban, tracing his lineage to his grandfather, from his uncle, Wasi’ ibn Habban, who said: The son of al-Dahdaha died. He was an illegitimate child, one for whom no lineage was known. He was among the Banu al-‘Ajlan and left no descendants. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi: “Do you know any lineage for him among you?” He said: “We do not know any, O Messenger of Allah.” So he called his niece’s son and gave him his inheritance.
Umar related from Ibrahim, from Al-A'mash, from my father, that Umar gave wealth to his maternal uncle.

Abu Naim narrated to me, saying: Abu Hani narrated: I asked Amir about a woman or a man who died leaving a maternal aunt and a paternal aunt. He said: "He has no heir or relative other than them." He then said: "Abdullah ibn Mas'ud would consider the maternal aunt as being in the position of his mother, and would consider the paternal aunt as being in the position of his brother."

Narrated Ahmad ibn Abdullah: Ahmad narrated to me from Abu Shihab, from Amr, from Hasan: Concerning a man who, at the time of his death, confessed to owing a man a thousand dirhams, and another presented evidence of a thousand dirhams, and the deceased left a thousand dirhams, it was said, "The money is to be divided between them, unless he was insolvent; in that case, his acknowledgment is not valid."

Abu Nu'aim narrated: I said to Shareek, "How did you mention regarding two brothers, one of them claiming brotherhood?" He said, "It enters upon him in his share." I said, "Who narrated it?" He said, "Jabir, from Amir, from Ali."

Narrated Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaiba: Narrated to me Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim: Concerning brothers who some claim kinship with and others deny, he said, "He enters with them in the position of a slave who is among brothers, and one of them emancipates his share." He said, "And 'Amir, Al-Hakam, and their companions said, 'He enters only into the share of the one who acknowledged him.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah reported from Waki‘, saying: If two brothers are, and one of them claims brotherhood and the other denies it? He (the narrator) said: Ibn Abi Layla used to say: "It is from six shares: Three shares for the one who did not claim, two shares for the claimant, and one share for the one who is denied."

Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Abu Awana narrated to me from Mughira from Hammad: "A man had three sons, and he said, 'One-third for my youngest son.' The middle son said, 'I agree,' and the eldest son said, 'I do not agree.' He said, 'It is from nine, taking three for him, and the share of the one who agreed.' Hammad said: 'He returns the share to them all.' And 'Amir said: 'He who returned, he only returned it to himself.'"
Narrated: 'Sharīh said, concerning a man who confessed to (having) a brother: "His declaration is that he is his brother."

Narrated Abu Nu'man: Abu 'Awana narrated to me from Mughira from Al-Harith Al-'Ukli: Concerning a man who, at the time of his death, admitted to owing a thousand dirhams in a partnership agreement, and a thousand dirhams in debt, and he left nothing but a thousand dirhams. He (the Prophet) said: "Begin with the debt; and if there remains anything, it is for the partner."

Abu Naim narrated to me, saying: Hasan narrated to me, from Mutarrif, from Al-Sha'bi: Concerning a man who died leaving three hundred dirhams and three sons. A man came claiming one hundred dirhams from the deceased, and one of them admitted the claim, saying, "He should enter and receive his share." Then Al-Sha'bi said: I do not see that it should be considered inheritance until the debt is settled.

Abu Khaythamah Mus’ab ibn Sa’id al-Harraani narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from al-Ash’ath, from Hasan: Concerning a man who died leaving two sons and two thousand dirhams, and they divided the two thousand dirhams. Then one of the sons disappeared. A man came forward claiming that the deceased owed him a thousand dirhams. [The Prophet (peace be upon him) said:] “Take all that is in the hand of this witness, and tell him: Follow your absent brother and take half of what is in his hand.”
"When some of the heirs acknowledge a debt, it becomes due upon them according to their shares."

Ibrahim (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If two of the heirs witness to a debt, it is from the entirety of the estate if they are trustworthy." Al-Sha'bi said: "It is upon them in a chapter concerning the inheritance of an apostate."
Narrated by Abu Hurairah: Ibn Mas'ud used to inherit the relatives of the apostate if he was killed.
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) decreed that the inheritance of an apostate be given to his Muslim relatives.
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) judged that the inheritance of an apostate should go to his relatives who are Muslims.

Zakarriya ibn ‘Adiyy narrated to me, he said: ‘Ubaydullah, who is Ibn ‘Amr, narrated to me from ‘Abd al-Karim from al-Hakam, who said: “If a man intentionally kills his brother, he will not inherit from his estate nor from his blood money (diyah). But if he kills him by mistake (unintentional killing), he will inherit from his estate, but not from his blood money.” He said: ‘Ata’ used to say this as well.

Narrated ‘Ali: A man threw a stone at his mother and killed her. Then he sought his inheritance from his brothers. His brothers said to him, “You have no inheritance.” So they approached ‘Ali. ‘Ali imposed the blood money (diyah) upon him and excluded him from the inheritance.

Narrated by Abu Nu'aim, he said: Zuhair narrated to me from Hasan ibn al-Harri from Al-Hakam: That a man, if he kills his wife unintentionally, "he is prevented from inheriting from her property and other things."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The killer does not inherit from the one he killed anything."
Narrated: Saeed bin Al-Mugirah, from Ibn Al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: Concerning a man who falsely accused his wife, and brought witnesses, and she was stoned? He said: "He inherits her."

Abu Nu'man reported: Abu 'Awana and Hammad said: "Concerning a man who was flogged with the prescribed punishment and it seemed he died, Abu Nu'man expressed doubt. He said: 'They will inherit from each other.'"
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The killer does not inherit, nor does he obstruct inheritance."
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The murderer does not inherit."
'Umar said: "A killer does not inherit, whether by mistake or deliberately."
"The killer does not inherit."

Narrated by Muhammad ibn Isa: He said, "Abd al-A'la told me, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Zuhri, that he said: 'If two lineages meet, inheritance is given through the more prominent of them, meaning the Persians.'"
One inherits from the side that is proper, and does not inherit from the side that is improper.

Hajjaj narrated to me, Hammad narrated to me, from Sufyan Thawri, from a man, from Al-Sha'bi: That Ali and Ibn Mas'ud said concerning the Zoroastrians: "If they embrace Islam, they inherit from both paternal and maternal relatives."

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to me, that Ibn Abi Zinaad narrated to me, from his father, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, concerning the woman of a prisoner of war: "She inherits from him, and he inherits from her."
Narrated Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz concerning prisoners who make a will: “I permit them their will as long as they remain upon their religion and do not alter from their religion.”
Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, Sufyan narrated, from Dawud, from Al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, who said: "The captive is inherited when he is in the hands of the enemy."
Narrated to me Muhammad, he said: Narrated to me Sufyan, he said: I was told by someone who heard Ibrahim say: "The captives are inheritable."
Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, from Dawood, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyib: That he used to say, "The captive does not inherit."
Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to Ash-Sha'bi: "Do not grant inheritance to a pregnant woman except with clear evidence, even if she comes to you in her tattered garments."
He narrated to me ‘Ubaidullah, from Isra’il, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "Inherit the laden (camel)."

Narrated from Abu Sa'id of the Banu Umayya, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdallah ibn Abi Maryam, from Damrah, and Al-Fudayl ibn Fadalah, and Ibn Abi Auf, and Rashid, and Atiyyah, they said: "The unborn do not inherit."

Sa'id ibn al-Mughira said: Ibn al-Mubarak said: He narrated to me Ibn ‘Awn from Muhammad, who said: A statement regarding boasting about lineage was mentioned before him, and he disliked it, and said: "The Muhajirun and the Ansar inherited their lineages as they were in the pre-Islamic era."
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to me from Ibn Idris, from Hisham, from Hasan and Ibn Sirin, who said: "The pregnant woman does not inherit until there is clear evidence [of the child's birth]."
Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Uthman used not to bequeath the riding animal (camel or horse) as inheritance.
A woman from the tribe of Harith, named Jaliba, whose lineage traced back to Jaliba, acknowledged (a kinship claim) through her. Then Abd Allah ibn Utba inherited from her through his sister.

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: I narrated to me Layth, who narrated to me Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from a man who said, while parting from this world: "I am the slave of so-and-so." He (the Prophet) said: "His inheritance will be returned to whoever declares that he is his slave when departing from this world, unless they bring forth clear evidence to the contrary; then they invalidate his statement, and his inheritance is returned to what that evidence establishes."
"Ali and Abdullah said: 'The child born out of wedlock is like the child of a cursed woman.'"

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Hasan ibn al-Huri, who narrated to me, from al-Hakam: That the child born out of wedlock does not inherit from the one who claims him, nor does the newborn inherit.

Narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaiba: He narrated to us, Rawh narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hafsah, from Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husain, that he did not inherit for the child born out of wedlock, even if the man claims him.

"Whenever a man comes to a boy claiming he is his son and that he had intercourse with his mother, and no one claims that boy, then he inherits from him." Bukayr said: I asked Urwa about this, and he said the same as Sulaiman ibn Yasar. Urwa said: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The child belongs to the bed, and the fornicator has the stone (i.e., disgrace)."
The son of mutual cursing is like the son born out of wedlock; his mother inherits him, his paternal relatives inherit him, and the relatives of his mother inherit him.
"The child born out of wedlock does not inherit."

Sa'id ibn al-Maghira narrated: From Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, or Yunus, from Zuhri, concerning the children of adultery: "They inherit from their mothers, and if a woman gives birth to twins and one of them dies, the surviving one inherits one-sixth."
"The son of adultery does not inherit. Inheritance is for him whose father has not been proven by legal punishment, or whose mother has been married (through marriage), or purchased."

Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to me from Musa ibn Muhammad al-Ansari from Isma'il, from Hasan, concerning a man who commits adultery with a woman and then marries her. He said: "There is no harm, unless she is pregnant, for the child does not belong to him."
