Narrated by Zayd ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Rashid, from Sulaiman ibn Musa, from Amr ibn Shu’aib, from his father, from his grandfather: That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, decreed, "Every acknowledged son is acknowledged by the inheritance of his father who claimed him after his death.” He decreed, “If he is from a slave woman, and his master possesses her on the night he is conceived, then he is acknowledged by those who acknowledged him, and he has no share in what was distributed of the inheritance before him. And whatever is discovered of an inheritance that has not been divided, he has his share. He is not acknowledged if the one for whom the claim is made denies it. And if he is from a slave woman whom he does not possess, or a free woman with whom she has committed adultery, then he is not acknowledged and does not inherit. And if the one for whom the claim is made is the one who claimed him, then he is an illegitimate child of the people of his mother’s side, whether they are free or slave.”
I asked al-Sha'bi about a slave I had, born of illicit relations. He said: "Do not sell him, and do not consume his price, but employ him."

Marwan ibn Muhammad reported: From Saeed, from Zuhri: He was asked about a child born out of wedlock who dies. He said: "If he is the son of an Arab woman, his mother inherits a third of his wealth, and the remainder of his wealth is placed in the public treasury. If he is the son of a free woman who is owned (as a slave), his mother inherits a third, and her emancipators inherit what remains." Marwan said: I heard Malik say that.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) judged that the inheritance of the child born of unlawful union should go entirely to his mother, due to the hardship she faced because of him.
Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the guardians of the mother concerning the child born out of wedlock: "Take your son, inherit him and acknowledge him, but he does not inherit from you."

Abu Nua'im and Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to me: They said, "Sha'bah narrated to me from Salama ibn Kuhail from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani who said: 'Abdullah said: 'The one who gives sadaqa (charity) disposes of his wealth as he wishes.' Abdullah ibn Yazid said: Sha'bah said: No one heard this from Salama except me."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, that Hatim ibn Wardan narrated to me, from Yunus, from Hasan: He was asked about the inheritance of a freed woman, and he said: "Every freed woman is a Sa'iba."
'Umar said: "Charity and the (female camel) Saibah are for their day or their time."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Zakariyya narrated, saying: 'Amir was asked about a slave who is set free without a specified master. He said: "It belongs to the one who set him free."

Abu Hatim al-Basri, that is Ruh ibn Aslam, narrated to me, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to me, Abdur-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated from his father, from Abdur-Rahman ibn ‘Amr, who said: “A servant died during the time of ‘Uthman without a guardian, so his property was ordered to be brought into the public treasury.”

Narrated by Ya’la, from Isma’il, from ‘Amir, from Masruq: Concerning a man who died without having a freed slave, it was said, "His wealth goes where he bequeathed it. If he did not bequeath it, then it is in the public treasury."

They (the companions like Damrah, Rashid ibn Sa'd, and others) said concerning the freeing of a female slave: “Her loyalty is to the one who freed her. He only emancipated her from slavery, but not from loyalty.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Dawud narrated to me from Shu'bah, who said: Mansur informed me from Ibrahim and Al-Sha'bi, that they said: "There is no objection to selling the freed woman's acknowledgment (of manumission) and gifting it."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Al-Mas'udi narrated to me from Al-Qasim, who said: "A man freed a slave who was a runaway, and he came to Abdullah and said: 'I have freed a runaway slave of mine, and this is his inheritance.' Abdullah said: 'It is yours.' He said: 'I have no need for it.' Abdullah said: 'Then place it [with them], for here there are many heirs.'"
Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Al-Ash’ath, from Abu Az-Zubair, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "When a baby laughs (or speaks clearly), he is inherited and prayers are offered for him."
"When a baby laughs (or speaks clearly), he inherits, and he is inherited from, and prayer is offered for him."

Malik related to me, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Every newborn cries, and his cry is at the time of Satan's influence in his belly; he cries out, except for Isa, the son of Maryam."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The newborn does not inherit until he cries out loudly, and if he falls [alive].”
Narrated by Jabir: "When a baby laughs (or gurgles), prayer is offered for him, and he inherits."
Narrated Abdullah ibn Muhammad: Narrated Ma'n from Ibn Abi Thieb from Al-Zuhri: He said: "I see 'the sneezing' as an expression of praise."
"The newborn is not inherited until he laughs, nor is prayer offered for him until he laughs. Once he laughs, prayer is offered for him, he is inherited, and the blood-wit is completed."

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to me, Layth narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: We asked him about stillbirths, and he said: "There is no prayer for them, and no prayer for a newborn until he cries out loudly."

Harun ibn Ma’wiya narrated to me from Abu Sufyan, from Ma’mar, from Qatada, who said: "When two emancipating slaves purchase each other, and one says to the other, ‘This is from his master,’ and the other says, ‘This is from his master,’ then the sale belongs to the first one. And the people of Medina say: ‘Loyalty belongs to the master of the seller,’ and they say: ‘This one only purchased what was incumbent upon the emancipating slave, so loyalty belongs to the master.’”

Umar (RA) said: "Whoever of a free man marries a slave woman, he has emancipated half of himself, and whoever of a slave marries a free woman, he has manumitted half of himself." Abu Muhammad said: "Meaning the child."

Abu Shihab narrated to me from Shaybani, from Ash-Sha'bi: Regarding a slave who marries a woman, then divorces her and has a child by her? He (the Prophet) said: "If she is free, then the maintenance is upon him (the slave). And if he (the child) is a slave, then the maintenance is upon his master."
They said, "His loyalty belongs to the one who initiated the manumission first."

Muhammad ibn Isa reported: He said, "Husheim narrated to me on the authority of Yunus, from Hasan. And Jarrir narrated to me on the authority of Aban ibn Taghlib, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, that they said: 'If he guarantees (for the slave), then the manumission is his; and if the slave seeks help, then the manumission is between them.'"

Yahya and Abu Nu'aim narrated to me: Zukrayya narrated to us from Amir: Concerning a slave between two men, one of them emancipated his share, he said: "His emancipation should be completed. If he has no property, the slave should be assessed in the half at a just value, and the Wala’ is for the one who emancipated."

Harun ibn Ma’wiya narrated to me from Abu Sufyan al-Ma’mari from Ma’mar from Ibn Taawus from his father: Concerning a slave between two men, one of them manumitted his share and the other retained his, he said: “His inheritance is between them.”

Harun narrated to me from Abu Sufyan, from Ma’mar, from Zuhri, who said: “Its inheritance belongs to the one who held it.” Qatadah said: “It is entirely for the manumitted slave, and its price is upon him.” And the people of Kufa say it as well.

Narrated: 'Ataa: Concerning a man who dies leaving a freedman obligated to him, and he has sons and daughters, do women have any share in the manumission? He said: "Women inherit from what is on his back of his manumission, and the manumission belongs to the men except for those women who have manumitted or emancipated [others]."
"Women do not inherit from the waqf except what they have manumitted, or what they have manumitted through others."

Narrated: Muhammad bin Isa said, "Abu Sufyan narrated to me from Ma'mar, from Yahya bin Abi Katir, who said, 'A man died leaving a person he had contracted with (for manumission). Then the person he had contracted with died and left property. So Ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Salama bin Abdur-Rahman distributed what remained of his contract between the male and female descendants of his master. And whatever remained of the property after the contract, it belonged to the males of his master’s descendants, excluding the females.'"

Narrated ‘Umar, ‘Ali, and Zaid: They said, “Manumission belongs to the eldest [amongst slaves], and women do not inherit from manumission except what they have freed or contracted to purchase their own freedom.”

Narrated by Muhammad bin Isa, narrated to me by Ismail bin Ibrahim, from Khalid, from Abu Qilaba; and narrated to me by Ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from Zuhairi, from Saeed bin Musayyib; and narrated to me by Ibn Abi Zinaad, from his father, from Sulaiman bin Yasir: that they said: "Women do not inherit from loyalty except what they have manumitted or contracted to purchase their freedom."

Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Mu’adh, from Ash’ath, from Hasan, who said: “Women do not inherit from manumission except what they have freed, or what they have freed through others, except for a cursed woman (mulā‘anah); she inherits from what her son has freed, and from what the one whose father has disowned has freed.”
Narrated by Salim from his father: That Umar’s freedmen used to inherit from him before his daughters did.

'Amru ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Khalid ibn 'Abdullah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha'i, from Abu Qilaba, concerning a woman who died leaving her sons. They inherited her wealth and slaves. He (Abu Qilaba) said: "Loyalty reverts to the relatives (asaba) of the woman."

Narrated ‘Ubaidullah, from Isra’il, from Mansur, who said: I asked Ibrahim about a man who contracted with a slave of his, then died and left behind adult sons and daughters. He said, "For the males, excluding the females."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Wahb narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan, that he used to say concerning a woman who died leaving a mawla (freed slave): "The wala' (kinship/obligation) is for her sons, and if they die, it reverts to her relatives (asaba)."
"Women have no right to manumit (a slave) except when they emancipate (slaves) from their own property."

Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Ibn 'Awn from Muhammad, who said: A servant of 'Umar died. So 'Umar's son asked Zayd ibn Thabit, "Do 'Umar's daughters have anything from his inheritance?" He said, "I do not see that they have anything. But if you wish to give them, then give them."
One secures kinship through inheritance.

Narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm: That a woman from the tribe of Muharib emancipated her slave and then gifted her emancipation to herself. Then she gifted her own emancipation to Abdur-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and she died. The freedmen then disputed the matter with Uthman, so Uthman called for witnesses to what they claimed. The witnesses came, and Uthman said to them, "Go, and become the freedmen of whoever you wish." Abu Bakr said, "So, I became the freedman of Abdur-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Hazm."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling wala’ (a bond of allegiance or patronage) and gifting it.
Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade selling a slave's manumission and gifting it.

Ya'la narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Malik narrated to me from Ata', who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "Manumission cannot be sold nor gifted, and manumission belongs to him who has freed [the slave]."
'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Loyalty (wala') is like kinship; it cannot be sold or given as a gift."
They both disliked the selling of manumission (freedom).
Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated: Ibn Idris narrated to me from Ibn Jurayj from Ata' who said: Ibn Abbas said: "Manumission cannot be sold. Would one eat up a man’s freedom twice?"
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Abbas: “Obligations are of six things, and we do not neglect them.”

Muhammad ibn Imran narrated from Muawiyah ibn Maysarah ibn Shurayh from Shurayh ibn al-Harith, who said: "A dispute was brought before Shurayh concerning two daughters, their parents, and a husband. He judged the matter. Then the husband came forward complaining about him in the mosque. So Abdullah ibn Rabah was sent to him and took him, and [they] sent to Shurayh, and said to him: 'What does this man say?' He said: 'He considers me a unjust man, and I consider him a wicked man, who displays complaint and conceals a judgment.' The man said: 'What do you say about two daughters, their parents, and a husband?' He said: 'The husband receives a fourth of the entire property, the parents receive two-sixths, and what remains belongs to the two daughters.' The man said: 'Why have you diminished me?' He said: 'I have not diminished you; Allah has diminished you. For the two daughters, two-thirds; for the parents, two-sixths; and for the husband, a fourth. This is a share out of seven and a half, and your share is for maintenance.'"
The narrator, Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah, relates from ‘Ali ibn Musahir, from Ash’ath, from Ash-Sha’bi, from ‘Ali, and ‘Umar, and Zayd, who said: "A father draws the allegiance of his son."
The grandfather pulls the tie of allegiance.
The father draws (or pulls) the loyalty of his son.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zakariyya narrated to me, from 'Amir: "Concerning a slave who died and had a free father, and he had children from a free woman, to whom belongs the loyalty of his son? He [the Prophet] said: To the mawali of the grandfather."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Israel narrated to me, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: "Concerning a slave who had entered into a contract [of manumission], who died after fulfilling half of his contract, and he had a child by a free woman, he said: I do not think but that he has discharged the manumission of his son."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me from Al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, who said: "Shurayh would not reverse a judgment he issued. Al-Aswad informed him that 'Umar said: 'If a slave marries a free woman and they have children, and those children are free, then if the slave is subsequently emancipated, the loyalty (wala') reverts to the freedman's former masters.'" Shurayh acted upon this statement.

Narrated Yahya, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Umar said, "A slave woman can be wed to a free man, a child is freed by the emancipation of his mother, and when the father is emancipated, emancipation extends to the child."

Muslim narrated: Abdu’l-Warith narrated to me from Kathir ibn Shinzir from ‘Ata: “Regarding a free woman who is under the ownership of a slave, he said: As for those she bears who are slaves, their loyalty is to the people of her master’s generosity, and as for those she bears who are free, their loyalty is to the people of his generosity.”

Narrated Umar: "If a free woman is married to a slave, and she bears him a son, then that son is freed by her emancipation, and his allegiance is to the freedmen of his mother. If the father is then freed, the allegiance shifts to the freedmen of his father."

Al-Ala' ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman said: "My mother was a slave of al-Hurqah, and my father was a freedman of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan al-Nasri. Then my father fulfilled his emancipation contract. Afterwards, al-Hurqah visited 'Uthman seeking his right – meaning the allowance – and Malik ibn Aws was with him. So al-Hurqah said, "That is my slave," and they disputed the matter before 'Uthman, and 'Uthman ruled in favor of al-Hurqah."

Narrated: Sahm bin Yazid al-Hamrawi: That a man died without any heirs, so it was written to Umar bin Abdul Aziz about him while he was a caliph, and he wrote: "Distribute his inheritance among those who used to receive stipends with them." So his inheritance was distributed among those who used to receive stipends with them in his company.
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “It is not permissible for a Muslim to spend two nights while he has something to bequeath without it being written.”
The believer does not eat in every stomach, and his will (or testament) remains beneath his side.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Qasim ibn Umar, who said: Thumamah ibn Hazn asked me, "What did your father do?" I said, "He died." He said, "Did he leave a will?" For it was said, "If a man leaves a will, his will completes what he neglected of his zakah." Abu Muhammad said, and another said: Qasim ibn Amr.
It was said, "Whoever makes a bequest and it is not altered or violated, he will receive a reward equivalent to that which he would have received had he given it in charity during his lifetime."

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to me, he said: Shu’bah narrated to me from Abu Yunus, from Qaza’ah, who said: It was said to Harim ibn Hayyan, "Give counsel." He said: "I counsel you to the last verses of Surah An-Nahl," and Ibn Hayyan recited: "Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in the best manner…” until “…and those who do good are rewarded.” [Surah An-Nahl (16:125-128]

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated from Malik ibn Mughul from Talha ibn Musrif al-Yammi, who said: I asked Abdullah ibn Abi Aufa: Did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) make a will? He said: No. I said: Then how was the will written for the people, or were they ordered to make wills? He said: He bequeathed the Book of Allah.

Huzayl ibn Surhabeel said: Abu Bakr would appoint someone to oversee the will of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). Abu Bakr hoped that he had found a covenant from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), so he sniffed his nose with a piece of cloth.

Yazid narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, from Qatadah, who said: "It is written upon you: When death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind any good, [to make] a will to his parents and relatives in righteousness – a duty enjoined upon [those] mindful of Allah." (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 180). He said: "The good is wealth; it was said: a thousand [dirhams] or more than that."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, and Ibn ‘Aun narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sirin: “That he bequeathed what he had bequeathed, or this is a reminder of what Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Amrah bequeathed to his sons and his family: #Fear Allah and amend that which is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger if you are believers. [Surah Al-Anfal, 8:1]# And he bequeathed to them what Abraham bequeathed to his sons, and Jacob: #O my sons! Allah has indeed chosen this religion for you, so never die except as Muslims. [Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:132]# And he bequeathed to them not to desire to be the clients of the Ansar and their brothers in religion, and that chastity and truthfulness are better and more righteous than adultery and falsehood. If an event occurs with him in this illness before I change this will of mine, then he mentioned his need.”

Narrated Anas: Thus, they used to give instructions (in wills): “This is what so-and-so, son of so-and-so, instructed, that he bears witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without any partner; and that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger; and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it; and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves. He instructed those he left behind of his family to fear Allah and to reconcile among themselves, and to obey Allah and His Messenger if they are believers. And he instructed them with that which Ibrahim instructed his sons and Yaqub: “O my sons! Allah has chosen this religion for you, so do not die except as Muslims.” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:132). And he instructed that if something happened to him from this illness, his need was such and such.”

Al-Hakim narrated to me, and said: Walid narrated to me from Hafs bin Ghailan from Makhul when he was giving a will, he said: "We bear witness to this, so bear witness with it: We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without any partner; and that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger; and [one] believes in Allah, and disbelieves in the tyrant. Upon this, he lives, if Allah wills, and dies, and is resurrected. And he wills in that which Allah has provided for him in that which he leaves behind, if an event occurs to him while he is thus and thus, if he does not change anything of that which is in this will."

Al-Hakim narrated, and said: Walid narrated to me that Ibn Thawban narrated to me from his father from Makhul, who said: "This is the will of Abu ad-Darda'."

Jarir narrated from his father that Rabic ibn Khuthaym wrote his will, saying: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what Rabic ibn Khuthaym has bequeathed, and I bear witness to it before Allah, and Allah is sufficient as a Witness, and the Reward-Giver to His righteous servants. I testify that I have accepted Allah as my Lord, Islam as my religion, and Muhammad as my Prophet. And I command myself and whoever obeys me to worship Allah among the worshippers, and to praise Him among the praisers, and to give sincere counsel to the Muslim community."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Hisham, from his father, that 'Ali entered upon a sick person, and the matter of the will was mentioned to him. 'Ali said: "Allah said, 'If anyone fears Allah and restrains himself from evil, then surely Allah is forgiving and merciful.' [Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:180] And I do not see that he restrained himself from evil." Hammad said: I retained that he left more than seven hundred [dirhams].

Muhammad ibn Kanasah reported: Hisham narrated to me from his father, who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib visited a man from his people who was ill. The man said, "Shall I make a will?" He (Ali) said, "No, you have not left any property. So, give your property to your son."

Narrated Abu Zayd: I narrated to me Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "Concerning a man who made a will, and the heirs were witnesses confirming [its validity], it was said, 'It is not permissible.'" Abu Muhammad said: "Meaning, if they deny [the will] afterward."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to me, saying: I asked Hakim and Hammad: "Concerning the awliya’ (friends/helpers), do they permit a will, and then, when someone dies, do they not permit it?" They said: "It is not permissible."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me from Dawud ibn Abi Hind from Amir from Shurayh: "Concerning a man who bequeaths more than a third of his estate, he said: If the heirs approve it, we approve it, and if the heirs say, 'We approve it,' then they are absolved when they shake the dust from the grave."

Narrated: Al-Qasim: That a man asked his heirs for permission to bequeath more than a third [of his estate], and they permitted him, then they revoked that permission after his death. So, Abdullah was asked about that, and he said: "This revocation is not permissible."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Hisham from Hasan: "Regarding a man who bequeaths more than a third [of his estate], and the heirs accept it, he said: It is permissible." Abu Muhammad said: We permit it, meaning [this acceptance] in lifetime.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Hammam narrated to me, he said: Qatadah narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn Sa’d, from his father, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) visited him while he was in Mecca, and he had no children but a daughter. He said, "I have only one daughter, so should I bequeath all of my wealth?" The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "No." He said, "Should I bequeath half?" The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "No." He said, "Should I bequeath a third?" The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "A third, and a third is much."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Zuhri from Amir ibn Sa’d from his father, who said: “I fell ill alongside the Prophet (ﷺ) during the Farewell Hajj until I was laid down. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to visit me, and I said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, I do not think but that pain has afflicted me, and I possess much wealth. I only have one daughter as an heir. Should I donate all of my wealth?’ He said: ‘No.’ I said: ‘Then half of it?’ He said: ‘No.’ I said: ‘Then a third?’ He said: ‘A third, and a third is abundant. Indeed, if you leave your heirs wealthy, it is better than leaving them poor, begging people for assistance. And indeed, you do not spend an expenditure except that Allah rewards you for it, even what you spend in the mouth of your wife.’”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn Suwaid, from Al-Ala’ ibn Ziyad: “That his father, Ziyad ibn Matar, made a will and said: ‘My will is what the jurists of Basrah agree upon.’ So I asked, and they agreed upon one-fifth [of inheritance].”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, that Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn Suwayd, from Al-Ala’ ibn Ziyad: That a man asked Umar ibn al-Khattab, saying: "My heir is a kalalah (a person who has no son but daughters), should I bequeath half [of my estate]?" Umar said: "No." He said: "Then a third?" Umar said: "No." He said: "Then a quarter?" Umar said: "No." He said: "Then a fifth?" Umar said: "No." He continued until he reached the tenth, whereupon Umar said: "Bequeath the tenth."

Yalaa narrated to me, Ismail narrated to me, from Amir, who said: "They used to give [as inheritance] only the fifth and the quarter, and a third was the limit of the generous [giving]." Abu Muhammad said: By 'generous,' he means a wild horse.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me from Humayd, from Bakr, who said: “I entrusted a bequest to Humayd ibn Abdur-Rahman, and he said: ‘I would not accept the bequest of a man who has children, bequeathing one-third.’”
Qabisa reported: Sufyan narrated to me from Hisham from Muhammad ibn Sirin from Shurayh who said, "A third is an effort, and it is permissible."
He said: "Two-thirds were more beloved to them than one-third."
The narrator, Abu al-Walid, states: Sharif narrated to me from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: "The testamentary trustee is trustworthy with that which he is entrusted with."

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to me, from Abu Wahb, from Makhul, who said: "The authority of a deputy is permissible in all matters except for purchasing. And if he sells something, he should not say, 'I sell,' – and this is the view of Yahya ibn Hamza."
The narrator, Yahya ibn Abi Katir, said: "The guardian (wasi) is trustworthy in all matters except in manumitting slaves; for in that case, he must establish the obligation (of loyalty)."
Narrated by Ibrahim: "The guardian is permitted to utilize the property of the orphan if he instructs a man [to do so]."
The guardian of the orphan should take care of his affairs and advocate for him, and the absent (person) is under his advocacy.

I was with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and with him were Sulaiman ibn Habib and Abu Qilaba, when a young غلام entered and said, "Our land is in such and such a place; the وصي sold you while we were children." Umar turned to Sulaiman ibn Habib and said, "What do you say?" He spoke hesitantly. Then Umar turned to Abu Qilaba and said, "What do you say?" He replied, "Return the land to the غلام." Umar said, "Will our wealth then perish?" Abu Qilaba replied, "You have destroyed it."

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ash'ath, from Hasan: Concerning a man who bequeathed half of his wealth to one person and a third of his wealth to another, he said: "They are to calculate both of them based on the third: this one [receives] according to the half, and this one [receives] according to the third."
The one who makes a will may alter it as he pleases, except for the manumission [of slaves].
Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) said: "A man may state whatever he wishes in his will, but the essence of the will is its final statement."

Sahlu ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: Hammam narrated to me, saying: Qatadah narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Dinār narrated to me that his father freed some slaves of his during an illness. Then he reconsidered and wished to return them and free others instead. He said: They contested with me to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and he ratified the freeing of the latter ones and invalidated the freeing of the former ones.
'Umar said: "A man may say whatever he wishes in his will, but the essence of the will is its final statement."
Sa'id ibn al-Mughira said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me from Ma'mar, from Zuhri: "Concerning a man who makes a will, then makes another will, he said: Both are permissible from his wealth."
'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The essence of a will is its last part."

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Al-Walid narrated to me, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya, who said: "If a judge suspects the guardian (wasi), he does not remove him, but appoints another with him." And that is the view of al-Awza'i.

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to me, from Shaybani, from Amir, who said: "Selling, buying, and marrying a sick person are permissible, and it does not come from the third [of inheritance]."
"Whatever a sick person undertakes in a sale or purchase during his illness, its value is justly assessed from his estate at one-third."

Abu an-Nu'man narrated: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Yahya, who is Ibn Sa'id, who said: A woman from our family gave [in charity], while she was pregnant. The question was posed to al-Qasim, and he said: "It is from all of the wealth." Yahya said: "And we say: If the labor pains seize her and she gives nothing, then it is from one-third."

Narrated on the authority of Hasan: Concerning a man who said to his slave, "If I enter the house of so-and-so, my slave is free," and he entered it while sick, it is decreed that he be freed from one-third of his estate. But if he entered it in good health, he is freed from the entirety of his wealth.

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to me, saying: Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me from Makhul, who said: "If the heirs are in need, I do not see any objection to returning to them from the one-third [of the inheritance]." Yahya said: So I mentioned this to al-Awza'i, and he was pleased by it.

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me, from Hasan. And Mughira narrated to me, from Ibrahim, they said: "If two witnesses from among the heirs testify, it is valid against all of them. And if one testifies, it is valid only in his share."
"If a witness is among the heirs, then he has a share according to his inheritance, and then he says: after that, in all of his share."

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to me, he said: Abu Shihab Abd al-Rabbi ibn Naafi’ narrated to me, from al-A’mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "If a man bequeaths a third and a quarter, then [the bequest is valid] in the property and debts. And if he bequeaths fifty or sixty, up to a hundred, then [the bequest is valid] in the property until it reaches a third."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A man is most entitled to one-third of his wealth, which he may dispose of as he wishes."

Abu Habibah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I asked Abu ad-Darda’ about a man who placed dirhams in the way of Allah. Abu ad-Darda’ said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: “The example of the one who gives charity at his death or emancipates [a slave] is like the one who gives after having been sated.”

Al-Hasan said: "Regarding a man who makes a will stipulating certain things, including manumitting a slave, and exceeds one-third, they begin with the manumission."

Al-Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated: We were told by Wuhayb, from Ayyub, from Muhammad: "According to the shares [of inheritance]."

"Whoever makes a will or emancipates [a slave], and there is a debt in his will, then that debt enters upon the people of the emancipations and the people of the will." 'Ata' said: "Indeed, the people of Medina overpower us, they begin with the emancipations before [dealing with] the will."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, saying: 'Amru ibn Dinār said, concerning one who recommends manumitting [a slave] and other [acts of charity], and exceeds one-third [of the estate], he said: "According to the shares [prescribed in Islamic law]."

Narrated to me Sulaiman ibn Harb, narrated to me Hammad ibn Zayd, from Kathir ibn Shanzir, from Al-Hasan: Concerning a man who bequeathed more than a third [of his estate], and there is a manumission [of a slave] involved? He said: Begin with the manumission.
Narrated by Ibrahim: "The emancipation of slaves is initiated before the will."
Al-Mulla Ibn Asad narrated to me: He said, "Abu Hurairah reported: A man bequeathed to the sons of so-and-so, saying: 'Their rich and their poor, their males and their females, are equal.'"
Narrated by Al-Hasan: "When one bequeaths to the children of so-and-so, then the male and female are equal in it."

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, saying: Zaidah ibn Musa al-Hamdani narrated to me, saying: Siyar ibn Abi Karib narrated to me: “That a man came to Sharh and asked him about a person who bequeathed a share from his wealth. Sharh said: ‘The inheritance is calculated, and whatever the number of its shares amounts to, the legatee is given a share equivalent to one of them.’”

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Saeed narrated to me from Makhool who said: "If a man gives more than one-half of his wealth to some of his heirs while he is in sound mind, it is reduced to one-third, and if he gives one-half, then it is permissible for him." Saeed said: "And the judges of the people of Damascus used to rule based on this."
“The shroud is from all wealth.”

Narrated from Ibn Musa, from Mu'adh, from Ash'ath, from Hasan: Concerning a man who died leaving assets worth two thousand dirhams, and upon him a debt of the same amount or more, he said: He should be shrouded from it, and his debt should not be paid.
"He began with the shroud, then the debt, then the will."
Qabisa reported: Sufyan narrated to me from Firas from Ash-Sha'bi: "Concerning a woman who dies," he said: "She is shrouded from her own property; the husband has nothing to do with it."
Sa'id ibn al-Mughira narrated to me from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: "The camphor and the shroud are from the principal property."

Muhammad ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Musahir, from Ismail, from Hasan, who said: "The shroud should be from the middle of the wealth; it should be sufficient for what he used to wear in his life, then the debt is paid, and then a third [of the remainder]."

Abu Nu'man narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, saying: Mansur narrated to me from Hasan, who used to say: "If a man entrusts a bequest to another while absent, then let him accept it. And if he is present, then it is within his choice: if he wills, he accepts, and if he wills, he leaves it."

Salih ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ayyub, who said: I asked Hasan and Muhammad about a man entrusting [his affairs] to another man. They said: “We prefer that [the entrustment] be accepted.”

Muhammad ibn As'ad narrated to me, Abu Bakr narrated to me, from Hisham, from Hasan, who said: "If a man entrusts something to another while he is absent, and then he arrives, if he wishes, he may accept it. If he accepts it, then he is not permitted to revoke it."
"Narrated by Hasan: If a man entrusts a matter to another, and the matter is presented to him while he is absent and he accepts it, then he is not permitted to retract (from it)."

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Shabih, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, who said: "If a man makes a will to someone while he is absent and deceased, and he is unaware [of it], then it is returned [rejected]."
Narrated Hasan: If someone bequeaths to his slave a third of his wealth, a quarter of his wealth, or a fifth of his wealth, then emancipation is included within his wealth.
It was said, "Indeed, a man may be deprived of the blessing in his wealth during his lifetime, and when he reaches death, he provisions himself with wickedness."
Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "The 'Murran' is restraint in life and extravagance at death." Abu Muhammad said: It is said, 'bitter in life and bitter at death.'
"If a man bequeaths to another a share equivalent to that of his son, then he does not grant him a share equivalent to his, until it is diminished from his own."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Al-Sha'bi: "Concerning a man who had three sons, and he bequeathed to a man the share that he would have received if they were four. Al-Sha'bi said: 'He gives him one-fifth.'"
We asked ‘Amir about a man who left behind two sons and bequeathed to each of them what would have been their share had they been three. He said, “He bequeathed a fourth.”

Narrated by Ibrahim: Concerning a man who bequeathed a portion equivalent to that of one of his heirs, it was said: It is not permissible, even if it is less than a third. Abu Muhammad said: It is sound (hasan).

Narrated from Qabisa, who said: Sufyan narrated to me from Ibn Abi Asfar, from Al-Sha'bi: "Concerning a man who bequeathed a dirham from the yield of his slave, and the yield was six, he said to him: 'Its sixth belongs to you.'"
Qabisa reported: I heard Sufyan saying: "If someone acknowledges a debt of one hundred dirhams to an heir and to a non-heir, I think that both acknowledgements should be declared invalid."

Muslim narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Qatadah narrated to me, from Ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, who said: "No acknowledgement (of inheritance) is permissible from an heir." He said: Hasan said: "The most rightful thing upon which one may acknowledge is on the first day of the Hereafter, and the last day of the world."
Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, Khalid narrated to me, from Khalid, from Abu Qilaba, who said: "A will does not devolve to an heir."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Humaid: That a man known as Abu Thabit admitted to his wife at his death that she was owed four hundred dirhams from her dowry. Hasan approved of this.

I was beneath the Prophet’s camel while it was swaying with its gait, and its saliva was splashing between my shoulders. I heard him say: “Indeed, Allah has given every possessor of a right his right, so a bequest to an heir is not permissible.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, from Qatadah, who said: "When death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind any good, the proper course is to make a will for his parents and relatives with kindness; it is a right upon those who fear Allah [Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 180]. Then he ordered that a will be made for parents and relatives. Afterwards, this was abrogated in Surah An-Nisa', which assigned a specific share for the parents, and attached the share of every heir from among them. They have no will; thus, the will became for someone who has no heir from relatives or others."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Abbas: "The property was for the son, and the bequest was for the parents and relatives. Then Allah abrogated that and legislated that the male should have the share of two females, and Allah made for each of the parents a sixth and a third, and for the woman an eighth and a quarter, and for the husband a half and a quarter."

"Malik narrated: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to me from Yazid from Ikrimah and Hasan: ‘Indeed, if one leaves behind goodness, the will for the parents and relatives is [as stated in] Surat al-Baqarah, verse 180. Thus, the will was [permitted] until it was abrogated by the verse of inheritance.’”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Humaid, from Hasan, who said: "It was asked about a man who bequeathed something while he had a wealthy brother. Is it permissible for him to bequeath to him? He said: Yes, even if he possessed twenty thousand [dirhams], and then he said: Even if he possessed one hundred thousand [dirhams], for his wealth does not preclude him from the right."

Narrated ‘Affan: Hammad bin Salama narrated to me from Qatada, from Hasan and Sa’id bin al-Musayyib, that a man said, “My sword belongs to so-and-so, if so-and-so dies, it belongs to so-and-so, if so-and-so dies, it returns to me.” They (Hasan and Sa’id) said, “It belongs to the first (recipient).” He (the narrator) said: Humayd bin ‘Abd ar-Rahman said, “It is enforced as he said.”

‘Urwa reported: A person gives a gift to another and says, “This is for you, but if I die, it is for so-and-so; and if so-and-so dies, it is for so-and-so; and if so-and-so dies, it returns to me.” It was said that it is implemented as he said, even if they are a hundred.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, Shayba ibn Hisham ar-Rasibi and Katir ibn Ma’dan said: We asked Salim ibn Abdullah about a man who bequeaths to someone outside of his relatives. Salim said: It is where he made it. We said: Indeed, Hasan says: It is returned to the closest relatives. Salim strongly disapproved of this and spoke harsh words.
"When a man makes a bequest (wasiyyah) concerning his relatives, it is for the closest of them in kinship; the male and female are equal in that regard."
Narrated: 'A man said, "One of my slaves is free, then he died without clarifying [which one]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The heirs are in his position; they manumit whichever one they prefer."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Yunus, from Hasan: That a man, while sick, said: “So much to such a person, and so much to such a person, and my servant so-and-so is free.” And he did not say, “If something happens to me.” Then he recovered. He said, “He is a slave.”

Narrated from Ahmad ibn Abdullah, who said: Abu Bakr narrated to me from Mutarrif from Al-Sha'bi: Concerning a man who emancipates his slave at the point of death, and he has nothing else (to leave), and he has a debt, it was said: "He should strive for the creditors in its price (the slave's value)."

Narrated ‘Hasan: That a man purchased a slave for nine hundred dirhams, and emancipated him without paying the price of the slave, and left nothing. Then ‘Ali said, "Let the slave seek (to earn) his price."
"The well-managed (portion) is from a third."
He said: "The well-managed (portion) is from a third."
Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Kathir from Hasan who said, "The freed slave is freed from a third of (the debt)."
The freed slave woman (who was freed) from her husband’s back and her child are from one-third (of the inheritance).
Mansur informed me, from Ibrahim, who said: "The freed slave is released from a third of the debt."
"The well-managed (or carefully considered) portion from all wealth is commendable."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Abu ‘Awana narrated to me from Abu Bishr from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The freed slave is freed from a portion of all property."

Abu Muhammad was asked: Which portion do you mean? He replied: One-third.
Do not bear witness to a will until it is read to you, and do not bear witness to someone you do not know.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to me, from Humaid, from Hasan: That Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) bequeathed four thousand [dirhams], four thousand, to each of his wives.
Yahyá ibn Hassan transmitted to me, from Ibn Abi Zayd, from his father, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: that he authorized a will for a period of thirteen years.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, who said: "A young boy from the tribe made a will, being seven years old. Then Shu'aib said: 'If the young boy’s will benefits him, it is valid.' Abu Muhammad said: 'This pleases me, but the judges do not approve.'"

Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, Abu Ishaq narrated that he witnessed Shurayh ratifying the will of Abbas ibn Ismail ibn Marthad in favor of his wet nurse from the people of Hira. And Abbas was a young boy.
Ja'far ibn 'Awn reported: Yunus narrated to me, and Abu Ishaq narrated: Said Sharh: "If a boy fears the riding animal, his bequest is valid."

Qabisa narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq: That a young boy among them, named Marthad, when he was nearing death, bequeathed forty dirhams to a wet nurse of his from the people of Hira. Sharh ibn Mansur approved of it, and said: "Whoever attains the truth, we shall approve of it."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Yahya informed me that Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm informed him: “That a young boy in Medina was nearing death, and his heirs were in Syria. They informed ‘Umar that he was dying, so they asked him to order him to make a will. ‘Umar ordered him to do so, and he bequeathed a well called Birjusham. Its people sold it for thirty thousand [dirhams]. Abu Bakr mentioned that the boy was ten or twelve years old.”

Yazid narrated from Hisham al-Dustawa'i, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "The will of a minor regarding his wealth is permissible in a third or less. However, his guardian prevents him from it during his sound mind out of fear for his poverty. But when he is dying, he is not allowed to prevent him."
Narrated Abdullah ibn Utbah: That a will of a female slave was brought to him, and they began to diminish it. So he said, "Whoever has attained the truth, we will fulfill it for him."

Sulayman al-Ghassani died at the age of ten or twelve years, and he bequeathed a well worth thirty thousand [dirhams]. Umar ibn al-Khattab approved of it. Abu Muhammad said: The people say: Amr ibn Sulayman narrated. Qabisa narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us from the sons of Ibn Abi Bakr, Abdullah and Muhammad, from their father, similar to that. One of them said: He was thirteen years old, and the other said: Before he reached puberty. Abu Muhammad said, from his sons, meaning the sons of Abu Bakr.
He (the Prophet) said: “His will is not a valid gift except for something of no consequence, meaning a boy before he reaches puberty.”

Amru ibn ‘Awn narrated to me, from Hushaym, from Yunus, from Hasan, who said: "The divorce, bequest, gift, charity, and manumission of a boy are not valid until he has attained puberty (i.e., has had a nocturnal emission)."
"The divorce of a minor, nor his manumitting, nor his bequest, nor his purchase, nor his sale, nor anything [of that nature] is not valid."

Abu al-Walid narrated to me, that Hammam narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Himayri, who said: "There is no validity in divorce or a will except in a sound mind, except for the intoxicated; for the divorce of an intoxicated man is valid, and his back is beaten."

I asked Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman and Muawiya ibn Qurra about a man who said in his will: "All of me are free, and he has a runaway slave." They said: "He is free." Hasan, Iyas, and Bakr ibn Abd Allah said: "He is not free."
Narrated by 'Abdullah ibn Maslama, who said: "Abdullah al-'Umari narrated to me from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: "That 'Umar instructed Hafsa, the mother of the believers."
Safiyyah entrusted a Jewish relative of hers.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Zuhayr narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, who said: "A boy from the Banu al-Hayy, named Abbas ibn Marthad, who was seven years old, bequeathed forty dirhams to a Jewish wet nurse from the people of al-Hira. Sharh said: 'If the boy’s bequest is valid, it is permissible, and he bequeathed only to someone deserving.'" Abu Muhammad said: "I agree with this view."

Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated: Abu Usama narrated to me from Hisham from his father: That Al-Zubayr made his houses a charity for his sons; they were not to be sold nor inherited. And the returned daughter has the right to reside in them without causing harm or being harmed. If she becomes self-sufficient through a husband, then she has no right.

Al-Hakim ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, saying: Al-Walid narrated to me from Hafs from Makhul: "Concerning a man who bequeaths dirhams for the sake of Allah to another man, and the one to whom it was bequeathed dies before spending them from his family, [it is said:] They belong to the guardians of the deceased who made the bequest, and they should fulfill it for the sake of Allah."

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Muhsir from Ash’ath from Hasan: “Concerning a man who entrusts a bequest to another man, and the one to whom the bequest was entrusted dies before the one who made the bequest, he said: It is permissible for the heirs of the one to whom the bequest was entrusted.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Muhsir from Ash’ath from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi’i, who said: “I was informed that ‘Ali permitted it in the same manner as the statement of Hasan.”

Abu Hurairah (RA) reported that a man came to Ibn Umar (RA) and said, "A man entrusted a camel to me as a bequest for Allah's sake, and this is not a time when it is taken out for raiding (ghazu). Should I carry it on during Hajj?" Ibn Umar (RA) said, "Hajj and Umrah are for Allah's sake."

Narrated from 'Ubaidullah ibn Musa, from Musa ibn 'Ubaida, from Waqid ibn Muhammad ibn Zaid ibn Abdullah ibn 'Umar: That a man bequeathed his wealth in the path of Allah. The guardian (of the estate) inquired about this from 'Umar, who said, "Give it to Allah’s workers." He said, "And who are Allah’s workers?" He said, "Those who perform Hajj to the House of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, the man in whose heart there is nothing of the Qur'an is like a ruined house."

"Indeed, this Qur’an is the provision of Allah, so take from it as much as you are able. I do not know of anything more virtuous than a house in which there is nothing of the Book of Allah. And the heart in which there is nothing of the Book of Allah is desolate, like a house that has no inhabitant."

"Learn this Qur'an, for you are rewarded with ten good deeds for every letter you recite. I do not say (regarding the letter) 'alif,' but rather 'alif,' 'lam,' and 'mim,' [meaning] for every letter, ten good deeds."

Abu Hurairah (RA) used to say: "Indeed, the house expands for its occupants, and the angels attend it and the devils shun it, and its goodness increases when the Quran is recited therein. And indeed, the house constricts for its occupants, and the angels shun it and the devils attend it, and its goodness diminishes when the Quran is not recited therein."
Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: “If the Qur’an were (written) on the skins of cattle, then thrown into the fire, it would not burn.”

Recite the Qur’an, for indeed it is a good intercessor on the Day of Resurrection. It will say, “O Lord, release him with the adornment of honor,” and he will be released with the adornment of honor. It will say, “O Lord, clothe him with the garment of honor,” and he will be clothed with the garment of honor. It will say, “O Lord, adorn him with the crown of honor,” O Lord, be pleased with him, for there is nothing after Your pleasure.

"The Quran will come as an intercessor for its companion, saying: ‘O Lord! Every worker receives a reward according to their work, and I withheld pleasure and sleep from him. So, honor him.’ It is then said: ‘Extend your right hand, and it will be filled with Allah’s contentment, then extend your left hand, and it will be filled with Allah’s contentment.’ And he will be clothed in garments of honor, adorned with jewels of honor, and wear a crown of honor."

Abu Salih narrated: "The Quran intercedes for its companion, and he is clothed in the garment of honor. Then it says, 'O Lord, increase him,' and he is clothed in another garment of honor. He says, 'O Lord, increase him,' and it is given to him, and given to him… He says, 'My pleasure.'" Abu Muhammad said: Wahb ibn Ward said: "Make your recitation of the Quran knowledge, and do not make it merely an action."

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Does any one of you love to find three plump dates behind his wife?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Then three verses of the Qur'an are better for him than that."

"Verily, this Qur’an is the banquet of Allah, so learn from its banquet as much as you are able. Verily, this Qur’an is the rope of Allah, the evident light, and the healing that is beneficial. It is a safeguard for one who clings to it, and salvation for one who follows it. It does not deviate so that one may seek correction, nor does it become crooked so that one may straighten it. Its wonders do not cease, and it does not diminish due to frequent recitation. So recite it, for Allah rewards you for its recitation with ten good deeds for every letter. And I do not say ‘Alif, Lam, Mim,’ but ‘Alif’ and ‘Lam’ and ‘Mim.’”

Narrated by Zayd ibn Arqam: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up one day delivering a sermon. He praised Allah and spoke highly of Him. Then he said: “O people, I am only a human being, and the messenger of my Lord will soon come to me, and I will respond to him. And I am leaving behind in your midst the two weighty things: the Book of Allah, in it is guidance and light, so adhere to the Book of Allah and take from it.” And he encouraged [adherence to it] and urged [people] towards it. Then he said: “And my family, I remind you of Allah concerning my family, three times.”

Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Indeed, this path [of Islam] is beset by ambush, where the devils lie in wait, calling out: ‘O worshippers of Allah, this is the way [to righteousness]! So hold fast to the rope of Allah, for the rope of Allah is the Quran.’”

Abu al-Mughirah narrated: 'Abdah narrated to me from Khalid ibn Ma'dan who said: "The reader of the Quran and its learner are prayed for by the angels until they complete the surah. So, if one of you recites a surah, let him delay two verses from it until he completes it at the end of the day, so that the angels may pray for the reader and the one who teaches it from the beginning of the day until its end."
Narrated by Abu Amama: He used to say, "Recite the Qur'an, and let not these suspended manuscripts deceive you. Indeed, Allah will not punish a heart that has committed the Qur'an to memory."
Recite the Qur’an, and let not these suspended manuscripts deceive you, for indeed Allah does not punish a heart that has committed the Qur’an to memory.
Narrated by Ibn Mas’ud: "There is no educator but that he loves to have his education returned to him, and indeed, the education of Allah is the Qur’an."
"Abdullah used to say: "Indeed, this Qur’an is Allah’s banquet, so whoever enters into it, he is secure."
Narrated Abdullah: "Whoever loves the Qur'an, let him rejoice."
Narrated ‘Abdullah: “Whoever loves the Qur’an, let him rejoice.”

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, from ‘Asim ibn Abi Najud, from Al-Sha’bi: That Ibn Mas’ud used to say: “The Qur’an will come on the Day of Resurrection and intercede for its companion, and it will be a guide for him to Paradise, and it will bear witness against him, and it will be a driver for him to the Fire.”

Narrated by Anas: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah has people among mankind who are His people." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "The people of the Qur'an."

"Adhere to the Quran, for it is the understanding of intellect, the light of wisdom, the springs of knowledge, and the most recent of the books from the Most Merciful, a covenant. And it is said in the Torah: ‘O Muhammad, indeed I am sending down to you a fresh Torah, with which you will open blind eyes, deaf ears, and hardened hearts.'"

"Indeed, this Qur'an will be a reward for you, and a remembrance for you, and a light for you, and a burden upon you. Follow the Qur'an, and let it not follow you. For whoever follows the Qur'an, he will descend with it into the meadows of Paradise. And whoever it follows, the Qur'an, it will surge upon his back and cast him into Hellfire."

Ali ibn Abi Talib took my hand and said: "If you remain alive, there will be three categories of people reading the Quran: a category for Allah, a category for argumentation, and a category for the world. And whoever seeks [knowledge] through it will attain [success]."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba: that a man said to Abu ad-Darda’, “Your brothers from the people of Kufa, the people of remembrance, send you their greetings.” He said, “And upon them be peace, and instruct them to give the Quran with its measurements (i.e., with careful consideration), for it will lead them to moderation and ease, and keep them away from injustice and sorrow.”

I entered the mosque and saw people engaged in frivolous talk about traditions. I went to Ali and said, "Do you not see that people are indulging in frivolous talk about traditions in the mosque?" He said, "Have they done so?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There will be trials.'" I said, "And what is the way out of them?" He said, "The Book of Allah. The Book of Allah contains the news of what happened before you, the news of what will happen after you, and the judgment between you. It is the decisive authority, not a matter of jest. Whoever abandons it out of arrogance, Allah will destroy him. Whoever seeks guidance other than it, Allah will lead him astray. It is Allah’s strong rope, the wise reminder, the straight path. It is that by which desires do not deviate, and tongues do not become confused, and scholars do not become sated. It does not become old due to excessive repetition, and its wonders do not cease. It is that which the jinn did not stop hearing, saying, 'Indeed, we have heard a marvelous recitation' [Surah Al-Jinn: 1]. It is that if one speaks with it, he speaks truthfully; if one judges by it, he acts justly; if one acts by it, he is rewarded; and if one calls to it, he is guided to a straight path.” He said, "Take it to you, O one-eyed man."

It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, your community will face trials after you." He (the Prophet) was asked, "What is the way out of them?" He said, "The Exalted Book, which # no falsehood comes to it, either from before or from behind, a revelation from a Wise, Praised [Allah] - [Quran 41:42] # Whoever seeks guidance other than it, Allah has led him astray. And whoever turns his back on this matter from a tyrant and rules by other than it, Allah will break him. It is the wise remembrance, the clear light, and the straight path. In it is the news of those who came before you, the news of what comes after you, and the judgment between you. It is the conclusive decision, not a jest. It is what the jinn heard and did not refrain from saying, # ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous recitation’ - [Quran 72:1] # It does not diminish with much repetition, nor do its lessons end, nor do its wonders perish.” Then Ali said to Al-Harith, “Take it to yourself, O one-eyed man.”
And whoever is granted wisdom, then indeed he has been granted abundant good. [Surah Al-Baqarah (2):269], He [the Prophet] said: "Understanding through the Qur'an."

Narrated from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: # "He grants wisdom to whom He wills," [Quran, Surat Al-Baqarah, 269] #, he said, "The Book grants its accuracy to whom He wills."
Narrated by Khaythamah: He said to his wife, "Beware, do not let anyone who drinks wine enter my house after the Quran used to be recited therein every three nights."
"What prevents any of you, when he returns from the market or from his need, from reclining on his bed and reciting three verses of the Qur’an?"
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.”
"Indeed, the best of you are those who teach the Quran or learn it."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it." He then took my hand and seated me in this place to be taught.
"There is no man who learns the Quran and then forgets it, but he will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection as a ghazzam."

Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud) reported: “Increase the recitation of the Qur’an before it is taken away. They said: ‘These manuscripts (of the Qur’an) are taken away.’ He said: ‘It is taken away from the hearts (of people) at night, so they wake up in the morning impoverished of it, and they forget the saying: ‘There is no deity except Allah,’ and they fall into the sayings and poetry of the pre-Islamic era, and that is when the word falls upon them.”
Qatadah used to say, "Revive your hearts with it and revive your homes with it." He said: I believe he meant the Quran.
"Indeed, the Qur’an will be traversed over on a night, so no verse will remain in a mushaf or in the heart of anyone, except that it will be lifted."

"No one sits with the Quran but he leaves it with increased understanding or diminished understanding." Then he recited: "And We send down of the Quran that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers and increases only loss for the wrongdoers." [Surah Al-Isra, verse 82]

Marwan ibn Muhammad reported: Rifdah al-Ghassani reported: Thabit ibn ‘Ajlan al-Anṣari reported: It was said, "Indeed, Allah intends to punish the people of the earth, but when He hears the instruction of wisdom to young boys, He diverts that punishment from them." Marwan said: By wisdom, he means the Quran.

Narrated by Mu'adh bin Jabal: "The Quran will wear out in the breasts of people, just as clothing wears out. They will recite it, but they will not find in it any desire or pleasure. They will wear the skins of sheep over the hearts of wolves. Their deeds will be driven by greed, devoid of fear. If they fall short, they say, 'We will reach [our goals].' And if they do wrong, they say, 'We will be forgiven.' They claim, 'We do not associate anything with Allah.'"

Narrated: Abu Wail, from Abdullah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): “It is bad for one of you to say, ‘I have forgotten such and such a verse,’ rather, it was forgotten, and remind yourselves of the Quran, for it vanishes from the memories of men faster than sheep vanish from their enclosures.”

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Learn the Book of Allah, and renew it, and recite it beautifully, and acquire it. By Him in Whose Hand my soul is, it is more fleeting than the pangs of labor in the wombs."

Narrated ‘Uqba bin ‘Amir: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Learn the Book of Allah, the Exalted, and adhere to it, acquire it and recite it, for I swear by Him in Whose Hand my soul is, it slips away from the hearts more swiftly than a pregnant camel loses its water.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: “That Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl used to place the Mus'haf (the written copy of the Quran) upon his face and say: ‘This is the Book of my Lord, the Book of my Lord.’”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, Thabit narrated, saying: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla used to, when he prayed Fajr, recite the Mus'haf until the sun rose." He said: "And Thabit used to do it too."

Indeed, Allah does not feel shame in striking a parable, even of a mosquito or what is below it. But as for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord. And as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this parable?" It misleads many and guides many. But Allah does not misguide except the fasiqun (transgressors). [Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 26]. He [the narrator] said, "Meaning, they know that it is the speech of the Most Merciful."
"There is no speech greater before Allah than His speech, and the servants do not return to Allah with a speech more beloved to Him than His speech."

Narrated Jabir bin Abdullah: Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) used to present himself to the people in the standing place (during the Hajj season) and would say: “Is there anyone who will carry me to my people? Verily, the Quraysh have prevented me from conveying the Message of my Lord.”
"Indeed, this Qur’an is the Word of Allah, so I will not allow you to interpret it based on your desires."

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever occupies himself with the recitation of the Qur’an to the exclusion of asking me (regarding matters) and remembering Me, I will grant him the best reward of those who ask, and the superiority of Allah’s words over all other words is like the superiority of Allah over His creation."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The superiority of Allah’s speech over the speech of His creation is like the superiority of Allah over His creation."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The Qur'an is more beloved to Allah than the heavens and the earth and all that is in them."
Narrated Jabir: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Recite the Qur'an as long as you are in agreement upon it. And if you disagree about it, then stop."
Recite the Qur’an while your hearts are united. And if there is discord among you regarding it, then cease [reciting].”
Recite the Qur’an while your hearts are united. And if you disagree about it, then cease [reciting].”

"There are people to whom faith comes but not the Quran, and there are people to whom the Quran comes but not faith, and there are people to whom both the Quran and faith come, and there are people to whom neither the Quran nor faith comes. Then he gave them an example, saying: As for the one to whom faith comes but not the Quran, his example is like a date, sweet in taste but without scent. And as for the one to whom the Quran comes but not faith, his example is like a colocynth, fragrant but bitter in taste. And as for the one to whom both the Quran and faith come, his example is like a citron, fragrant and sweet in taste. And as for the one to whom neither the Quran nor faith comes, his example is like a wild melon, bitter in taste and without scent."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The example of a believer who recites the Qur’an is like an orange: its taste is sweet, and its scent is pleasant. The example of a believer who does not recite the Qur’an is like a date: its taste is sweet, but it has no scent. The example of a hypocrite who recites the Qur’an is like basil: its scent is pleasant, but its taste is bitter. The example of a hypocrite who does not recite the Qur’an is like the colocynth: it has no scent, and its taste is bitter."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The example of one who is given faith but not the Qur’an is like a date – its taste is good, but it has no fragrance. The example of one who is given the Qur’an but not faith is like a withered sweet basil – its fragrance is good, but its taste is bitter. The example of one who is given the Qur’an and faith is like a citron – its fragrance is good, and its taste is good. The example of one who is given neither faith nor the Qur’an is like a coloquint – its fragrance is foul, and its taste is foul."

Narrated by 'Amir bin Wathila: That Naafi' bin 'Abd al-Harith met 'Umar bin al-Khattaab at 'Usfan, and 'Umar had appointed him as governor of the people of Makkah. Naafi' greeted 'Umar, and 'Umar asked him, "Whom have you appointed over the people of the valley?" Naafi' replied, "I have appointed Ibn Abza over them." 'Umar asked, "And who is Ibn Abza?" Naafi' replied, "He is a client from among our clients." 'Umar said, "So you have appointed a client over them?" Naafi' said, "O Commander of the Believers, he is a reciter of the Book of Allah and knowledgeable about the rulings (Faraa'id)." 'Umar said, "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah raises some people up by means of this Book and brings others down by it.'"
"Indeed, the one who recites the Qur'an has a reward, and indeed, the one who listens to [him reciting] has two rewards."
One who listens to a verse from the Book of Allah, it is light for him.
The one who recites the Quran and is proficient with it, he is with the noble, righteous reciters (of the past). And the one who recites it while it is difficult for him, he receives two rewards.

Marwan ibn Muhammad narrated: Saeed, who is the son of ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, narrated to me from Ismail ibn ‘Ubaydullah, from Wahb al-Zimari, who said: "Whoever Allah grants the Qur’an, and he observes it during the hours of the night and the hours of the day, and acts upon what is in it, and dies while obeying Him, Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection with the scribes and the judges." Saeed said: "The scribes are the angels, and the judges are the prophets." He said: "And whoever is eager for it while he neglects it, yet does not abandon it, he will receive his reward twice. And whoever is eager for it while he neglects it and dies while obeying Him, he is among their elite, and they are preferred over the people, just as eagles are preferred over other birds, and just as a green pasture is preferred over the surrounding lands. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it is said: ‘Where are those who used to recite My Book, whom distraction from the pursuit of livestock did not divert?’ Then they are given immortality and bliss. If their parents died while obeying Him, a crown of kingship is placed upon their heads, and they say: ‘Our Lord, our deeds have not reached this level?’ And He says to them: ‘Yes, indeed, your son used to recite My Book.’”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "In the opening chapter (Surah Al-Fatiha) of the Book (Quran) is a cure for every disease."

Narrated Abu Sa’id Al-Ansari: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me and said, “Did Allah not say, ‘O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when they call you to that which gives you life,’ and Allah intervenes between a person and his heart, and that you will all be gathered to Him?’” [Quran 8:24] He then said, “Shall I not teach you the greatest chapter in the Quran before I leave the mosque?” Then, when he intended to leave, he said, “All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.” [Quran 1:1] And it is the Seven Oft-Repeated [Surah Al-Fatiha], and the Mighty Quran which you have been given.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The opening of the Book [i.e., Al-Fatiha] is the Seven Oft-Repeated [verses].”

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nothing has been revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, or the Qur’an like it – meaning Um al-Qur’an (Surah al-Baqarah) – and it is indeed seven of the oft-repeated (verses), and the Qur’an is the Great Qur’an which I have been given."
Narrated by Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All praise is due to Allah, the mother of the Qur'an, the mother of the Book, and the Seven Oft-Repeated [Surah Al-Fatiha]."
Narrated Abdullah: "There is no house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited, but the Shaytan leaves it, and he is screeching."
The chapter of al-Baqarah is a blessing when taught, a regret when abandoned, and the hypocrites cannot master it; and it is the foremost of the Qur’an.

"Indeed, everything has a peak, and the peak of the Qur’an is Surah al-Baqarah. And indeed, everything has an essence, and the essence of the Qur’an is the detailed (Muftal) verses.” Abu Muhammad said: “The essence is the purified [or the pure].”
One who recites Surat al-Baqarah, he will be crowned with it in Paradise.
Narrated ‘Abdullah: “Indeed, Satan leaves a house when Surah Al-Baqarah is recited in it.”

Narrated: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, which surah of the Quran is the greatest?" He said, "Say, 'He is Allah, the One.'" He said, "Which verse in the Quran is the greatest?" He said, "The Ayat al-Kursi: 'Allah! There is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining. His is the dominion, His the praise, and He is powerful over all things.' [Surah al-Baqarah, 2:255]." He said, "O Messenger of Allah, which verse do you love to befall you and your community?" He said, "The last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, for they are from the treasures of Allah’s mercy, from beneath His Throne. Allah has given them to this Ummah, and they contain all good of this world and the Hereafter."

Abdullah ibn Mas’ud narrated: A man from the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him) met a jinn. They wrestled, and the man wrestled the jinn, and he overpowered him. The man said to him, “I see you as weak and gaunt, as if the span of your hands is the span of a dog’s. Such are you, O people of the jinn, or are you among them like that?” The jinn replied, “By Allah, I am strong among them! But return to me for a second round, and if you overpower me, I will teach you something that will benefit you.” So he returned, and the man overpowered him again. The jinn said, “Tell me, teach me.” The man said, “Yes.” The jinn said, “Do you recite, ‘Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Self-Sustaining. [Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:255]’?” The man said, “Yes.” The man said, “Then you do not recite it in a house but the Shaytan leaves it with agitation like the agitation of an ass, and he does not enter it until morning.” Abu Muhammad said: “The weak (al-da’eel) means the slender one; the gaunt (al-shakheet) means the emaciated one; the strong (al-dalee’) means having a good ribcage; and the agitation (al-khabaj) means the wind.”

Narrated Abdullah: “Whoever recites ten verses from Surat al-Baqarah in a night, Shaytan does not enter his house that night until the morning. Four verses from its beginning, Ayat al-Kursi, two verses after it, and three verses from its end. Its beginning is: ‘To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. If you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, He will surely reckon for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah has power over all things.’ [Surat al-Baqarah, 284]”

"One who recites four verses from the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, Ayat al-Kursi, two verses after Ayat al-Kursi, and three verses from the end of Surah al-Baqarah, then neither the Shaytan nor anything he hates will approach him or his family on that day. And these verses should not be recited to a madman except that he regains his sanity."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “I did not think that anyone possessing understanding would sleep until he recited these verses from the end of Surah al-Baqarah, and indeed they are from a treasure beneath the Throne.”

"One who recites ten verses from Surah al-Baqarah at the time of sleep will not forget the Quran: four verses from its beginning, Ayat al-Kursi, two verses after it, and three verses from its end." Ishaq said: "He will not forget what he has memorized." Abu Muhammad said: "Some say that the narrator is al-Mughirah ibn Sumay'.”

"Whoever recites Ayatul Kursi and Surah Al-Fatiha until the verse: 'The Forgiver of sins, the Acceptor of repentance, the Severe Punisher, the Bestower of grace,' [Surah Ghafir, verse 30] - 'There is no god but He, to Him is the return (of all),' then he will not see anything he dislikes until the morning. And whoever recites it when evening comes, he will not see anything he dislikes until the morning."

Narrated by Nu’man bin Bashir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Allah wrote a Book a thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth. From it, He revealed two verses with which He sealed Surat al-Baqarah, and they should not be recited in a house for three nights without the devil approaching it.”
"Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah in a night, that suffices him."

Narrated by Asma bint Yazid: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah’s Greatest Name is in these two verses: 'Allah! There is no god but He, the Living, the Eternal Sustainer,' [Surah Al-Baqarah (2):255], and 'And your God is one God only,' [Surah Al-Baqarah (2):163]."

Narrated Jabir ibn Nufair: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah has sealed Surah Al-Baqarah with two verses that were given to me from His treasure beneath the Throne. So learn them and teach them to your women, for they are prayer, and Quran, and supplication."

Narrated Abdullah bin Buridah, his father said: I was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) and I heard him say: "Learn Surah Al-Baqarah, for taking it brings blessing, and abandoning it brings regret, and the hypocrite cannot master it." Then he remained silent for a while, and then he said: "Learn Surah Al-Baqarah and Surah Ali Imran, for they are the luminous verses, and they will shade their companions on the Day of Resurrection like two clouds, or two canopies, or two flocks of birds flying in serried ranks. And the Quran will find its companion on the Day of Resurrection when the grave splits open for him, like a pale man, and it will say to him: 'Do you know me?' He will say: 'I do not know you.' It will say: 'I am the Quran, your companion, with whom you thirsted in the scorching heat, and lost sleep at night.' And every merchant is accountable for his trade, and you today are accountable for every trade. Then he will be given the kingdom with his right hand and eternal life with his left hand, and a crown of dignity will be placed on his head, and his parents will be clothed in two garments that the world cannot compensate for. They will say: 'With what have we been clothed?' It will be said to them: 'Because of your son taking the Quran.' Then it will be said to him: 'Read and ascend in the degrees of Paradise and its mansions.' He will continue to ascend as long as he recites [the Quran], whether it be a murmuring or a melodious recitation."

Abu Amama reported: "Indeed, a brother among you was shown in a dream that people were traversing a long, rugged cleft in a mountain. And upon the peak of the mountain were two green trees, calling out: ‘Is there among you one who recites Surah al-Baqarah?’ ‘Is there among you one who recites Surah Ali Imran?’ So, when a man says, ‘Yes,’ they draw near with their branches until they attach to him, and they carry him across the mountain.” Abu Muhammad said: “The branches are the branches.”

Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi narrated from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr from Zayd from Jabir from Abu adh-Dhuha from Masruq from Abdullah (i.e., Abdullah ibn Mas'ud) who said: "A man recited (al-Baqarah and Aal 'Imran) before Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud). He said: 'You have recited two surahs in which is the Name of Allah, the Greatest, by which, if one calls upon Him, He answers, and if one asks Him, He gives.'"
