One who recites Surah al-Baqarah and Surah Aal ‘Imran, they will come on the Day of Resurrection and say, “Our Lord, there is no argument against him.”
Narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas’ud: “Whoever recites the family of Imran (Surah Al-Imran), he is wealthy, and the women are beautified.” Abu Muhammad said: Beautified means adorned.
One who recites the last verses of Surah Al-Imran in a night, it is recorded for him as if he has performed the night prayer.
"Whoever recites Surat Al-Imran on Friday, the angels will pray for him until nightfall."

Abu 'Ubaid, reported from Salam, said: I was told by 'Ubaidullah al-Ashja'i, who reported from Mis'ar, who reported from Jabir, before the events that occurred concerning him, from ash-Sha'bi, who said: 'Abdullah (ibn 'Umar) said: "Indeed, a good treasure is Surah Al-Imran, [reciting] it during the last part of the night."

Narrated Abu As-Sulai: A man was wounded by blood. He sought refuge in Wadi Majanna, a valley in which no one spends the night but is struck by a snake. On the edge of the valley were two hermits. One of them said to his companion, "By Allah, the man is dead!" So he began reciting Surat Al-Imran, and they recited a good chapter, hoping that he might survive. He awoke in good health. Abu Muhammad (Abu As-Sulai) said: Dhurayb bin Nuqayr, and it is said, bin Nafir.

'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The seven lengthy [surahs] are like the Torah, the thirty are like the Gospel, the two [surahs, al-Ikhlas and al-Mu'awwidhatayn] are like the Psalms, and all the rest of the Qur’an is superior to that."
'Umar said: "The livestock are among the obligations of the Qur'an."

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Hammam narrated to me, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Abdullah ibn Rabah, who said: I heard Ka'b say: "The opening of the Torah is al-An'am (The Cattle), and its ending is Hud."
Narrated by K’ab: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Recite Surah Hud on Fridays."
Recite Surah Hud on the day of Jumu'ah.
"Narrated by Khalid bin Ma'dan: 'Whoever recites ten verses from Surah Al-Kahf, he will not fear the Dajjal.'"

Narrated: Zirr ibn Hubaish: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat al-Kahf during a time when he intends to stay awake [during the night], he will remain awake." 'Abda said: We tested it, and we found it to be so.
"Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on the night of Friday, light will shine for him between him and the Sacred House (Ka'bah)."

Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us on the authority of ‘Abdah, from Khalid ibn Ma’dan, who said: "Recite the Mu’ajjiyat (the protective verses), which are: (Al-Mulk - The Sovereignty). It has reached me that a man used to recite nothing but these verses, and he was a man of many sins. So, they spread their wings over him and said: ‘O Lord, forgive him, for he used to frequently recite Me.’ So, the Lord accepted their intercession for him and said: ‘Write for him a good deed for every sin, and raise him a degree.’”

Narrated: K’ab bin ‘A’s said, “Whoever recites (Alm tanziil as-sajdah, and Tabarak alladhi bi yadihil mulk), seventy good deeds are recorded for him, and seventy sins are expunged from him, and he is elevated seventy degrees because of it.”

Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn Salih: Narrated to me Mu’awiyah ibn Salih: That he heard Abu Khalid, ‘Amir ibn Jasib, and Bahir ibn Sa’d, relating: That Khalid ibn Ma’dan said: “Indeed, the verses: ‘This is the Book [al-Quran] with no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds,’ [Surah Al-Sajdah (32:1-2)] argue on behalf of its companion in the grave, saying: ‘O Allah, if I am from Your Book, then intercede for him through me, and if I am not from Your Book, then erase me from it.’ And it is like a bird placing its wing upon him, so intercession is granted to him, and it protects him from the torment of the grave. And (Surah Al-Mulk - Glory be to Him) is like it.” So Khalid would not sleep until he recited them.

Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to me, from Layth, from Abu Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would not sleep until he recited (Tanzil) the prostration chapter, and (Wa Tabarak) [the opening verses of the chapter of the Glory]."
"These two [Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Falaq] have been given precedence over every other chapter in the Qur’an with sixty good deeds."

Hajjaj ibn Mihal narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Murrah narrated to me, saying: I heard Murrah say: "A man was brought before his grave, and he was brought to the side of his grave. Then a chapter of the Qur’an, thirty verses long, began to intercede for him, until we – I and Masruq – looked, and we did not find in the Qur’an a chapter of thirty verses except "Tabarak."

Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah, blessed and exalted, recited (or revealed) Surah Taha and Surah Yasin a thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. So when the angels heard the Qur’an, they said: ‘Blessed are the people upon whom this is sent down, blessed are the wombs that carry this, and blessed are the tongues that speak with it.’”

Abu al-Walid Musa ibn Khalid narrated to me, saying: Mu’tamir narrated to me from his father, who said: It reached me from Hasan that he said: "Whoever recites (Surah Yasin) in a night, seeking the countenance of Allah or seeking to please Allah, he will be forgiven. And it reached me that it equals the entire Quran."
Narrated Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Every thing has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Ya-Sin. Whoever recites it, then it is as if he has recited the Qur’an ten times.”
Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites Yasin in a night seeking the countenance of Allah, he will be forgiven in that night."
It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever recites Yasin in the early morning, his needs will be met."

Ibn Abbas (RA) said: "Whoever recites (Surah Yasin) in the morning, he will be given ease throughout the day until evening, and whoever recites it in the early part of the night, he will be given ease throughout the night until morning."
It was narrated to me that whoever recites (Ha-Mim) Surah Ad-Dukhan on Friday night with faith and belief in it, will wake up with his sins forgiven.
"Whoever recites (Ha-Mim) ad-Dukhan on Friday night, he will rise in the morning with his sins forgiven and will be married to the Houris."
Ja'far ibn 'Awn reported from Mis'ar, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, who said, "They were called 'al-Hawamim' as brides."

Narrated Hasan: "Whoever recites three verses from the end of Surah Al-Hashr in the morning and dies on that day, he will be sealed with the seal of the martyrs. And if he recites them in the evening and dies during that night, he will be sealed with the seal of the martyrs."

Narrated by Khalid bin Ma’dan from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): That he used to recite the Musabbahat (chapters of remembrance of Allah) at the time of sleep, and he said: “Indeed, there is within them a verse that equals a thousand verses.”

"Whoever says, when morning comes: ‘I seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the accursed Satan,’ and recites the last three verses of Surah Al-Hashr, Allah appoints seventy thousand angels to pray for him until evening. And if he says it in the evening, that is the same until morning.”

Abu Zayd, Sa’id ibn al-Rabee’, narrated to me, saying: “I narrated from Shu’bah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Muhajir, who said: ‘A man came to Kufa during the time of Ziyad. I heard him recounting that he had been with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on a journey. He said: ‘My knee would touch or brush against his knee.’ Then he heard a man reciting, “Say, ‘O disbelievers,’” and he said, “He is cleared of disbelief.” And he heard a man reciting, “Say, ‘He is Allah, the One,’” and he said, “He is forgiven.”'

Narrated from his father by Farwa bin Nawfal: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Whatever has come, has come with you.” He said: “I have come to learn something to say at my time of sleep.” He (the Prophet) said: “When you take your bed, recite ‘Say, O disbelievers!’ and then sleep upon its last verse, for it is a declaration of innocence from associating partners with Allah.”
Narrated Nawf bin Bikail: "Indeed, Allah has divided the Quran into three portions, and He made (Surah Al-Ikhlas - Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad) one-third of the Quran."

Narrated Abdullah ibn Yazid: Narrated Hayyah: He told me Abu Aqil that he heard Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever recites Surah Ikhlas (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahmad) ten times, a palace will be built for him in Paradise. And whoever recites it twenty times, two palaces will be built for him in Paradise. And whoever recites it thirty times, three palaces will be built for him in Paradise." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, then our palaces will increase!" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah is more expansive than that." Abu Muhammad said: Abu Aqil was Zuhair ibn Mabad, and they claimed that he was among the Abdal.
Abu al-Mughira reported from Utba ibn Damra ibn Habib, from his father: That he used to, when he recited a chapter, follow it with: "Say, 'He is Allah, the One.'"

Narrated Abu ad-Darda’: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Is it possible for any of you to recite a third of the Qur’an in a single night?” They said, “We are too weak and incapable of that.” So he said: “Indeed, Allah has divided the Qur’an into three parts, and ‘Say, He is Allah, the One’ is a third of the Qur’an.”
Abu Hurayrah used to say: "Reciting 'Say, He is Allah, the One' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) is equal to one-third of the Qur'an."

Abdullah (RA) said: "Indeed, (Say, "He is Allah, the One") equals one-third of the Qur'an." Another narration states: Abdullah (RA) said: "Indeed, (Say, "He is Allah, the One") equals one-third of the Qur'an."

Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, Mubarak ibn Fadalah told me, he said: Thabit narrated to me, from Anas: That a man said: “By Allah, I love this Surah: (Say, He is Allah, the One).” So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Your love for it has entered you into Paradise.”
Narrated by Ummi: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about Surah Al-Ikhlas (Qul Huwallahu Ahad), and he said: "It is one-third of the Quran, or it equals it."

Narrated ‘Abdu Allah ibn Musa, from Isra’il, from Mansur, from Hilal, from Ar-Rabee’ ibn Khuzaim, from ‘Amr ibn Maymun, from ‘Abd Ar-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from a woman of the Ansar, from Abu Ayyub, who said: He (the Prophet) came to her and said, "Do you not see what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) has brought?" She said, "Perhaps much good has come to us through the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)." She said, "What is it?" He said, "He said to us, 'Is any of you unable to recite a third of the Qur’an in a night?'" So we feared that he wanted to order us to do something we were unable to do, so we did not return to him anything until he said it three times. Then he said, “Is any of you unable to recite (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad, Allahu As-Samad)?”
Narrated by Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites Surah Al-Ikhlas (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad) fifty-one times, Allah will forgive him the sins of fifty years."

Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated: Hwayah and Ibn Lahe'ah narrated to me that they heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib say: He told me Abu Imran that he heard Uqbah ibn Amir say: I clung to the foot of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: O Messenger of Allah, recite to me Surah Hud and Surah Yusuf. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Uqbah, you will not recite from the Quran a surah more beloved to Allah or that reaches Him more than ‘Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the dawn’." Yazid said: Abu Imran never abandoned it; he would keep reciting it in the Maghrib (evening) prayer.

I walked with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and he said to me, "Say, O 'Uqba." I said, "What should I say?" He fell silent with me, then he said, "O 'Uqba, say." I said, "What should I say?" He said, "Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of the dawn.'" I recited it until I reached its end, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said at that time, "No seeker has ever asked for something like it, nor has any one seeking refuge sought refuge with anything like it."

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Indeed, verses have been revealed to me that I have not seen the like of them, nor has anyone seen their like, meaning: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn.”
Temim ad-Dari said, “Whoever recites ten verses in a night, he will not be recorded among those who are heedless.”
"One who recites ten verses in a night, it is recorded for him among those who pray."
"Whoever recites ten verses in a night, he will not be recorded among the heedless."

Malik related to me, saying, "Abu Ishaq told me, from Mughira ibn Abdullah al-Jadali, from Ibn Umar, who said: 'Whoever recites ten verses in a night, he will not be recorded among those who are heedless.'"
"Whoever recites fifty verses in a night, he will not be recorded among those who are heedless."
"One who recites fifty verses in a night, his name is recorded among the memorizers (of the Quran)."
"Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night, he will not be recorded among the heedless."
Narrated ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar: “Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night, it will be recorded for him among those who persevere in prayer.”
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night, the standing (Qiyam) of that night will be recorded for him."
Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to me from Al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, who said: Kacb said: "Whoever recites one hundred verses, it will be recorded that he is among those who persevere in prayer."
One who recites one hundred verses in a night, his name is recorded among those who persevere in devotion.
Narrated by Abdullah: "Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night, he will be recorded among those who persevere in prayer."
One who recites one hundred verses [of the Quran] will not be recorded among the heedless.
Narrated: Habib bin 'Ubaid said: I heard Abu Amama saying: "Whoever recites two hundred verses, his name will be recorded among those who persevere in prayer."
"Whoever recites two hundred verses in a night, he will be recorded among those who observe the Qunut."

"One who recites ten verses in a night, he is not recorded among the heedless. And one who recites one hundred verses in a night, he is recorded among those who are diligent in prayer. And one who recites two hundred verses in a night, he is recorded among the successful."

"Whoever recites ten verses in a night, he is recorded among the rememberers (of Allah); and whoever recites one hundred verses, he is recorded among those who are devoted in prayer (qanit); and whoever recites five hundred verses to a thousand, he awakens and has a qintar of reward. It was said, 'What is a qintar?' He said, 'A full measure of gold.'"

Abu Nu'man narrated: We were told by Wahb, from Yunus, from Hasan: That the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night, the Quran will not argue with him that night. Whoever recites two hundred verses in a night, it will be written for him the Qunut of that night. Whoever recites five hundred verses to a thousand verses in a night, he will awaken with a qintar for him in the Hereafter." They said: What is a qintar? He said: Twelve thousand."

Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Whoever recites three hundred verses in a night, a qintar is written for him, and whoever recites seven hundred verses." I do not know what Abu Nu'aim said regarding her (the narration).

Al-Hakam ibn Naafi’ narrated to me, Hariz narrated to me, from Habib ibn ‘Ubaid, who said: I heard Abu Amama saying: "Whoever recites a thousand verses, a qintar of reward is written for him. And the qirat is from that qintar, and it is not sufficient for your world. He says: Nothing in your world equals it."

"Tameem ad-Dari and Fadala ibn Ubaid reported: 'Whoever recites a thousand verses in a single night, a qintar will be written for him. And the qirat is better than the world and all that is in it, and he will acquire as much reward as Allah wills.'"

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever recites a thousand verses, or five hundred verses, it is written for him a qintar of reward, and a qirat is like a huge mountain from it."
Abu Hurairah (RA) said: "A qintar is twelve thousand [dirhams]."
"Al-Qintar is filling the skin of a bull with gold."
Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "A qintar is forty thousand [dirhams]."
Ishaq narrated to me from Mubarak, from Hasan, who said: "A qintar is the diyya (blood money) of one of you, twelve thousand."
Muslim narrated to me, that is Muslim the Black, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Qintar is seventy thousand dinars."
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The qintar is a thousand awqiyyah and two hundred awqiyyah."
Abu Nu'aim narrated to me, Sharik narrated to me, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Qintar is seventy thousand mithqals."

One who witnesses the opening of the Qur’an is as if he has witnessed a victory for the sake of Allah, and one who witnesses its closure when it is concluded is as if he has witnessed the spoils of war being divided.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Saleh al-Murri narrated to me from Qatada, who said: "There was a man who used to recite [the Quran] in the mosque of Medina. Ibn Abbas had set a watch over him. And whenever it was the day of his death, he would stand up and turn towards him."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Saleh narrated to me from Thabit al-Bunani who said: Anas ibn Malik would, when he neared the completion of the Quran at night, leave a portion of it until the morning, and then he would gather his family and complete it with them.
Anas would, whenever he completed reciting the Quran, gather his children and his family and invoke blessings upon them.

Abu al-Mughirah narrated: al-Awza'i narrated to me from 'Abdah who said: "When a man completes the recitation of the Qur'an during the day, the angels send blessings upon him until evening, and if he completes it at night, the angels send blessings upon him until morning."

Narrated Zararah bin Aufi: That the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked, "Which work is best?" He said, "The reciter who moves from the beginning of the Quran to its end, and from its end to its beginning, every time he completes (a portion), he moves on." It was said, "What is the reciter who moves on?" He said, "The one who recites the Quran, moving from its beginning to its end and from its end to its beginning, every time he completes (a portion), he moves on."

Ibrahim narrated to me from Jarir, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "When a man recites the Quran during the day, the angels pray for him until evening, and if he recites it at night, the angels pray for him until morning."

Sulaiman said: "I saw our companions liking to complete [their recitation] at the beginning of the day and at the beginning of the night."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Firyabi narrated to me from Sufyan, from Al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, a similar narration, except that it does not contain Sulaiman's statement.
One who recites the Qur’an from the depths of his heart, then for him is a supplication either in this world or in the Hereafter.
One of them said, "Whoever recites the Quran during the night or day, the angels will send blessings upon him until the night." And the other said, "He will be forgiven."
One who recites the Qur’an and then makes supplication, forty thousand angels guarantee the acceptance of his supplication.

Sa'id ibn al-Rabee' narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to me from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, who said: Mujahid sent for me, and said: "We only called you because we wanted to conclude the Quran, and it has reached us that supplication is accepted at the conclusion of the Quran." He said: "So they made supplications."

Sa'd narrated: "When the recitation of the Quran coincides with the beginning of the night, the angels pray upon it until morning. And if its recitation coincides with the end of the night, the angels pray upon it until evening. Sometimes, something remains with one of us, so he delays it until evening or morning."
The carriers of the Quran are the elite of the people of Paradise.
Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Malik narrated to me from Sa’id ibn Jubayr: that he used to complete the recitation of the Quran every two nights.

Abdullah ibn Amr reported: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, in how much [time] should I complete the recitation of the Qur'an?" He [the Prophet] said, "Complete it in a month." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am capable [of doing so]." He said, "Complete it in twenty-five [days]." I said, "I am capable." He said, "Complete it in twenty [days]." I said, "I am capable." He said, "Complete it in fifteen [days]." I said, "I am capable." He said, "Complete it in ten [days]." I said, "I am capable." He said, "Complete it in five [days]." I said, "I am capable." He said, "No."
"The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered me not to recite the Quran in less than three [rak'ahs]."

Narrated by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "None of us is one who does not recite the Quran." Ibn Uyaynah said: He seeks sufficiency through it. Abu Muhammad said: The people say: 'Ubaidullah ibn Abi Nahik.

Narrated Tawus: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was asked: "Who among the people has the best voice for the Quran and the best recitation?" He said: "He whose recitation, when you hear it, makes you feel that he fears Allah." Tawus said: "And he was eloquent like that."
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Allah has not permitted anything as He permitted a Prophet to chant the Quran.” A companion said to him, “You mean to recite it aloud?”
"Allah has not permitted anything as He permitted a Prophet reciting the Quran."

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: Narrated to me Layth: Narrated to me Yunus: From Ibn Shihab: He told me Abu Salama bin Abdur-Rahman: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say to Abu Musa, who had a beautiful voice in reciting the Quran: "Indeed, this has been given to him from the Psalms of the family of David."

Narrated Abdullah bin Salih: Narrated to me Layth: Narrated to me Yunus: From Ibn Shihab: He said: Abu Salama also told me: That Umar ibn al-Khattab, whenever he saw Abu Musa, would say, "Remind us of our Lord, O Abu Musa," and he would recite [the Quran] in his presence.

Narrated Abdullah: “I would not like to find any of you placing one leg over the other, singing, and neglecting to recite Surat Al-Baqarah. For Shaytan flees from the house in which Surat Al-Baqarah is recited. And the most barren of houses are those which are devoid of the Book of Allah.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ayyub, who said: Some of the family of Salim ibn Abdullah told me: "Salama al-Baydaq came to Medina and led them in prayer. It was said to Salim: ‘If you had come and listened to his recitation.’ When Salama reached the door of the mosque, he heard his recitation, so he turned back and said: ‘[It is] chanting, chanting!’"
Abu Salama reported: Abu Musa used to come to Umar, and Umar would say to him: "Remind us of our Lord," so he would recite [Quran] before him.
The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah has not permitted anything as He permitted a Prophet reciting the Quran, proclaiming it aloud."
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, Abu Musa was given a flute from the harps of the family of David."

Narrated Abu Huraira: 

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered (a place) and heard the recitation of a man. He asked, "Who is this?" It was said, "Abdullah ibn Qais." He said, "Indeed, this one has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David."
"Adorn the Quran with your voices."
Narrated by Al-Baraa’ bin ‘Aazib: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Beautify the Quran with your voices, for a good voice enhances the beauty of the Quran."

Abdullah ibn Sa’id narrated from Abdullah ibn Idris from Al-A’mash, who said: “A man recited before Anas with a tune from these tunes, and Anas disliked it.” Abu Muhammad said, and another stated: “Gurak ibn Abi al-Khidrim recited [it].”
Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "They considered these melodies to be innovations within the Quran."
